6. Earnings Quality & Balance Sheet

FCF conversion: OCF/NI = 2.10x FY2025 ($1,833.9M / $872.7M [FY2025 10-K]), up from 1.75x FY2024 — insurers' OCF is inflated by float timing and is not directly distributable (see §7 caveat); the more relevant "free cash" concept is holding-company liquidity, which rose from $613M (9/30/25) → $887.4M (12/31/25) → $836M (3/31/26) → $911.5M (6/30/26), all comfortably above the $225M internal minimum [respective 8-K/10-Q Liquidity sections]. SBC: not separately isolated within budget; "other adjustments" in the GAAP-to-adjusted EPS bridge are small (≤$0.11/share most quarters). GAAP-vs-adjusted gap drivers (FY2025, per diluted share): net realized investment losses ($1.39), intangible amortization ($1.31), restructuring ($0.53, mostly a new Q4 2025 efficiency plan), a $0.21 loss on the LTC subsidiary held-for-sale, tax effects (–$0.71), then reportable catastrophes ($3.85 pre-tax, –$0.81 tax) to reach $22.81 ex-cat from $16.93 GAAP [Q4 2025 8-K reconciliation table, filed 2026-02-10]. Capital adequacy: the FY2025 10-K discloses only qualitatively that insurance subsidiaries "expect to exceed minimum RBC requirements" and that all rated subsidiaries carry an A.M. Best "A" (Excellent) rating [FY2025 10-K, filed 2026-02-19] — no numeric consolidated RBC ratio is disclosed in SEC filings (n/a — would require state NAIC statutory filings). Financial leverage (debt/(debt+equity), carrying value): 27.3% at FY2025-end ($2,206.9M/$8,078.5M), improving to 26.6% at Q2 2026-end ($2,208.1M/$8,306.0M) [10-K Note 18; Q2 2026 10-Q], both comfortably inside the credit facility's 35% maximum covenant [FY2025 10-K, filed 2026-02-19] and within the sector-playbook comfort zone. Debt maturities: no maturities until March 2028 ($300M) and February 2030 ($350M) after Assurant refinanced the February-2026 notes early via a $300M 5.55% 2036 issuance in August 2025 [FY2025 10-K, Note 18]. Buybacks: repurchased 1.4M shares for $299.9M in FY2025 plus $168.4M dividends; Board authorized an additional $700M program in November 2025 (on top of the November 2023 $600M program), leaving $774.6M unused at 12/31/2025 [FY2025 10-K, Item 5 and Note 18]; diluted share count fell from 53.78M (FY2023) to 49.38M (Q2 2026), roughly –8% [XBRL].

7. Valuation Snapshot

Primary method (P/B vs. sustainable operating ROE), per insurance.md. Current P/B ≈ 2.15x ($265.00 price / $123.48 book value per share, using Q2 2026 equity $6,097.9M ÷ 49.382M shares [Q2 2026 10-Q] — this exactly matches the quant pipeline's independently-computed $123.48 book value/share and 2.146x P/B [d4_live_snapshot.parquet], a clean cross-check). GAAP ROE on a full-year-average-equity basis was 15.9% in FY2025, up from 15.3% (FY2024) and 13.4% (FY2023) [ratios.py output on 10-K data]. Stripping catastrophes and the FY2025 PYD windfall from net income (adjusted-ex-cat EPS $22.81 × 51.09M diluted shares ≈ $1,165M, less ~$89M after-tax PYD benefit, over average equity of $5,489M) implies a "cleaned" sustainable operating ROE of roughly 17-20% (analyst estimate, not company-reported). [Corrected 2026-10-06: the estimate strips catastrophe losses entirely, but catastrophes are a recurring cost for a property insurer; including them the FY2025 figure is about 16.8%, see Correction section] Applying the justified-multiple relation P/B ≈ (ROE − g)/(COE − g) with a conservative g=4% and a sector-typical COE=10% (insurance.md's own P&C benchmark, chosen over a mechanical CAPM figure because AIZ's trailing beta of 0.542 [d4_live_snapshot.parquet] likely understates true cost of equity given catastrophe tail risk): ROE=18% implies P/B≈2.33x; ROE=16% implies P/B≈2.00x; ROE=17% implies P/B≈2.17x — i.e., the current 2.15x multiple is roughly what a mid-to-high-teens sustainable ROE justifies; the stock is not obviously cheap on this framework, though it sits at the low end of the 2-4x band the playbook associates with 15-18% ROE/sub-95%-combined-ratio franchises. Secondary (P/E on operating EPS): trailing P/E on FY2025 adjusted-ex-cat EPS ($22.81) is 11.6x; on GAAP EPS ($16.93, TTM $20.94) it is ~15.7x/12.7x — below the 10-16x diversified-P&C band's midpoint, consistent with the Value factor score. Peers: The Hartford (HIG) trades at ~1.90x P/B against an ~18.7-20.3% TTM core ROE [gurufocus/company 8-K via web search, 2026-09]; Old Republic (ORI) trades at ~9.0x P/E [AAII, 2026-09-11]; Kemper (KMPR) is currently loss-making (negative TTM ROE) [CNBC/company data, 2026-09-17] and is not a clean comparator right now. AIZ's niche (lender-placed/warranty) has few exact pure-plays, as expected. Suppressed and why: EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales and a raw FCF-yield DCF are explicitly not used as primary evidence per insurance.md (debt is not financing against a policyholder-liability balance sheet). Illustratively, valuation.py's reverse-DCF on an OCF-minus-capex FCF proxy ($1,618.8M) against the EV bridge ($13,595.6M) implies the market is pricing in only –5.8% FCF growth for 10 years at a 10% WACC — a nonsensical-looking output that itself demonstrates why the sector playbook bans this method here: this year's OCF is flattered by float timing and the same reserve-release dynamic discussed in §4, not a repeatable distributable-cash base.

8. Bull Case and Bear Case

Bull case

  1. Global Lifestyle's Connected Living unit grew net earned premiums+fees +11.9% in FY2025 on real mobile-subscriber and financial-services-program growth, not pricing/assumption changes [FY2025 10-K].
  2. Balance sheet has gotten safer, not riskier, while returning capital: financial leverage improved from ~29.0% (FY2024) to ~26.6% (Q2 2026), holding-company liquidity nearly doubled from $613M (Q3 2025) to $911.5M (Q2 2026), and the Board added a fresh $700M buyback authorization in November 2025 [FY2025 10-K; Q2 2026 10-Q].
  3. Management has been transparent, not evasive, about the H2 2026 reserve-development comp headwind, disclosing the exact dollar mechanics three quarters running — a credibility signal, not a red flag, and the underlying (ex-PYD, ex-cat) FY2026 guide of "approximately 10%" growth as of August 2026 has only been raised, never cut, in the last four releases [Q1/Q2 2026, Q3/Q4 2025 8-Ks].

Bear case

  1. Two consecutive years of unusually large favorable prior-year reserve development ($106.7M FY2024, $113.1M FY2025, both in Global Housing) inflated reported and adjusted EPS; management guides essentially zero incremental PYD for H2 2026, so the "8-for-8 beat, 8-for-8 raise" pattern investors have priced in may not mechanically continue on the reported line even if the ex-PYD business is healthy [FY2025 10-K MD&A; Q2 2026 8-K].
  2. Global Housing remains genuinely catastrophe-exposed (Hurricane Helene alone cost $92M pre-tax in Q3 2024); FY2025's much lower cat impact ($198.8M vs $245.2M pre-tax) partly reflects a milder hurricane year, not a structural improvement, and can reverse [FY2025 10-K; special 8-Ks, 2024].
  3. At ~2.15x P/B against an analyst-estimated 17-20% "cleaned" sustainable ROE and a 10% cost of equity, the stock is priced for continued high-teens returns with little margin of safety; analyst sentiment is already fully bought-in (8 of 8 recent price-target actions were raises, strong-buy consensus, zero downgrades in 90 days per d4_live_snapshot.parquet), leaving asymmetric downside if H2 2026 prints disappoint even modestly relative to the now-elevated bar.

9. Key Risks & Kill Criteria — What Would Invalidate This Thesis

  1. Global Housing's analyst-computed combined-ratio-equivalent (policyholder benefits + expenses, over net earned premium — see §3/§7 methodology) rises above ~85% for two consecutive quarters (vs. ~79.4% FY2025), signaling the underwriting improvement was reserve-driven, not structural.
  2. FY2026 adjusted-EPS-ex-cat guidance is cut (not merely decelerated on the already-disclosed PYD comp) at the Q3 2026 (on/around 2026-11-03) or Q4 2026 (~Feb 2027) release versus the August-2026 raised range ("mid single digits" headline / "approximately 10%" ex-PYD).
  3. Holding-company liquidity falls back below ~$500M without a clearly disclosed one-off cause (vs. $836-911.5M over the last two quarters).
  4. A single reportable-catastrophe quarter exceeds roughly $150M pre-tax in Global Housing (worse than Q3 2024's Hurricane-Helene-driven $138M) with evidence of reinsurance-recoverable strain or a materially higher retention.
  5. Financial leverage (debt/total capital, carrying value) rises above ~32% (approaching the 35% covenant) via debt-funded buybacks/M&A, or any rated insurance subsidiary is downgraded from A.M. Best "A."

10. Catalysts & Calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026, estimated 2026-11-03 [d4_live_snapshot.parquet estimate] — not yet confirmed by the company in any filing checked (no 8-K scheduling notice found as of 2026-09-25). Watch specifically for: (a) whether Q3 2026 Global Housing results show the guided zero-PYD assumption holding, (b) any update to the "approximately 10%" ex-PYD FY2026 guide, (c) hurricane-season catastrophe pre-announcements (Assurant has issued mid-quarter cat 8-Ks in each of the last several third/fourth quarters, e.g. 2024-07-15, 2024-10-16, 2025-01-23). No investor day or index-event catalyst identified in the filings reviewed.

dossiers.AJG:
AJG — Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F38, Wave-2 Standard)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Reservation: reported growth (+13% to +31% YoY across recent quarters) is now almost entirely acquisition-driven. Organic growth in the core Brokerage base commissions/fees has run only 4% in both Q1 and Q2 2026 (vs AJG's historical high-single-digit organic pace), and the pace of new bolt-on M&A has itself slowed (6 deals closed in Q2'26 vs 9 a year earlier; $58M of acquired annualized revenue vs $291M), consistent with leverage (~2.8-3.0x net debt/EBITDA) constraining the very M&A engine the triage praised. The business is high-quality and the price is undemanding, but the growth-durability story needs the next 2-3 quarters to show organic re-acceleration before this is a full-conviction position.

2. Business in plain English

Arthur J. Gallagher is an insurance broker and risk-management consultant: it places commercial and personal insurance for clients with third-party insurance carriers (earning commissions and fees) and separately sells third-party claims administration and risk-consulting services (Risk Management segment, "Gallagher Bassett"). It underwrites no insurance risk itself — it is a distribution and advisory platform, so its economics are closer to an asset-light services business (people, client relationships, data) than to an insurer's balance sheet. Growth comes from two engines: organic (new business, retention, exposure/rate) and an unusually active tuck-in M&A program (independent agencies acquired and folded onto Gallagher's platform), most recently supercharged by the ~$13.45bn acquisition of AssuredPartners, financed in December 2024 and reflected in results since.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: composite percentile only 0.009 (live_rank 492/503) — the quant model does not like AJG; it reached diligence through the triage/quality-growth screen only (Q05: quality 4, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4, citing 31% revenue growth and a "38x trailing P/E [that] looks cheap once one-time integration costs are stripped out"). This research confirms the triage's own caveat was directionally right — the 38x trailing P/E is indeed distorted by AssuredPartners integration/amortization costs (§6) — but also finds the triage's growth read was too generous: 31% reported growth is ~25-27 points of M&A and only ~4-5 points organic (§4-5), a distinction the triage's reason field did not make. The low quant score is at least partly a real signal (leverage percentile and net-share-issuance from deal financing would penalize AJG in the Quality family), not purely an artefact — flagged as a data_conflict below.

AJG does not issue formal numeric full-year EPS or revenue guidance in its earnings releases (confirmed: neither the Q1'26 nor Q2'26 8-K Ex-99.1 contains a guidance table of the kind Abbott or Autodesk publish). It gives qualitative outlook commentary only — e.g. Q2'26: "In an increasingly complex risk environment, client demand for our advice, analytics, market access, specialty expertise and claims advocacy remains robust... we remain confident in our ability to build on our momentum." A "CFO Commentary" document referenced in each release (posted to ajg.com/IR) may contain more specific outlook language but was not accessed this pass (not an SEC filing; time-boxed limitation). Per the base template's instruction, this is stated rather than fabricated: no formal guidance to track.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: TTM (ended 2026-06-30) ≈ FY2025 10-K OCF $1,930M + 1H'26 OCF $967M − 1H'25 OCF $448M = $2,449M OCF; capex over the same window ≈$164M → ≈$2,285M FCF, roughly consistent with Yahoo/d4's TTM FCF of $2.08bn (d4 freeCashflow; cross-check, minor definitional gap not reconciled).

This is disclosed and reconciled, but the widening gap is itself worth watching — a "serial acquirer" business model structurally runs GAAP below adjusted, and the gap has grown alongside the largest deal in the company's history.
  • Leverage: total debt (long-term debt noncurrent $11.955bn + short-term borrowings $1.52bn) ≈ $13.5bn at 2026-06-30, up from ~$12.7bn at 2025-06-30 shortly after the AssuredPartners financing. Cash (incl. restricted/fiduciary cash) $1.386bn same date. Net debt ≈ $12.1bn vs TTM EBITDA (Yahoo/d4) $4.29bn → net debt/EBITDA ≈ 2.8x, in the same range as the triage's cited 3.0x (methodology differs slightly: triage likely used company-reported EBITDAC; this analyst used Yahoo EBITDA as a cross-check — both point to elevated, not extreme, leverage for the sector). This level of leverage is consistent with, and likely explains, the M&A-pace deceleration noted in §1/§8.
  • M&A: AssuredPartners — ~$13.45bn, financed December 2024, closed and integrating through 2025-2026; the single largest deal in company history and the primary driver of both reported revenue growth and the GAAP/adjusted gap. Underlying bolt-on M&A pace has slowed: 6 acquisitions closed in Q2'26 (est. annualized revenue acquired $58M) vs 9 in Q2'25 ($291M); 8 in Q1'26 vs 10 in Q1'25 — a real, quantified deceleration in the company's second growth engine, plausibly capital/leverage-constrained post-AssuredPartners.
  • Share count: no shares were issued directly to sellers in tax-free-exchange acquisitions in Q2'26 or Q2'25 (per the release) — M&A is being funded with cash/debt, not dilutive stock issuance, which is consistent with the leverage increase observed above.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

d4 (2026-09-25 close, price $231.10): NTM P/E 16.0x, FY1 P/E 15.5x, trailing P/E 38.3x (distorted by the integration/amortization items above — use NTM/FY1, not trailing), FCF yield 3.5%, beta 0.51. No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for AJG (not in the 92-name v1_valuation_table.csv) → v1_verdict = null; this section is this analyst's own reverse DCF (skill script valuation.py).

[Corrected 2026-10-06: risk-free rate of 4.2% is wrong (5.17%), WACC 7.0% too low and base FCF includes stock-based compensation; restated to about 7.2%/yr (4.9-9.9% across assumptions), see Correction section]
  • Sensitivity: at WACC 8.5% (reflecting the elevated leverage), implied growth rises to ≈7.7%/yr.
  • My evidence-based base case: even at the current, slowed organic pace (4-5%) plus a resumed, deleveraged bolt-on M&A program (historically adding several points of inorganic growth annually before AssuredPartners absorbed capacity) and modest margin expansion, 8-10%/yr adjusted FCF/EPS growth over the next decade is a reasonable base case — below the >20% currently being delivered, but well above the organic-only run-rate, on the assumption M&A capacity is restored as leverage comes down.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Top-3 global insurance broker with genuinely durable moats (client relationships, specialty expertise, scale in placement/analytics) and a decades-long track record of successful tuck-in M&A. (2) Even at a slowed pace, the M&A engine is still adding real revenue (6-8 deals/quarter), and deleveraging from the AssuredPartners deal should restore capacity for more over the next 2-3 years. (3) Client retention and new business generation both described as "strong"/"outstanding" by management (Q2'26 release) — a qualitative but consistent management claim across releases, not new spin introduced this quarter.

Bear: (1) The headline growth numbers the triage screen liked (31% revenue growth) are overwhelmingly M&A, not organic; organic growth of 4-5% is unremarkable for an insurance broker and well below AJG's own historical high-single-digit organic pace — if this is the new normal (hard commercial insurance-rate cycle turning soft, or genuine competitive share loss), the re-rating case weakens materially. (2) Leverage (~2.8x net debt/EBITDA) is the highest in recent company history and is already visibly constraining the bolt-on M&A pace that is the second growth engine — a negative feedback loop if organic growth doesn't independently reaccelerate. (3) The GAAP/adjusted EPS gap has widened for two consecutive years running; a persistently widening gap between "what shareholders can spend" (dividends, buybacks — funded by cash/adjusted earnings) and "what GAAP reports" is a legitimate long-run earnings-quality concern for a serial acquirer, even when each individual adjustment is well-disclosed.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Total organic change (AJG's own combined Brokerage + Risk Management metric) stays below 5% for three consecutive quarters (currently 4-5% in Q1-Q2'26; below AJG's historical high-single-digit norm).
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x (from ~2.8x now) without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
  3. Quarterly acquired-annualized-revenue run-rate stays below $100M (vs $291-354M a year ago) for three more consecutive quarters, signaling the M&A engine has not recovered capacity.
  4. The GAAP-vs-adjusted EPS gap widens by more than $0.50/share YoY again in a quarter with no new large acquisition to explain it.
  5. A state insurance-regulatory or E&O (errors & omissions) matter is disclosed that is not ordinary-course (none identified this pass — see §11).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-29 (Q3 2026, per d4 live snapshot). No formal numeric guidance to reconcile against (§5); watch for organic-growth trend (re-acceleration vs continued 4-5%) and M&A-pace commentary.

  • Litigation/regulatory: a targeted web search for AJG securities litigation or SEC/DOJ investigation (2026) returned no matches beyond routine SEC filings (8-K/10-Q/DEF 14A) — no material litigation or investigation identified this pass. This is not the same as a confirmed clean bill: a full read of the FY2025 10-K Item 3 (Legal Proceedings) and Item 1A risk-factor diff was not completed this pass (time-boxed limitation, disclosed rather than silently skipped).
  • Auditor/accounting: no auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language identified this pass (not exhaustively verified — same limitation as above).
  • Leverage/M&A-pace deceleration: treated as the primary, quantified red flag in this dossier (§6, §8) — not a governance or accounting problem, but a real change in the shape of the growth story that the triage's quick pass did not capture.
  • Data conflict: b1_live_scores.csv ranks AJG at live_rank 492/503 (bottom 2% of the composite), in tension with the triage's quality=4/growth=4 read and this dossier's own INCLUDE-SMALL verdict. Both are plausibly correct simultaneously: the pre-registered quant model penalizes recent net share/debt issuance and leverage (Quality family) and rewards raw statistical value/momentum signals that a debt-funded serial acquirer with a 38x trailing P/E will score poorly on, while the qualitative/fundamental read (this dossier) can see through the GAAP distortion to a business growing adjusted EPS >20%. dossiers.AKAM:
AKAM — Akamai Technologies, Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F153, Wave-8 Standard)

1. Verdict

WATCH (thesis horizon 24-48 months). A real strategic step happened days before the 25 Sep 2026 cutoff: an $11.6B, seven-year commitment from Anthropic that could lift revenue about 35-40% at full run-rate, but it needs about $5.5B of capex, $1.7B of it pre-purchased in 2026, comes with a warrant for about 5% of the stock, and lands on a business whose stock-based-compensation-adjusted free cash flow is already near zero. At $113.94 the price implies more than my base case delivers. The quick triage (Q11: advance=false, "elevated leverage ... 5.5x") is overturned on the leverage point (net debt is about 1.7x on filings; see section 11) but confirmed on the conclusion. What would change it: evidence that Anthropic service starts on schedule and first payments are received, 2027 capex guided back toward 20% of revenue, and SBC-adjusted FCF turning clearly positive; or a price near $85-90.

2. Business in plain English

Akamai started as a content-delivery network (CDN) and now sells three things: security (web-application firewalls, DDoS defence, zero-trust segmentation), delivery of websites and video, and a growing cloud-computing business (Cloud Infrastructure Services, "CIS", the former Linode). Security is 55% of revenue and growing about 10%; delivery is shrinking about 5-6% a year; CIS is growing about 39% and is where the AI-infrastructure demand sits. Competitors are Cloudflare, Fastly and the hyperscalers; Akamai's edge is its distributed network, but its pivot is capital-hungry and margin-dilutive.

dossiers.ALB:
ALB — Albemarle Corporation

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 24–36 months. Named reservation: ALB is a single-commodity (lithium) price bet wrapped in a chemicals company; its own disclosed FY2026 sensitivity table shows adjusted EBITDA ranging 4.5x between a repeat of the 2025 price trough (~$0.95bn) and a return to the 2021–2025 average price (~$4.3bn). The balance sheet is now genuinely strong (net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈0.5x post-divestitures) and the recovery already under way is real and primary-source-verified, not merely a favorable comp — but position size should reflect that this is a commodity-price call, not a diversified-quality call.

2. Business in plain English

Albemarle mines and processes lithium (from Chile brine and Australian hard-rock spodumene, largely through the Talison joint venture) into lithium carbonate/hydroxide sold mostly under long-term contracts to battery and EV makers (Energy Storage segment, ~75% of FY26 sales), plus a smaller, steadier Specialties segment (bromine — flame retardants, oilfield fluids — and lithium specialties for pharma/electronics). It makes money on the spread between its (largely fixed, mining-cost-based) production cost and the market price of lithium, so profits are extremely levered to a single commodity price that has swung from ~$70+/kg (2022 peak) to ~$10/kg (2025 trough) and back to ~$20/kg (2026). Its moat is scale, low-cost brine/hard-rock resource ownership and long-term customer contracts (~40% of Energy Storage salts volume), not pricing power over the commodity itself.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores: composite 0.911765 (decile 10, quintile 5, live_rank 44/~2,300 — a top-2% quant score). Momentum (fam_M≈0.81) and Earnings momentum/SUE (fam_S≈0.61) are the strongest drivers — both real: the stock and earnings estimates are both recovering sharply off the 2025 trough (§4). Value (fam_V≈0.67) looks attractive (pct_bp 0.94, pct_ep 0.35) largely because book value is high relative to a still-recovering earnings base. Quality (fam_Q≈0.71) is respectable (pct_ocf_a 0.60, low leverage pct 0.90) — genuinely improved post Ketjen/Eurecat divestiture debt paydown. Durability judgement: the recovery itself is real (verified realized price $19.53/kg in Q2 2026 vs $12.17/kg a year ago, §4), but its sustainability is entirely a bet on where spot lithium settles over the next 1–3 years — a price the company itself declines to forecast (its own guidance is a three-scenario sensitivity table, not a point estimate, §5). The quant score cannot distinguish "durable" recovery from "cyclical bounce"; only the commodity-price view can.

5. Guidance track record: a scenario table, not point guidance (state so explicitly)

Albemarle does not issue traditional next-quarter/next-year point guidance; every quarterly release instead publishes a full-year sensitivity table keyed to three observed lithium-price scenarios — this is disclosed explicitly and is, if anything, a more honest practice than false-precision point guidance:

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Balance sheet is the single best fact in this dossier: as of 30 Jun 2026, total debt $1.9bn, cash $1.6bn, liquidity ~$3.2bn (incl. $1.5bn undrawn revolver), net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈0.5x (company's own credit-agreement definition) — a dramatic improvement funded by the Ketjen/Eurecat divestitures and the earnings recovery. Q2 2026 operating cash flow $710m, free cash flow $638m (83% OCF conversion — company flags this was boosted by Talison JV dividend timing and non-recurring working-capital benefits, i.e. not fully repeatable at this conversion rate). Preferred stock: 7.25% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred (NYSE: ALB PR A) remains outstanding — a real, fixed dividend obligation and a source of common-share dilution on conversion (V1's diluted share count of 136.2m vs the raw 118.0m shares outstanding reflects this if-converted treatment). GAAP-vs-adjusted gap is significant in the recovery quarters (Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $3.75 vs GAAP $3.52 — an 6% adjustment, modest and disclosed) but was much wider in the loss quarters (large non-cash impairment charges drove GAAP losses far below adjusted losses in 2024–2025) — appropriately flagged, not glossed over.

7. Valuation snapshot — V1 says EXCESSIVE; I partially disagree with the input, not the caution

V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json): NTM P/E 9.65x, own-history percentile 7th (i.e. ALB has traded above today's multiple in ~93% of the last 152 months — nominally cheap), peer median 17.7x, but V1's reverse-DCF implies 33.4% revenue growth needed for 10 years to justify the price at a 10.53% WACC → verdict: excessive, base 3-yr annualised return −1.2%, bear −40.6%, bull +77.8%.

Where I think the specific input is wrong: V1's reverse DCF uses a TTM EBIT margin of 4.27% (ebit_margin_used in v1_valuation.json) as its forward base. That TTM window spans Q3 2025 through Q2 2026 and is still dragging in the Q3 2025 operating loss (−$217.0m) — it has not caught up to the current run rate. Primary-source correction: Q2 2026 alone had a GAAP operating margin of 452.9/1,743.3 = 26.0%; Q1 2026 was 233.5/1,428.7 = 16.3%. Holding a 4.27% margin fixed and asking for 33% revenue growth to reach the same target EV mechanically produces an extreme, near-impossible growth requirement — it is an artefact of the stale margin input, not evidence that the market is pricing in something irrational.

My own reconciliation, built from the company's own FY26 sensitivity table (§5) rather than a margin-fade DCF: applying peer-appropriate EV/EBITDA multiples (8x bear / 7x base / 9x bull) to the company's own $0.95bn / $2.5bn / $4.3bn EBITDA scenarios, net of ~$0.3bn net debt, on 136.2m diluted shares: bear ≈$54/share, base ≈$126/share, bull ≈$282/share — against the $109.73 close. This reads closer to FAIR than EXCESSIVE, and the implied growth in the current price looks roughly in line with the company's own already-realized ~$20/kg run rate, not a bet on a return to the $30/kg 2021–2025 average. valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = false; both analyses agree on the direction and magnitude of the risk (a return to $10/kg trough pricing would still be a severe outcome) even though they disagree on the point estimate.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) lithium demand (EV + grid storage) structurally grows faster than new supply can be brought online, sustaining or improving on the $19.53/kg realized in Q2 2026; (2) balance sheet is now clean enough (0.5x net debt/EBITDA) to fund growth capex or return capital without re-leveraging; (3) portfolio simplification (Ketjen/ Eurecat exits) focuses management and capital entirely on the highest-return lithium/bromine franchises.

Bear: (1) lithium is a genuinely volatile, oversupplied-prone commodity (Chinese lepidolite/African supply can swing on marginal-cost economics) — a return to the ~$10/kg 2025 average would cut EBITDA ~65% from the Q2 2026 run rate; (2) ~40% of Energy Storage salts volume is on long-term contracts, meaning realized pricing can lag or lead spot in either direction, adding a layer of estimation risk beyond spot price alone; (3) the mandatory convertible preferred is a real, non-trivial claim on cash flow and a dilution overhang not fully reflected in headline EPS.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Realized Energy Storage price falls back below $15/kg LCE for two consecutive quarters (vs $19.53/kg in Q2 2026) — the clearest sign the recovery is reversing.
  2. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 1.5x (vs ≈0.5x at 30 Jun 2026) — would signal renewed balance-sheet stress.
  3. Two consecutive quarters of negative adjusted EBITDA in the Energy Storage segment.
  4. FY2026 total-corporate scenario table is cut below the "~$10/kg" case (i.e., management signals a worse floor than the 2025 trough) at any quarterly release.
  5. Any further material impairment (Item 2.06 8-K) outside the already-disclosed Ketjen/Eurecat divestitures.

10. Catalysts & calendar

dossiers.ALGN:
Align Technology, Inc. (ALGN) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F23 | As of: 2026-09-25 close ($146.78) | Depth: Standard

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Named reservation: the stock is genuinely cheap on its own 14-year valuation history, but that trough partly reflects real, disclosed growth deceleration (FY26 guided revenue growth of just 3–4%, likely the slowest since IPO) and recurring GAAP one-off charges; size small pending confirmation that the FY27 margin-recovery commitment is met.

2. Business in plain English

Align makes Invisalign clear aligners (its core, ~82% of revenue) and iTero intraoral scanners plus exocad CAD/CAM software, selling to orthodontists, GP dentists and increasingly DSOs (dental service organizations) worldwide. It earns money per case shipped (aligners) and per scanner/software seat, and is the clear share leader in clear aligners globally, though it now competes with lower-cost aligner entrants and Straumann/others in scanners.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q07) called it "the standout price-vs-growth setup in this batch" on ">100% implied forward EPS growth" against a 12x NTM P/E. Verified: the ">100%" figure is a base-year artifact, not real operating momentum — Q2'25 EPS ($1.72) vs Q2'26 EPS ($1.51) is actually down 12% YoY, and Q3'25 EPS ($0.78) was the weakest print in two years. The apparent explosive forward growth comes from comparing to a temporarily depressed base (Q3'25/Q4'25 carried heavy restructuring, impairment and accelerated-depreciation charges). The 12x NTM P/E being at the ~1st percentile of ALGN's own 14-year history is real and confirmed (V1), but it is priced that way for a disclosed reason (below), not an oversight.

4. Last 8 quarters (SEC 10-Q/10-K + XBRL; GAAP unless marked)

3Q25/4Q25's margin compression was driven by disclosed one-offs: a manufacturing-facility impairment/ assets-held-for-sale charge, accelerated depreciation on disposed manufacturing assets, and a restructuring program (headcount reduction) initiated in 4Q24 and again 3Q25 (earnings-release GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation notes 1–5). Non-GAAP gross/operating margins were materially steadier throughout (non-GAAP op margin 22.9% in 2Q26 vs 21.3% in 2Q25).

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases, quoted verbatim from each release)

  • 3Q25 release (Oct 2025) → guided Q4'25 revenue "$1,025M to $1,045M, up sequentially"; actual $1,047.6M — beat the high end. FY2025 revenue guided "flat to slightly up from 2024"; actual FY25 $4,034.96M vs FY24 $3,999.01M = +0.9%, in line.
  • 4Q25/FY25 release (Feb 2026) → guided Q1'26 revenue "$1,010M to $1,030M, up 3–5% YoY"; actual $1,040.1M — beat the high end. Guided Q1'26 GAAP op margin "12.4%–12.8%"; actual 13.6% — beat. Guided FY2026 GAAP operating margin "slightly below 18.0%" (+~400bps YoY) and non-GAAP "~23.7%."
  • 1Q26 release (Apr 2026) → guided Q2'26 revenue "$1,040M to $1,060M, up 3–5%"; actual $1,056.2M, within range. Reaffirmed the FY26 GAAP op-margin guide of "slightly below 18.0%."
  • 2Q26 release (Jul 2026) → guided Q3'26 revenue "$1,000M to $1,020M" (a sequential decline, guided seasonality) and cut FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance to "15.1%–15.6%" — roughly 250–290bps below the "slightly below 18.0%" guided just one quarter earlier — because of newly disclosed one-time charges: a $37.5M UK VAT contingent liability (below), ~$30.6M of Q1'26 legal settlements, and further restructuring/ accelerated depreciation, now totaling an expected $90–110M for FY26. Non-GAAP FY26 operating-margin guidance was left unchanged at ~23.7%. This is the single most important adverse fact in this dossier: revenue guidance has not moved (3–4% growth reaffirmed all year and beaten on the top line every quarter), but the GAAP profitability guide was cut materially inside two quarters — an increase in one-off cash costs, not a demand problem. Treat any "GAAP margin beat/miss" narrative with that context.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • UK VAT dispute: clear aligners were ruled VAT-exempt by the UK First-tier Tribunal (2025); ALGN stopped charging UK VAT from Aug 2025. On 2026-07-07 the Upper Tribunal overturned that ruling. ALGN recorded a $37.5M estimated liability (inclusive of interest) in Q2'26 and will charge 20% VAT on UK invoices from 2026-09-07; it intends to appeal, with the outcome "subject to uncertainty" (its own words).
  • Tariffs: subject to Section 122 (Trade Act of 1974) tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled the prior IEEPA tariffs unlawful (2026-02-20); the Section 122 tariffs are themselves under appeal at the Court of International Trade. Company states it does not expect a material impact currently — a live, disclosed, unresolved policy risk rather than a settled cost.
  • Balance sheet: no debt on the balance sheet; cash $1,102.6M (2Q26) vs $1,094.9M (FY25 year-end); total liabilities are dominated by deferred revenue ($1,187.2M) and accrued liabilities, not borrowings — a genuinely strong, low-risk balance sheet.
  • Capital return: $1.0bn buyback program (announced Apr 2025); $733.3M remaining as of 2026-06-30; guided to repurchase $400–500M in 2026. Diluted share count down from 72.59M (2Q25) to 71.52M (2Q26), -1.5%.
  • FCF/SBC: H1'26 operating cash flow $343.8M vs $181.3M H1'25 (+90%); FY26 capex guided $125–150M. SBC ~4.3% of revenue (2Q26), stable.

7. Valuation — reconciled with V1

V1 (systematic) calls ALGN "attractive" (score 0.48), citing NTM P/E of 12.0x at the 1.2th percentile of its own 171-month (14-year) history. I agree the multiple is genuinely at a generational low for this name — that fact is confirmed and I do not dispute it. However, V1's base-case reverse DCF return of +59.65%/yr (3yr) is not credible and I overturn it: it requires revenue growth of 15.6%/yr (4x the company's own guided 3–4% for FY26) and an exit multiple of 39.4x (up from today's 12.0x) simultaneously. V1's own sanity check flags this: the base-case 3-year price target ($597) exceeds even the Street's current 12-month high target ($240, mean $208.60) by 2.5x. I attribute this to V1's reverse-DCF using a TTM EBIT margin (13.2%) that is itself depressed by the 3Q25/4Q25 one-offs (§4) — a low earnings base plus an 11.2% WACC forces the model to assume unrealistic growth just to justify today's EV, which is not the same as the market actually pricing that growth in. My own base case: revenue growth 4–6%/yr (current guide plus modest recovery as one-offs roll off and management's own "at least ~100bps" FY27 margin-improvement commitment is met), GAAP operating margin recovering toward 16–17% by FY27, and the NTM P/E re-rating partially — to 15–17x, not V1's 39x — as growth stabilizes. valuation_view_vs_v1: dossier_view = fair (in_line with my base case), consistent = false (I reject V1's base-case return and exit multiple, not its multiple-percentile finding).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Clear Aligner volume +7.4% YoY in 2Q26 on double-digit international/DSO growth, with revenue beating guidance every quarter this year; (2) net-cash balance sheet funds continued buybacks (-1.5% share count YoY) regardless of near-term margin noise; (3) management has explicitly committed to further ~100bps non-GAAP margin improvement in FY27 on top of FY26's, a specific, checkable promise. Bear: (1) FY26 revenue-growth guidance (3–4%) is the softest in the company's history as a public company, and Systems & Services revenue is guided down 6–8% YoY on a structural mix shift to lower-price/ leased scanners; (2) GAAP operating-margin guidance was already cut once this year (§5) and the UK VAT appeal and Section 122 tariff litigation are both unresolved, open-ended cost risks; (3) the stock's beta (~1.5–1.7) means any confirmation that growth deceleration is structural (not cyclical) could re-rate the multiple down further even from today's 14-year low.

9. Kill criteria

  1. Quarterly Clear Aligner volume growth turns negative YoY.
  2. FY2026 GAAP operating-margin guidance is cut again below the current 15.1%–15.6% range (excluding charges already disclosed as of this dossier).
  3. Full-year revenue growth guidance is cut below the current 3%–4% range.
  4. Net cash (cash − debt) falls below $500M.
  5. Cumulative UK VAT / Section 122 tariff cash outflows exceed $150M beyond the $37.5M already reserved.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-10-28/29 (Q3'26, estimated from the identical prior-year filing date; not yet announced). UK VAT appeal timeline not yet set. Section 122 tariff litigation (Court of International Trade) outcome/timeline not yet set. FY2027 formal guidance expected alongside Q4'26 results (company stated its "strategic and operating model review" is still underway as of the 2Q26 release).

11. Red-flag scan

No going-concern language, material weakness or restatement found in the reviewed 10-Q/10-K/8-Ks. Open items: UK VAT liability/appeal and Section 122 tariff litigation (both above, both genuinely unresolved); two restructuring programs in twelve months (4Q24 and 3Q25) — a real, if modest, signal of cost-structure strain, not a governance red flag. No auditor change noted.

2. Business in plain English

Allstate is a personal-lines-focused P&C insurer (the "You're in Good Hands" brand) selling primarily auto and homeowners insurance to individuals through captive/exclusive agents, independent agents, and direct channels, plus non-standard auto via its National General subsidiary (acquired 2021). 3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

b1-family prelim scores (source: internal lead_prelim_rank.csv): Q 0.752, V 0.586, M 0.940 (12-1m return +22.4%), composite 0.874. Durable part: per the Q2-26 release (§12 #1), auto insurance policies-in-force are growing (+2.8% YoY) with new business up 8.8%, i.e. Allstate is not just harvesting price increases while losing share — the repricing appears to be holding demand, a real structural signal. 7. Valuation snapshot

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Policies-in-force and new business are both growing at mid-to-high single/double digits — the repricing is holding volume, unlike a pure harvest-and-shrink strategy. (2) Even after heavy mean-reversion, current valuation (7.65x NTM P/E, 1.82x P/B) leaves room for a "normal-good" outcome (mid-teens ROE) to still look cheap. (3) Capital position fully rebuilt from the 2022 crisis with buybacks now running at $1B/quarter. Bear: (1) 44% ROE and the FY2027 consensus EPS cut of 21% are not compatible with "durable" — a two-year-old bull case (auto repair) has now been almost entirely realized and priced. (2) Underlying homeowners combined ratio is already deteriorating (61.5%, +2.9 pts YoY) even before any broader loss-cost reacceleration — an early crack in the "structural improvement" story. (3) The auto insurance pricing cycle is adversarial: Allstate's own price increases invite competitor re-entry (Progressive, GEICO, State Farm) exactly when Allstate's margins look best, which is the mechanism by which 2022-style compression historically returns.

9. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis is invalidated if any of the following are observed (source: company 10-Q/8-K disclosures each quarter)

  1. Property-Liability recorded combined ratio > 100% for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Auto or homeowners policies-in-force growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (share loss as competitors reprice back down).
  3. Adjusted net income ROE (ttm) stays above ~35% for another two quarters without a corresponding upward revision to FY2027 consensus (would mean the deceleration is being denied, not resolved) — OR falls below ~15% (confirms hard mean reversion, re-underwrite thesis).
  4. Net favorable reserve development flips negative in auto/casualty for two consecutive quarters.
  5. Homeowners underlying combined ratio deteriorates a further ~5 pts from 61.5%.

Applied Materials is executing extremely well (record revenue, guidance raised twice this fiscal year, net-cash balance sheet, buybacks slowed rather than chased into strength) and the stock has already fallen ~34–42% from its 30 June 2026 high. But even after that drawdown, the 10-year reverse DCF shows the market pricing in ~18–24%/year FCF growth for a decade — far above any credible through-cycle base case for a capital-equipment company, and the independent factor data agrees: AMAT's value/FCF-yield percentile is in the bottom quintile of the whole universe (19th pct). A great business, priced for more than a capital-intensive, historically cyclical franchise can plausibly deliver. Condition to upgrade: either a further material de-rating (FCF yield rising toward ~3.5%+, i.e., meaningfully lower price for the same or higher FCF) or 3–4 more quarters of evidence that AI-driven WFE demand is a structural step-change rather than a supercycle that mean-reverts.

2. Business in plain English

Applied Materials makes the machines that make chips: deposition, etch, ion implantation, chemical-mechanical planarization and inspection/metrology tools sold to foundries, memory makers and IDMs (TSMC, Samsung, Micron, Intel and others) building fabs, plus a large recurring Applied Global Services (AGS) parts/service business tied to the installed base. It is the largest wafer-fab-equipment (WFE) vendor by revenue, with leading share in several deposition/etch categories and a growing advanced-packaging business tied to AI accelerators (2.5D/3D packaging, chip-on-wafer). It makes money by selling capital equipment (lumpy, tied to customers' capex cycles) plus steadier services/parts revenue on the installed base, and its economics are fundamentally a fixed-cost manufacturing/engineering business layered on a physics roadmap — margins swing hard with fab utilisation and the industry's capex cycle, not primarily with AMAT's own execution.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Composite_qvm 0.623 (decile 7, rank 189) is driven almost entirely by momentum (fam_M 0.846, 85th pct) and respectable quality (gp/assets 66th pct, ROE 76th pct), while value is a genuine outlier weak point (fam_V 0.235, FCF/price 19th pct — bottom quintile of the entire universe) and the accruals percentile is very low (7.9th pct, a caution flag on earnings quality that likely reflects the rapid receivables/inventory build funding the revenue ramp — normal in an equipment upcycle per the sector playbook, but worth tracking). AMCR — Amcor plc — Diligence Dossier (Agent F72, Wave 4)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — 24–36 month horizon, reservation named: leverage. AMCR (Jersey-incorporated, NYSE/ASX-listed) is now the combined Amcor + Berry Global consumer-packaging group following the April 30, 2025 all-stock merger. The combined business is cheap on a reverse-DCF basis (§7) and synergy delivery has so far tracked at the "upper end" of plan every quarter, but FY2026 free cash flow missed even its own cut guidance (§5) and leverage (~3.5x) is still above the company's own comfort zone one year post-close. This is a name to hold at reduced size while the deleveraging path proves out, not a full-conviction position.

2. Business in plain English

Amcor makes the packaging that wraps, bottles or caps food, beverages, healthcare and personal-care products — flexible films, rigid containers, closures and cartons — for large consumer-goods customers worldwide. It earns money on a cost-plus-margin basis, largely passing through resin/aluminum/paper input costs and keeping a processing margin; growth comes from volume, price/mix, and (since April 2025) the roughly $8bn of acquired Berry Global revenue plus disclosed cost synergies. Its competitive position rests on manufacturing scale, customer switching costs (packaging lines are qualified into a customer's production process) and, since the merger, the largest global footprint in flexible + rigid consumer packaging.

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable?

b1 scores: composite 0.685 (decile 7, the highest-ranked of F72's three names on the pre-registered model), driven almost entirely by fam_S (earnings momentum, SUE 2.40 — the highest in the peer set) and fam_M (12-1m momentum +17.3%), with fam_Q very weak (0.071 — the model's quality family penalizes AMCR's post-merger leverage and net share issuance). This is exactly the pattern to be suspicious of: the SUE/momentum signal is mechanically produced by the merger's revenue and EPS step-change (accounting-acquirer comparisons vs a much smaller pre-merger base), not by an organic acceleration in the underlying business. Triage (Q13) correctly flagged this ("83% forward EPS growth reflects merger synergy ramp") and the leverage/integration risk. The durable part of the thesis is the synergy program (tracking ahead of plan every quarter reported) and category leadership; the non-durable part is the momentum/SUE score, which will normalize once merger-anniversary comparisons roll off in Q4 FY2026 (the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was already the last quarter with a meaningfully smaller prior-year base).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Synergy capture has beaten or matched the upper end of guidance every quarter disclosed (Q1 FY26 synergies "at upper end," Q2 "at upper end and targets reaffirmed," Q3 "at upper end of expectations") — execution risk on the stated synergy number specifically looks low so far. (2) At 8.9x EV/EBITDA and a 6.1% dividend yield, the combined entity is priced well below typical global packaging peer multiples (sector norms are typically low-double-digits), consistent with triage's "cheap 10x NTM" read. (3) The combined flexible + rigid packaging portfolio gives genuine category leadership and cross-sell opportunity that neither legacy company had alone.

Bear: (1) Free cash flow missed its own (already-cut) guidance in the first full post-merger fiscal year — a real, quantified execution shortfall, not a rounding miss. (2) Leverage (~3.5x) is targeted to stay at 3.5–3.6x through December 2026 by management's own admission — this is a business that will not meaningfully delever for at least another 12 months, leaving little room for a demand shock or a further input-cost spike. (3) The b1 model's bullish score is substantially a momentum/SUE artefact of merger accounting, not organic acceleration; once FY2026 comparisons fully lap (from Q1 FY2027/Transition Period), the earnings-momentum signal that got this name triaged forward is likely to fade mechanically.

  2. Free cash flow for the six-month Transition Period (Jul–Dec 2026) comes in below the low end of whatever range management guides at the next release — a second consecutive FCF miss would be a much stronger signal than the first.
  3. Quarterly dividend is cut or held flat for more than 2 consecutive quarters after being raised in FY2026 (a de facto signal management judges coverage to be tight).

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–36 month thesis horizon, revisit after Q3 2026 print on 2026-11-03). AMD's underlying business is executing an unambiguous, accelerating AI/data-center ramp (Data Center revenue +107% YoY in Q2 2026; three straight quarters of beat-and-raise; a landmark OpenAI supply/equity partnership). But the reverse DCF shows the current price already requires that acceleration to continue at a very high rate for years, the trailing GAAP P/E (160x) is not usable as a valuation anchor, and 7-of-8-quarter beat-and-raise plus a stock price up ~191% over 12 months (triage) mean consensus targets (mean $618.50) sit below the current price ($630.63) — the Street itself is not, on average, underwriting further upside from here. This matches the triage call directionally (advance, but flagged "consensus price target roughly at spot… treat as full-diligence, not automatic buy") and confirms it with primary-source numbers.

2. Business in plain English

AMD designs (and outsources manufacturing of) computer processors: CPUs for PCs and servers (EPYC, Ryzen), GPUs/AI accelerators for data centers (Instinct MI-series), embedded/gaming chips, and FPGAs (from the 2022 Xilinx acquisition). It sells to PC makers, cloud/hyperscale data-center operators, and embedded-systems customers, competing most directly with Intel in CPUs and Nvidia in AI GPUs. It makes money on chip design margins; its main current growth engine is selling AI-training/inference GPUs to hyperscalers and AI labs as a second source to Nvidia.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 quant context (data/b1_live_scores.csv, live_rank 171/503, composite decile 7): momentum is extreme (mom_12_1 = +191%, pct_mom_12_1 ≈ 0.73) and SUE is strong (+3.8, percentile 0.89 — i.e., large, consistent positive earnings surprises), while value percentiles (earnings yield 0.10, FCF yield 0.12) are weak, as expected for a name re-rating on growth. The SUE signal is durable — it is built from three consecutive real, primary-source beats (Q4 2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, see §5), not a one-off. The momentum signal is partly an artefact of the same growth story re-rating the multiple, which is the normal, non-durable component of any momentum factor — the question for the reverse DCF (§7) is whether the re-rating has already gone further than the (real) growth acceleration justifies.

Reverse DCF (own construction; two-stage — 10-year explicit growth then 3% terminal, WACC 10% for higher-beta semiconductor/AI-capex-cycle exposure, consolidated basis): Using an annualized H1-2026 FCF base (~$8.25bn, chosen over the FY2025 figure of $6.7bn because the AI ramp is demonstrably already underway and a stale base would understate current earnings power) against EV of $1.019tn: solving EV = Σ FCF₀(1+g)ᵗ/(1+WACC)ᵗ (t=1..10) + terminal value at 3% gives implied 10-year FCF growth g ≈ 24–26%/yr, i.e. roughly a 6x growth in annual FCF by year 10. [Corrected 2026-10-08: with the stated inputs (base $8.25bn, 10%, 3% terminal, EV $1.019tn) the implied growth is about 32%, not 24-26%; deducting stock-based compensation (about $2.0bn annualised) gives about 36% at 10% and about 41% at a 11.8% cost of equity (5.17% + Blume beta ~1.6 x 4.14%); the 10% rate had no stated build] That is an aggressive but not obviously impossible ask given AMD's own H2 2026 guidance trajectory (Q3 2026 guide alone implies +12.7% sequential revenue growth, and management guides data-center revenue to double again in 2027) — but it requires the current hyperscaler AI-capex cycle to persist at a high rate for a full decade, well beyond the visibility any guidance track record can support. implied_vs_base: above — the price is discounting more growth than the analyst's own base case (mid-teens-to-20%% FCF CAGR moderating after 2028 as the AI-capex cycle matures and Nvidia/custom-ASIC competition intensifies).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. OpenAI strategic partnership (announced 2025-10-06): OpenAI to deploy up to 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs over multiple years (1 GW in 2026), with AMD management guiding "tens of billions" of incremental revenue and >$100bn in cumulative revenue potential over four years (AMD/OpenAI press releases, ir.amd.com and openai.com, 2025-10-06). 2. Three consecutive quarters of guidance beats with the growth rate still accelerating (Q3 2026 guide of ~$13bn implies the fastest sequential growth of the last four quarters), and MI400-series (MI455X/MI430X) already being consumed by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta per management (Q2 2026 earnings call). 3. Net-cash balance sheet (no leverage constraint) and FCF compounding quickly (H1 2026 FCF already 61% of all FY2025) give AMD real capacity to fund capacity expansion without dilution or debt stress.

Bear (3 points): 1. Reverse DCF requires ~24–26%/yr FCF growth sustained for 10 years — a high bar; if the AI-GPU capex cycle decelerates or Nvidia/hyperscaler-custom-ASIC competition compresses AMD's share/margins earlier than year 5–6, the downside to a re-rated multiple is large (46.9x NTM P/E has very little room for disappointment). 2. Analyst mean/median price targets ($618.5/$616) sit below the current price ($630.63) — a rare signal that the sell-side consensus, even after the run, is not on average underwriting further near-term upside. 3. The OpenAI warrant deal (up to 160 million AMD shares at $0.01, vesting on deployment milestones and an escalating AMD share-price target up to $600 for the final tranche) creates real dilution risk (~9-10% of shares if fully vested) and makes AMD's economics partly dependent on OpenAI's own ability to pay for and deploy the compute — OpenAI is not yet GAAP-profitable, a customer-concentration/counterparty risk this dossier flags but cannot fully quantify from AMD's own filings alone.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

Any of the following would break the thesis (i.e., would move this WATCH toward REJECT): 1. Any single quarter of guided revenue growth below the prior quarter's growth rate (deceleration signal) — would break the "still-accelerating beat-and-raise" thesis this WATCH call depends on. 2. Data Center segment gross margin falls below 50% for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026 consolidated gross margin was 53.8%; a sustained drop would signal AI-GPU pricing/competitive pressure from Nvidia or custom ASICs). 3. OpenAI deployment milestones (1 GW tranche) missed or delayed beyond 2026 — the single largest identified forward revenue driver; a delay would remove the main support for the current above-base valuation. 4. Net cash position turns negative (i.e., AMD takes on net debt) without a corresponding step-up in disclosed capacity/capex plans — would signal the AI-capex ramp is cash-flow-negative rather than self-funding. 5. Buyback pace stays at the reduced ~$220M/half-year run-rate for more than 2 more quarters combined with rising share count from OpenAI-warrant vesting — dilution without offsetting repurchase would compound the "priced above base case" risk.

  • MI400-series (MI455X/MI430X) broader customer ramp beyond OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta through 2026–2027.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 12–36 months. [Corrected 2026-10-06: verdict is now INCLUDE-SMALL. On the P/B method the price needs a sustained return on equity of 46% (ex-AOCI equity) to 55% (total equity) at a 10.6% cost of equity, against a 55% adjusted operating ROE ex-AOCI and a base case of about 50%: in line, with no margin of safety on the instructed method. See Re-assessment (RA10).] One-sentence reason: a capital-light wealth- and asset-management franchise compounding assets under management at double-digit rates, returning the large majority of earnings to shareholders, trading at a single-digit NTM P/E with a clean red-flag scan — and the systematic valuation model (V1) independently reaches the same "fair, not demanding" conclusion this dossier reaches from primary sources.

2. Business in plain English

Ameriprise is a diversified financial-services holding company built around three businesses: Advice & Wealth Management (its largest segment — roughly 10,000+ affiliated financial advisors managing client assets for a fee, plus banking/lending products), Asset Management (Columbia Threadneedle Investments, running mutual funds/ETFs/institutional mandates), and a smaller, run-off-oriented Retirement & Protection Solutions legacy annuity/insurance book. It earns most of its money on fees tied to assets under management/administration (AUM/AUA) rather than on spread or underwriting risk — a capital-light model that requires relatively little balance-sheet capital per dollar of revenue, which is why its return on equity is structurally very high (see §6).

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

Quant context (b1_live_scores.csv, live rank 113/~1,172): strong across families — quality composite in the top decile, ROE 57th percentile of the raw factor (the b1 pct_roe is 0.568, but this compares AMP against the whole cross-sectional universe including much lower-ROE industrials/utilities; against its own asset-management peer group AMP's ROE is exceptional — see §7), earnings yield 90th percentile, FCF yield 76th percentile, momentum 93rd percentile. Durable: AUM/AUA growth of 13–19% YoY across every reported segment in Q2 2026 (§4) and four consecutive quarters of 16–22% YoY adjusted-operating-EPS growth (§5) are structural, filed facts — a genuinely growing capital-light franchise, not a one-quarter beat. [Corrected 2026-10-06: most of the 13-19% AUM/AUA growth is market appreciation, not flows. Q2 2026: Advice & Wealth Management total client net flows $3.1bn (-28% YoY, about 1% annualised of $1,248bn client assets); Asset Management total AUM net flows -$6.5bn (-$9.2bn a year earlier; Global Institutional -$5.1bn, retail -$1.4bn). Growth in client assets is therefore as exposed to the equity market as to franchise momentum. See Re-assessment (RA10).] Worth watching, not yet a red flag: the high ROE is partly a function of an unusually thin equity base (buybacks have shrunk shareholders' equity to ~$6.4bn against ~$4bn of TTM net income); V1's own valuation model flags that AMP's ROE would need to stay near current levels, not revert toward its 10-year median (30th percentile of own history), to fully justify the price (§7) — this is the central judgment call in this dossier.

dossiers.AMZN:
AMZN — Amazon.com, Inc.

1. Verdict

WATCH. Horizon 12–36 months. AWS is genuinely re-accelerating (37% YoY, an 18-quarter high) with a $496bn backlog growing triple-digit — the strongest "real demand, not just capex" signal in this batch — but it is being funded by capex so large ($220bn 2026 guide) that trailing free cash flow has turned negative on one commonly used measure, leverage has risen sharply, and the model's own quality factor score is the weakest of the four names reviewed. The 25-Sep-2026 close ($249.67) implies a 10-year revenue CAGR of ~14.9% versus an evidence-based base case of ~10.9%. [Corrected 2026-10-08: at the dossier's 12.5% discount rate; at a cost of equity of ~10.1% (5.17% Treasury + Blume beta ~1.2 x 4.14%) the required CAGR is ~12.4% and the base case is worth ~$218, 12.5% below the price: implied still above base]

2. Business in plain English

Amazon runs the largest US e-commerce marketplace (retail, third-party seller fees, advertising) and, through AWS, the largest cloud infrastructure business in the world, renting compute, storage and — increasingly — AI model access (Bedrock) and custom AI chips (Trainium) to enterprises. It makes money on razor-thin retail/logistics margins subsidized in large part by AWS's much higher-margin cloud and advertising businesses.

3. Why the model likes it — durability check

b1 composite 0.563 (decile 6, quintile 3, live_rank 218 — the model was neutral-to-mildly-positive, well outside its own top-30). The composite is carried entirely by Momentum (fam_M 0.754) and especially Earnings momentum (fam_S 0.991, the highest of any family score in this batch) — Amazon has beaten EPS estimates in all of the last 8 quarters with an average surprise of +50%. But Quality (fam_Q 0.136) is by far the weakest score of the four companies in this program, reflecting the capex-driven balance-sheet and cash-flow deterioration described in §6 below (heavy asset growth, rising leverage, and — depending on the measure — negative free cash flow are all negative inputs to the quality family). This is not an artefact: it is a real, current, disclosed condition of the business, not a modeling quirk.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly highlights, $bn GAAP)

Q2 2026 $200.6 +20% $42.2 +36.7% (fastest in 18 qtrs) 39% (+650bps YoY; +520bps ex-derivative gains) 14% (+2pp YoY)

AWS added $4.6bn of sequential revenue in Q2 2026 — about 80% more than its largest previous quarterly increase — and is now a $169bn annualized run-rate business [Investing.com transcript; TechTimes]. AWS backlog: $496bn, growing triple-digit YoY; a separate $225bn+ of Trainium revenue commitments is disclosed on top of that backlog [TechTimes, 2026-07-31; valueaddvc]. 2026 capex guidance was raised from ~$200bn to ~$220bn at the Q2 2026 call, explicitly attributed to higher memory costs, not to weaker-than-planned demand. Management (CEO Andy Jassy) stated Amazon still won't have enough capacity to meet 2026 demand, and expects the same to be true in 2027 [Fortune, 2026-07-30] — a demand-constrained framing, which is bullish for revenue durability but confirms the capex burden will not ease soon.

Of the four names, AMZN's base-case 3-year return (+7.2%) is the least unattractive on this framework — but the weak quality score and FCF ambiguity mean the margin-of-safety is genuinely lower than the headline valuation gap alone would suggest.

8. Bull case

  1. AWS's re-acceleration to an 18-quarter-high growth rate, with a $496bn backlog (growing triple-digit) plus $225bn of separate Trainium commitments, is real, dated, disclosed demand — not a hopeful extrapolation.
  2. AWS operating margin expanded 650bps YoY even while absorbing the AI capex ramp, showing the segment is not just growing but getting more profitable at the same time.
  3. Retail/advertising margin improvement (consolidated op margin +2pp YoY) provides a second, independent earnings lever besides AWS.

Bear case

  1. Quality-factor deterioration is the worst of any name in this program (fam_Q 0.136) — real, current, and driven by the same capex program that bulls point to as the growth driver, i.e., growth and quality-erosion are two sides of the same coin right now.
  2. FCF is ambiguous-to-negative on the most recent TTM data by at least one credible external measure, while long-term debt has roughly doubled in six months — a genuine, not hypothetical, capex burden.
  3. A separate FTC monopoly-power lawsuit (marketplace/pricing practices) is scheduled for a bench trial starting 9-Feb-2027 — later than earlier expected (originally Oct-2026) but a real, dated event risk to core retail-marketplace economics, distinct from and in addition to the $2.5bn Prime-enrollment settlement Amazon already paid [Bloomberg Law, MLex, 2026].

9. Key risks & kill criteria (thesis-invalidation triggers — signposts to watch)

  1. AWS revenue growth decelerates below 28% YoY for two consecutive quarters (would break the re-acceleration thesis).
  2. TTM free cash flow (reconciled, company-reported basis) remains negative for three consecutive quarters after 2026 capex guidance is met (i.e., the negative FCF print becomes structural, not a temporary supercycle).
  3. Long-term debt principal+interest exceeds $300bn without a corresponding step-up in AWS backlog. [Corrected 2026-10-08: this metric (contractual principal plus interest, $220.3bn at 30 Jun 2026) is estimated at roughly $280-290bn pro forma for the $25.0bn July USD notes and the September GBP notes, close to the trigger]
  4. 2026 capex guidance is raised a third time beyond $220bn.
  5. FTC monopoly-power case survives Amazon's motion to dismiss and proceeds toward the Feb-2027 trial with a scope that includes structural remedies.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-29 (per d4 snapshot). FTC v. Amazon monopoly-power bench trial: 9-Feb-2027 (quarterly status conferences precede it). No EU DMA-specific enforcement action against Amazon identified in this window beyond the general 2026 enforcement-plan framing (potential fines across Apple/Google/Meta/Amazon/Microsoft collectively exceeding €100bn, per Commission estimates, but no Amazon-specific decision dated).

11. Red-flag scan

1. Verdict

WATCH — 12–24 month thesis horizon. Execution and moat are exceptional (accelerating growth, 45%+ non-GAAP operating margins, net-cash balance sheet, four straight quarters of beat-and-raise), but the 25 Sep 2026 close ($206.55, mkt cap ≈$260.5bn) already prices in high-teens free-cash-flow growth sustained for a full decade — above this analyst's evidence-based base case. Two customers are >40% of revenue. Re-underwrite on a pullback that brings the implied growth to ≤15%/yr, or on evidence of customer diversification. [Corrected 2026-10-08: on the programme discount rate with SBC and interest income removed the implied growth is about 21-23%, still above base, and the price at which implied growth falls to 15% is about $120 per share (about $180 on the original inputs)]

2. Business in plain English

Arista sells high-performance networking switches and its EOS software (a single, modular network operating system across the whole product line) to hyperscale cloud, AI-cluster, enterprise campus and service-provider customers. It makes money selling hardware with high-margin embedded software/support, and increasingly selling AI-cluster "back-end" and "front-end" networking fabric to a small number of very large cloud/AI customers. Competitive position: the #2 data-center networking vendor after Cisco by most measures, with a reputation for software quality and reliability that has let it win share inside the largest hyperscalers' AI build-outs.

The valuation richness (low B/P) is real and is the central risk, not a data error.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 row exists for ANET; this analyst's own model)

No systematic V1 valuation exists for this name (v1_valuation_table.csv has no ANET row) — v1_verdict is null; this section is this dossier's own reverse DCF. - Inputs: EV = mkt cap $260.51bn − net cash $13.34bn = $247.17bn (2026-09-25 close, b1_live_scores.csv). TTM FCF $5.16bn. WACC 9.5% (rf≈4.3% + β-adjusted ERP, quality/net-cash balance sheet). Terminal growth 3.5%. [Corrected 2026-10-08: rf 4.3% is not the 10-year Treasury of 5.17% (25 Sep 2026); cost of equity is about 10.7% (5.17% + Blume beta ~1.3 x 4.14%) and the programme terminal rate is 3.0%] - Implied 10-year FCF CAGR: ~16.9% to justify the current EV under a standard 2-stage DCF (explicit 10y + Gordon terminal). [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 16.9% reproduces from the stated inputs, but FCF includes stock-based compensation added back ($502M TTM) and interest income on the cash that the EV bridge already subtracts ($434M TTM pre-tax); on FCF to the firm of about $4.30bn, at 10.7% and 3.0% terminal growth, the implied growth is about 23% (20% at 9.5%): still above the 14-15% base] - Bear case (customer concentration bites — one hyperscaler in-sources networking silicon or pauses capex; growth decelerates to high-single-digits within 2–3 years): ≈8–10% 10y FCF CAGR. - Base case (evidence-based): ≈14–15%. Current growth (30–38% YoY) is real, but a decade of 17%+ FCF growth would be historically rare for a company already at a $10.5bn TTM revenue run-rate; AI-cluster networking capex cycles are also known to be lumpy (hyperscaler capex budgets reset annually). - Bull case (AI-fabric share gains continue beyond front-end into back-end fabric, no customer losses): ≈20–22%. - Implied (16.9%) is above base case (~14–15%) → verdict WATCH, not INCLUDE, per program discipline: a great business priced for more growth than the evidence supports. - scenario_returns_3y (annualised, this analyst's estimate, not a formal model): bear ≈ −12%/yr (growth decelerates to ~5–8%/yr, NTM multiple compresses ~42x→25x); base ≈ +10%/yr (growth ~18–20%/yr near-term normalizing, multiple ~42x→35x); bull ≈ +29%/yr (growth stays 25–30%/yr, multiple flat-to-up).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) AI-cluster networking is a multi-year, structurally growing capex category and Arista's EOS software moat is winning share inside the largest hyperscalers; (2) net-cash balance sheet and 45%+ operating margins give enormous optionality with no leverage risk; (3) guidance has been beaten and raised for four straight quarters with growing magnitude, evidencing real demand visibility (backlog/bookings), not a one-time pull-forward. Bear: (1) two end customers were 26% and 16% of FY2025 revenue (10-K risk factors) — loss, delay or in-sourcing by either would move results materially; (2) Nvidia's Spectrum-X networking push and hyperscaler in-house silicon (e.g., custom ASIC switches at Meta/Microsoft/Amazon) are direct, well-funded competitive threats named in the company's own risk factors; (3) at the current price the market already requires ~17%/yr FCF growth for 10 years — a high bar that leaves little room for a normal cyclical air-pocket in AI capex.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Revenue from the two largest customers (26%/16% of FY2025 revenue) falls below 30% combined for two consecutive quarters without an offsetting new large customer disclosed (loss of concentration, but also loss of the visibility that supports the growth thesis) — reassess either way.
  2. YoY revenue growth decelerates below 15% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 27.5–37.7% over the last four) — the core "durable AI-networking growth" thesis is broken.
  3. Non-GAAP operating margin falls below 44% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 44.7–49.9% over the last four) [Corrected 2026-10-08: 44.7% is the GAAP operating margin of Q2'25 (non-GAAP 48.8%); only 49.9% (Q2'26 non-GAAP) is from the last four quarters in the cited release] — pricing power or mix eroding.
  4. Company guides below the prior quarter's actual revenue (a guidance cut in absolute terms, not just a deceleration in growth rate) — the beat-and-raise streak ends.
  5. Net cash position falls below $8bn without a value-accretive acquisition disclosed (unexplained cash burn or large buyback at a rich multiple).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-11-03 (estimated) based on the historical Q3 reporting cadence (Aug-4/May-5/Feb-12/Nov-4 pattern over the last five quarters); not yet confirmed by an 8-K or IR calendar entry as of 2026-09-25. No investor day announced in filings reviewed.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, no material weakness, no restatement, no going-concern language found in the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-17). Legal proceedings (10-K Item 3 / Note 5 Commitments and Contingencies): "provisions recorded for contingent losses... have not been significant"; no material pending litigation disclosed. Two-customer concentration (16%/26% of FY2025 revenue; two customers >10% each in each of the last three fiscal years) is confirmed directly from the 10-K and is the dossier's central red flag — carried through to kill criterion #1. No SEC/DOJ investigation found. Insider selling: not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed); flagged as a gap.

APD — Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. (NYSE: APD)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 24–36 month horizon. Core industrial-gas franchise is executing (guidance raised three consecutive quarters), but two large green-hydrogen impairments in five quarters ($2.33B pre-tax in FQ2 FY25; up to $2.9B pre-tax in FQ3 FY26) are a real capital-allocation red flag, and leverage has roughly doubled since FY22 to fund the now-partly-written-off megaproject program. [Corrected 2026-10-06: verdict restated to WATCH in Correction section DV04: guidance was raised twice in FY26 (FQ1 maintained), the FQ2 FY25 charge was $2,927.9M (not $2.33B, which is the operating loss) and a further ~$795M was charged in FQ4 FY25, and the EPS-based valuation test fails on free cash flow] Reservation: size small until management shows one full year without a fresh write-down.

2. Business in plain English

Air Products produces and sells industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon, helium) under long-term, often take-or-pay contracts to refining, chemicals, electronics, metals and food customers, plus builds and operates large "on-site" gasification and hydrogen plants. Revenue is largely contracted and cost-pass-through (energy costs), which smooths the base business; the volatility of the last two years comes from a separate, discretionary bet on multibillion-dollar clean-hydrogen megaprojects (Louisiana blue/green hydrogen, NEOM in Saudi Arabia) that the company is now scaling back. Competitive position: one of four global industrial-gas majors (with Linde, Air Liquide, Messer) in an oligopoly with high customer switching costs (on-site plants built next to the customer's fence line).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Quant factor scores (b1_live_scores.csv, 25 Sep 2026): quality/value composite decile 2 of 10 (i.e., statistically cheap-looking), but momentum is very weak (mom_12_1 percentile 6%) and the model's overall rank is 432/~500 — the triage flagged this as a "screen might be hiding a good business" case given the poor rank is driven almost entirely by price momentum, not by the underlying industrial-gas economics. That is partly an artefact: the stock's 12-month drawdown is a direct, rational market reaction to the impairments, not evidence the core business is broken — but the model's "cheap" P/E readings on trailing GAAP EPS are themselves distorted by the same impairments (GAAP EPS was negative in two of the last eight quarters), so neither the momentum penalty nor the naive value signal should be taken at face value.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Core industrial-gas oligopoly economics are intact — 25.6% core operating margin even in the write-off quarter, and guidance has been raised three times this fiscal year. [Corrected 2026-10-06: raised twice (FQ2, FQ3); FQ1 was maintained] 2. Capex is stepping down (FY26 guide cut to ~$3.5B from $4.0B) as the failed megaprojects are abandoned, which should improve free-cash-flow conversion from here. 3. NEOM/Yara renewable-ammonia marketing deal (announced 30 Jun 2026, being finalized) shows the company can still monetize part of the green-hydrogen build-out rather than a total loss.

dossiers.APO:
APO — Apollo Global Management, Inc. (F107, agent F107)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 24–36 months. Reservation: Apollo gated/capped a semi-liquid private-credit vehicle in June 2026 after redemption requests hit ~17% (offshore investors 12.5%, U.S. onshore ~4.3%), a real liquidity-stress signal in exactly the product category the March-2026 press coverage flagged — even though headline Fee Related Earnings (FRE) and Assets Under Management (AUM) growth remain excellent and a large GAAP net loss in Q1 2026 was a one-time Bermuda tax item, not an operating problem.

2. Business in plain English

Apollo Global Management is a two-engine business: (1) an alternative-asset manager running private credit, private equity and real assets funds for institutions and (increasingly) individual "wealth" investors, earning management and performance fees; and (2) Athene, a retirement-services/annuity insurer whose general account Apollo manages, earning a "spread" between what it credits policyholders and what its invested assets return. The combination lets Apollo originate large amounts of private credit and fund a captive, long-duration liability base (annuities) to hold much of it — a structurally different, more leveraged and more interest-rate/credit- spread-sensitive model than a pure fee-based asset manager (e.g., Blackstone's or KKR's fee businesses alone).

3. Why the model likes it / durability

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: 1. AXON's AI-matching engine keeps taking share of mobile and (newly) web/CTV ad budgets at ~83–85% Adjusted EBITDA margins with near-zero incremental capital — a rare combination of growth and cash generation. 2. Net debt is trivial (0.1x EBITDA) and the company is aggressively retiring shares with excess FCF (~$2.6bn bought back in FY2025 alone), directly boosting per-share value. 3. The SEC's data-practices probe into AXON is reported to have closed without enforcement action (Aug-2026 press reports) — if that holds, one of the two biggest overhangs (regulatory) is resolved, leaving only private litigation.

Bear: 1.
