Balance sheet is genuinely conservative: net cash position ex-leases, an undrawn $1.25B revolver through 2030, interest coverage of 38x EBIT/interest (TTM, ratios.py), and a 4.2% dividend yield backed by ~57-64% payout — a shareholder-yield floor while the turnaround plays out.

Bear case: 1. Leadership discontinuity at the worst possible time. CEO Corie Barry (7 years in the role) departs 2026-10-31 and CFO Matt Bilunas departs 2026-07-31 with an external CFO search still ongoing as of the 2026-09-25 cutoff — both transitions land inside the next two quarters, with a new, first-time CEO (Jason Bonfig) and possibly a new external CFO simultaneously executing a strategy pivot (Marketplace/Ads/Retail-media) neither has run before. BDX — Becton, Dickinson and Company — Diligence Dossier (Agent F73, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). One-sentence reason: a genuinely durable, diversified med-tech franchise now trading as standalone "New BD" post spin-off, with guidance raised in both quarters since the separation and cash generation ahead of plan — tempered by a live, unresolved FDA quality-system problem (repeat warning letters, potential ChloraPrep recall) and thin quality-of-earnings visibility in only two clean post-separation quarters. Thesis horizon: 24–36 months (let the standalone story re-rate once BD Excellence margin gains and the FDA remediation are proven, not assumed).

2. Business in plain English

BD makes the disposable and durable hardware hospitals and clinics use every day — needles and syringes, IV catheters and infusion pumps, medication-dispensing cabinets (Pyxis), patient monitors, and devices used in surgery, urology and interventional care, plus injection systems supplied to pharma/biotech customers (BioPharma Systems) for drugs like GLP-1s. It sells mostly to hospitals, ambulatory care and pharma manufacturers on razor/razor-blade economics (placed equipment, recurring consumables). Competitive position: #1 or #2 share in most of its categories (vascular access, infusion, specimen management, pharmaceutical delivery systems), which is also why its FDA quality-system record matters — its products touch nearly every hospital bed in the U.S.

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable

Gates: checked — no pending-deal exclusion, no volatility disqualifier, no V1 defective-input flag applies to BDX (no V1 row exists at all; see §7). 7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for BDX (outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json have no BDX entry) — v1_verdict is null, consistent with BDX being a triage-advanced (not top-70) name not yet run through V1. - NTM P/E (d4 snapshot, 2026-09-25): 13.8x (pe_ntm 13.84, pe_fy1 13.83) vs. FY26 adjusted-EPS guidance midpoint ~$12.67 and price $183.82. FCF yield ~8.9% on the (overstated) trailing FCF figure; on the normalised ~$2.2–2.3B New BD FCF run-rate, FCF yield is closer to 4.3–4.6% of the $50.1B market cap — a more honest number, and materially less "cheap" than the headline aggregator FCF yield implies. - Historical/peer context (qualitative — no D2/D3 own-history series exists yet for "New BD" as a distinct entity since it only started trading in this form Feb 2026): pre-spin BDX historically traded 15–20x forward EPS; med-tech large-cap peers (Zimmer Biomet, Stryker, Boston Scientific, Stryker/Becton peer set) trade roughly 14–22x forward earnings depending on growth profile. At 13.8x, New BD is priced at a discount to the peer group, which is consistent with (a) genuine post-spin index/investor-base churn and thin trading history, and (b) the market pricing in the unresolved FDA quality-system risk (§11). - Reverse DCF (own build, 10-year explicit + Gordon terminal, WACC 7.5–8.0%, terminal growth 3.0%): using the [Corrected 2026-10-06: method corrected below: 5.6-7.0% reproduces only with levered FCF (incl. SBC add-back) divided into EV and an unstated risk-free/ERP; restated implied growth about 7.4% (range 6.3-7.6%)] normalised New-BD FCF run-rate (~$2.3B) against the current enterprise value (~$64.9B), the market is pricing in a 10-year FCF/earnings CAGR of roughly 5.6–7.0%. 8. Bull case and bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. BD Excellence cost program continues to expand adjusted operating margin (10.5%→13.3%→15.6%+ quarterly progression [Corrected 2026-10-06: continuing-ops GAAP operating margin was 10.4% (Q1), 2.0% (Q2, after the 450M impairment), 13.3% (Q3); 15.6% is the Q3 FY25 GAAP margin, not an FY26 or adjusted figure, so there is no 10.5%-13.3%-15.6% progression] in FY26 even through a loss-making impairment quarter suggests underlying margin trajectory is intact). 2. Standalone "New BD" re-rates toward peer med-tech multiples (16–20x) as trading history lengthens and index inclusion/ownership normalises post-spin, without needing any upgrade to the growth outlook. 3. BioPharma Systems (prefillable syringes/injection pens for GLP-1s and biologics) is a genuine structural volume-growth tailwind tied to obesity-drug demand, largely outside BD's control but a real multi-year tailwind.

Bear (3 points): 1. The FDA quality-system problems are not resolved, not one-off, and touch multiple facilities/product lines (§11) — a further Warning Letter, an actual ChloraPrep recall, or a consent-decree expansion would directly cut into the Medical Essentials/Connected Care franchise the model likes. 2. Only two clean post-spin quarters exist; "New BD" stand-alone cost allocation, TSA income roll-off (as corporate overhead currently borne by Waters via TSA unwinds), and dis-synergies are not yet stress-tested by a full fiscal year. 3. Hernia-mesh and other product-liability litigation (~7,000 pending claims even after the FY24 settlement) is a recurring cash drag ($52–63M pre-tax legal charges in a single quarter) that could re-escalate.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. A new FDA Warning Letter, Form 483, or consent-decree expansion covering any BD manufacturing site within the next 4 quarters.
  2. Full-year FY26 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut (vs. the current $12.62–$12.72 range) at any future quarterly release.
  3. Organic/reported revenue growth falls below the "low single-digit" floor of guidance for two consecutive quarters.
  4. Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 3.0x (from ~2.1x currently), signalling debt-funded buybacks outrunning [Corrected 2026-10-06: kill criterion 4 starts from a wrong base: the corrected ratio is already about 3.0x adjusted / 4.0x GAAP, so the 3.0x trigger must be re-based] deleveraging.
  5. Any voluntary or FDA-mandated recall of a top-5-revenue product line (e.g., BD Alaris, Pyxis, ChloraPrep, or a BioPharma Systems platform).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-11-05 (Q4/full-year FY26 results, first full annual report as standalone New BD).
  • FDA response/resolution timeline on the El Paso Warning Letter and San Diego Dispensing Warning Letter — no fixed date disclosed; company says it is "preparing a comprehensive response."
  • TSA (transition services agreement) with Waters unwinds over time — watch for standalone cost-structure normalising in FY27 guidance.

11. Red-flag scan

  • FDA quality-system issues, ongoing and multi-site: CareFusion 303 (Pyxis dispensing) received a Form 483 in May 2024 and a Warning Letter in November 2024 (San Diego facility, Dispensing quality-management system); BD is also operating under a pre-existing Infusion-systems Consent Decree (Alaris pumps). Separately, an El Paso Warning Letter (drug/combination products) is unresolved as of the Q2 FY26 10-Q, with the company stating potential outcomes could include "additional corrections and corrective actions, including potential product recalls"; BD has voluntarily paused/adjusted its ChloraPrep product line pending resolution as of May 6, 2026. This directly confirms and sharpens the triage's "history of FDA warning letters" flag — it is not purely historical, it is live. [10-Q filed 2026-05-07, Legal Proceedings/Regulatory Matters notes]
  • Litigation: ~6,995 pending hernia-mesh product-liability claims as of March 31, 2026 (down slightly from 6,905 [Corrected 2026-10-06: stale: 10-Q for 30 Jun 2026 states approximately 7,090 claims (6,905 at 30 Sep 2025)] at Sep 30, 2025 — note the count is not obviously declining despite the FY24 settlement, since new claims continue to be filed); other mass-tort matters referenced but not separately quantified in the extract reviewed.
  • Auditor/accounting: no restatements, no material-weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed 10-Qs.
  • Insider selling / Form 4 pattern: not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as a gap, not a finding.
  • No pending M&A beyond the completed Waters spin-off/combination.

BE - Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE) - diligence dossier (agent F161, wave 8)

Verdict: WATCH. A genuine AI-data-center power winner, but the 25 Sep 2026 close ($288.70) already discounts roughly 31% a year of free-cash-flow growth for ten years; my evidence-based base case is about 19%. Thesis horizon 12-36 months. Condition to upgrade: price near or below roughly $190 (base-case value), or backlog conversion and cash flow clearly beating the guidance ladder without further customer-equity giveaways. Triage (Q09, advance=false) is confirmed, not overturned.

1. Business in plain English

Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel-cell "Energy Servers" that run on natural gas (or biogas, hydrogen) and generate electricity on site without combustion. Customers are now mostly AI data-center operators and hyperscalers who cannot wait for grid connections, plus industrial and utility buyers. Revenue is product sales (about 88% of Q2'26 revenue), installation, 5-20 year service contracts (terminable annually for convenience) and a shrinking electricity-sales line. The moat is proprietary stack technology, US manufacturing scale and speed-to-power; the weak spot is extreme customer concentration.

2. Why the model likes it, and is that durable

b1/d4 context: quality family strong on gross profit/assets (0.155) and growth (asset growth 79%, revenue +165% YoY in the Q2'26 10-Q); value/price momentum drive the rest (12-1 momentum +144%). b1 ROE is 0.8% (d4/Yahoo shows 22%, a data conflict from trailing-period timing) and the model's value family is weak. The score is momentum-and-growth driven, not cheapness: d4 shows P/E 106x FY26 and 58.6x FY27 consensus, FCF yield 0.6%, and a Street mean target of $280 (below price). Durable only if the order book converts; the cyclical/one-off risk is an AI-capex pause.

BF-B — Brown-Forman Corporation

1. Verdict

WATCH — 24–48 month horizon. Valuation has already de-rated to reflect the volume malaise, but management's own fiscal-2027 guidance is for organic operating income to decline (not just flat sales); buying ahead of a company-guided earnings decline is not disciplined, even at a reasonable multiple. Re-underwrite on evidence of a turn (see kill criteria).

2. Business in plain English

Brown-Forman owns Jack Daniel's, Woodford Reserve, Old Forester, Herradura and other spirits brands, sold worldwide mostly through third-party distributors/retailers with high gross margins (~60%) driven by brand strength and pricing power rather than volume growth. It is family-controlled (Brown family, dual-class B shares), a long-standing dividend grower ("dividend aristocrat"), with concentrated exposure to US whiskey and, increasingly, to trade-policy and consumer-moderation headwinds.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

b1 factor data (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as-of 2026-09-25): decile 8/10, quintile 4/5; strong quality/profitability (gp_a percentile 41st but roe percentile 50th, ep percentile 78th cheap-on-earnings), and notably weak recent price momentum (mom_12_1 percentile 27th) — consistent with a stock that has been sold off. Triage's own red flags are accurate and current: "US spirits category volume malaise (moderation/GLP-1 headwind)" and "tariff exposure on American whiskey exports to Canada/EU." These are not durable "moat" reasons for the quant score — the model likes it on value/quality factors precisely because the market has already priced in real, ongoing damage; the open question is whether the damage is cyclical (destocking, one-off tariff shock) or a structural volume decline that will keep pushing the "fair" multiple down.

1. Verdict

WATCH (thesis horizon 12-36 months). The quick triage (consolidated figures) said "no" for the wrong reason (it quoted 5.2x net debt/EBITDA and -30.9% FCF yield; neither reproduces from the 10-Q, see section 6). The business is good and 2026 earnings are rising, but at $109 the stock already prices roughly 5% a year of free-cash-flow-per-share growth for ten years against my base case of about 3%, and cash flow is negative. Condition to upgrade: a price near or below $90 (my base-case DCF is about $94), or two more quarters of positive trailing free cash flow with adjusted EPS holding at or above $9.

2. Business in plain English

Bunge buys soybeans, wheat, corn and oilseeds from farmers, crushes and refines them into meal, vegetable oils and flour, and ships grain worldwide; it earns a margin per tonne handled and processed, plus trading gains. The July 2025 merger with Viterra roughly doubled its grain origination and shipping network (Q2 2026 net sales $24.0B versus $12.8B a year earlier, with diluted shares up from 136M to 195M). Its edge is scale and logistics in a thin-margin, commodity business; returns swing with crush margins, biofuel policy and trade flows.

3. Why the model likes it (b1, d4)

b1 shows a low price-to-earnings (earnings-yield and value percentiles high) and strong recent surprise. The price-to-earnings is cheap only because the multiple is applied to a raised, mid-merger earnings base; the value reading ignores that trailing free cash flow is negative. Durable part: more earnings power after Viterra. Artefact part: crush margins in 2026 are described by the company as "improving market conditions", i.e. cyclical.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Horizon: 18–36 months. One-sentence reason: Leqembi (Alzheimer's) and the newly acquired Apellis geographic-atrophy franchise are real, growing revenue streams that should let earnings snap back sharply once $5.6bn of debt-funded M&A integration costs roll off [Corrected 2026-10-06: the Apellis consideration was $5,410.1M (10-Q acquisition note), funded mainly from cash and marketable securities; new debt was a $2.0bn term loan plus a $400M revolver draw that was repaid in June. What rolls off is deal, restructuring and acquired-IPR&D cost, not 'debt-funded' cost], but the balance sheet is now meaningfully more levered and H1 2026 GAAP earnings collapsed, so this is not a full-weight position until the post-merger run-rate is proven for 2–3 quarters.

2. Business in plain English

Biogen is a neuroscience/immunology biotech. Its legacy multiple-sclerosis (MS) franchise (Tecfidera, Tysabri, Vumerity, Spinraza) [Corrected 2026-10-06: Spinraza (SMA) is in Biogen's rare-disease line and Vumerity is in its Growth Portfolio; the company's 'Legacy MS Portfolio' is AVONEX, PLEGRIDY, TECFIDERA and TYSABRI, $767M in Q2 2026 (Ex-99.1 0000875045-26-000073)] is in secular volume/price decline as it faces generics and newer competitors. Growth now comes from Leqembi (lecanemab, Alzheimer's, co-marketed with Eisai) and, since May 2026, from Apellis Pharmaceuticals' pegcetacoplan franchise (Syfovre for geographic atrophy, Empaveli), acquired for ~$5.6bn. It also earns royalties (Spinraza/Zurzuvae economics) [Corrected 2026-10-06: royalty-type income is mainly anti-CD20 (OCREVUS) revenue of $514M in Q2 2026; Spinraza and Zurzuvae are product sales, Zurzuvae shared with Supernus] and sells rare-disease drugs. Customers are neurologists, ophthalmologists and health systems; reimbursement runs through Medicare Part B/D and commercial payers.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Q06 triage flagged +194% forward EPS growth (Leqembi ramp + restructuring) and a +55% trailing run, with the Street seeing only ~5% further upside — hence "full diligence" was ordered. That EPS-growth read is now partly an artefact: much of the 2026 forward-EPS jump is a base-effect bounce off the H1 2026 M&A-cost trough (see §4), not pure operating leverage. The durable piece is Leqembi's volume ramp (+74% YoY global in-market sales in Q1 2026 per company release) [Corrected 2026-10-06: stale: the Q2 2026 release (0000875045-26-000073, 29 Jul 2026) reports LEQEMBI global in-market sales of $184M, up only 15% YoY (U.S. $97M), after $168M and +74% in Q1; the +74% is not the current growth rate] and pegcetacoplan's growing GA market share — both real, IP-protected franchises with limited near-term generic risk.

BKNG — Booking Holdings Inc. — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — 24–36 month horizon. The world's largest online travel agent is statistically as cheap versus its own history as it has ever been, operating income has grown in every comparable quarter for four years, and leverage on a cash-flow basis is very low. I agree with V1's directional "attractive" call. Named reservation: V1's +39.3%/yr "base case" is not a credible base case — it depends on the NTM P/E more than doubling (13.8x→30.1x), an assumption management's own guidance does not support — so size this as attractive-but-not-39%/yr-attractive, and be aware of two unresolved items: a rapidly deepening negative-equity/rising-debt position, and a live EU regulatory/litigation overhang.

2. Business in plain English

Booking Holdings is an online travel agent (Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak, OpenTable) that connects travelers with hotels, alternative accommodations, rental cars and flights, earning a commission (agency model) or a margin on room revenue it collects and remits (merchant model — now ~73% of gross bookings, +4pts YoY). It makes money on the volume of "room nights" booked and the take rate per booking, funded by heavy performance-marketing spend to acquire direct and paid traffic. Its competitive position is the largest global OTA by gross bookings, competing chiefly with Expedia, Airbnb, and direct hotel-chain booking channels, with Booking.com itself now designated an EU "gatekeeper" platform.

Note on share count/EPS: Booking Holdings executed a 25-for-1 forward stock split effective April 2, 2026 (record date 2026-03-06; traded split-adjusted from 2026-04-06). All EPS and share-count figures below are presented on a split-adjusted basis for comparability; pre-split GAAP releases (e.g., Q2 2025's originally-reported $27.43 EPS) are divided by 25 throughout ($27.43⁄25=$1.10, matching the figure below).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

B1 ranks BKNG #63 (composite 87.3rd percentile) on strong Value (earnings yield 87.3rd percentile, book/price 78.6th, EBIT/EV 91.6th) and reasonable Quality, with weak recent Momentum (50.6th percentile, unremarkable) and weak Earnings-momentum/SUE (11.3rd percentile — the SUE-based earnings-momentum factor is actually a negative contributor, worth noting since it cuts against the "attractive" quant read). The value read is durable, not an artefact: it is confirmed independently in this review — Q2 2026 room nights +5%, gross bookings +9% reported, operating income growth positive in every comparable quarter since 2022 (Q1: $450M→$791M→$1,062M→$1,271M; Q3: $3,103M→$3,179M→$3,483M) — this is a genuinely cheap multiple on a genuinely still-growing business, not a statistical illusion.

7. Valuation snapshot — reconciliation with V1 (task explicitly asks to scrutinise this)

V1 verdict: attractive (score +0.993 — among the highest in the entire ~500-name universe). NTM P/E 13.8x — 1.1st percentile of its own ~14.75-year history (essentially the cheapest it has ever traded) and roughly in line with a peer median of 13.1x (peer set ABNB, CCL, EXPE, HLT and others — note CCL is a cruise operator with a very different capital/risk profile; peer comparability is imperfect). Implied 10-year growth from the current price is only +2.3% (i.e. the price itself does not require much growth), but V1's bear/base/bull 3-year annualised returns are +11.3% / +39.3% / +86.4% — even the bear case is positive, reflecting how cheap the starting point is. I do not accept V1's +39.3%/yr figure as a credible "base case." Decomposing the scenario: revenue growth assumed 16.8%/yr, and the NTM P/E exit multiple assumed to expand from 13.8x to 30.1x — more than doubling — by year 3. That multiple-expansion assumption, not fundamentals, is doing most of the work: management's own FY2026 guidance (high-single-digit bookings/room-nights/revenue, low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth) implies something like 10–15%/yr EPS growth with a flat multiple, not 39%/yr. The model's base-case fair value ($443.57) is 47% above the single highest Wall Street 12-month price target ($301) — a useful sanity check that the "base" is really more like this model's bull case. My view: the stock is genuinely, statistically cheap (1.1st percentile of own history is a real, checkable signal) and the business is executing (bookings/room-nights growth, raised guidance, very low cash leverage) — I agree with "attractive" as a direction. But I would treat V1's 39.3%/yr as the upside case, and underwrite a realistic base case closer to high-teens-to-low-20s%/yr (management's own EPS growth guidance plus a partial, not total, re-rating), which is still an attractive risk/reward but materially different position-sizing math than 39%/yr compounded for three years. 8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: 1. 13.8x NTM P/E is at roughly the 1st percentile of BKNG's own trading history; Q2 2026 room nights +5%, gross bookings +9% reported (+8% cc), FY2026 guidance just raised to high-single-digit growth plus low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth. 2. Net debt/EBITDA ≈0.3x despite deeply negative book equity — ample capacity funding a rapidly growing capital-return program (H1 2026 buybacks +112% YoY, $14.5bn authorization remaining) that mechanically compresses share count. 3. Operating income has grown in every comparable quarter for four years — the core marketplace economics are intact regardless of GAAP net-income noise below the operating line.

Bear: 1. V1's +39.3%/yr "base case" requires the NTM multiple to more than double (13.8x→30.1x) — management's own guidance does not support anything close to that without a multiple re-rating; the base-case fair value already exceeds the Street's highest 12-month target by 47%. 2. Shareholders' equity is deeply and rapidly more negative (−$10.78bn, −$4.67bn in the last four quarters) funded partly by fresh debt (+$2.975bn raised in H1 2026 alone, total debt +9.2% YoY) — low leverage today, but a capital-markets-dependent model. 3. GAAP net income fell sharply in Q1 2025 (−57%) and Q2 2025 (−41%) for reasons not fully isolated in this review, making 2026's headline GAAP growth rates partly a base-effect artefact; separately, the EU Digital Markets Act "gatekeeper" obligations (parity-clause restrictions) took effect November 2024 and remain a live overhang — the European Parliament in April 2026 pressed the Commission to open a formal non-compliance investigation, Italy's AGCM opened its own April 2026 consumer-protection inquiry, and a hotel-industry class action (potentially up to ~18,000 European hotels) is seeking billions in damages for 2004–2024 parity-clause conduct.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Room-night or gross-bookings growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters (currently +5% / +9%).
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (currently ≈0.30x). [Corrected 2026-10-06: criterion restated to gross debt / TTM adjusted EBITDA above 2.5x (1.95x now) because net debt nets customer funds against debt; 1.5x on the net measure would not trigger until debt rose by about $12bn.]
  3. FY2026 guidance (high-single-digit volume/bookings/revenue, low-to-mid-teens adjusted EPS growth) is cut.
  4. The European Commission opens a formal DMA non-compliance proceeding against Booking.com, or the EU hotel class action produces a disclosed material damages award/settlement.
  5. Quarterly buyback spend falls by more than 50% quarter-over-quarter without a stated capital-return-policy reason — a signal management itself sees less value at the prevailing price.

BlackRock, Inc. (BLK) — Diligence Dossier (F22, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 24–36 months (per this dossier's own §7 reverse DCF and §4 quarterly filings, not a data-provider figure). One-sentence reason: the world's largest, most durable asset-management franchise is compounding fee earnings at a rate the current price does not fully require, but roughly 30% of headline growth is acquisition-driven (GIP/HPS/Preqin, per §3/Q2-26 8-K) and GAAP EPS has been distorted by non-cash contingent-consideration marks (§4, Q1-26 10-Q), so full weight is not warranted until organic, adjusted growth is cleanly separable for another 2–4 quarters.

Thesis (≤25 words): As of the 2026-09-25 close, the world's #1 asset manager (iShares, Aladdin, and newly acquired private-markets platforms per Q2-26 8-K) growing AUM 20%+ a year (§4), priced at a market-average multiple (§7).

2. Business in plain English

Per its Q2 2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-30) and 8-K earnings release, BlackRock manages $15.3tn of client assets (index funds/ETFs via iShares, active strategies, and now private markets) for a fee, plus licenses its Aladdin risk-management/data platform to other institutions. It earns a percentage of assets under management (AUM), so revenue scales with markets and net client inflows; it does not take principal risk on client money. Competitive position (as characterized in the FY2025 10-K and Q2-26 8-K, filed 2026-02-25 and 2026-07-15 respectively): #1 global AUM, #1 ETF platform (iShares), and a quasi-operating-system moat in Aladdin used by hundreds of institutions including some competitors.

b1 factor data (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as_of 2026-09-25): Quality 5, Growth 4, price_vs_growth 4; factor composite driven by quality (gp/assets, ROE, low accruals) and growth (54% forward EPS growth cited in v4/outputs/Q04_triage.json). 1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months

A genuinely improving, well-diversified growth portfolio and a deleveraging balance sheet are real, but the "statistically cheap" framing overstates the case: BMS's own 10-Q attributes a $1.4bn H1-2026 operating-cash-flow decline directly to the Eliquis Medicare price cut even as headline Eliquis revenue keeps growing, FY2025 non-GAAP EPS actually missed the company's own most-recently-reissued guidance range once a fourth-quarter M&A charge landed, and a reverse-DCF shows the current price already assumes roughly flat-to-declining free cash flow in perpetuity — i.e., the market is pricing this as a melting-ice-cube income stock, not an undiscovered bargain. Own it for the covered, growing dividend and multi-year LOE-defense optionality; do not size it as a high-conviction compounder. [Corrected 2026-10-06: verdict is now WATCH. On a levered-FCF basis with a 9.0% cost of equity (10-year Treasury 5.17% + 0.8 x 4.8%), SBC deducted and business-development cash included, the price of $62.86 is above the base-case value ($42-62, central about $50) and the 3-year base return is +3.8% a year, below the 5.17% Treasury. See Re-assessment (RA10).]

2. Business in plain English

Bristol-Myers Squibb is a global biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops and sells prescription medicines, mainly in oncology, hematology, cardiovascular disease, immunology and neuroscience, to patients via physicians, hospitals, pharmacies and payers (Medicare/Medicaid, commercial insurers, and international health systems). It earns money by selling patent-protected branded drugs at a large gross margin (~71% GAAP) while losing that margin rapidly once patents/exclusivity expire and generics enter. Its historically dominant products — the anticoagulant Eliquis and the multiple-myeloma drug Revlimid — are both now past peak and in structural decline (Revlimid) or newly subject to U.S. government price-setting (Eliquis), while a second wave of newer drugs (Opdivo/Opdivo Qvantig, Breyanzi, Reblozyl, Camzyos, Opdualag, Cobenfy, Krazati) is scaling to replace that lost revenue. Competitive position: top-5 global oncology/immunology franchise with real depth (not a single-product story), but facing the same IRA Medicare price-negotiation and patent-cliff dynamics as every large-cap innovator.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Quant snapshot (d4_live_snapshot.parquet, 2026-09-25): composite 0.842 (rank 9/503); Q 0.791, V 0.860, M 0.876 (sector-relative percentiles). - V (0.860, "statistically cheap"): confirmed directionally — trailing P/E ≈13.9x and NTM P/E ≈9.4-9.6x are well below the ~17.8x healthcare-sector average forward P/E (general market context, Sept 2026) and below the sector playbook's own 10–16x "core EPS" range for developed-market innovator pharma. But valuation.py's reverse-DCF on TTM FCF ($11.44bn) at a 7.5% WACC shows the current EV already implies ≈‑0.3% FCF growth for 10 years fading to 1% — the market is not underpricing growth, it is pricing BMS as a flat-to-shrinking cash cow. Cheap-on-a-ratio and cheap-on-a-DCF are different claims; only the first is clearly true here. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the -0.3% implied growth paired a 7.5% enterprise WACC with a levered FCF (OCF after interest) and an EV, and used FCF that adds back SBC ($553m) and excludes business-development cash ($3,944m of business acquisitions in FY2025). On equity value $128.4bn, FCF less SBC less $2.0bn of normalised business development ($8.89bn) and a 9.0% cost of equity, the implied 10-year growth is +2.4% (+0.5% at 8.0%, +4.2% at 10.0%); on FY2026E cash flow it is higher. See Re-assessment (RA10).] - Q (0.791) — the ROE question the brief flagged: TTM ROE (computed via ratios.py) is 43.3% (FY2025 36.7%), close to the prelim snapshot's 41.6%. DuPont (3-step) shows this is not primarily a margin or efficiency story: net margin 13.2%→17.9% and asset turnover ~0.53x→0.55x are both unremarkable; the equity multiplier is 5.25x–4.36x (average assets ÷ average equity) and the tool's own 5-step DuPont flags "largest move: interest/tax burden, financing-driven" as the dominant swing factor. Mechanically, BMS's tangible book value is negative in every period tested (avg tangible equity −$19.6bn TTM; tangible BVPS −$8.21) — goodwill ($21.7bn) plus acquired intangibles ($17.4–23.3bn) exceed total equity, a direct legacy of debt/stock-funded M&A (Celgene 2019, then Karuna/RayzeBio/Mirati in 2024) that also produced a $43.6bn treasury-stock balance shrinking the equity base. Current-period buybacks are zero (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock = $0 every quarter, FY2024–FY2026 YTD, per XBRL) — so the high ROE is not being freshly manufactured by today's capital allocation; it is a structural artefact of a thin/negative tangible-equity base plus a real (but partly base-effect) margin recovery as the 2024 mega-impairment year rolls off. 6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • OCF/FCF — the clearest adverse fact in this file: FY2025 OCF $14.156bn vs FY2024 $15.190bn (−6.8%, 10-K MD&A: "higher GTN [gross-to-net] payments"). It has worsened materially since: H1 2026 OCF $4.497bn vs H1 2025 $5.871bn (−23.4%, −$1.4bn), and the Q2 2026 10-Q states plainly: "The $1.4 billion decrease in cash provided by operating activities compared to 2025 was driven by lower net customer receipts, primarily due to a list price reduction for Eliquis, partially offset by lower expenses due to the ongoing strategic productivity initiative." TTM FCF is $11.44bn vs a prior-TTM $14.58bn (−21.5%). This is BMS's own quantification that the Eliquis IRA Medicare price cut (see below) is landing at the cash-flow line even while headline Eliquis revenue is still growing — a real tension the market does not appear to be pricing separately from the revenue growth.
  • Eliquis IRA Maximum Fair Price (verified against CMS's primary published price list): effective 2026-01-01, CMS's negotiated Medicare Part D price is $231/30-day supply vs a 2023 list price of $521 (a 56% discount) (CMS, "Negotiated Prices for Initial Price Applicability Year 2026," Aug 2024). Despite this, reported Eliquis WW revenue grew +16% YoY (Q1'26) and +22% YoY (Q2'26), and FY2026 Eliquis growth guidance was raised from 10–15% to 20–25%. BMS's press releases attribute this only to generic "demand" and do not publish a volume/price bridge. Both things are simultaneously true and both are primary-sourced: revenue is growing, and BMS's own 10-Q says the Eliquis price cut is the primary driver of a $1.4bn cash-flow decline. This is a watch item, not a resolved question — gross-to-net/rebate accounting can lag, and a reader relying only on the revenue line would miss the cash-flow deterioration entirely.
  • GAAP vs. non-GAAP gap and its drivers: the gap is large and volatile — driven mainly by (i) Amortization of acquired intangibles ($3.3bn FY25, $8.9bn FY24 — declining as Revlimid-related intangibles fully amortize) and (ii) Acquired IPR&D charges, which BMS's non-GAAP explicitly does NOT exclude ("GAAP and non-GAAP EPS include the impacts of Acquired IPRD charges and licensing income," repeated in every release) — a genuine mitigant vs. peers who strip M&A charges from non-GAAP entirely.   • SBC: $553M FY2025 / ~$562M annualized (H1'26 ×2) ≈ 1.1–1.2% of revenue — low, not a dilution concern.
  • Restructuring/impairment quantification (angle 6): 2023 Restructuring Plan — total expected charges ~$2.5bn through 2027, of which $1.8bn incurred to date (through Q2 2026 10-Q, Note 6); separately, a ~$2.0bn cost-savings target by end-2027 is stated but no cumulative realized-savings figure is disclosed (flagged as not available). Acquired-IPRD/impairment charges on acquired pipeline assets (Mirati/RayzeBio/Karuna-era): FY2024 $13.4bn, FY2025 $3.7bn (Orbital), Q2 2025 alone $1.5bn — both GAAP and non-GAAP, per company definition.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Growth Portfolio is real and broad-based, not one drug: Breyanzi +82% FY25, Camzyos +77%, Reblozyl +31%, Opdualag +28%, Opdivo Qvantig (subcutaneous, LOE-defense reformulation) scaled from ~$0 to $238M FY2025 in one year — this is genuine multi-product execution, not a single bet. (2) Balance sheet is genuinely deleveraging (LT debt −$7.5bn since FY2023) while still funding a growing, well-covered dividend (4% yield, 17 consecutive annual increases). (3) Despite a 56% Medicare price cut taking effect Jan 2026, Eliquis revenue is still growing double digits and FY2026 growth guidance was raised, not cut — the single biggest headline policy risk has not (yet) broken the franchise. Bear: (1) FY2025 non-GAAP EPS missed BMS's own most-recently-reissued guidance range once a Q4 M&A charge landed — the guidance "raises" investors cite structurally exclude the next dilutive deal, which recurred once already. (2) OCF is down 23% H1-over-H1 and BMS's own 10-Q says this is "primarily" the Eliquis price cut — a real, quantified, ongoing cash-flow headwind that the revenue-growth headline obscures. (3) The single largest near-term de-risking catalyst for the growth portfolio's terminal narrative — Cobenfy's Phase 3 ADEPT-2 readout in Alzheimer's-disease psychosis — has been delayed from a planned H2 2026 readout to "beginning early 2027" after the company disclosed clinical-trial-execution irregularities at a small number of sites and re-opened enrollment (BMS press release, 2025-12-03; corroborated by trade press).

1. Verdict

2. Business in plain English

BNY is the world's largest custody/asset-servicing bank: it holds, settles, values and finances securities for asset managers, pension funds, insurers and broker-dealers (Pershing platform), and also runs a large treasury/markets book on the interest-bearing balance sheet. It earns fee income tied to assets under custody/administration (AUC/A ~$60T) plus net interest income, so results move with market levels, asset flows, and interest rates rather than with a single product cycle. Competitive position: one of only three global scale custodians (with State Street and JPMorgan), with high switching costs once a client's securities master file is on the platform.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — thesis horizon 12–36 months. A ~90%-recurring-revenue processor of proxy voting, mutual-fund/annual-meeting communications and multi-asset trading/post-trade technology, compounding recurring revenue at high-single digits and adjusted EPS at low-double digits for a decade, trading at 15.2x NTM P/E and a 6.3% FCF yield — a valuation that (on a conservative reverse DCF) prices in only ~2.9%/year 10-year FCF growth against a company that has never grown FCF that slowly and has just guided to another year of 6–8% recurring-revenue / 8–12% adjusted-EPS growth. Four straight quarters of raised guidance in FY2026, a clean balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA ≈1.7x), and a 14th double-digit dividend increase in 15 years support the quantitative "cheap growth compounder" read from the triage. The reservation that keeps this from a larger weighting: BR's own recurring-revenue growth is itself decelerating on a multi-year view (FY24 +6.6%, FY25 +5.9%, FY26 +8% cc — noisy, not a clean trend) and a portion of FY2026's growth and cash flow was flattered by non-recurring digital-asset mark-to-market gains that will not repeat every year. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the digital-asset gain did not flatter cash flow: the FY2026 cash-flow statement deducts 'Digital assets change in fair market value (231.4)' from operating cash flow, so free cash flow is unaffected. It flattered GAAP net income only. See Re-assessment (RA6).]

2. Business in plain English

Broadridge is the plumbing behind shareholder democracy and a large piece of the back office of Wall Street. When a public company or mutual fund needs to send proxy materials and collect votes from millions of retail and institutional shareholders, Broadridge does it — its ProxyEdge platform handles the vote processing for the large majority of US institutional share volume. That is the Investor Communication Solutions (ICS) segment ($5,561m of FY2026's $7,477m revenue, 74%). The Global Technology and Operations (GTO) segment ($1,916m, 26%) sells outsourced technology and operations platforms — trading, clearing, wealth/investment-management middle- and back-office systems — to banks and broker-dealers, recently expanded via the CQG acquisition (multi-asset futures/options execution and connectivity, completed 1 May 2026) into global futures/options trading infrastructure. Both businesses monetize on long-term, multi-year contracts with high switching costs (a bank does not re-platform its clearing operations casually), which is the source of the ~90%+ recurring-revenue mix.

3. Why the model likes it — and is it durable?

B1 composite is upper-mid (live_rank 223/~2,300, decile 6, quintile 3; composite 0.553). Durability check: the value signal is corroborated by four consecutive quarters of guidance raises through FY2026 (see §5) built on real, filed-and-verified operating results (recurring revenue growth, closed sales, adjusted margin), not an accounting artefact. The weak momentum is the honest counterweight — the market has not yet rewarded the beat-and-raise pattern, which is exactly the "genuine mispricing" the triage flagged. dossiers.BRO:
BRO — Brown & Brown, Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F40, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), reservation stated explicitly: organic revenue growth just turned negative (Q2-26: −0.7%) after decelerating for five straight quarters [Corrected 2026-10-06: organic growth was already -2.8% in Q4 2025 (flat in Q1 2026, -0.7% in Q2 2026), so it turned negative in Q4 2025], and leverage roughly tripled to fund the Accession deal. Valuation is not demanding, but the growth thesis triage relied on ("32% revenue growth, 54% EPS growth") does not survive a GAAP/organic check. Horizon: 12–24 months; revisit for full weight once organic growth re-stabilises at ≥3%.

2. Business in plain English

Brown & Brown is an insurance broker/wholesaler — it doesn't take underwriting risk, it earns commissions and fees placing property-casualty, employee-benefits and specialty (E&S) insurance for businesses and individuals through four segments (Retail, Programs, Wholesale Brokerage/Specialty Distribution, and now the newly-acquired Accession/National Programs businesses). It grows by winning new accounts, raising rates/exposure with existing clients ("organic"), and buying smaller brokers ("bolt-on M&A") — plus, since August 2025, one very large acquisition.

3. Why the model likes it — and why that's now an artefact, not durable

b1/triage liked BRO for "32% revenue growth and 54% EPS growth at 12.8x forward." That headline growth is not organic — it is the consolidation of Accession Risk Management Group (parent of Risk Strategies), acquired for a $9.825bn gross, cash-and-debt-free price, closed August 1, 2025 (Brown & Brown 8-K/press release; Holland & Knight deal summary). Financed with ~$4.3bn of new equity (42.16M shares at $102, June 2025) and ~$4.2bn of senior notes. Stripping the deal out: organic revenue growth has decelerated every quarter since Q1-25 — +6.5% (Q1-25) → +3.6% (Q2-25) → +3.5% (Q3-25) → flat (Q1-26) → −0.7% (Q2-26), per Brown & Brown's own press releases (investor.bbrown.com). [Corrected 2026-10-06: the series omits Q4'25 organic of -2.8% (release acc 0001193125-26-022760); organic was negative in Q4'25 and Q2'26 and flat in Q1'26] GAAP diluted EPS has been flat-to-down YoY in three of the last five quarters (Q2-25 −10%, Q3-25 −16%, Q2-26 +7.7% but off a much larger diluted share base) [Corrected 2026-10-06: Q4'25 (-19.2%) and Q1'26 (-7.8%) were also down; four of the last five quarters were down, only Q2'26 rose] because acquisition financing (interest expense, intangible amortization, +18% more diluted shares) outran GAAP net income growth; only the company's own adjusted EPS shows consistent growth (+15% Q3-25, +7.8% Q1-26, +3.9% Q2-26 — itself decelerating). The triage's "54% EPS growth" figure is not supported by either GAAP or adjusted quarterly EPS in the SEC filings checked this session — treat it as an error or a stale/mismatched comparison.

5. Guidance track record

Brown & Brown does not issue formal quantitative revenue/EPS guidance — only qualitative commentary, which I track like guidance: at Q4-25 (Feb-26) management said it "expects improved organic performance in 2026" and flagged a 2026 headwind from lower investment income. That expectation was not met — Q1-26 organic was flat and Q2-26 organic went negative. At Q3-25 (Oct-25), management guided Q4 Specialty Distribution organic to "decline mid-single digits" and Retail organic "similar to 2.7%"; full FY25 organic came in at 2.8%, roughly as flagged. Net: the company's near-term qualitative calls have been reasonably accurate on the segment mechanics but the "improved 2026" framing has so far been wrong.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

FCF (OCF − capex, TTM Q3'25–Q2'26) ≈ $1.45bn vs GAAP NI $1.2bn (≈1.2x conversion) — but BRO's OCF includes swings in fiduciary/premium funds held on behalf of insurers and clients, which can inflate or deflate reported OCF independent of underlying economics; treat this FCF figure as directional, not precise. SBC ≈$49M in H1-26 (~1.4% of revenue) — modest. Leverage jumped materially: long-term debt $3.60bn (year-end 2024) → $7.35bn (Q2-26); net debt (LT+ST debt − cash) ≈ $6.84bn, versus TTM adjusted EBITDAC roughly $2.5bn → net debt/EBITDAC ≈ 2.8x, up from well under 1x pre-deal. Diluted share count rose from ~284M (2024) to ~335M (Q2-26), an ~18% increase, funding part of the Accession purchase price. Bull: (1) private-credit and infrastructure fundraising is structurally scaling as banks retreat and AI capex needs financing; (2) realizations ($144.5bn LTM) show the portfolio can actually monetize, not just mark up; (3) a growing permanent-capital/insurance base (per the sector playbook, the highest-quality alternative-manager earnings) reduces reliance on episodic fundraising cycles. Bear: (1) BREIT/BCRED-style nontraded vehicles have already broken once (2022–23 BREIT gating) and remain a structural liquidity mismatch — repurchase requests being "fully met" today is a point-in-time fact, not a guarantee; (2) an 85% DE payout ratio combined with rising standalone debt leaves less room to defend the dividend in a carry-light year; (3) GAAP earnings volatility (see §4) makes headline "EPS growth" numbers easy to misread without the DE/FRE reconciliation.

  3. Any nontraded vehicle (BREIT, BCRED, or successors) reinstates repurchase gating/proration for more than one quarter.
  4. Standalone long-term debt/FRE exceeds roughly 3.0x (monitor against current ~$13.3bn debt vs. run-rate FRE).

dossiers.C:
C — Citigroup Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F108, Wave 6)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Horizon: 24–36 months. One-sentence reason: the Jane Fraser turnaround is now showing up unambiguously in the numbers (RoTCE 13.0% in Q2 2026, up ~430bps YoY, on record quarterly revenue), and the stock still trades near tangible book value, but the turnaround is not finished (target RoTCE >11% "through the cycle" was only recently re-set, Banamex separation keeps slipping, and ROE is still below best-in-class peers), so I am not yet willing to call it a full-conviction INCLUDE.

2. Business in plain English

Citigroup is a global, systemically important bank organized around five core businesses: Services (transaction banking/treasury and trade solutions and securities services — its crown jewel and highest-return unit), Markets (fixed income and equities trading), Banking (investment banking, corporate lending), Wealth (private bank/wealth management), and U.S. Personal Banking (branded cards, retail banking, Banamex in Mexico, being separated). It earns net interest income on loans/deposits/trading books plus fees on payments, custody, trading and advisory. Under CEO Jane Fraser (since 2021) it has been simplifying the structure (exiting most international consumer franchises, separating Banamex) and cutting costs to raise a chronically sub-peer ROE.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Q04 triage: 39% forward EPS growth and a cheap 10.8x NTM P/E reflect "real turnaround progress" (32% momentum), but a weak statistical-model rank (418/500) and sub-par 8.5% ROE (still below peers) triggered full diligence. The Q1/Q2 2026 prints (below) confirm the EPS-growth read is not a one-off: diluted EPS accelerated from $1.96 (Q2-25) to $3.15 (Q2-26), and RoTCE improved 430bps YoY with "significant improvement in returns across every single business" (company Q2 2026 results). This looks durable rather than an artefact — it is broad-based (Services, Markets and Banking all improved), not a single trading-desk beat — though the ROE base remains below JPM/BAC-level peers.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated Citigroup Inc.; source: structured 10-Q balance-sheet data,

cross-tied to filed statement line items where checked, as of Jun 30, 2026 vs Mar 31, 2026 / Dec 31, 2025) - Total assets: $2,894,654m (Jun-26) vs $2,777,687m (Mar-26) vs $2,657,202m (Dec-25) — growing, consistent with the revenue acceleration above. - Total stockholders' equity: $212,015m (Jun-26) vs $210,959m (Mar-26) vs $212,291m (Dec-25) — roughly flat as buybacks offset retained-earnings growth; total equity incl. minority interest $214,450m. - CET1 ratio: 12.8%, about 120bp above the regulatory minimum, with management targeting ~12.6% under current rules — i.e., capital return (buybacks) is being funded out of a deliberate glide-down toward target, not from weakness (Citigroup Q2 2026 results release, July 14 2026). - RoTCE: 13.0% in Q2 2026, 13.1% year-to-date, up 430bp YoY firm-wide. - Tangible book value per share (my calc): total equity $212,015m less preferred $19,550m = $192,465m common equity; less goodwill $19,012m and intangibles $5,004m = ~$168,449m tangible common equity; ÷ ~1,700.9m weighted-average basic shares (Q2-26) ≈ $99/share tangible book. At the $134.28 close (2026-09-25) that is ~1.36x tangible book — up from sub-1x a few years ago, but still well below best-in-class peers (JPM trades above 2x TBV), consistent with the triage's "still below peers" framing. - Net debt/long-term-debt figures shown by the structured balance-sheet extract ($813.9bn total debt, $447.4bn "net debt" at Jun-26) are not economically meaningful for a bank on this definition — most of that is customer deposits, repos and short-term wholesale funding, not leverage in the industrial-company sense; I flag this as a data conflict between a generic "net debt" field and how a bank's balance sheet should actually be read (use CET1/RWA and deposits/loans instead, per the sector playbook). - Banamex: 51% still owned by Citi as of the most recent updates; a further 24% stake was sold to a consortium (General Atlantic, Afore Sura, BTG Pactual, Chubb, Blackstone, Liberty Strategic Capital, Qatar Investment Authority) in February 2026 for ~$2.5bn at 0.85x book, following an earlier 25% sale to Fernando Chico Pardo's family (closed Dec 2025, subject to Mexican antitrust clearance). Deconsolidation is now targeted for early 2027, with the Banamex IPO itself pushed out further — Citi is currently marketing a >$3bn Banamex IPO per a Bloomberg report dated 2026-09-25 (i.e., still in progress, not closed, as of the cutoff date).

7. Valuation snapshot & reconciliation with V1

There is no row for ticker "C" in v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv or v1_valuation.json — I checked both files directly and confirmed the absence; per the wave-6 prompt, v1_verdict = null for this ticker (not silently assumed — genuinely absent from the systematic model's output for this run).

My own valuation read: price $134.28 (2026-09-25 close), market cap ≈$225.3bn, trailing P/E ≈14.6x (TTM diluted EPS ≈$9.28, cross-checking as 1.86 + 1.21(derived) + 3.06 + 3.15 = 9.28 — consistent with the ~14.6x quoted). Using a simple bank Gordon-growth framework, justified P/TBV ≈ RoTCE ÷ cost of equity for a no-growth franchise: at the current 13% RoTCE and a ~10–11% cost of equity assumption for a G-SIB, that formula implies a "fair" no-growth multiple of roughly 1.2–1.3x tangible book — very close to the ~1.36x the stock actually trades at. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 10-11% cost of equity was not tied to the 5.17% 10-year Treasury. Programme basis: Ke = 5.17% + Blume beta 1.04 x 4.14% = 9.5%; reported TBV/share is $100.89 (Q2-26 release), so P/TBV is 1.33x, not 1.36x. Justified P/TBV at RoTCE 13.0% is 1.37x with no growth (1.54x with 3% growth; 1.31x at an 11.5% through-cycle RoTCE). Implied vs base stays in_line.] Implied vs. base: in_line. The market is pricing in that the current 13% RoTCE run-rate is durable, but is not yet paying up for further improvement toward management's own longer-term aspiration; if RoTCE keeps climbing (as the Q1→Q2 2026 trend suggests) there is room for further re-rating, but if the 13% print proves to be a good-quarter high-water mark, the stock is close to fully valued on today's numbers.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: 1. Broad-based, accelerating operating leverage (Services, Markets, Banking all improving) with RoTCE up 430bp YoY — the turnaround is showing in every segment, not just one trading quarter. 2. Capital return: CET1 at 12.8% (120bp above minimum) gives room for continued buybacks even as the bank grows the balance sheet, directly supporting EPS growth on top of the operating improvement. 3. Banamex separation, once it clears (IPO now targeted with a >$3bn deal size being marketed as of Sept 2026), removes a historically low-return, capital-intensive legacy business and should be a further ROE tailwind on completion.

Bear: 1. Banamex timeline has slipped repeatedly (2025 → 2026 → now "early 2027" deconsolidation, IPO beyond that) — this is the single most-delayed part of the turnaround story and remains a source of execution risk and headline risk. 2. RoTCE of 13% is still below top-tier US bank peers; if the Q1/Q2 2026 acceleration was partly cyclical (strong Markets revenue, benign credit costs) rather than structural, mean-reversion in a weaker macro quarter would hit the multiple hard given how much of the recent re-rating is tied to the "13% is durable" read. 3. It's a G-SIB: regulatory capital requirements, stress-test (CCAR) outcomes, and any adverse action on the Banamex IPO structure from either US or Mexican regulators are risks largely outside management's control.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. RoTCE falls below 10% for two consecutive quarters (a clear reversal of the current trend, not just quarterly noise).
  2. CET1 ratio falls below 12.0% (within 20bp of an involuntary buyback pause under the bank's own stated glide path).
  3. Banamex deconsolidation is not completed by end-2027 (a further, third slip past the "early 2027" target now guided).
  4. Net interest income growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters (a rates/credit-cycle warning sign for a bank whose recent beat has been partly NII-driven).
  5. Any regulatory enforcement action or material adverse finding tied to the long-running consent orders on data/risk infrastructure (monitor 8-K filings for this specifically; none identified in this pass, but not exhaustively searched).

  • Banamex IPO marketing process (>$3bn target size reported Sept 25, 2026) — watch for a launch/pricing date.
  • Continued CCAR/stress-test cycle outcomes (typically mid-year) affecting the capital-return glide path.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 18–36 months. One-sentence reason: a thin-margin, oligopoly drug distributor with a four-quarter, no-cuts, beat-and-raise guidance record, a real (if early) higher-margin diversification (10.4% segment margin in "Other" vs 1.2% in core Pharma), and a reverse DCF that prices in roughly flat-to-negative 10-year growth — well below what the evidence supports — against real, disclosed opioid-liability and goodwill-impairment red flags that are sized and monitorable, not thesis-breaking. 2. Business in plain English

Cardinal Health is one of three companies (with Cencora/COR and McKesson) that distribute the large majority of branded and generic prescription drugs to US pharmacies, hospitals and clinics — an oligopoly with structurally thin (~1–2%) distribution margins earned on volume and working-capital efficiency, not pricing power. Alongside that core Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions business, it runs Global Medical Products and Distribution (GMPD: medical/surgical products, own-brand Cardinal Health products) and a faster-growing, higher-margin "Other" segment built via acquisition (Nuclear & Precision Health Solutions/oncology and urology physician-practice platforms, at-Home Solutions medical supplies, OptiFreight Logistics freight brokerage). Competitive position rests on scale, distribution infrastructure and long-term contracts with drug manufacturers and providers.

3. Why the model likes it, and whether that's durable

Triage flagged 23% street-target upside, buyback-driven EPS growth and steady volume growth, with the historical opioid litigation as the only red flag (already reflected in financials). That is largely confirmed and is durable: adjusted diluted EPS guidance for FY2026 was raised at all four quarterly releases in the year (see §5), and the raises were not driven only by the one-off IEEPA tariff-refund benefit recognized in Q4 (ex that benefit, FY2026 non-GAAP EPS still grew 33%). The "Other" segment's 10.4% margin (vs 1.19% Pharma, 2.03% GMPD) is a genuine mix shift, not an accounting artefact, funded by disclosed cash M&A (Solaris Health $1.9bn in FY2026; GI Alliance, ADS, Specialty Alliance, ION and Urology America named in the 10-K's intangible-asset note). Less durable / worth discounting: revenue growth decelerated every quarter through FY2026 (+22%, +19%, +11%, +6% YoY in Q1–Q4) — largely a base-effect and GLP-1/drug-mix arithmetic (revenue scales with drug list price, gross profit does not), so it is not a demand signal either way, but it means the market's revenue-growth read should not be over-weighted relative to segment profit and cash generation.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Stockholders' equity is negative (−$2,883m at 2026-06-30), the mechanical result of buybacks exceeding retained cumulative earnings over many years — a known, disclosed feature of this business model (also true of peer COR), not a going-concern signal given the low net leverage and IG-typical debt profile.
  • Opioid litigation (the disclosed, quantified red flag): $4.3bn accrued at 2026-06-30 for the National Opioid Settlement Agreement and related claims; the company expects to pay the majority of the remainder through 2038; FY2026 cash payments were $417m, including the fifth annual $366m NOSA installment.   • Other legal/governance items: a Department of Justice Civil Investigative Demand (received Nov 2023, still open per the FY2026 10-K) concerning Anti-Kickback Statute/False Claims Act questions on a 2022 GPO and rheumatology-MSO transaction; company states it is cooperating. 8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Four-for-four guidance raises in FY2026 and an FY2027 initial guide (+13–15%) already above the company's own long-term algorithm, with net debt/EBITDA near 1x giving ample buyback/M&A capacity. (2) The "Other" segment (10.4% margin, +26% revenue, +37% profit FY2026) is a real, executing diversification away from thin-margin core distribution, funded by disclosed, named acquisitions. (3) The reverse DCF shows the market paying for almost no growth in a business with a demonstrated growth and margin-mix track record — a real margin of safety if the growth continues even at a much slower pace than FY2026's.

Bear: (1) $4.3bn of opioid-settlement payments still owed through 2038 is a permanent claim on cash flow, and the DOJ CID (open since Nov 2023) could still produce an adverse outcome not yet accrued for. (2) The Navista & ION goodwill impairment ($184m, Q3 FY26) shows the M&A-funded diversification carries real execution/valuation risk, not a guaranteed payoff. (3) FY2026's cash generation was flattered by working-capital timing (OCF $5.17bn vs a guided FY2027 FCF of only $3.5–4.0bn) and a one-off tariff refund inflated the reported non-GAAP EPS growth rate — the "beat" narrative should be read on the ex-one-off, normalized-working-capital basis, which is still good but less dramatic than the headline.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance is cut (vs. raised or maintained) at any quarterly release — breaks the core track record this thesis rests on.
  2. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x (from ≈1x today) without a value-accretive reason disclosed.
  3. A second goodwill/intangible impairment >$100m in the Other segment (Navista/ION/Solaris/GI Alliance/ADS platforms) within any four-quarter window.
  4. The DOJ Civil Investigative Demand (Anti-Kickback/False Claims Act, opened Nov 2023) converts to a filed complaint or a settlement exceeding $250m not previously accrued.
  5. "Other" segment margin falls below 8% for two consecutive quarters (loss of the diversification thesis's economics).

DOJ CID open since Nov 2023 (Anti-Kickback/False Claims Act) — unresolved, not separately accrued as far as disclosed. dossiers.CARR:
CARR — Carrier Global Corporation — Diligence Dossier (Agent F73, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). One-sentence reason: a genuine, verified data-center-cooling order boom (orders +300% in Q2 2026) is layered on top of a core HVAC/refrigeration business whose organic growth only just turned positive again (+3% in Q2 2026, after -1% in Q1), leverage is the highest among named HVAC peers, and full-year guidance — while raised twice in 2026 — has been raised on the strength of the data-center order book, not yet on delivered core-business acceleration; named reservation: do not size this as if the data-center order surge is already converted to recognised, de-risked earnings — it is orders/backlog, not yet trailing revenue. Thesis horizon: 12–30 months (the next 2–3 quarters should show whether data-center orders convert to shipped revenue and whether core CSA/CSE Residential stabilises).

2. Business in plain English

Carrier makes and services heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC&R) equipment — residential and light-commercial air conditioners and furnaces, commercial building HVAC and controls, and transport/commercial refrigeration — plus a fast-growing niche supplying precision cooling systems to AI/cloud data centers. It sells to homebuilders, contractors, building owners, transport/cold-chain operators and (increasingly) hyperscale data-center developers, earning both equipment margin and higher-margin recurring aftermarket service/parts revenue. Competitive position: one of the "big three" global HVAC players (with Trane Technologies and Lennox/Johnson Controls-adjacent peers), historically weaker on margin and leverage than Trane, but currently the beneficiary of an unusually large data-center cooling order wave.

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable

Gates: checked — no pending-deal exclusion, no volatility disqualifier, no V1 defective-input flag applies to CARR (no V1 row exists at all; see §7). Triage (Q09) flagged NTM P/E 17.6x vs. 37.7% Street upside, with data-center orders +300% and FY26 guidance raised to ~$23B sales / ~$2.90 adjusted EPS, against a backdrop of only ~3% core organic growth and higher leverage (~3.6x) than peers TT/LII. b1 factor read (as_of 2026-09-25): composite decile 1/10 (bottom decile — genuinely mixed quant picture, not a screaming quant favourite), Value pct_ep 0.14 / pct_fcfp 0.20 (not particularly cheap on trailing earnings or FCF yield — this is a name that screens on forward growth/guidance, not on trailing value factors), Quality weak (pct_roe 0.16, pct_leverage 0.21 — leverage percentile confirms the peer-relative debt-load concern), Momentum weak (pct_mom_12_1 0.29 — stock has lagged despite the data-center narrative, plausibly reflecting the market discounting the weak core/leverage). Durability check: the data-center order growth is real and independently disclosed (orders, not sales, but management states "backlog fully covers expected 2026 data center sales" as of Q1 2026) — this looks like a genuine, if early-stage, structural tailwind, not an accounting artefact. But the model's "attractive" read leans heavily on forward Street estimates and guidance, which triage could not independently verify against 2+ years of delivered numbers; this dossier does that verification in §5.

4. Last two years of results

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Entity scope: Carrier Global Corporation, consolidated, balance sheet as of June 30, 2026, per 10-Q filed 2026-07-28 (accession 0001783180-26-000032). - FCF conversion: Q2 2026 FCF of $810M against adjusted net income roughly in the $500–600M range for the quarter (adjusted EPS $0.86 on ~617M shares ≈ ~$530M) — a healthy quarter of cash conversion, but Q1 2026 FCF was negative [Corrected 2026-10-08: adjusted net earnings from continuing operations were $721M in Q2-26 (GAAP $501M) on about 838M diluted shares; the '~617M shares / ~$530M' is wrong; FCF $810M was 112% of adjusted net earnings] ($(15)M) against a positive adjusted profit quarter, and working-capital build (accounts receivable rose from $2,639M at Dec 31 2025 to $3,246M at Jun 30 2026, +23%, faster than the ~4% net-sales growth over the same period) is consistent with the data-center ramp requiring working-capital investment ahead of cash collection — not alarming on its own, but a real use of cash that offsets some of the order-book optimism, and explains why FY26 FCF guidance (~$2B) was not raised alongside the sales/EPS raise. - GAAP vs. adjusted gap: Q2 2026 GAAP operating profit $825M vs. adjusted operating profit $1,095M (a $270M gap, ~25% of the adjusted figure) — driven by restructuring, acquisition-amortisation and separation/divestiture (Riello/NORESCO exit) costs. This is a large and persistent GAAP/adjusted gap; the size of the gap itself is not disclosed as newly widening, but it means investors relying on adjusted EPS alone are looking through a materially different (lower) GAAP earnings reality. - Balance sheet: cash $1,344M (Jun 30, 2026) vs. $1,555M (Dec 31, 2025); total debt $11,952M vs. $11,833M; net debt $10,608M, up slightly from $10,278M at year-end (net debt actually grew in H1 2026, driven by working capital and continued shareholder returns outrunning FCF, not by new M&A). Total equity $13,472M (down from $14,128M). Net debt/adjusted EBITDA: using FY26 guided adjusted operating profit (~$3.5B) as an EBITDA proxy (Carrier does not separately disclose a clean adjusted-EBITDA guide in the extract reviewed), net debt/adjusted-op.-profit ≈ 3.0x; on trailing GAAP EBITDA (~$3.09B per d4/Yahoo), net debt/EBITDA ≈ 3.4x — close to, slightly below, the triage's cited ~3.6x (the small gap is attributable to different EBITDA bases; both readings confirm Carrier carries the highest leverage of the named HVAC peer set, as triage flagged). Goodwill $15,313M (Jun 2026) against equity of $13,472M — goodwill again exceeds equity, a legacy of the UTC Climate/Carrier 2020 spin-merger history. [Corrected 2026-10-08: goodwill was $15,267M at 30 Jun 2026 ($15,501M at 31 Dec 2025), 10-Q acc 0001783180-26-000032] [10-Q filed 2026-07-28, balance sheet] - Capital return: ~$0.5B returned in Q1, ~$0.64B in Q2 (dividends + repurchases); board-authorized buyback capacity of $4.58B remaining as of June 30, 2026 against a $12.1B cumulative authorization since Feb 2021 — capital return continuing at a steady pace even as net debt ticks up, which is the leverage risk to watch (§9). - Share count: trending down via ongoing repurchases (see table in §11 buyback activity — not separately broken out here, but consistent with steady buyback cadence). - Divestitures, not M&A adds: Riello (European heating) divestiture completed July 1, 2026 (closed slightly later than the "end of Q2 2026" target stated in the Q1 release — a one-quarter slip from the original Q1 2026 target, now the second slip disclosed); NORESCO exit also announced/in progress. Both reduce revenue (~$225M and ~$125M FY26 headwinds respectively per the Q2 guidance table) but are described as margin/strategic-focus positive. No pending acquisitions disclosed.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for CARR (checked outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json — no CARR entry) — v1_verdict is null. - NTM P/E (d4 snapshot, 2026-09-25): 17.6x (pe_ntm 17.64) at price $56.37, vs. FY26 adjusted-EPS guidance of ~$2.90 (implying the market is already pricing a re-rated multiple relative to Carrier's own trailing multiple — trailing GAAP P/E is 40.3x, reflecting the depressed FY2025 GAAP EPS base). FCF yield on trailing FCF (~$0.86B TTM, an understated figure given the negative Q1 2026 quarter) is only ~1.8% — but using the company's own FY26 FCF guidance [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: TTM free cash flow is $1,928M (Q3-25 $224M + Q4-25 $909M + Q1-26 -$15M + Q2-26 $810M; FY25 $2,121M less H1-25 $988M plus H1-26 $795M), not $0.86B, so trailing FCF yield is about 4.1% on a $46.5bn market cap (824.3M shares x $56.37, 10-Q cover), not ~1.8%. The 'negative Q1 distortion' explanation is also wrong] of ~$2.0B, FCF yield on the $46.8B market cap is a more reasonable ~4.3%. - Peer context (qualitative): Trane Technologies (TT) and Lennox (LII) — the peers triage cites — both trade at premium multiples to Carrier (historically TT and LII have carried mid-20s to low-30s forward P/E vs. Carrier's high-teens), which the model and Street partly explain by TT/LII's higher margins and lower leverage; Carrier's discount is not unearned. - Reverse DCF (own build, 10-year explicit + Gordon terminal, WACC 8.0%, terminal growth 3.0%): using trailing TTM FCF (~$0.86B) as the starting point implies an unrealistically high required growth rate (~17.8%/yr) — this is a known distortion from the negative-FCF Q1 2026 quarter dragging the TTM figure down, and should not be used. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 17.8%/yr figure rested on the wrong $0.86B TTM FCF. Programme basis (equity DCF, Ke 9.7% = 5.17% + Blume beta 1.09 x 4.14%, FCF after SBC about $75M, 10 years then 3.0%): TTM FCF $1,853M implies about 9.5%/yr; guided FY26 FCF $1,925M implies about 9.0%/yr. Carrier's own guided algorithm (data-center order book converting to sales, continued double-digit commercial-HVAC/aftermarket growth, offset by a low-single-digit-growth-at-best residential core) plausibly supports high-single-digit-to-low-double-digit earnings growth if the data-center ramp continues at anything like its current order pace — meaning the priced-in growth (~7%) looks at or below a reasonable evidence-based base case, not above it. [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated: implied about 9.0-9.5%/yr is at the top of the dossier's own 7-9% base range, not below it. in_line (upper edge) is the most the evidence supports; the margin of safety the original text claimed is gone] - Verdict on implied growth: implied_vs_base = in_line (base case ≈ 7–9% FCF/EPS CAGR over 10 years, blending a decelerating data-center growth rate with a slowly recovering low-single-digit core; the 7% implied by the reverse DCF sits within, at the low end of, that range).

8. Bull case and bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Data-center cooling backlog "fully covers expected 2026 data center sales" (Q1 2026 release) — i.e., 2026 revenue from this line is already substantially locked in, de-risking near-term delivery even if new order growth slows. 2. Organic sales inflected positive in Q2 2026 (+3%) after two quarters of decline, and management attributes this to broad CSA (commercial) strength, not just data centers — a genuine core-business green shoot. 3. Guidance has been raised, not cut, twice in the two most-recent releases reviewed, on both sales and adjusted EPS, which is a real (verified) signal of improving visibility, not just optimistic messaging.

Bear (3 points): 1. Net debt actually grew in H1 2026 (to $10.6B from $10.3B) even as guidance was raised — cash is being consumed by working-capital build (receivables +23% vs. sales +4%) and continued buybacks, and FCF guidance was not raised alongside the sales/EPS raise, a mismatch worth watching. 2. Adjusted operating margin compressed ~190bps YoY in the very quarter (Q2 2026) that produced the guidance raise — the EPS growth story currently rests more on lower share count/financing costs than on margin expansion, [Corrected 2026-10-08: EPS fell year on year in Q4-25, Q1-26 and Q2-26 (see section 4 correction); the bear point stands but is stronger: guidance was raised while quarterly EPS declined] which is a lower-quality growth mix than the headline "raises outlook" framing suggests. 3. The core Residential/Light Commercial business (ex-data-center, ex-divestitures) is still only flat-to-low-single- digit at best; if data-center order growth decelerates faster than the core recovers, the 2027 guide could disappoint even if 2026 delivers as guided.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Data-center segment orders growth decelerates below +50% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from the current +300–500% pace), signalling the boom is normalising faster than the backlog can be replenished.
  2. Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated, using guided adjusted operating profit as the EBITDA proxy) rises above 3.5x (from ~3.0x currently).
  3. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance is cut from the current ~$2.90 at any future quarterly release.
  4. Core (non-data-center) organic growth falls back below 0% for two consecutive quarters after the Q2 2026 +3% print.
  5. Free cash flow for FY26 comes in below the guided ~$2.0 billion (currently un-raised despite the sales/EPS raise — a miss here would confirm the cash-conversion concern flagged in §6).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-10-27 (Q3 2026 results).
  • Riello divestiture closed July 1, 2026 — watch FY26 Q3/Q4 for the full run-rate revenue headwind (~$225M FY26) to show up cleanly.
  • NORESCO exit — timing/financial impact not fully quantified in the sources reviewed; watch for an 8-K or 10-Q update.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation/regulatory: the Q2 2026 10-Q's Legal Proceedings item states "no material changes" versus the 2025 Form 10-K, and Risk Factors are also unchanged — no new material litigation, investigation, subpoena, restatement, material-weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed filing. This is a genuinely clean red-flag scan relative to BDX and CCL in this batch.
  • Insider selling: not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as a gap.
  • Auditor: no auditor change disclosed in the sources reviewed.
  • Divestiture execution risk: the Riello close slipped one quarter (from "end of Q1 2026" to "end of Q2 2026" to actually closing July 1, 2026) — a minor but real pattern of execution slippage on a disclosed corporate action, worth noting as a small credibility flag on management's stated timelines.

CASY — Casey's General Stores, Inc.

Agent F129 (wave 8, standard depth). As of 2026-09-25 close: $598.46 (Yahoo/d4 snapshot); 36.96M shares; market cap about $22.1bn. Research only, not personal investment advice.

1. Verdict

WATCH. A genuinely excellent rural convenience-store and prepared-food compounder, but at $598.46 the price needs roughly 10.5% a year of free-cash-flow growth for ten years (reverse DCF, 8.5% discount rate), above my evidence-based base case of about 8%. Not the business, the price: a great business priced for more than it can deliver. Horizon 12-36 months. What would change it: a price near or below about $490 (my base-case value is about $486 per share), or evidence that free cash flow is compounding at 10% or more. Triage (Q03_triage.json: advance=false on price vs growth) is confirmed, but the stock is already 27% below its 25 Aug high of $824.92 (Yahoo daily closes), so it is closer to fair than triage's "27x NTM" implied.

2. Business in plain English

Casey's runs about 2,959 company-owned convenience stores in 19 states, about two-thirds in towns of 20,000 people or fewer (Investor Day deck, 8-K 0001140361-26-026167). It sells fuel, groceries and general merchandise, and prepared food (it is the fifth-largest US pizza chain by kitchen count, per the same deck). Prepared food earns about 59% gross margin, fuel about 14%. Its edge is rural density, owned distribution centres and its own fuel fleet, which let it serve small towns that competitors skip, and it grows by building and buying stores (Fikes/CEFCO closed 1 Nov 2024, 198 stores).

3. Why the model likes it, and whether that is durable

b1 (live rank 169 of the universe, not top-30; composite_qvm 0.43): momentum family 0.93 (12-1 month return +33.5%) and sentiment family 0.83 (earnings surprise 2.88); value family only 0.16 (EBIT/EV percentile 0.04, i.e. expensive); quality 0.32. So the signal is momentum and surprise, not value. It is partly an artefact: the Q1 FY27 gross-profit gain of $117.7M was 62% fuel ($73.4M fuel vs $44.3M inside, release of 8 Sep 2026), and the stock then fell 14.2% on 9 Sep ($733.49 to $629.03, Yahoo). The cause is not stated in any filing; my inference is an unchanged full-year outlook, slower inside same-store sales (3.2% vs 4.3%) and a fuel margin (47.8 cents/gal) above the company's own "mid 40s" plan assumption. dossiers.CBRE:
CBRE Group, Inc. (CBRE) — Diligence Dossier (F32, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 12–36 months. One-sentence reason: the world's largest commercial-real-estate services firm is compounding earnings through a genuine leasing/infrastructure recovery at a price that is roughly fair (not obviously cheap) once the reverse DCF is done properly, and a growing UK fire-safety liability plus negative price momentum argue for a starter position rather than full weight.

Thesis (≤25 words): The world's largest commercial real-estate services firm, riding a leasing-market recovery and fast-growing data-center/infrastructure work, priced close to what it can actually deliver.

2. Business in plain English

CBRE advises, manages and invests in commercial real estate for corporate and institutional clients. It earns transaction commissions (Advisory: leasing and sales brokerage), recurring fees for running buildings and portfolios for clients (Building Operations & Experience, including a fast-growing "infrastructure/data-center services" line), fees for overseeing construction/fit-out projects (Project Management), and investment-management/development profits (Real Estate Investments, "REI"). It is asset-light — revenue scales with transaction volumes and square footage under management, not with owned property. Competitive position: #1 global commercial real-estate services franchise by revenue, ahead of JLL and Cushman & Wakefield, with particular scale advantages in outsourced facilities management and, increasingly, data-center/mission-critical infrastructure services.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q14_triage.json, as_of 2026-09-25) scored CBRE quality 4, growth 5, price_vs_growth 5 — the highest combination among wave-1 names — reasoning that "15% revenue growth, 16% ROE and low leverage at only 15x NTM P/E is a statistically compelling combination as commercial real estate transaction volumes recover." Data conflict to disclose: the pre-registered quant composite (b1_live_scores.csv) ranks CBRE near the bottom of the S&P 500 — decile 2, quintile 1, live_rank 427 of 503 — the opposite signal from triage. The gap is explainable and not a sign the fundamentals are weak: CBRE's quality percentiles are genuinely strong (gross-profit/assets pct 0.96, ROE pct 0.83), but (a) its 12-1-month price momentum is negative and in the bottom 12th percentile (raw −10.8%), and (b) its FCF-yield and EBIT/EV value percentiles are weak (26th and 22nd), because an asset-light services firm's enterprise value is mostly goodwill/intangibles and human capital rather than hard assets the value factors are calibrated for. So: the composite's poor rank reflects recent price weakness and a value-factor construction that fits CBRE's business model poorly, not a fundamental red flag — but the negative momentum itself is a real, current fact (the market has not yet rewarded the beat-and-raise pattern below), and is one reason for the half-weight sizing rather than full weight.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet
