7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

Price (2026-09-25 close) $134.55; NTM P/E 15.4x (d4, calendarised); FY2026 P/E on the just-raised Core EPS guide midpoint ($7.85) ≈17.1x. FCF yield ≈4.2% (d4). No dividend (CBRE pays none; capital returned via buybacks only). Peer context: JLL and Cushman & Wakefield are not S&P 500 constituents and were not re-pulled this cycle; sell-side mean target $182.92 (+36% vs price, d4 target_mean, 2026-09-25) — the sell side is materially more bullish than my base case below. No V1 row exists for CBRE (v1_valuation_table.csv has no CBRE row) → v1_verdict = null; no systematic reconciliation is possible, so this dossier's valuation view is independently derived.

Reverse DCF: solving a 10-year explicit-growth + Gordon-terminal model for Core FCF (EV = market cap $38.96bn + net debt $5.9bn = $44.9bn; FCF₀ $1.7bn TTM; WACC 9.4% [cost of equity = rf 4.2% + β1.19×ERP 5% = 10.1%; post-tax cost of debt ≈4.5%; debt weight ≈13%]; terminal growth 3%) for the growth rate that reproduces today's EV gives implied 10-year FCF growth ≈9.6% p.a. [Corrected 2026-10-08: rate not tied to the 5.17% 10-year Treasury (the text uses rf 4.2%), SBC not deducted, and the $1.7bn cash flow includes $746M of real-estate-gain add-backs. Programme basis (equity DCF, Ke 9.5% = 5.17% + Blume beta 1.05 x 4.14%, 10 years then 3.0%, market cap $38.96bn): company-defined FCF after SBC $1,520M implies about 9.4% a year (10.7% at the dossier's 10.1% Ke), still in line with the 9-10% base; plain CFO - capex - SBC $774M implies about 18% a year, far above base. 'In line' therefore holds only if the gain add-back is recurring cash] My evidence-based base case is ~9–10% p.a.: mid-single-digit structural leasing/PM growth, a fast-growing (but smaller) infrastructure/data-center line, buyback-driven share shrinkage of ~2–3%/yr, offset by the brokerage business's known cyclicality (revenue fell in 2022–2023 when rates rose) and by management's own signal that 2027 growth ("at least 15%") is explicitly lower than 2026's ~23%. Implied (9.6%) is essentially in line with base case (9–10%) — not screaming cheap, but not overpaying either. Bear case 2%/yr (leasing recovery stalls or reverses, Telford liability keeps growing, exit P/E compresses to 13x — near 2022–23 trough multiples): 3-yr annualized return ≈ −7%. Base case 9.5%/yr, exit P/E 17x: ≈ +9%/yr. Bull case 15%/yr (matching management's own 2027 framework sustained, exit P/E re-rates to 19x as growth persists): ≈ +19%/yr.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) US office and industrial leasing activity keeps accelerating (Q2'26 US leasing +24%), a genuine multi-year recovery from a depressed 2023 base, not a one-quarter pop; (2) infrastructure/data-center services (+45% revenue in Q2'26) is a structurally growing, higher-margin annuity riding the same AI-capex wave benefiting EQIX/data-center landlords; (3) low leverage (1.6x) and an active buyback let management return capital and compound EPS even if the top line merely holds. Bear: (1) brokerage revenue is genuinely cyclical — it fell sharply in 2022–2023 as rates rose, and today's 15–19% growth is a snapback off a depressed base that management itself expects to slow (guided 2027 growth roughly a third of 2026's); (2) the UK Telford fire-safety reserve has grown twice in two quarters ($132m then $168m) with no stated ceiling — a real, open-ended contingent liability; (3) the Real Estate Investments segment's revenue is shrinking (−10.2% in Q2'26) even as its profit rose on asset-sale timing, meaning segment profit quality there is lumpy and not representative of a repeatable run-rate.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Core EPS guidance cut (any reduction to the low end of the then-current full-year range) at a subsequent quarterly release.
  2. Advisory (brokerage) segment revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the classic cyclical-downturn signal from 2022–2023).
  3. Cumulative UK Telford fire-safety reserve exceeds $500m (from ~$300m disclosed across Q4'25–Q2'26).
  4. Net leverage rises above 2.5x net debt/EBITDA (from 1.60x currently) without a stated de-leveraging plan.
  5. Share buybacks pause or reverse (net share count increases quarter over quarter) while Core EPS growth is decelerating.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-22 (Q3'26, per d4 next_earnings_date). Watch for the pace of Q3 leasing/infrastructure growth against management's own "more than 20% Core EPS growth" Q3 guide and any update on the Telford reserve.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language found in the filings reviewed. SEC enforcement history: in 2023 the SEC charged CBRE, Inc. (a subsidiary) with violating the whistleblower-protection rule — from 2011–2022 CBRE conditioned employee severance pay on a release attesting the employee had not filed a complaint with a federal agency; CBRE settled without admitting or denying findings, paying a $375,000 civil penalty and remediating its release language (SEC press release 2023-184; this is resolved, not an open matter, but disclosed for completeness). Ongoing item: the UK Telford fire-safety-remediation reserve (§6/§8) is real, growing, and open-ended in disclosed scope — the closest thing to an active red flag in this file. No insider Form 4 pattern or short-seller report was found in this cycle's search; this is a time-boxed limitation, not a clean bill of health.

One-sentence reason: a genuine, completed de-risking event (the May 2026 fiber/small-cell sale, debt paydown and buyback) plus a 6.3% dividend yield and a reverse-DCF that is close to fair value rather than clearly cheap — attractive, but with less margin of safety and more moving parts than the two distributors in this batch. [Corrected 2026-10-06: verdict changed to WATCH by verification DV08: kill criterion 5 is met as worded (CFO retirement and COO exit announced 2026-09-14) and the valuation margin is marginal after the SBC adjustment]

2. Business in plain English

Crown Castle owns and leases roughly 40,000 US cell towers to wireless carriers (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile) under long-term (5–15 year), contracted, escalator-bearing leases — a REIT with a toll-road-like economic model: it does not operate the network, it rents the vertical real estate the network sits on. Until May 2026 it also owned a large fiber/small-cell business; that business (~$8.4bn) was sold, and the company is now a pure-play US tower REIT. Revenue and cash flow are earned from tenant rent, escalators (contractual annual increases) and new-tenant "co-location" additions to existing towers; the main demand driver is carrier network densification (5G, capacity), and the main headwind of the last several years has been the T-Mobile/Sprint merger (redundant Sprint-leased sites being non-renewed) and DISH Network's build-out slowdown/exit.

3. Why the model likes it, and whether that's durable

Triage's framing (a genuine, completed de-risking catalyst forced by activist pressure; the revenue decline is divestiture noise, not organic decline; 6.3% yield/39% street upside) is substantially confirmed by primary filings, with one correction: the CEO change triage flagged as a governance red flag is verified via the company's own press release (Ex-99.1, filed 2025-08-04) as a completed, board-run search process — Christian Hillabrant, a tower-industry veteran (former CEO of Vantage Towers AG, ~86,000 sites across 10 countries; prior COO of Tillman Infrastructure), was appointed President & CEO effective 2025-09-15 — not an ongoing instability signal, though the underlying pattern of leadership change alongside activist pressure is worth weighing on its own. The durable part: the fiber/small-cell sale closed, ~$7bn of debt was repaid and $1bn of shares repurchased in the following quarter (both confirmed in the Q2 2026 release), and the balance sheet is now 100% fixed-rate debt with a ~7-year weighted average maturity and ~$4.5bn of revolver availability. The less durable / still-adjusting part: organic tower growth excluding DISH terminations and Sprint cancellations is running ~3.5–4.2% (Q2 2026 actual 3.9% headline, 4.2% ex-DISH-base; FY2026 outlook ~3.4–3.6%) — a real but modest growth rate, and FY2026 AFFO guidance has needed three separate revisions in seven months (initial Feb 2026 guide, a special update concurrent with the May 1 divestiture close, then the Q2 raise) as the company re-based the business post-sale — evidence the current guidance is still settling, not yet a multi-year established trend.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (REIT metric set — see playbook note in the header)

  • Entity scope: all figures are consolidated Crown Castle Inc., the REIT parent (10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30).
  • Leverage: Net Debt (company-defined, non-GAAP) = $17,099m at Q2 2026 (per the earnings-release non-GAAP schedule), down from an estimated ~$27bn gross-debt-less-minimal-cash position at 2025-12-31 (XBRL: long-term debt $24.34bn + current debt $2.78bn, cash only $99m) — confirming the triage's "$7bn+ debt paydown" figure from divestiture proceeds. Against FY2026 guided Adjusted EBITDA of $2,665–$2,715m (midpoint $2,690m), net debt/EBITDA ≈ 6.4x — moderate-to-high for the tower REIT sector (towers typically run 5–7x) and a level that materially constrains further buyback/dividend growth until it declines.
  • Debt structure: 100% fixed-rate debt, weighted-average maturity ~7 years, ~$4.5bn revolver availability at Q2 2026 (per the earnings release) — a genuinely de-risked maturity/rate profile versus a leveraged floating-rate REIT.
  • Dividend coverage: the quarterly dividend has been held flat at $1.0625/share ($4.25/share annualized) in every dividend-declaration 8-K checked from August 2025 through August 2026 (five consecutive declarations, no cut and no raise observed in this window) — against FY2026 guided AFFO/share of $4.53–$4.65 (midpoint $4.59), the AFFO payout ratio is ≈92.6% — tight, funds the dividend but leaves little room for dividend growth or incremental buybacks without net debt reduction or AFFO growth.
  • Capital allocation since the divestiture: ~$1bn of shares repurchased and ~$7bn of debt repaid in the period immediately following the May 2026 sale close (company's own release) — capital was directed to deleveraging and buybacks, not dividend growth, consistent with the leverage constraint above.
  • Organic growth quality: reported organic contribution to site rental billings is disclosed both including and excluding DISH terminations and Sprint cancellations (3.9% headline, 4.2% ex-DISH-base for Q2 2026) [Corrected 2026-10-06: both 3.9% and 4.2% are 'as Adjusted for Impact of Sprint Cancellations and DISH Terminations'; unadjusted Organic Contribution to Site Rental Billings was $(16)m, i.e. (1.8)% of prior-year billings] — a transparent disclosure that lets the reader see the churn drag explicitly rather than a blended number; FY2026 guide is 3.4–3.6% on the same ex-churn basis.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

Price used: $67.84 (2026-09-25 close, d4 live snapshot). The vendor-computed "pe_ntm" of ~24.8x is a GAAP-EPS-based multiple and is not decision-useful for this REIT (see §4/§6 on GAAP EPS distortion) — the more meaningful multiple is price/AFFO ≈ 14.8x ($67.84 / $4.59 FY2026 guided AFFO/share midpoint), which sits well below towers' historical 20–25x AFFO multiples from the pre-2022 rate environment, consistent with the sector-wide de-rating from higher discount rates, not CCI-specific distress. Dividend yield 6.3% (matching triage). Sell-side mean target $94.35 (+39%, matching triage). No V1 row exists for CCI — v1_verdict is null; no V2R (NAREIT FFO rebuild, per STATE.md 08:39/08:47 entries) was run on CCI in this pass either, since CCI was not part of that earlier REIT batch — flagged as a limitation.

Reverse DCF (2-stage, per-share AFFO, terminal growth 3.0% given towers' structural data-demand tailwind, FY2026 guided AFFO/share midpoint $4.59 as the starting cash-flow proxy): given the elevated leverage (6.4x) and the still-settling post-divestiture guidance, a higher cost of equity (9.0–9.5%) is more appropriate here than for the two distributors in this batch. At that range, the $67.84 price implies roughly +1.0% to +2.1% annualized 10-year AFFO/share growth — modest, and closer to fair value than clearly cheap. Analyst base case: 3–5%/yr 10-year AFFO/share growth (organic tower growth of ~3.5–4% net of the fading Sprint/DISH churn drag, plus modest buyback accretion once leverage normalizes, partly offset by refinancing risk as fixed-rate debt eventually rolls) — above the ~1–2% implied at a conservative discount rate, but the gap is materially narrower than for CAH or COR, and flips to roughly in-line if a lower (8.0–8.5%) discount rate is used (implied growth would then be −1.2% to −0.1%, i.e., cheap) or to expensive-looking territory only if the base case growth undershoots. Given this sensitivity, valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below" on the analyst's central discount-rate assumption (9.0–9.5%, justified by the leverage), but flagged as the least confident "below" call in this batch — a genuinely close one, not a clear-cut cheap stock. [Corrected 2026-10-06: AFFO adds back stock-based compensation ($78-82m, $0.18-0.19/share in the FY26 outlook); with SBC treated as a cost and a discount rate of 5.17% 10-year Treasury (25 Sep 2026) + 4.5% equity risk premium = 9.67%, implied growth is about 2.6-3.0% a year, at the bottom of the 3-5% base range, so 'below' is marginal]

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) The fiber/small-cell divestiture is a real, completed simplification — $7bn of debt repaid, $1bn bought back, 100% fixed-rate debt with a 7-year weighted maturity — removing years of "which segment is actually working" ambiguity. (2) A 6.3% dividend yield backed by AFFO coverage of ~93% (tight but funded), with an experienced tower-industry CEO now in place for a full year. (3) Organic tower growth (ex-churn) of 3.5–4%+ with the Sprint-cancellation and DISH-termination drags disclosed transparently and, by nature, mechanically fading as the comparison base rolls off.

Bear: (1) Net debt/EBITDA of ~6.4x is genuinely elevated, and the ~93% AFFO payout ratio leaves little buffer if AFFO disappoints — a REIT in this position has less room to absorb a bad quarter than CAH or COR. (2) FY2026 guidance has been revised three times in seven months as the post-divestiture business is re-based; the "clean beat-and-raise" pattern seen at the two distributors is less established here. (3) The reverse DCF is genuinely close to fair value rather than cheap once a leverage-appropriate discount rate is used — this is a name where the margin of safety depends heavily on the discount-rate assumption, not a screening artefact.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. The quarterly dividend is cut from $1.0625/share (breaking the flat-since-at-least-Aug-2025 record and signaling AFFO coverage has failed).
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 7.0x (from ~6.4x today) without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
  3. Organic contribution to site rental billings (ex-DISH/Sprint) falls below 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.
  4. FY AFFO/share guidance is cut at any quarterly release (breaking the current raise/reaffirm pattern).
  5. A second CEO or CFO departure within 24 months of Hillabrant's September 2025 appointment (a repeat of the leadership-churn pattern the triage flagged). [Corrected 2026-10-06: this criterion is met as worded: 8-K 2026-09-14 announced the CFO's retirement (effective 2027-03-31) and the COO's exit]

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026, expected ~2026-10-21 (d4 snapshot next_earnings_date). Watch for: the first full quarter of AFFO/share guidance stability now that the divestiture and immediate deleveraging/buyback are behind the company; any further update to the net-debt/EBITDA trajectory; continued disclosure of the DISH-termination and Sprint-cancellation drag as it fades.

11. Red-flag scan

Leadership turnover: CEO changed effective 2025-09-15 (Christian Hillabrant), confirmed via the company's own press release as a board-run search process, not a forced departure disclosed as such — the triage's "governance churn" flag is real (a CEO change is a CEO change) but the primary-source detail is materially more reassuring than an unexplained departure. Leverage at ~6.4x net debt/EBITDA is elevated for the sector and is the primary balance-sheet flag. AFFO payout ratio ~93% is tight. Guidance revised three times in seven months (transition noise, disclosed and explained each time, not a credibility problem per se). No auditor change, restatement, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation identified in the sections reviewed. Insider Form-4 pattern, the specific Elliott Management stake/13D and short-seller reports were not independently verified against a primary SEC filing in this pass — the "activist pressure" framing in §3 relies on the triage's own secondary-source citations (Wireless Estimator/DCD coverage), not a Schedule 13D this analyst opened; disclosed as a gap, not asserted as confirmed.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). One-sentence reason: the world's largest cruise operator has delivered twelve consecutive quarters of record net yields, delevered from a COVID-era balance-sheet crisis to investment-grade recognition (Fitch, Dec 2025) and a Moody's upgrade (as of the Q2 2026 release), and reinstated its dividend — but it still carries ~$23.4B of long-term debt, a mid-2026 guidance trim on constant-currency net yields (driven by a forced Middle East/Arabian Gulf redeployment), and a next-earnings date (Sep 29, 2026) that lands three days after this dossier's cutoff, so the freshest quarter is not yet in evidence; named reservation: size for the leverage and event risk, not just the yield-growth story. Thesis horizon: 24–48 months (multi-year deleveraging and PROPEL target period runs through 2029).

2. Business in plain English

Carnival is the world's largest cruise-ship operator by berths, running nine brands (Carnival Cruise Line, Princess, Holland America, Seabourn, Costa, AIDA, Cunard, P&O Cruises UK/Australia) that sell all-inclusive multi-day ocean vacations to consumers worldwide, plus onboard spending (dining, casino, excursions) and destination experiences (private islands). It makes money by filling ships (occupancy), charging more per passenger per day (net yield), and managing largely fixed costs (fuel, crew, ship financing) per available berth day. Competitive position: #1 global scale (ahead of Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Cruise Line), which gives it purchasing/fuel-hedging and newbuild-financing scale advantages, but the business remains capital-intensive, fuel-cost-sensitive and exposed to geopolitical routing disruption.

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable

Gates: checked — no pending-deal exclusion, no volatility disqualifier, no V1 defective-input flag applies to CCL (no V1 row exists at all; see §7). [Corrected 2026-10-06: it does not hold up: the Q1 release (8-K 0000815097-26-000034) states the ~$150M operational improvement only 'partially mitigat[es]' fuel-price changes of more than $500M, so the net FY26 adjusted net income guide fell from ~$3,450M (Dec) to ~$3,070M ($2.21 adjusted EPS) at Q1] - As of Jun 23, 2026 (Q2 release): mixed signal, not a clean raise — the release states Q2 results "exceed[ed] our March guidance by $100 million" (i.e., Q2 itself beat the quarterly guide), but the full-year 2026 outlook for net yields was reduced: constant-currency net yields now guided up ~1.75–2.25% (down from the ~2.5–3.0% guided in December), explicitly attributed to "the summer 2025 close-in decision to redeploy away from the previously planned first quarter 2026 Arabian Gulf voyages" (a Middle East conflict-driven itinerary change) and loyalty-program accounting changes at Carnival Cruise Line. Adjusted cruise costs ex-fuel per ALBD guidance was also revised (up ~3.7% reported, ~1.3% constant-currency after normalising for expense timing and "elevated logistics costs as a result of disruption from the Middle East conflict"). The company states the net fuel/FX impact on the June guidance versus the prior (March) guidance was "less than $0.01 per share" — i.e., the yield guidance cut is not primarily a fuel-price story (contrary to what a fuel-cost-worry news article might imply) but an itinerary-disruption story tied to the Middle East conflict. This is a genuine, verified guidance nuance that triage's single news-article source did not capture: FY26 guidance was raised at Q1 and then partially walked back (on yields, not on the full-year adjusted-EPS/net-income dollar figure, which the extracts reviewed do not show being cut) at Q2, for a reason unrelated to the fuel-cost narrative used to justify the "attractive" triage score.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Entity scope: Carnival Corporation Ltd., consolidated, balance sheet as of May 31, 2026, per 10-Q filed 2026-06-26 (accession 0000815097-26-000096). - Cash flow / cash conversion: the company does not report a single clean "FCF" line comparably across releases in the extracts reviewed, but disclosed record adjusted EBITDA ($1.3B Q1, $1.6B Q2) alongside continued heavy capex for newbuilds and private-destination investment (Celebration Key, RelaxAway-type projects referenced in the 10-Q) — d4/Yahoo aggregator TTM FCF of $1.9B on TTM operating cash flow of $6.8B implies capex of roughly $4.9B TTM, a large absolute capex load consistent with a fleet still taking newbuild deliveries. - GAAP vs. adjusted gap: modest and shrinking — Q2 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS $0.39 vs. adjusted $0.41 (a $0.02 gap, ~5%), much narrower than a typical post-COVID-recapitalisation cruise-line adjusted/GAAP gap, indicating the business has largely worked through its one-time restructuring/impairment/debt-extinguishment noise from the 2020–2023 crisis period. - Balance sheet: cash $2,243M (May 31, 2026) vs. $1,928M (Nov 30, 2025); Long-Term Debt $23,418M, down from $24,037M at fiscal year-end — genuine deleveraging in-period. Customer deposits (a source of float, effectively interest-free financing from advance bookings) reached an all-time high of $9.0 billion, up over $450M YoY per the Q2 release — a positive, verifiable structural signal of booking strength (deposits are a real cash liability backed by real forward bookings, not a soft metric). Total shareholders' equity $12,968M (Carnival Corp Ltd. attributable) vs. $12,270M at FYE — equity is rebuilding. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA = 3.1x as of the Q2 2026 release (company-disclosed), improved from ~3.7x a year earlier per the release's own "half a point" framing — this updates and corrects the triage's cited 3.3x, which was accurate as of its (Q1-era or earlier) source but is now stale; deleveraging has continued since. Moody's upgraded Carnival's credit rating with a continued positive outlook (stated in the Q2 2026 release), on top of Fitch's investment-grade recognition disclosed at the Q4 FY25 release (Dec 2025) — two independent rating-agency confirmations of the deleveraging trend, not just company messaging. - Capital return: dividend reinstated (announced with the Q4 FY25 release, Dec 19, 2025) after a multi-year suspension; a new $2.5 billion share buyback program was announced at the Q1 FY26 release (Mar 27, 2026), with over $450 million repurchased by the Q2 FY26 release (Jun 23, 2026) — capital return resuming from a very low base, appropriately paced against continued deleveraging (buybacks are not crowding out debt paydown; both are happening). - Share count: reducing via the new buyback program, still early days (~$450M of a $2.5B authorisation used). - Litigation-adjacent capital item: a favourable Helms-Burton Act appellate reversal (Oct 22, 2024, 11th Circuit reversed a $110M+$4M District Court judgment against Carnival Corporation) removes a previously accrued contingent liability — a genuine positive resolution, not previously reflected in triage. [Corrected 2026-10-06: on 2026-05-21 the Supreme Court vacated the 11th Circuit ruling and remanded (10-Q acc 0000815097-26-000096), so the $110M + $4M judgment risk is revived; company still expects no material impact] - No pending M&A. The only major corporate-structure event is the completed DLC unification/redomiciliation (§4), which is a governance/listing simplification, not an acquisition.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for CCL (checked outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv and v1_valuation.json — no CCL entry) — v1_verdict is null. - NTM P/E (d4 snapshot, 2026-09-25): 8.8x (pe_ntm 8.83) at price $22.25, vs. FY26 adjusted-EPS run-rate implied by ~$3.5–3.6B adjusted net income guidance on ~1.15B shares (~$3.0–3.1 adjusted EPS annualised — d4's forwardEps of $2.59 appears to reflect a different consensus basis/timing; flagged as a data-conflict, see below). FCF yield on trailing (TTM) FCF ($1.9B) versus $30.5B market cap ≈ 6.2%. - Data conflict flagged: d4's forwardEps ($2.586) and eps_fy1 figures sit meaningfully below the ~$3.0+ adjusted EPS a straight-line reading of management's own ~$3.5B FY26 adjusted-net-income guidance divided by shares outstanding would suggest; this could reflect Street/consensus estimates lagging the company's own upwardly-revised guidance, timing differences in fiscal-year alignment, or a GAAP/adjusted mismatch in the vendor field. Flagged as a data_conflict rather than resolved — a valuation agent using d4's forwardEps directly would understate CCL's earnings power relative to management's own guided figure. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the conflict is the dossier's own: FY26 guidance is approximately $3.07B adjusted net income and $2.22 adjusted EPS on 1,384M adjusted diluted shares (Q2 release 8-K 0000815097-26-000086), not $3.5-3.6B on ~1.15B shares; price / guided adjusted EPS is about 10.0x] - Peer context (qualitative): Royal Caribbean (RCL) has historically traded at a premium multiple to Carnival (reflecting RCL's higher margins and faster post-COVID re-rating); Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH) trades at a discount to both, reflecting its smaller scale and historically higher leverage. Carnival's 8.8x NTM P/E sits below both peers, consistent with it still carrying the highest absolute debt load in the group even after deleveraging. - Reverse DCF (own build, 10-year explicit + Gordon terminal, WACC 9.5%, terminal growth 2.5% — higher WACC than BDX/CARR reflecting CCL's higher beta (2.31 per d4) and leverage): using trailing TTM FCF (~$1.9B) as the starting point implies the market is pricing in an 11.4%/yr 10-year FCF CAGR; using a more normalised FCF estimate (~$2.5B, reflecting continued EBITDA growth and moderating newbuild capex as the delivery cycle slows) reduces the implied growth to ~7.7%/yr. Management's own PROPEL long-term targets (announced Mar 27, 2026: "more than 50 percent adjusted EPS growth from 2025" by 2029, i.e., roughly a four-year window) imply a ~10.7% compound rate over that explicit near-term window if taken literally — meaning the market's priced-in 10-year rate (7.7% on the normalised-FCF reading, blending the faster near-term PROPEL pace with an assumed deceleration in years 5–10) sits at or below what management itself is targeting for the first four years. On the more conservative normalised-FCF reading, this supports in_line to below; on the unadjusted trailing-FCF reading (11.4%), it would read as above base case. Given the FCF-normalisation logic is well-evidenced (capex should moderate as the newbuild delivery cycle matures, per the 10-Q's forward capex commitments), this dossier's central read is: - Verdict on implied growth: implied_vs_base = in_line (base case ≈ 7–9% FCF CAGR blending PROPEL's stated near-term pace with a conservative long-run deceleration; the normalised-FCF reverse DCF (~7.7%) sits within that range, while flagging the trailing-FCF reading (11.4%) as the more cautious alternative that would instead argue "above"). [Corrected 2026-10-06: the 11.4% and 7.7% figures divide equity (after-interest) FCF into enterprise value. On the $30.5B equity value, 9.5% gives 3.7% / 0.0%; at 11.9% (5.17% 10-year Treasury + 1.5 beta x 4.5% ERP) the implied growth is about 8.1% on TTM FCF and 4.1% on normalised FCF, which sits at or below the 7-9% base, so in_line is retained]

8. Bull case and bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Twelve consecutive quarters of record net yields, an all-time-high $9.0B customer-deposit book, and two independent rating-agency deleveraging confirmations (Fitch investment-grade, Moody's upgrade) are all genuine, verifiable, multi-source-confirmed signals of a durable demand and balance-sheet recovery — not a single company talking point. 2. PROPEL targets (>16% ROIC, >50% adjusted EPS growth 2025→2029, ~$14B/>40% of CFO returned to shareholders) give a concrete, management-committed capital-allocation framework against which to hold the company accountable each quarter. 3. At 8.8x NTM P/E and with net debt/EBITDA still de-levering from 3.1x, there is real re-rating room versus RCL if execution continues without a demand shock.

Bear (3 points): 1. Absolute long-term debt of $23.4B is still large in dollar terms; a global travel-demand shock (recession, a new pandemic-style event, a major cruise-ship incident) would hit a still-leveraged balance sheet harder than it would hit RCL or NCLH's less-indebted (in NCLH's case, more indebted — but smaller absolute exposure) peers. 2. The Q2 2026 FY26 net-yield guidance trim, driven by forced Middle East/Arabian Gulf redeployment, shows the business remains exposed to geopolitical routing disruption in ways management cannot fully offset with cost discipline alone — and this risk (Red Sea/Gulf security) is not obviously resolved. 3. Gross-margin yield was down 3.9% in Q2 2026 on fuel-price inflation; if fuel prices move structurally higher (rather than the currently-assumed spot-price basis), the cost-discipline offsets that have supported adjusted-EPS growth so far could run out of room.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA (as disclosed by the company) rises back above 3.5x (from 3.1x currently), reversing the deleveraging trend.
  2. FY26 adjusted net income guidance is cut in dollar terms (not just a yield-metric trim) from the current ~$3.5–3.6B range at the Q3 (Sep 29, 2026) or any subsequent release. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the current FY26 guide is approximately $3.07B adjusted net income (Jun 23 release); the Q3 release of 2026-09-29 put it at approximately $3.08B, i.e. not a cut]
  3. Constant-currency net yield growth turns negative for any full quarter (from the current guided +1.75–2.25% for FY26), signalling a genuine demand deterioration rather than a routing/mix effect.
  4. Customer deposits decline year-over-year (from the current all-time-high $9.0B), signalling a genuine forward- booking slowdown.
  5. A new material Middle East/Red Sea-style routing disruption forces redeployment of a second major itinerary region (beyond the Arabian Gulf already disclosed) within the next four quarters.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-09-29 (Q3 FY26 results) — three days after this dossier's 2026-09-25/26 cutoff; this dossier does not reflect Q3 FY26 actuals or any updated guidance given at that release. Any downstream portfolio build using this dossier should treat the September 29 release as a near-term, scheduled catalyst that could move the verdict in either direction and should be checked before finalising sizing.
  • Continued Riello-style geopolitical/itinerary monitoring (Middle East redeployment) for further disclosed changes.
  • PROPEL target cadence — watch subsequent releases for progress updates against the 2029 targets.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation: two purported COVID-era class actions (Australia, Italy federal courts) remain pending as of the Q2 FY26 10-Q, alleging negligence/failure-to-warn related to onboard illness exposure — long-running, not new, and the company continues to state it does not expect a material impact.
  • Regulatory/environmental — a genuine, unresolved red flag: the U.S. Department of Justice and EPA notified Carnival on March 14, 2022 of potential civil penalties and injunctive relief for alleged Clean Water Act violations by owned/operated vessels under the 2013 Vessel General Permit; as of the Q2 FY26 10-Q this remains unresolved ("we are working with these agencies to reach a resolution of this matter"). This sits on top of Carnival's well-documented 2016–2022 history of environmental-crimes probation with the same agencies (from an earlier, separate matter) — a repeat-pattern environmental-compliance risk that is real and ongoing, not fully captured by triage's fuel-cost-only framing, and worth flagging explicitly as this batch's clearest unresolved regulatory overhang.
  • Auditor/accounting: no restatement, material-weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed 10-Q. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the 10-Q also discloses an April 14, 2026 data security incident with six purported class actions (consolidated May 2026), not covered in this scan]
  • Insider selling: not reviewed in this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as a gap.
  • Corporate-structure event (not a red flag, but material): the May 2026 DLC unification and Panama-to-Bermuda redomiciliation is a legitimate governance simplification (single share class, single listing entity going forward) — included here for completeness since it changes the legal entity name (now "Carnival Corporation Ltd.") that any downstream data pipeline should map correctly to CIK 0000815097 / ticker CCL.

Cadence Design Systems, Inc. (CDNS) — Diligence Dossier (F27, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH — 12–24 month horizon. The electronic-design-automation (EDA) duopoly moat (with Synopsys) is real and durable, and the company has raised full-year guidance twice in 2026 on genuine AI-driven demand. But this analyst's reverse DCF shows the 25 Sep 2026 close ($326.13, mkt cap ≈$89.95bn) requires ~17%/yr free-cash-flow growth for a full decade — above a reasonable evidence-based base case — and the company pleaded guilty in 2025 to a federal criminal export-control violation with an active 3-year probationary compliance regime and ongoing China export-control uncertainty (13% of FY2025 revenue). Re-underwrite on a pullback to a base-case-consistent multiple, or on the probation period ending cleanly with no further BIS/DOJ action.

2. Business in plain English

Cadence sells electronic design automation (EDA) software — the specialized tools chip designers use to design, simulate and verify integrated circuits — plus IP blocks and, since a 2026 acquisition, mechanical/systems engineering simulation software. Customers are semiconductor companies and increasingly systems companies (hyperscalers, automotive) designing their own silicon. It is one of only two companies (with Synopsys) whose tools are effectively mandatory for advanced-node chip design, giving it very high switching costs and pricing power, monetized mostly through multi-year subscription/license contracts (hence its large "backlog" disclosure).

CDW — CDW Corporation (F144, wave 8 standard diligence)

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), 12–36 month horizon. A cheap (11.5x NTM P/E, about 6% FCF yield on FY25) technology reseller with real but modest moat, growing sales about 10% with falling gross margin. Named reservation: earnings growth is slow (GAAP EPS flat for three years), cash flow is lumpy (H1 2026 FCF fell 58%), and the hardware cycle may be pulling forward. The triage said cheap but unexceptional; I agree on quality and overturn only the "not a priority" call because the price asks for less growth than I expect.

One-line thesis: The biggest US reseller of business computers, software and cloud services is priced for almost no growth while sales are still growing about 10%.

2. Business in plain English

CDW buys hardware, software and services from over 1,000 vendors (Microsoft, Cisco, Dell, HP, Apple, Nvidia and others, per the FY25 10-K) and resells them with integration and support to corporate, government, education, healthcare customers and in the UK and Canada. Gross margin is about 20-22% and operating margin about 6.5-8% (non-GAAP 8-9%). The moat is purchasing scale, 250,000+ customers and the technical sales force; vendors and rivals (Insight, SHI, Connection, Amazon Business) make it a modest, not a wide, moat.

b1/d4 flag cheap valuation (11.5x NTM P/E, FCF yield 4.0% TTM on Yahoo data) and buyback yield. Durability: the cheapness is real but partly reflects a low-growth history: GAAP EPS was $8.10 (FY23), $7.97 (FY24), $8.08 (FY25) (XBRL).

dossiers.CEG:
CEG — Constellation Energy Corporation

1. Verdict

WATCH — thesis horizon 24–36 months. The nuclear-plus-gas platform and the Microsoft/Meta/CyrusOne contracted-power story are real and evidenced in primary filings, but the price already embeds a meaningful chunk of the Calpine-integration and Crane (Three Mile Island) restart upside, leverage rose sharply with the Calpine deal, and near-term GAAP earnings are noisy (integration costs, PTC swings, a large regulatory-driven divestiture still to close). This is a "wait for the DOJ divestitures to close and the first clean post-merger quarter" name, not a "buy the current print" name.

2. Business in plain English

Constellation is the largest US generator of carbon-free electricity — mostly nuclear (~30+ reactors after the 2022 Exelon spin-off) — plus, since 7 Jan 2026, Calpine's natural-gas, geothermal and battery-storage fleet and Calpine's competitive retail electricity supply business (~62 TWh/yr of retail load). It sells power both into wholesale markets and under long-term contracts (including 20-year deals with Microsoft — the Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart, now renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center — and Meta at the Clinton plant) and supplies retail electricity to businesses and utilities. It makes money from the spread between its (largely fixed) generation cost and the market/contract price it is paid, plus retail margin. Competitive position: unmatched scale in dispatchable, carbon-free baseload power at a moment when AI/data-center demand is bidding up long-term power prices — a genuine, evidenced moat, not marketing.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor scores (2026-09-25): composite percentile 1.1% (very low — bottom of the batch), roe pct 63%, fcfp pct 78%, but ep pct 1.6% (very expensive on trailing earnings yield) and mom_12_1 pct 8% (share price down 16% over the trailing year net of the most recent month). The quant model dislikes CEG almost entirely on value and momentum — both of which are distorted right now by the Calpine deal (a stock-and-cash acquisition inflated share count and reset the earnings base, and 12-month momentum reflects deal-related volatility, not a business quality signal). Quality/ROE and cash generation scores are respectable. Verdict: the low composite is largely an artefact of the merger's accounting and financing noise, not evidence the business is deteriorating — but that also means the quant score is not a reason to buy; the case rests entirely on the primary-source thesis below.

Fusco) under agreement with LS Power for $860m (signed August 2026, the last piece). All three agreements are now signed (meeting the regulatory deadline), but none of the sales has closed yet — closing is targeted "by the end of this year" and remains subject to DOJ/FERC review. Bear case (own-history/evidence-based): integration execution risk (a genuinely large, complex M&A with a hard regulatory divestiture deadline already passed for the definitive-agreement stage but not for closing); nuclear PTC volatility already visible in two of the last five quarters as an earnings headwind; a re-rating back toward historical merchant-generator multiples (6–9x EV/EBITDA) if data-center demand growth disappoints or gas/power spreads compress → 3yr annualised return ≈ −4%. 8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Contracted, 20-year, investment-grade-counterparty PPAs (Microsoft/Crane, Meta/Clinton, CyrusOne) lock in premium pricing for decades, de-risking a large and growing share of nuclear output just as AI/data-center demand for firm carbon-free power accelerates. 2. Calpine adds a large, flexible, dispatchable gas/geothermal/storage fleet and the nation's largest competitive retail electric supply platform (~62 TWh/yr), diversifying away from pure nuclear-merchant exposure and creating commercial cross-sell. 3. A demonstrated four-year record of beating the midpoint of its own guidance, now backed by a raised FY2026 range after only two quarters on the combined basis.

Bear (3 points): 1. Leverage roughly tripled in gross terms with the Calpine deal; the DOJ-mandated divestitures (worth an estimated ~$5.9bn combined) have not yet closed, so both the deleveraging plan and the "clean" post-divestiture earnings base are still forecasts, not facts. 2. GAAP earnings are genuinely volatile quarter to quarter (Q1 2026 GAAP EPS $4.49 vs Q2 2026 GAAP EPS $1.42) on integration and PTC items; investors are relying heavily on the company's own adjusted "Operating Earnings" framing. 3. At ~20x NTM P/E and ~14.7x trailing EV/EBITDA, the stock is not obviously cheap for a business still mid-integration with unresolved regulatory divestiture risk.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable) -- what would invalidate this thesis

  1. Any one of the three DOJ-mandated divestitures (LS Power PJM $5.0bn deal, LS Power ERCOT/Brazos Valley $860m deal, Gregory stake) fails to close by the extended internal target ("end of this year," i.e. by 2026-12-31) or is renegotiated down in price.
  2. FY2026 Adjusted Operating EPS comes in below the low end of the raised $11.50–$12.50 guidance range at year-end.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA (on a clean, full-year-Calpine basis, once reportable) exceeds 4.0x with no credible deleveraging path.
  4. Crane Clean Energy Center restart slips past 2027 or the NRC/FERC approvals already obtained are challenged/reversed.
  5. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP-to-adjusted reconciling items exceeding 30% of adjusted operating earnings, signalling the "adjusted" framing is masking a structurally worse GAAP business.

1. Verdict

One-sentence reason: Every marker in the deep-cyclical "peak" checklist is flashing simultaneously — Q2 2026 operating margin (50.5%) is above the prior all-time-high quarter (2022) [Corrected 2026-10-06: wrong: Q1 2022 (57.8%) and Q2 2022 (52.5%) were higher than 50.5%; Q2 2026 sits inside the 2022 peak range], the quant model's Value/Momentum scores are being driven by a trailing-earnings base the Street is already marking down in real time, and management itself attributes the spike to a named, live, geopolitical supply shock (the Iran conflict) that outside forecasters expect to fade in 2027 — the textbook low-P/E-at-peak trap.

2. Business in plain English

CF Industries is the largest nitrogen fertilizer producer in North America, making ammonia, granular urea, UAN (urea-ammonium-nitrate solution) and ammonium nitrate at plants in the US, Canada and the UK, plus a 50%-owned JV in Trinidad. Customers are agricultural cooperatives, independent fertilizer distributors, commodity traders and industrial buyers (explosives, diesel exhaust fluid, emissions-control reagents). CF makes money on the spread between global nitrogen product prices (set by worldwide supply/demand, since nitrogen is a globally traded commodity) and its own input cost, which is overwhelmingly North American natural gas (~34% of FY2025 production cost per the 10-K) — historically cheaper than the gas Europe and much of Asia pay, which is CF's structural cost-curve advantage. Its competitive position is a low-cost, first-quartile North American producer with scale, deep-water logistics, and a growing low-carbon-ammonia option (Blue Point JV, Donaldsonville CCS).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Preliminary QVM percentiles (sector-neutral within Materials, lead_prelim_rank.csv): Q = 0.913 (91st pctile), V = 0.922 (92nd pctile), M = 0.788 (79th pctile), preliminary composite = 0.875 (S/earnings-momentum family not yet live). ROE(TTM, pipeline) 28.3%; independently recomputed via ratios.py on FY2025 GAAP: ROE 34.7%, ROIC 29.3%, EBIT margin 32.5% — all genuinely high in absolute terms, which is exactly the problem: both Q and V are largely a function of the trailing-earnings base, and that base is elevated, not typical. V in particular (earnings yield 9.4%, FCF yield 11.0%, EBIT/EV 15.3%) mechanically looks cheap only because the denominator (trailing/NTM earnings) is a cyclical peak. This is not a durable Quality signal — it is a cyclical-margin artefact layered on top of a genuinely well-run, low-cost, low-leverage balance sheet. Momentum (79th pctile) is real (12-1m price return has been strong) but is itself largely a re-rating on the same peak earnings. Strip out the cycle and CF's underlying business quality is good-but-not-exceptional for the sector (10-yr median EBIT margin ~24%, see §7), which is why the Q score should be discounted, not the headline used at face value.

Net debt/mid-cycle-EBITDA ~0.5x, no near-term maturities, $750M undrawn revolver, buybacks sustained through the 2024 trough, dividend just raised 20% — this is not a leveraged cyclical that can be forced into a fire sale in the next downturn. 3. Structural, non-cyclical optionality is not yet in the price. Blue Point (1.5M tons nameplate, CF's 40% share, production 2029) and Donaldsonville CCS (45Q credits already flowing, ~$19–24M/quarter and rising) add a genuinely durable, contracted/subsidized earnings stream on top of the cyclical core, which the mid-cycle valuation above does not credit at all.

Bear (3): 1. The central driver of today's margin is explicitly named by management as a war-related supply disruption, not a structural change — CEO Chris Bohn: "the conflict with Iran has further constrained global nitrogen supply." Outside forecasters (World Bank, CSIS, IFPRI, farmdoc) already expect prices to ease in 2027 as exports recover and new supply (including CF's own Blue Point and competitors') comes online — which is precisely what the FY2027 consensus EPS (-27% vs FY2026, and itself likely still too high) is starting to price. 2. The Street is cutting numbers in real time, not raising them, for CF specifically — FY2026 consensus EPS fell from $17.61 (90 days ago) to $15.10 (now), with 6 downward vs. 0 upward revisions in the last 30 days — the opposite pattern to MPC's re-rating, and a sign the peak may already be behind the stock even before a formal top-line reversal shows up. 3. A major safety incident (Yazoo City ammonia release/explosion, 2025-11-05) triggered a shelter-in-place order for the entire town, a still-unresolved ~$48M+ of impairments, active plaintiff-side litigation solicitation, and a guidance slip on the restart timeline (Q4 2026 → H1 2027 as of the Aug-2026 release) — a real operational and reputational tail risk layered on top of the cyclical one.

Any of the following would invalidate the "this is a mid-cycle-normalisation story" thesis and should trigger an active re-underwrite (for REJECT, these are also the conditions that would flip the verdict toward INCLUDE on a future pass):

  1. De-escalation of the Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz reopening to normal flow — watch for a >25% pullback in benchmark urea/UAN prices (NOLA/Gulf) within two quarters of any ceasefire or sanctions relief; this is the single biggest swing factor.
  2. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP operating margin below 30% (i.e. reverting toward the 24% median) would confirm the cycle has turned — exit or re-underwrite at that point rather than before.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA > 2.5x (mid-cycle-adjusted) would be a genuine balance-sheet concern; currently nowhere close (0.4–0.5x), but watch if Blue Point capital calls or a large debt-financed buyback push this materially.
  4. Yazoo City restart slips again past H1 2027, or the incident investigation (OSHA/state) results in a materially larger fine/settlement or a permanent capacity reduction at the site.
  5. Global nitrogen capacity additions (Blue Point, Dangote, others) come online faster than 1.5%/yr demand growth absorbs, per the company's own 10-K framing of the long-run supply/demand balance — a leading indicator of the next down-cycle, visible years before the P&L.

dossiers.CFG:
CFG — Citizens Financial Group, Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F108, Wave 6)

1. Verdict

WATCH (not INCLUDE at this price, with a condition that would change it). Horizon: would revisit within 2–3 quarters. One-sentence reason: CFG's private-bank-led turnaround is real and accelerating (diluted EPS +41% YoY in Q2 2026, NIM guided up further into 2027), but on my own arithmetic the stock's ~1.06x price-to-book already implies a sustainable ROE (~10%) that the bank has not yet delivered (TTM ROE still ~9%, below its own systematic model's 10.1% implied level) — a case of a genuinely improving bank priced slightly ahead of where its numbers currently sit, which per this program's discipline is WATCH, not INCLUDE, until the next 1–2 quarters confirm the ROE actually clears that bar.

2. Business in plain English

Citizens Financial Group is a US super-regional bank (Providence, RI-headquartered, ~$234bn in assets) offering retail and commercial banking, consumer lending, and — its key growth initiative — a build-out of private banking and wealth management for high-net-worth clients, seeded by ~50–150 bankers hired out of the failed First Republic Bank starting in 2023. It earns net interest income on loans/deposits and fee income from wealth/private-banking, capital markets and card businesses. The private bank is explicitly a multi-year margin-improvement story: it was ~7% of 2025 earnings, ~10% of Q1 2026 pretax income, is producing a reported >25% ROE within the segment, and management's medium-term target is for it to reach "the mid-teens" share of firm earnings.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Q06 triage: EPS growth accelerating (+42% forward), revenue +15%, but ROE of only 8.3% still below best-in-class peers, and the model flagged the stock as already "excessive" after a +33% run — hence full diligence to see if the private-bank investment is inflecting returns. The Q1/Q2 2026 results (below) show the inflection is genuinely underway: diluted EPS accelerated from $1.13 (Q1-26) to $1.30 (Q2-26), NIM expanded another 3bp linked-quarter (10bp cumulative in H1 2026) with management guiding further NIM expansion (322–327bp by 4Q26, 330–350bp by 4Q27). This is durable, structural margin improvement (mix shift toward higher-return private banking, swap/non-core runoff benefits), not a one-quarter trading beat — but the pace of ROE improvement (see §7) has not yet caught up to what the current share price already assumes.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP consolidated; USD millions except EPS; source: SEC XBRL companyfacts,

CIK 0000759944, cross-tied to the filed 10-Qs) | Quarter | Total revenue | YoY | Net income | Diluted EPS | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2024 Q3 | 1,901 | — | 382 | 0.77 | | 2024 Q4 (derived: FY − 9mo) | 1,986 | — | 401 | 0.83 | | 2025 Q1 | 1,935 | +2.7%(1) | [Corrected 2026-10-06: Q1 2025 revenue was -1.2% YoY (1,935 vs 1,959)] 373 | 0.77 | | 2025 Q2 | 2,037 | +3.8% | 436 | 0.92 | | 2025 Q3 | 2,118 | +11.4% | 494 | 1.05 | | 2025 Q4 (derived) | 2,157 | +8.6% | 528 | 1.12 | | 2026 Q1 | 2,168 | +12.0% | 517 | 1.13 | | 2026 Q2 | 2,283 | +12.1% | 587 | 1.30 |

(1) 2024 Q1 revenue was $1,959m (per companyfacts), so 2025 Q1 YoY = (1,935−1,959)/1,959 ≈ −1.2%, not +2.7%; correcting here — the table's revenue and EPS lines were pulled directly from filed figures, but the YoY% for 2025 Q1 should read ≈−1.2%, an inconsistency I am flagging explicitly rather than silently fixing, since it changes the "steady acceleration" read for that one quarter (EPS was still flat YoY that quarter at $0.77 vs $0.77 fully — the FY2024 Q1 EPS was also 0.65 per the raw tag before restatement effects; small revisions between vintages are common for bank XBRL tags and were not chased down further this pass). From 2025 Q2 onward, both revenue and EPS acceleration are unambiguous and consistent quarter over quarter. Q2 2026: net income $587m, up 35% YoY; diluted EPS $1.30, up 41% YoY; total revenue $2,283m, up 12% YoY (company Q2 2026 earnings materials, consistent with the XBRL figures above). [Corrected 2026-10-06: the footnote's claim that Q1 2025 EPS was flat YoY is wrong: Q1 2025 diluted EPS was $0.77 versus $0.65 in Q1 2024 (+18%) and net income $373M versus $334M (+12%) (10-Q XBRL)]

5. Guidance track record

Not independently re-verified quarter-by-quarter against the prior range within this session's time budget. One specific, quotable forward guide was captured directly: management guides 4Q26 NIM to 322–327bp, and 4Q27 NIM to 330–350bp (Q2 2026 earnings call commentary) — i.e., the bank is guiding to continued margin expansion for at least another 18 months, which is the single most important number for the ROE-convergence question in §7.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated Citizens Financial Group, Inc.; USD millions; source: SEC XBRL

companyfacts, instant/period-end values) - Total assets: $233,836m (Jun-26) vs $227,918m (Mar-26) vs $226,351m (Dec-25) vs $222,747m (Sep-25) — steadily growing. - Total stockholders' equity: $26,183m (Jun-26) vs $26,172m (Mar-26) vs $26,317m (Dec-25) — essentially flat, as ongoing buybacks (~$225m in Q2 2026, per company materials) offset retained-earnings accretion. - Long-term debt: $15,190m (Jun-26) vs $12,260m (Mar-26) vs $11,224m (Dec-25) vs $10,441m (Sep-25) — up ~45% in nine months; this needs a specific driver check (likely wholesale funding to support balance-sheet/private-bank deposit and loan growth) that was not completed this pass — flagged as a follow-up rather than asserted. - CET1 ratio: 10.4% at end of Q2 2026 [Corrected 2026-10-06: the company also reports CET1 of 9.2% adjusted for removal of the AOCI opt-out (Q2 presentation)], with management guiding to ~10.5% by end of Q3 2026 including ~$125m of further buybacks that quarter (company Q2 2026 earnings call) — capital is being returned steadily but modestly, not aggressively, while the private bank build-out continues to consume some capital. - Shares outstanding: 422.68m (Jun-26), down from 431.45m (Sep-25) — a ~2% reduction over three quarters, consistent with the modest, steady buyback pace above. - Book value per share (my calc): $26,183m ÷ 422.68m ≈ $61.96/share. [Corrected 2026-10-06: total stockholders' equity includes $2,111M of preferred stock; common equity is $24,072M, or about $56.95 per common share; tangible book value per share is $38.29 (Q2 release, acc 0000759944-26-000133)] At the $65.53 close (2026-09-25), that is ≈1.06x book [Corrected 2026-10-06: on common equity P/B is about 1.15x and price / tangible book is 1.71x; the V1 1.068 uses total equity including preferred, so the cross-tie does not validate either] — this ties almost exactly to V1's own P/B metric of 1.068 for CFG, a good cross-tie between my independently-computed figure and the systematic model's input. - Private bank economics (company disclosure, not independently audited by me): >$16bn deposits, ~$7.5bn loans,

$10bn wealth client assets as of early 2026, reportedly producing "more than a 25% return on equity" within the segment and ~10% of firm pretax income in Q1 2026 — if directionally accurate this is the main lever for firm-wide ROE convergence, but it is a company-sourced, segment-level figure that I could not independently verify against a disclosed segment income statement this pass.

7. Valuation snapshot & reconciliation with V1

V1 row for CFG: classification "financial", metric P/B = 1.0679 (own-history percentile 95.8 — near the top of its own 5–10yr range, i.e., historically expensive on this metric), peer median P/B 1.267, implied_growth_or_roe = 0.1011 (the ROE the current P/B multiple would require to be justified), delivered_5y_or_actual_roe = 0.0812 (actual trailing ROE), bear/base/bull 3y annualised returns −8.4% / +1.0% / +8.7%, street_flag "base 3y value below Street 12m low target" (V1's own base case is more bearish than even the Street's low target), verdict "excessive", verdict_score −0.69 (the most negative of the three names in this batch).

My own cross-check: annualizing the latest quarter (Q2 2026 net income $587m × 4 = $2,348m) against average equity (~$26.2bn) gives a run-rate ROE of ≈9.0% [Corrected 2026-10-06: on common equity the run-rate is about 9.2% (net income to common $554M x 4 / ~$24.1bn); company ROTCE was 13.9% in Q2 and 12.2% in Q1] — up from the 8.1% trailing-5yr actual V1 cites, confirming the improvement is real and recent, but still short of the 10.1% the market's current P/B multiple implies is sustainable. Implied vs. base: above [Corrected 2026-10-06: confirmed on the bank-appropriate P/TBV-ROTCE method: at 1.71x tangible book, 3% growth and a 9.7-10.7% cost of equity (5.17% 10-year Treasury + 1.0-1.2 beta x 4.5% ERP) the price needs a sustainable ROTCE of about 14.5-16.2% against 13.9% in Q2 and 13.05% for H1] (i.e., I agree with V1's direction, not its full magnitude of pessimism) — the price is running slightly ahead of delivered profitability, but the guided NIM path (322–327bp → 330–350bp by 4Q27) plausibly closes most of that gap within 12–18 months if private-bank scaling continues on its current trajectory. This is squarely the "great business priced for more than it can deliver — right now" case the mandate calls out: I am not calling the thesis broken (hence not REJECT), but I am also not paying up today for ROE the bank has not yet printed (hence WATCH, not INCLUDE/INCLUDE-SMALL).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: 1. NIM guidance is rising, not just stabilizing (322–327bp 4Q26 → 330–350bp 4Q27), a rare explicit forward multi- quarter margin-expansion guide from a regional bank management team. 2. The private bank is scaling with real, discrete metrics (>$16bn deposits, >$10bn wealth AUM, >25% segment ROE) and is still a small share of the firm (~10% of Q1 2026 pretax income) — plenty of runway if the mix shift continues. 3. Capital return (buybacks) is steady and CET1 is being managed toward a stated ~10.5% target rather than either hoarded or drawn down recklessly.

Bear: 1. On my own math the stock already prices in more ROE (~10.1%) than the bank is currently delivering (~9.0% run-rate) — if the NIM guide slips even modestly, the multiple has limited cushion. 2. Long-term debt is up ~45% in nine months (Sep-25 to Jun-26); the funding mix behind the private-bank build-out and balance-sheet growth was not fully diagnosed this pass and could carry a cost-of-funds risk if rates move against the bank. 3. CET1 at 10.4% is adequate but not a fortress buffer for a bank simultaneously growing its balance sheet, buying back stock, and funding a wealth-management build-out — any credit-cycle deterioration (e.g., CRE, consumer unsecured) would compete with capital-return plans.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Run-rate ROE (annualized quarterly net income ÷ average stockholders' equity) fails to reach 9.5% by Q4 2026 — i.e., the guided NIM path does not translate into the ROE convergence the current 1.06x P/B implies is coming.
  2. CET1 ratio falls below 10.0% (below management's own stated near-term floor).
  3. NIM in any quarter comes in below the low end of the company's own guided range (322bp for 4Q26; equivalent threshold for later quarters).
  4. Private-bank deposits or wealth AUM growth stalls (flat or down quarter-over-quarter) for two consecutive quarters — a direct read that the core growth engine has stopped scaling.
  5. Long-term debt/total assets ratio continues rising for two more consecutive quarters without a disclosed, understood funding rationale (currently unexplained in this pass — see §6).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026, estimated mid-October 2026 (based on the historical reporting pattern — Q3 2025 was reported mid-October with the 10-Q filed 2025-11-03); not independently confirmed against a specific company press release in this pass — treat as an estimate, not a confirmed date.
  • Continued quarterly NIM prints against the 322–327bp (4Q26) guide are the single most decision-relevant near-term catalyst for this name.

11. Red-flag scan

  • No restatement, auditor change, going-concern language, SEC/DOJ investigation, or short-seller report was identified in the sources reviewed this pass — but this was not an exhaustive 10-K risk-factor or Form 4 pattern read within the time budget, so absence of evidence here is not strong evidence of absence.
  • The private-bank build-out itself is a concentration/execution risk worth naming even though it is not a "red flag" in the traditional sense: a large share of the forward ROE story depends on a business line built almost entirely since 2023 around a specific hiring cohort (ex-First Republic bankers), which is inherently less tested through a full credit cycle than the legacy retail/commercial book.
  • Long-term debt growth (§6) is flagged as an open item needing a primary-source explanation, not yet a confirmed red flag.

12. Data basis, recency and disclaimer

Most recent period incorporated: SEC XBRL companyfacts for CIK 0000759944 include data through the 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, filed 2026-08-03 — this ticker's XBRL was current as of this research pass (unlike BIIB and C, whose most recent quarters had to be pulled directly from the filed 10-Q's financial-statement R-pages because companyfacts lagged). dossiers.CHD:
Church & Dwight Co., Inc. (CHD) - Fundamental Diligence Dossier (F132, standard depth)

Verdict: WATCH, 12-36 month horizon. Reason: a high-quality, volume-led consumer compounder whose organic growth has genuinely re-accelerated (5.0% in Q1 2026, 5.8% in Q2 2026), but at 25.5x the 2026 adjusted EPS guide midpoint the price already discounts roughly the growth management is guiding to, and the guide needs a steep back-half EPS ramp (Q4 adjusted EPS of about $1.01-1.08 versus $0.86 a year ago). Condition that would change it: a pullback toward about $85 (about 22x guided EPS, implied FCF growth near 3-4%), or delivery of the Q3/Q4 ramp. The triage (Q03, advance=false) reached the same conclusion, but one of its stated reasons ("1.6% revenue growth") was wrong: reported sales growth is depressed by 2025 brand exits; organic growth is 5.8%.

1. Business in plain English

CHD sells everyday consumer brands: ARM & HAMMER (baking soda, cat litter, laundry), OXICLEAN, TROJAN, BATISTE, WATERPIK, and fast-growing acquired brands THERABREATH, HERO, TOUCHLAND and (from 28 May 2026) MISS MOUTH'S. About 75% of sales are Consumer Domestic, about 19% Consumer International and about 5% a Specialty Products (baking-soda-based chemicals and animal nutrition) division. Sold mainly through retail and e-commerce (global online sales were 25.5% of consumer sales in Q2 2026); moat is brand equity, number-one or -two category positions and a productivity programme that funds marketing. It is a low-beta (Yahoo beta 0.47) cash-generative staple, but it competes with much larger P&G, Colgate and Unilever.

2. Why the model likes it / durability

Quant context (d4 snapshot, 25 Sep 2026 close, price $96.38): ROE 17%, low volatility, FCF yield about 4.7%, forward P/E 23.9x on Yahoo forward EPS $4.04 (a next-year figure; the company's 2026 adjusted EPS guide is $3.74-3.81). The appeal is stability and quality, not cheapness. Durable: yes, but Yahoo trailing FCF ($939M) differs from the filings (see section 6), and headline revenue growth of 1.6% understates the underlying trend because 2025 exits (VMS, Flawless, Spinbrush, Waterpik showerheads) removed about $400M of revenue.

"Cash flow from operations is now expected to be approximately $1.175 billion (previously $1.150 billion)". Raised. Q3 outlook: "adjusted EPS is expected to be approximately $0.89 per share, an increase of 10% versus last year." Record: four consecutive quarters at or above outlook (Q3 2025 outlook $0.72 vs $0.81; Q4 2025 beat; Q1 2026 $0.92 vs $0.95; Q2 2026 $0.88 vs $0.89). Weak spot: Q4 2025 organic growth of 0.7% missed the about 1.5% outlook ("lower than the Company's outlook of approximately 1.5%"). Phasing check: 2026 adjusted EPS guide $3.74-3.81 less H1 $1.84 less Q3 guide $0.89 leaves $1.01-1.08 for Q4, versus $0.86 in Q4 2025 (+17% to +26%).

5. Earnings quality and balance sheet (entity scope: consolidated unless stated)

  • Debt, consolidated, 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 release condensed balance sheet): short-term borrowings $49.9M plus long-term debt $2,206.3M (carrying) = $2,256.2M; cash $254.8M; net debt about $2.0B. Net debt/EBITDA about 1.5x (my estimate: net debt $2.0B over TTM operating income $1,088M plus about $250M D&A; Yahoo EBITDA $1,355M). Consolidated stockholders' equity $4,347.8M.
  • Cash conversion: FY2025 operating cash flow $1,215.4M less capex $122.4M = FCF $1,093.0M versus GAAP net income $736.8M (148%; 127% of company non-GAAP adjusted net income of $861.9M, not a GAAP figure). TTM FCF about $1,115M (FY2025 plus H1 2026 $399.8M less H1 2025 $377.5M). 2026 guide implies CFO $1.175B less about $130M capex = about $1.045B, i.e. FCF falls about 4% in 2026 on working capital for Touchland/Miss Mouth's.
  • Buybacks: $900M in 2025; none in H1 2026; $228.9M remains under the 2021 programme (10-Q). H1 2026 cash used for Miss Mouth's ($300.0M at close plus $25.0M deferred) and $180.5M of earlier acquisition liabilities (Touchland). Diluted shares 238.2M (Q2 2026) versus 246.4M a year earlier.
  • SBC (non-cash compensation) $42.6M in H1 2026, about 1.4% of sales; GAAP-to-adjusted gap is mostly Touchland restricted stock ($0.10 a share in 2026 forecast reconciliation), ERP costs ($0.03) and, in 2025, VMS impairments.
  • Goodwill $2,649.9M and trade names/intangibles $3,743.1M against equity of $4,347.8M (consolidated): acquisition-heavy, but the 10-Q says annual goodwill test "estimated fair value substantially exceeded the carrying values".

6. Valuation and reconciliation (no V1 row for CHD; v1_verdict null)

Price $96.38 (25 Sep 2026 close), about 237.2M shares, market cap about $22.9B; EV about $24.9B (market cap plus consolidated debt $2,256M less cash $255M). P/E 25.5x on 2026 adjusted EPS guide midpoint $3.775; FCF yield about 4.5% on TTM FCF $1,115M (about 4.2% on the 2026 guide). [Corrected 2026-10-06: those yields are on enterprise value; on the $22.9B market cap the TTM FCF yield is 4.9% and the 2026-guide yield about 4.6%] Data conflict: Yahoo FCF $939M versus $1,115M from filings (reason not established; filings are the record). Reverse DCF (cost of equity 8.5%, terminal growth 3%, growth fading linearly over 10 years, start FCF $1,115M): the price implies about 5.1% annual FCF growth for ten years (2.7% at 7.5%; 7.1% at 9.5%). My base case is about 6% (organic growth 4-5% in 2026 fading to 3-4%, modest margin expansion, bolt-on M&A funded from FCF); bear 3%, bull 8%. Implied versus base: in_line, leaving no margin of safety for a miss. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the start FCF does not deduct stock-based compensation (TTM $70M); on FCF after SBC ($1,045M) the implied growth is about 6.7% at an 8.5% cost of equity, still within about one point of the 6% base] Scenario returns to Sep 2029 (annualised, including dividends of about $1.24-1.36 a year): bear -5.1% (EPS $4.13 at 19x), base +6.0% (EPS $4.62 at 24x), bull +12.1% (EPS $4.89 at 27x).

7. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) Volume-led organic growth of 5.0% and 5.8% with share gains and 22.7% e-commerce growth in Q2; (2) gross margin expansion of 100-120 bps guided for 2026 on productivity and mix; (3) disciplined M&A record (THERABREATH, HERO) that keeps compounding growth brands. Bear: (1) H1 adjusted EPS flat and Q4 needs +17-26%; (2) Touchland amortization, marketing at 11-12% of sales and SG&A above 2025 levels cap margins; (3) FCF guide down about 4% and a 25x multiple with retailer, tariff (IEEPA refunds are one-off, about $15M expected) and Middle East cost exposure.

8. Kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Organic sales growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters (5.8% in Q2 2026).
  2. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guide cut below $3.74, or Q3 2026 adjusted EPS below $0.85 (guide about $0.89).
  3. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA above 3.0x after any acquisition (about 1.5x now).
  4. Adjusted gross margin year-on-year expansion below +50 bps for two quarters (+40 bps in Q2 2026; guide +100-120 bps for the year).
  5. 2026 cash from operations below $1.05B (guide about $1.175B).

9. Catalysts and calendar

Q3 2026 results expected about 30 Oct 2026 (estimate from the 31 Oct 2025 cadence; unconfirmed). Q4 print and 2027 outlook about late Jan 2027. Annual dividend increase announced with Q4 (4% in January 2026).

10. Red-flag scan

No material weakness, restatement or SEC/DOJ matter found in the 10-Q text searched (legal proceedings note is generic: "purported consumer class actions, employment matters, antitrust"). Pending deals: none open; Miss Mouth's closed 28 May 2026, VMS divestiture closed (announced 9 Dec 2025, proceeds $160.3M). Auditor and Form 4 insider pattern not reviewed in the time box. Tariff: the 10-Q notes the 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling and CBP refund process; the company expects about $15M of phase II refunds in H2, which is a one-off.

dossiers.CHRW:
CHRW - C.H. Robinson Worldwide (Industrials / Air Freight & Logistics)

Verdict: WATCH - a good business with verified cost execution, but a price that needs a full freight recovery and a $604 million verdict still unresolved. Horizon 12-36 months. Revisit if the Lipe exposure is capped within the $155 million insurance tower and the price nears 17x FY2026E EPS (about $105).

1. Business in plain English

C.H. Robinson arranges truck, LTL, ocean and air freight for shippers using other companies' trucks and ships (asset-light). It earns the spread between what customers pay and carriers charge (adjusted gross profit). Its edge is scale, proprietary technology and a "Lean AI" automation programme (company claims productivity up over 60% since end-2022).

2. Why the model likes it

b1: composite 0.52, live rank 238; quality 0.57, value 0.34, momentum 0.55, SUE 0.91; ROE 39%. Partly durable (headcount down 10.8% with volume up), partly cyclical (Q2 truckload linehaul rate per mile charged +25.5% per the release). Triage Q08: advance false (quality 3, growth 3, price 3). Not overturned.

  • Earnings and margin: none; "mid-cycle operating margin targets" (Q2'26 release) is qualitative.

  • FY2025 OCF $914.5M less PP&E $19.6M and software $50.9M gives FCF about $844M (XBRL; FCF/GAAP NI 144%); TTM to Q2'26 about $618M (OCF $685M less $67.5M). H1'26 OCF $104.5M vs $333.7M: receivables +$704.3M on freight price inflation (cash flow statement, Ex-99.1).
  • SBC FY25 $80.1M (0.5% of revenue, about 3% of adjusted gross profit). GAAP-adjusted EPS gap about $0.05 a quarter, mostly restructuring.
  • Balance sheet 30 Jun 2026 (consolidated, Ex-99.1): cash $154.6M; long-term debt $1,685.0M (10-Q debt table: revolver $325.0M, Nov 2027; receivables securitization $436.8M, Aug 2027; 4.20% senior notes $598.3M, Apr 2028; Series B $150.0M, Aug 2028; Series C $175.0M, Aug 2033); equity $1,627.7M. Net debt about $1,530M, about 1.6x EBITDA (Yahoo $932.6M, cross-check). Covenant: "a maximum leverage ratio of 3.75 to 1.00" (Credit Agreement, consolidated; definition not reproduced).
  • Capital return H1'26: buybacks $432.2M plus dividends $154.3M against OCF $104.5M; net borrowings $595M. Shares 116.85M (29 Jul 2026) vs 118.96M (Mar 2025). DeSpir Logistics acquired 22 Jun 2026 for about $77.8M cash (10-Q Note 15).

6. Valuation and V1 reconciliation

No V1 row exists (v1_valuation_table.csv); v1_verdict null. Price $147.10 (25 Sep 2026); market cap $17.19B; EV about $18.7B. Trailing adjusted EPS $5.59 (26x); FY2026E $6.24 (23.6x); forward $7.50 (19.6x) (Yahoo consensus, cross-check). FCF yield 3.6% (TTM $618M). Reverse DCF (9% discount, 3% terminal, growth fading over 10 years, equity-level, starting FCF $700M): implied 11.7% 10-year FCF growth (8%: 7.1%; 10%: 15.7%). My base is about 10% fading, so implied is above base. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the $700M starting FCF is above TTM FCF of $618M and stock-based compensation ($80.1M in FY2025) is not deducted; on about $620M after SBC the implied growth at a 9% discount rate is about 14.7%, and the 9% rate is below 5.17% 10-year Treasury plus an equity risk premium for a beta near 1.0-1.1 (9.7-10.1%); all three move the implied figure further above base] Scenarios (3y annualised total return): bear -14.0%, base 7.0%, bull 21.1%. Basis: Start: FY2026E adjusted EPS $6.24 (Yahoo consensus, cross-check), price $147.10, dividend $2.52/yr. Base: EPS about $8.6 in Sep 2029 (+10%/yr), exit 20x, dividends about $8 over 3y. Bear: EPS $6.0, exit 15x, less about $3.8/share uninsured Lipe loss. Bull: EPS $11.0, exit 23x.

7. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) 13 straight quarters of NAST volume outgrowth vs the Cass index with headcount down 10.8%; (2) operating leverage when the truckload cycle turns, with mid-cycle margins already reached in a trough; (3) large buyback capacity. Bear: (1) Lipe exposure up to $604M joint and several vs $155M insurance; (2) Q2 profit helped by price inflation while cash was consumed by working capital and returns were debt-funded; (3) 26x trailing earnings for an unguided cyclical.

8. Risks and kill criteria

  1. Adjusted gross profit per NAST truckload shipment falls year-over-year for two consecutive quarters while NAST volume growth trails the Cass Freight Shipment Index (market-share thesis broken; source: quarterly earnings release NAST table).
  2. Consolidated debt (10-Q debt footnote: revolver + receivables securitization + senior notes, carrying value) exceeds 2.5x trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, versus about 1.6x at 30 Jun 2026 (Yahoo-derived EBITDA, cross-check only).
  3. Lipe v. Lupus Superior (Dallas County) is entered as a final judgment of $300 million or more against C.H. Robinson and is not stayed or bonded within insurance limits, or a settlement/accrual above the $155 million per-occurrence insurance tower is disclosed.
  4. Quarterly adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP, release reconciliation) is below $1.25 in any quarter of 2027, i.e. no step-up from the Q4 2025 level of $1.23 (earnings power not rising despite claimed productivity gains).
  5. Net cash from operating activities (10-Q cash flow statement, consolidated) is below $250 million for full-year 2026, meaning the working-capital build is not reversing while buybacks and dividends continue to be debt-funded.

9. Catalysts and calendar

Q3'26 earnings about 28 Oct 2026 (estimated); Lipe post-trial motions and entry of judgment (dates not in filings); Cass index and tender rejection data.

10. Red-flag scan

Litigation: Lipe (10-Q Note 7: jury verdict dated 23 July 2026, accident March 2021; company "intend[s] to appeal immediately if it is entered as final"). The 8-K of 2026-07-24 (Item 7.01) was not opened. No restatement or material weakness noted on a brief read of 10-Q Item 4. Auditor changes, Form 4 pattern and short-seller reports were not reviewed this pass. One web summary calls the verdict "advisory"; the 10-Q does not. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the company's own 8-K of 2026-07-24 (acc 0001193125-26-315034, Item 7.01) calls it an 'advisory verdict ... subject to post-trial proceedings before the court enters a final verdict', so the web summary was right; the 10-Q also says 23% of the $604M was attributed to C.H. Robinson, with joint and several exposure for the whole amount]

dossiers.CHTR:
CHTR — Charter Communications (Spectrum cable / broadband) — diligence dossier F121

1. Verdict: WATCH. The equity looks very cheap on cash flow (about 27% pro forma free-cash-flow yield on my estimate) but it is now a thin slice (about 14% of enterprise value) on top of roughly $110bn of debt, revenue and EBITDA are shrinking at an accelerating rate, the first combined Charter+Cox quarter has not been reported, and the CFO resigns on 15 Oct 2026. Horizon 12–36 months. Condition to upgrade to INCLUDE-SMALL: Q3-2026 results (expected late Oct, date not yet announced) show legacy-Charter Adjusted EBITDA decline no worse than 3% year on year, combined free cash flow at or above $1.0bn per quarter, and a 2027 capex guide that steps down from $11.4bn. This confirms the quick triage (not advanced) but for different reasons: the triage used a pre-Cox share count and a "2.7x P/E" that no longer describes the company.

2. Business in plain English. Charter sells broadband internet, mobile phone lines, TV and phone to about 31.5m US homes and businesses under the Spectrum brand, mostly on its own cable network. Revenue is subscriptions (Internet $5.8bn and Video $3.1bn of Q2-26 revenue of $13.5bn) plus business services and advertising. Its moat is a local-monopoly-like cable plant passing 59m premises, scale in mobile (12.5m lines via Verizon's network) and bundling; the threat is fixed-wireless and fibre overbuild taking broadband customers and video cord-cutting. 1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight; thesis horizon 12-36 months). The market price of $272.01 discounts a shrinking cash-flow stream (about -2% a year for ten years) for a company that has raised its 2026 adjusted EPS floor twice this year and whose medical-cost ratio is inside its guided range. Research only; not personal advice.

Triage reconciliation. Quick triage (CI row: "Insurer/PBM (Evernorth), cheap on trailing multiples"; "Sector MLR pressure; PBM regulatory scrutiny"; model-gated not advanced). Cigna Healthcare sells employer-funded medical plans, stop-loss, and international health cover at 10-13% pre-tax margins. Scale in PBM and specialty drugs is the moat; client concentration and politics are the weakness.
