ECHO - EchoStar Corporation (F143, wave 8 standard-depth diligence; filing ticker SATS)

1. Verdict: WATCH (event-driven special situation, not a fundamental compounder). The equity is now mainly $14B of post-AT&T cash plus a fixed-price claim on about 262M SpaceX shares due around 30 Nov 2027, inside a group with two subsidiary bankruptcies and unquantified cash taxes. Market price implies a SpaceX value of about $87 a share against my base of $100 (hence "below") [Corrected 2026-10-08: $87 is a present value, $100 a Nov-2027 price; discounted at 9.67% the base is $89.7, so in_line, not below], but that base rests on SpaceX marks that are not in any filing, so I will not size it as a full position. Horizon 12-36 months (closing date of the SpaceX leg is the key event). Confirms the quick triage's "event-driven" framing and overturns its "legacy net debt/EBITDA 8.6x" red flag: that data card pre-dated the 28 Jul 2026 closing and the 30 Jun 2026 deconsolidation.

Condition that would move it to INCLUDE-SMALL: (a) an audited cash-tax figure for the AT&T and SpaceX gains below $4B in total, (b) bankruptcy court confirmation of the DISH DBS plan and the Hughes (HSSC) plan with no parent claims above $1B, and (c) a public SpaceX price that, after any lock-up, supports at least $100 a share.

2. Business in plain English

EchoStar owns Boost Mobile (a hybrid MNO/MVNO on AT&T's network, post-sale), Hughes (satellite broadband and enterprise/government networks; HughesNet), and, until 30 Jun 2026, DISH pay-TV and Sling (DISH DBS) and the legacy 5G network. It sold spectrum: 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz to AT&T (closed 28 Jul 2026) and AWS-4/H-block/AWS-3 to SpaceX (transferred to a trust on 22 May 2026; final acquisition closing "targeted for November 30, 2027"). Control sits with the Ergen family through Class B (131.3M Class B vs 159.1M Class A shares at 21 Jul 2026, 10-Q cover); I did not verify the voting ratio.

3. Why the model likes it (b1)

It does not: rank 287 (decile 5), Quality fam_Q 0.12 and Value fam_V 0.07 (ep -17.9%, ebit_ev -34%), but Momentum 0.80 and Shareholder/Sentiment 0.92 lift it. That is a re-rating of an asset-value story, not earnings. The b1 card uses pre-deconsolidation, pre-closing data, which is why it looks distressed.

5. Guidance track record

No numeric guidance: the 10-Q (acc. 0001104659-26-089370) and the 8-Ks contain no revenue, EBITDA or cash-flow outlook, and EchoStar does not hold earnings-release guidance. I have not inferred a range. The only forward commitments are contractual (SpaceX closing "targeted for November 30, 2027"; DBS plan emergence "targeting ... the second half of 2026"; both from 10-Q Notes 2-3).

6. Earnings quality, capital and balance sheet (entity scope labelled)

Consolidated balance sheet, 30 Jun 2026, 10-Q "Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets" (DBS and DISH Wireless deconsolidated): cash and equivalents $440M; current restricted cash/securities $1,056M (of which $1,051M is DBS advances held for vendor payments, matched by a liability); marketable securities $56M; regulatory authorizations held for sale $16.8B (AT&T licenses, sold 28 Jul); remaining regulatory authorizations $17.1B (mostly the SpaceX spectrum); total assets $39.4B; debt, finance lease and other obligations $17.4B (current $1.45B + long-term $15.99B); deferred tax liabilities $3.4B; EchoStar stockholders' equity $14.2B. Consolidated debt table (Note 10, carrying amounts): 10 3/4% Secured 2029 $5,506M; 6 3/4% Secured 2030 $2,373M; 3 7/8% Convertible Secured 2030 $1,943M (fair value $6,045M; about 58M shares); 11 3/4% Secured 2027 $3,500M (redeemed 28 Jul 2026); DISH 2021 Intercompany Loan 2028 tranche $2,844M (repaid 28 Jul 2026); Hughes Satellite Systems (HSSC, subsidiary): 5 1/4% Secured 2026 $627M and 6 5/8% 2026 $750M, both due 1 Aug 2026 and unpaid. The "Seller Notes" (10 3/4%, 6 3/4% and the convertible) total $9.821B and are to be paid off from the SpaceX consideration. AT&T closing (8-K 0001415404-26-000035, 28 Jul 2026): "Seller received proceeds of $20,250,000,000 and an additional $2,400,000,000 was deposited by the Buyer into the mandated FCC Trust". Uses: "approximately $3.686 billion outstanding (inclusive of early redemption premium and accrued but unpaid interest) of the 11 3/4% Senior Secured Notes ... was redeemed in full"; the $2.844B intercompany loan was settled to DBS, which repaid its $2.0B 7.75% notes (8-K Item 1.02). SpaceX leg (10-Q Note 2): total consideration about $20B, "up to $11 billion to be paid in SpaceX's Class A common stock", "approximately 261.8 million shares ... at a fixed value of $42.40 per share"; interim debt service of about $2B is advanced by SpaceX and cancels at closing; $828M of it already recorded as a long-term liability to be recognised as a gain on closing. Bankruptcies: DISH DBS and DISH Wireless filed prepackaged Chapter 11 on 30 Jun 2026 (RSA supported by holders of "more than 88%" of DBS notes). Hughes (HSSC) and 11 subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on 2 Aug 2026 (8-K 0001415404-26-000038, filed 3 Aug): "constitutes an event of default under the applicable indentures ... which results in automatic acceleration". Retained equity in the deconsolidated subsidiaries was measured at a fair value of "$0" (10-Q Note 3; net liabilities $11.4B). ECHO is bidding for the DISH Wireless assets as stalking horse (Section 363) with up to $85M of DIP claims to credit bid. Taxes: the 10-Q says the deconsolidation gain "is not currently taxable"; it does not quantify cash taxes on the $22.65B AT&T proceeds or the $20B SpaceX consideration. This is the largest unverified number in the valuation. Share count: 290.5M basic (159.1M A + 131.3M B) plus about 58M convertible shares = about 348.6M diluted; the 10-Q reports 351.6M diluted weighted shares for Q2 26. Repurchase authorization extended on 30 Jul 2026 (10-Q item 2). Stock comp is small ($10M in Q1 26).

7. Valuation (no V1 row, so v1_verdict = null)

Price $90.11 (b1, 25 Sep 2026); fully diluted market cap about $31.4B (348.6M x $90.11); b1 shows $31.7B. A DCF of the operations is not meaningful (Boost loses money; Hughes is in Chapter 11; DBS equity carried at $0). Reverse sum-of-the-parts on the equity (my estimates, $B): - Cash at parent/consolidated after 28 Jul: 0.5 (30 Jun free cash) + 20.25 (AT&T) - 3.69 (11 3/4% notes) - 2.84 (intercompany loan to DBS) = 14.2. - Less estimated cash taxes on AT&T gain (assumption $2.7B; not disclosed), ops burn (assumption $1.0B over 3 years): net about 10.5. - SpaceX leg: surplus cash after paying the non-convert Seller Notes about +1.1, less assumed tax on the SpaceX gain about -3.0, giving about -1.9; total fixed adjustments 8.6. - Equity value = 8.6 + 0.2618 x (SpaceX price per share). At the contractual $42.40 that is $19.7B ($56.5 a ECHO share); at $100, $34.8B ($99.8); at $149, $47.6B ($136.6). - Reverse DCF equivalent: the market cap of $31.4B implies a SpaceX price of about $87 a share (range $79-$95 if taxes and burn are off by +/- $2B). SpaceX is private; the web sources I searched (analyst commentary, unverified) cite about $149-$201, which would be 70-130% above the price implied here. Those figures are not in any filing and are not used as primary evidence. Scenarios (3-year annualised total return, no dividends): bear -14% (SpaceX valued at the contract $42.40, taxes as assumed), base +3.5% (SpaceX $100, about two-thirds of the highest private marks), bull +15% (SpaceX $149). Basis: equity = $8.6B + 261.8M x P over 348.6M diluted shares; start $90.11; no dividend. Implied ($87) is below base ($100) by 13%, within the error of the tax and burn assumptions; I therefore label it "below" but WATCH.

8. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) $14B of cash already in hand with all secured holding-company debt above it retired; (2) 261.8M SpaceX shares at a contractual $42.40 that secondary-market commentary values several times higher; (3) Hughes and DBS restructurings remove the largest liabilities while DBS pay-TV cash flows may return on reconsolidation. Bear: (1) two subsidiary bankruptcies, with a Special Committee (8-K 3 Aug 2026) reviewing "related party transactions between HSSC ... and EchoStar", so claims against the parent are possible; (2) unquantified cash taxes (DTL $3.4B already on the balance sheet); (3) the SpaceX closing is 14 months away, depends on the Seller Notes make-whole period, and SpaceX is not a public price; plus Boost, now hybrid, still loses money (DISH Wireless pre-tax loss $418M in Q2 26 alone).

9. Key risks and kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Cash taxes disclosed for the AT&T plus SpaceX transactions above $6B in total (10-Q/10-K tax note, consolidated).
  2. SpaceX acquisition closing not completed by 31 Mar 2028, or the $11B equity amount cut by amendment (8-K under Item 1.01/8.01).
  3. Bankruptcy court orders or a Special Committee finding that shifts more than $1B of HSSC or DBS claims to the EchoStar parent (docket / 8-K).
  4. Consolidated unrestricted cash plus marketable securities below $12B on the 31 Dec 2026 balance sheet (10-K consolidated balance sheet).
  5. Wireless segment operating loss above $1.0B on an annualised basis after the hybrid transition (10-Q segment table).

10. Catalysts and calendar

Q3 2026 10-Q about 5-6 Nov 2026 (estimated from 6 Nov 2025; not confirmed). DBS plan confirmation and emergence (target 2H 2026), HSSC Chapter 11 milestones, Boost asset sale process, the SpaceX closing (target 30 Nov 2027), any SpaceX IPO.

11. Red-flag scan

Ergen, Carlson and Orban filed 23 Mar 2023, qui tam and state False Claims Act suits on Boost sales tax, FCC review history. Director Paul Gaske resigned from all positions on 28 Jul 2026 (8-K). Bye (3,508 and 5,000 at $89.73-$89.90, 11 Aug 2026); no purchases. Auditor changes and restatements: none found in filings opened; 10-K auditor report not reviewed.

dossiers.ECL:
Ecolab Inc. (ECL) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Verdict: WATCH — thesis horizon 12–36 months if valuation resets. One-sentence reason: a genuine, durable water/hygiene/pest moat with a well-documented raise-not-cut guidance record, now layering on a $4.75bn, debt-funded, 29x-EBITDA bet on AI-data-center liquid cooling (CoolIT Systems) — but at 30–34x NTM adjusted EPS the price already assumes more 10-year growth (≈14%/yr) than this analyst's evidence-based base case (≈9%/yr) delivers, so it is priced for perfection rather than a demand or integration miss.

1. Business in plain English

Ecolab sells water treatment, cleaning, sanitizing and pest-elimination chemistries, dosing/dispensing equipment and digital monitoring services to restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food and beverage plants, data centers and industrial/energy customers worldwide, organized into four segments: Global Industrial (largest, incl. Water), Global Institutional & Specialty, Global Pest Elimination and Global Life Sciences. It makes money on a razor/razor-blade model — installed equipment plus recurring consumable chemistry and service visits — which is small relative to a customer's own operating or downtime cost, giving Ecolab real pricing power and switching costs. In March 2026 it entered a new, adjacent growth vector: data-center liquid cooling for AI infrastructure (CoolIT Systems), extending "water/fluid management" into cooling-as-a-service for hyperscalers.

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1 quant composite is actually weak (composite 0.127, decile 2, live_rank 434 of ~500) — low despite the fundamental quality story, because the model's Quality family (gross profit/assets 0.248 raw) penalizes capital-intensive chemicals manufacturing, and Value (earnings yield 2.7%, FCF yield 2.4%, both raw) and Momentum (12–1m return 4.3%, modest) are unexciting for a stock trading at ~30x. This stock was not surfaced by the quant top-70 gate; it reached diligence via the fundamental triage pass (quality 5/5, growth 4/5), which is itself evidence the quant composite and the fundamental read disagree here (recorded as a data conflict below) — the model sees an expensive, capital-intensive industrial; the analyst read sees a recurring-revenue compounder with real ROE (22.0% TTM) and pricing power. The durable part (customer switching costs, energy-surcharge/pricing pass-through, One Ecolab productivity program) is verifiable in the filed numbers below; whether the CoolIT bet is durable growth or overpaying into an AI-capex cycle is the open question.

3. Last 8 quarters ($M except EPS; GAAP)

4. Guidance track record (last 3 releases; adjusted diluted EPS, FY2026)

  • 20-Mar-2026 (CoolIT deal announcement, Item 2.02 8-K): reaffirmed FY2026 ex-CoolIT guide of $8.43–$8.63 (+12–15% vs FY2025's $7.53).
  • 28-Apr-2026 (Q1 2026 release): MAINTAINED ex-CoolIT guide at $8.43–$8.63, Q2 guide $2.02–$2.12.
  • 28-Jul-2026 (Q2 2026 release, post CoolIT close 2-Jul-2026): RAISED to $8.05–$8.25 (+7–10%), explicitly "higher than prior expectations of $8.03 to $8.23" — the step-down from $8.43–8.63 to ~$8.03–8.23 reflects CoolIT's non-cash amortization and financing costs now being included; we could not locate a discrete interim 8-K disclosing the exact date of that reset within the filings reviewed (flagged, not asserted). Q3 2026 guide: $2.13–$2.23 (+3–8% vs $2.07 a year ago). Net: no outright cut of the underlying (ex-acquisition-cost) operating guide has occurred in the period reviewed; the CoolIT dilution was flagged in advance (17-Mar-2026 press release said the deal would not be EPS-accretive, excluding amortization, until 2028).

5. Moat and competition

  • Switching costs & recurring revenue: equipment/dosing systems plus consumable chemistry create high switching costs versus commodity chemical suppliers; pricing has offset commodity-cost inflation for 8+ consecutive quarters per company commentary.
  • CoolIT Systems acquisition (data-center liquid cooling): agreed 20-Mar-2026 for $4.75bn cash, "29x and 24x estimated next-12-month and 2027 adjusted EBITDA" (company's own figure); CoolIT ~$550M revenue base; closed 2-Jul-2026. Expected to lift Global Water organic growth by 2pts and total company organic growth by 1pt beginning one year after close; doubles Ecolab's "Global High-Tech" addressable market from $5bn to $10bn. This is the single largest strategic and valuation swing factor in the name — a genuine new growth engine if AI data-center buildout continues, a rich (29x EBITDA) and dilutive-through-2027 bet if it slows.
  • Ovivo Electronics (semiconductor ultrapure water), closed 16-Dec-2025 for $1,596M net of cash — a second, smaller adjacent-growth deal in the same 12-month window; together the two deals add ~$6.3bn of debt-funded M&A.
  • Competitors include Diversey/Solenis (institutional cleaning), Veralto (formerly Danaher water) and, in the new cooling business, established thermal-management players (Vertiv, Schneider) — Ecolab is a scale challenger there, not the incumbent.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) FCF (OCF $3,056.8M − capex $1,182.3M) ≈ $1,874.5M; FCF/TTM NI (~$2,116.4M) ≈ 89% — good conversion. Data conflict: the d4 vendor snapshot shows TTM FCF of only $1,474.8M (FCF yield 1.88%), ~21% below this analyst's XBRL-derived figure; the OCF component reconciles exactly to the vendor field (both $3,056.8M), so the gap is in the capex or timing convention used by the vendor — flagged, primary filings used throughout this dossier.
  • SBC: not separately quantified in this pass (time-boxed); flagged as unverified rather than asserted.
  • Balance sheet (consolidated Ecolab Inc., single reporting entity, from the 10-Q "Long-term debt" note): total debt $13,170.8M at 30-Jun-2026 (up from $8,125.3M at 31-Dec-2025) after issuing $5.0bn of senior notes (4.60% 2029 / 4.80% 2031 / 5.15% 2033 / 5.35% 2036) on 29-May-2026 to fund CoolIT; cash $5,135.3M (temporarily elevated pre-close). Net debt ≈$8.0bn at quarter-end; management's own stated target is pro forma net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈3x at CoolIT close, delevering to 2x by end of the second year after close — consistent with our own back-of-envelope (~$12.8bn net debt post-close ÷ ~$4.3bn TTM adjusted EBITDA ≈ 3.0x).
  • Covenants: company states it is "in compliance with all covenants" as of 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q).
  • Share count: repurchased ~1.2 million shares in Q2 2026 (modest, secondary to debt-funded M&A this cycle).

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 systematic valuation row exists for ECL)

Inputs: EV ≈$86.0bn (market cap $78.3bn + net debt); TTM FCF $1,874.5M (primary-source); WACC 8.0% (beta 0.89, ~90/10 equity/debt) [Corrected 2026-10-08: inconsistent with 5.17% Treasury: cost of equity 9.2-9.67%; levered FCF was set against EV]; terminal growth 2.5%; 10-year horizon. Solving for the constant FCF growth rate that justifies the price: ≈14.1%/year for 10 years. Equifax Inc. (EFX) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F64 | As of: 2026-09-25 close ($148.11, d4_live_snapshot.parquet) | Depth: Standard

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (24–36 month horizon), with a specific, named reservation: an open CFPB investigation into data accuracy and dispute handling at Workforce Solutions — the business unit that houses the Work Number database, Equifax's single most important competitive moat — has been running since July 2023 with three civil investigative demands through August 2024 and no disclosed resolution as of the 2026-07-21 10-Q. Fundamentals are reaccelerating (revenue growth +3.8% → +14.3% YoY over the last six quarters), the company has beaten its own quarterly guidance in every recent quarter, and this dossier's own reverse DCF shows the price implies materially less growth than the evidence-based base case — genuinely cheap — but the regulatory overhang on the core data asset, plus two other open legal matters, keeps this from being a full-weight INCLUDE.

2. Business in plain English

Equifax is one of three major U.S. consumer credit bureaus (with Experian and TransUnion), selling credit reports and scores to lenders (USIS segment) and, through its Workforce Solutions segment, operating "The Work Number" — a database of payroll/employment records sourced from employer payroll systems — which lenders, employers and government agencies use to instantly verify income and employment for mortgages, auto loans, background checks and benefits eligibility. Workforce Solutions is the higher-margin, harder-to-replicate asset (44.9% segment operating margin in 2Q26) because building an equivalent payroll-data network from scratch is extremely difficult; USIS is the more commoditized, more mortgage-cyclical bureau business.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q10) called margin and momentum "depressed by the weak mortgage-origination/hiring cycle, not any structural loss of moat," at 15.2x NTM P/E. Independently confirmed and refined from XBRL: quarterly revenue YoY growth has accelerated over the last six quarters — Q1 2025 +3.8%, Q2 2025 +7.4%, Q3 2025 +7.2%, Q4 2025 +9.2%, Q1 2026 +14.3%, Q2 2026 +10.6% (own calculation, differencing 10-Q/10-K XBRL revenue figures) — so the "depressed" framing is becoming dated; growth is clearly re-accelerating, not merely stable. Operating margins (17–20% consolidated over the same period) remain below Equifax's stronger historical cycles, so there is real margin-recovery optionality if mortgage volumes normalize. b1_live_scores.csv, however, shows a much weaker quant picture than the fundamentals suggest: composite decile 3/10, live_rank 394, 12-1 month price momentum −25.4% (percentile 3.8%, i.e. among the worst in the universe) and SUE percentile only 16.7% despite EFX beating guidance every recent quarter (d4: 8 beats, 0 misses in the last 8 reported quarters, avg surprise +4.3%) — a genuine data conflict between weak price momentum/quant scores and strong, accelerating, primary-source fundamentals. Everest Group, Ltd. (EG) — Diligence Dossier (F22, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 18–30 months. Reason: the market is pricing continued, permanent earnings decline (implied 10-year growth is deeply negative — see §7) [Corrected 2026-10-06: the -11.9% figure came from treating EPS as distributable cash with a 4.2% risk-free rate; on the corrected P/B-vs-ROE method (see Re-assessment RA12) the price implies a sustainable ROE of about 9.4%, close to the 10-11% base case, so the market is not pricing a permanent decline] despite two consecutive clean quarters of results since the company capped its worst known casualty-reserve exposure with a $1.2bn reinsurance cover; the reservation is that reserve adequacy is unproven beyond two quarters and premium is still shrinking sharply, so this is a statistically cheap, evidence-supported turnaround, not a proven one.

Thesis (≤25 words): Global reinsurer that twice surprised the market with US casualty reserve charges, now capped its worst legacy exposure with a $1.2bn cover, priced at 6.4x earnings.

2. Business in plain English

Everest is a Bermuda-based global reinsurer and specialty insurer: it takes on underwriting risk from other insurers (reinsurance) and directly insures specialty commercial risks, collecting premiums and paying claims, and investing the "float" between the two. It makes money when premiums plus investment income exceed claims and expenses (a "combined ratio" below 100%). Its competitive position is mid-tier-large among global reinsurers (peers: RenaissanceRe, Arch, Aracle), respected in property-catastrophe reinsurance, but its US casualty/liability insurance book has been the source of repeated, market-moving reserve problems.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

b1 factors: Quality 4, Growth 3, price_vs_growth 5 (highest of the three F22 names — b1_live_scores.csv). Triage: management said no further 2026 casualty-loss-pick adjustment was needed and reported favorable prior-year development in Q2-26; at 6.4x NTM P/E and 14.5% FCF yield the stock is [Corrected 2026-10-06: the 14.5% 'FCF yield' is operating cash flow over market value; for a reinsurer OCF moves with float and premium timing and is not owner earnings. Read with the Re-assessment (RA12) section] "priced for continued reserve problems." This durability read is only partly confirmed: Q1-26 ($33m favorable development) and Q2-26 (no material development disclosed) are clean, but this follows two separate adverse-development events within the prior 12 months (Q4-24 loss quarter and a $478m Q3-25 US-casualty charge), so two good quarters do not yet establish a new pattern — they establish that the ADC (see §6) has removed the tail risk on 2024-and-prior accident years, which is a real, durable de-risking, distinct from the still-open question of new-accident-year adequacy.

5. Guidance track record

Everest gives no formal EPS/combined-ratio guidance. Management's stated focus (Q1-26 and Q2-26 releases) is "underwriting discipline and accelerating capital return" / "profitably developing our Core businesses" — directionally consistent quarter to quarter, not a numeric commitment. Estimate revisions (d4, 2026-09-25): FY0 +3.9% over 90 days (positive), FY1 −1.4% over 90 days (slightly negative) — mixed, consistent with a name where near-term (this-year) numbers are being taken up on the clean Q1/Q2 prints while out-year forecasts remain cautious pending more data.

Shareholders' equity $15,430m (Jun-26) vs $15,461m (Dec-25) — roughly flat, book value per share $398.83 (ex-unrealized-loss adjustment $407.67) vs $379.70 (Dec-25); P/B 0.93x (d4), i.e. the market values Everest below net asset value, unusual for a reinsurer without an active going-concern issue. H1-26 operating cash flow $939m vs H1-26 net income $1,212m (~77% conversion), reasonable for a P&C (re)insurer where investment income and premium timing create normal noise; not a red flag. Adverse Development Cover (ADC) with Longtail Re (effective 1-Oct-2025, Stone Ridge affiliate): $1.2bn of gross limit in two layers ($700m + $500m) above $5.4bn of North America liability subject reserves for accident years 2024-and-prior, with Everest retaining a $100m co-participation per layer and sole claims-handling authority; consideration paid was ~$1.25bn of transferred in-the-money reserves plus ~$122m cash for the second layer (recognized as an incurred loss in Q4-25). This materially caps — but does not eliminate — legacy casualty tail risk; it does not cover new (2025+) accident years, which is where the open question sits. Net investment income improved to $562m (Q4-25) from $473m (Q4-24) on a larger, higher-yielding asset base.

(a third reserve-strengthening event, or premium shrinkage continuing without an offsetting margin gain — i.e., the market's implied path is close to my bear case, not a strawman); bull case +9% p.a. 8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) the $1.2bn ADC caps the single largest known tail risk (2024-and-prior US casualty), and two subsequent quarters (Q1/Q2-26) show clean, even favorable, development; (2) trading at 0.93x book value with a 6.4x P/E, any evidence of stabilization is a large re-rating opportunity — even partial re-rating to 9–10x (still below high-quality reinsurance peers) implies large upside; (3) management is deliberately shrinking the worst-margin business (Global Wholesale & Specialty combined ratio ~95–97%) which should raise the blended margin over 2026–27 even as premium shrinks. Bear: (1) Everest has now had two distinct adverse-reserve or loss events in five quarters (Q4-24, Q3-25) — a base rate of one surprise roughly every 12–15 months is not disproven by two clean quarters; (2) net premiums written down 26.3% YoY (Q2-26) is a large, ongoing top-line contraction that could pressure future scale/fixed-cost absorption even if margins improve; (3) the ADC does not cover 2025-and-later accident years, so if current-accident-year casualty pricing is still inadequate industry-wide (a live industry debate), Everest could face a new reserve problem the ADC does nothing to protect against.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Any new adverse prior-year development charge on North America casualty exceeding $150m in a single quarter (a signal the ADC's 2024-and-prior fix was insufficient or a new-year problem has emerged).
  2. Group combined ratio above 100% for two consecutive quarters (last two: 91.2%, 92.0%).
  3. Net premiums written declines exceeding −15% YoY for three consecutive quarters (currently 2 of the last 2 quarters at −14.7% and −26.3%; a third would signal the shrinkage is not stabilizing on schedule) [Corrected 2026-10-06: only Q2-26 (-26.3%) is worse than -15%; Q1-26 (-14.7%) is not, so the count is 1 of 2, not 2 of 2].
  4. Book value per share (ex-AOCI) declines quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters.
  5. Rating-agency downgrade (A.M. Best/S&P) of Everest Re's financial-strength rating.

Next earnings: 2026-10-28 (Q3-26, per d4 next_earnings_date) — the first anniversary of the ADC's effective date; watch specifically for any 2025-accident-year casualty commentary, since that is outside the ADC's coverage. No SEC investigation or securities litigation specific to Everest Group found in this search cycle. The core red flag is internal to the business, not external/legal: a documented pattern of two casualty reserve surprises within roughly 12 months (Q4-24, Q3-25), which is the reason this is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE despite the statistically compelling valuation.

EIX — Edison International (parent of Southern California Edison)

Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-30). Checked SEC EDGAR filing index for events to 2026-09-25 (no 10-Q/10-K filed after 2026-07-30 as of that date; next scheduled filing is Q3 2026, due around late October) and checked news coverage (Bloomberg via Claims Journal, Courthouse News, Bloomberg Law, CalMatters, Utility Dive) through 2026-09-23. Two EIX 8-K exhibit folders on SEC EDGAR (the Q2 2026 earnings-release exhibits) returned repeated server errors during this research session and could not be opened directly [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: the Q2 2026 Ex-99.1 text release is available, acc 0000827052-26-000058; see Correction section]; the 10-Q itself, which contains the material financial and legal disclosure, was fully accessible and is the primary source below.

Basis: consolidated GAAP (Edison International, the parent holding company, together with its regulated utility subsidiary Southern California Edison, "SCE"), USD millions except per-share. Non-GAAP "core" EPS, where referenced, is labeled explicitly and is the company's own definition.

1. Verdict

WATCH. Re-assess after Q3 2026 earnings (2026-10-27) and any outcome from a possible year-end special legislative session. One-sentence reason: EIX is statistically cheap (P/B ~1.2x, EV/EBITDA ~7.3x, both below typical regulated-utility ranges) with an intact rate-base growth story (~7% CAGR to a $67.9bn rate base by 2030), but it carries a currently unquantifiable wildfire liability — the company's own words are "unable to reasonably estimate a range of losses" for the Eaton Fire — with a statutory shareholder cap ($4.3bn) that can be voided two separate ways, a bellwether trial in January 2027, and a wildfire-liability legislative reform that just failed (triggering a 23% single-day stock decline around 2026-08-31/09-01). This is a case where the range of outcomes is genuinely dominated by a binary legal/regulatory question that neither this analyst nor the company can resolve today — a reason to wait for the next catalyst, not to size a position now.

2. Business in plain English

Edison International is the holding company for Southern California Edison, a regulated electric utility serving roughly 15 million people across a 50,000-square-mile service territory in central, coastal and Southern California (excluding the City of Los Angeles, served by LADWP). SCE earns a regulator-approved return on its "rate base" (approved capital investment in poles, wires, substations and grid-hardening equipment) set by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) through periodic General Rate Cases — revenue and profit are a function of approved capital spending and the allowed return, not of a competitive product market. Competitive position is that of a monopoly franchise utility; the business risk is almost entirely regulatory, political and — as this dossier documents — wildfire-liability risk, not commercial risk.

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

Preliminary quant rank 24 of 503 (composite 0.757; Q 0.728, V 0.942 — very high value/cheapness score, M 0.602 — weak, roughly flat 12-1-month momentum of +3.0%). The Value score is genuinely earned: sourced multiples (below, via valuation.py) confirm EIX trades below typical regulated-utility bands on P/B and EV/EBITDA. This is not obviously a value trap nor obviously a bargain — it is a real, quantifiable discount for a real, currently unquantifiable risk, and the two need to be held apart rather than netted into one score.

Important, quantified limitation of the momentum input: EIX stock fell ~23% in a single day around 2026-08-31/09-01 (its largest one-day decline in over 25 years, per CEO Pedro Pizarro) when a legislative wildfire-liability reform bill (SB 492) died without a vote at the end of the California legislative session. The "12-1 month" momentum factor construction excludes the most recent month — so, depending on the exact calendar-month cutoff used, this shock may sit substantially or entirely outside the window the M score measures. The model's weak-but-not-alarming M=0.602 should not be read as having priced in this event; the spot price and P/E multiples used elsewhere in the model (as of 2026-09-25) do reflect it, but the momentum signal specifically is a poor guide to how fresh and severe this repricing was. Flag this explicitly as a data conflict/model blind spot, not a reason for comfort.

This is a genuine, adversarial finding this dossier ran to ground rather than left unexplained: per the Q1 2025 earnings release's own non-GAAP reconciliation (8-K Ex-99.1, filed 2025-04-29), $908 million after-tax ($2.36/share) of "non-core" items were recorded that quarter (core EPS was a much more pedestrian $1.37, core earnings $528m) — and the dominant piece, per the release's own footnote, is not Eaton Fire-related at all: it is a $1,341 million pre-tax ($966m after-tax) regulatory-recovery gain tied to the TKM Settlement Agreement, which in Q1 2025 authorized cost recovery (through customer rates) of previously-expensed 2017/2018 Thomas/Koenigstein/Montecito wildfire and mudslide claim costs — a much older litigation matter (§11) whose settlement approval happened to land in the same quarter the Eaton Fire ignited, creating a one-time, non-cash, GAAP-only income spike unrelated to Eaton. The operating picture that quarter (core EPS $1.37, up from $1.13 a year earlier) was unremarkable and driven mainly by a TKM-related interest-expense benefit, not the fire. This is exactly why core (non-GAAP) EPS, clearly labeled, is the more useful run-rate metric for this name, and why this dossier treats the GAAP EPS series as noisy. 5. Guidance track record

Sourcing caveat: both of EIX's Q2 2026 8-K exhibits turned out, on retrieval, to be image-based slide decks (a "Business Update Presentation" and an "Earnings Teleconference" deck — confirmed by opening the filings' own document index, accessions 0000827052-26-000058 and -000061), not text press releases, so the guidance table could not be grepped from a primary text source the way it was for the other two companies in this batch [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: Ex-99.1 is a text press release stating the guidance verbatim]. The figures below are therefore secondary-sourced (multiple independent contemporaneous news reports of the 2026-07-30 earnings call — Seeking Alpha and BigGo Finance both report the same numbers) and are flagged aggregator-sourced, cross-corroborated but not independently verified against the primary exhibit rather than stated with full primary-source confidence:

  • FY2026 core (non-GAAP) EPS guidance: $5.90–$6.20, REAFFIRMED (not raised or cut) at the Q2 2026 release — unchanged from prior guidance per these reports.
  • Q2 2026 core EPS reported at $1.54, up 59% YoY from $0.97 in Q2 2025 — versus the GAAP diluted EPS of $1.38 this dossier verified directly from the 10-Q (§4) for the same quarter. The ~$0.16/share GAAP-vs-core gap is real and should be labeled every time either figure is used; this dossier could not independently confirm the exact reconciling items (likely wildfire-related items excluded from "core") from a primary source this pass.
  • Long-term target reaffirmed at the same release: 5–7% core EPS growth, attributed by management to the 2025 GRC authorization and lower interest expense tied to Woolsey Fire cost recovery.

A reaffirmed (not raised or cut) guide, at a modest premium to the 12-month-trailing run-rate implied by Q1+Q2 2026 core EPS, is a genuinely neutral-to-mildly-positive signal on the pure operating business — but it says nothing about the Eaton Fire liability question, which sits outside "core" EPS by construction. Only one data point was obtained this pass (Q2 2026); the full 4-release track record (Q3 2025 through Q2 2026) recommended by the standard template was not completed given the image-exhibit obstacle and time constraints — a follow-up item for the lead.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Eaton Fire accounting mechanics (the central earnings-quality issue for this name): self-insurance recoveries were exhausted as of 2026-02-11. Above a $1.0bn retention, SCE is reimbursed from the AB1054/SB254 Wildfire Fund's "Initial Account," confirmed by the fund administrator as covering the Eaton Fire as a "covered wildfire." For the six months ended 2026-06-30, SCE recorded $511m of gross Eaton Fire wildfire-related claims, fully offset by an equal $511m expected Wildfire Fund recovery — a $0 net pre-tax P&L impact. The statewide fund is reported to have ~$21bn of claims-paying capacity available for the Eaton Fire. This offset accounting is the reason GAAP earnings have not (yet) shown a large, sustained Eaton Fire charge — but it depends entirely on that recovery being realized (§9).
  • The company states plainly it cannot size the total exposure: "While SCE recorded losses related to settlements that have been entered into related to the Eaton Fire, Edison International and SCE are currently unable to reasonably estimate a range of losses that may be incurred in connection with the Eaton Fire." (10-Q, Note 12). This is as close to an explicit "we cannot bound this liability" statement as a filing makes, and is the single fact this whole dossier turns on.
  • Leverage (utility-appropriate reading, not generic D/E): FY2025 total debt (short + long-term, per internal pipeline cross-check) ≈ $43.3bn against equity of $17.3bn — an equity multiplier of ~5.4x, which the utilities-power.md playbook says is normal-to-expected for a regulated network financed against contracted/regulated cash flows, not a red flag on its own. Edison International Parent's own credit-facility covenant caps consolidated debt/total-capitalization at 0.70:1; actual at 2026-06-30 was 0.66:1 — inside the covenant, with limited headroom, per the 10-Q MD&A.
  • Credit ratings, updated for the most recent event: S&P BBB- with negative outlook (downgraded 2025-10-21, citing Wildfire Fund concerns); Moody's Baa2 stable (reaffirmed after SB 254 passed, Sept 2025 — not re-confirmed after the more recent SB 492 failure); Fitch BBB, outlook cut to negative from stable in early September 2026, explicitly "citing the stalled reform push" (SB 492's failure). Two of three agencies now carry a negative outlook; all three sit at the lower end of investment grade, and management itself frames a further downgrade to junk as a real, customer-cost-relevant risk.
  • Preferred stock: EIX redeemed all Series A Preferred Stock and repurchased some Series B in Q1 2026 ($414m + $4m); Series B preferred remains outstanding and can restrict common dividends under its terms.
  • Financing/equity: multiple capital-markets shelf offerings (424B2/424B5 filings) in March 2025, February 2026 and April/May 2026 — type and size were not individually confirmed this pass (not available), a real gap given "equity issuance needs" was specifically flagged as a diligence priority for this name. What is confirmed, from a 2026-09-23 CEO interview (Bloomberg via Claims Journal): management's current public claim is that the $38–41bn capital plan requires no new common equity issuance through 2030, funded instead by cash flow and capital-markets debt. Treat this as management's own claim, not an audited fact — it is inherently contingent on the Eaton Fire liability not exceeding what is already funded/capped, which is precisely the unresolved question in §9.

7. Valuation snapshot

Per the utilities-power.md playbook, a mixed regulated/holdco entity should ideally be valued sum-of-the-parts on EV/RAB or P/B-against-earned-ROE; that full build was not completed this pass given time constraints, so the figures below (from valuation.py, FY2025 financials, price 2026-09-25) are trailing cross-checks, not the primary method:

The discount to typical regulated-utility multiples is real and roughly proportionate to a genuine, unresolved risk — this dossier does not conclude the stock is mispriced in either direction.

8. Bull case and bear case

Bull (3 points, evidence-based) 1. Core regulated-utility earnings power is intact and growing: ~7% rate-base CAGR guided through 2030 to a $67.9bn rate base, under a General Rate Case that already runs through 2028 — a business-model tailwind unrelated to the wildfire litigation. 2. The existing AB1054/SB254 framework has already survived one legislative cycle (SB 254 passed and expanded the Wildfire Fund in September 2025); the Eaton Fire has been confirmed a "covered wildfire," the $1.0bn self-insurance retention is already exhausted (the worst of the direct P&L hit may be behind, not ahead), and management is publicly committed to no new equity dilution through 2030. 3. Valuation already reflects real stress (P/B 1.2x, EV/EBITDA 7.3x, both below typical regulated-network ranges) — the probability-weighted scenario value is modestly above the current price even before crediting any chance of a favorable prudency finding or a successful special legislative session.

Bear (3 points, evidence-based) 1. The company itself cannot bound the liability. The 10-Q's own words — "unable to reasonably estimate a range of losses" — mean neither this analyst nor, on the record, the company can currently size the downside. A bellwether trial is set for January 2027, and "investigators have tied [the fire] to Edison equipment" per contemporaneous reporting, even though SCE's own filing language is more guarded ("likely associated"). 2. The $4.3bn shareholder liability cap can be voided two separate ways: a CPUC finding of "conscious or willful disregard" (a high bar, but not a zero-probability one given SCE's own account of a de-energized line being associated with the ignition), or simple depletion of the statewide $21bn Wildfire Fund — a risk EIX does not fully control, since the fund is shared with PG&E and SDG&E's own wildfire liabilities. A recent, still-live legislative push (SB 492) to add further protections just failed, and Fitch has already moved to a negative outlook citing exactly that failure. 3. Political/regulatory risk is acute and current, not theoretical: the -23% single-day stock move on the SB 492 failure (versus PG&E's -18-26%, depending on source) shows the market treats this as a live, first-order risk, not a resolved historical event — and management's own CEO says a further downgrade to junk would raise customer costs by "hundreds of millions of dollars," implying the company itself views the credit-rating trajectory as fragile.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. CPUC issues (or signals it is likely to issue) a "conscious or willful disregard" prudency finding on the Eaton Fire — this would remove the $4.3bn cap entirely.
  2. Credible signs the statewide $21bn Wildfire Fund is being materially depleted (by this fire, a new fire, or PG&E/SDG&E claims) before SCE's claims are resolved — the second, EIX-uncontrolled way the cap disappears.
  3. Any additional Eaton-Fire-related GAAP charge that is not offset dollar-for-dollar by a Wildfire Fund recovery accrual (i.e., a break in the $0-net-impact pattern seen in H1 2026) — this would signal the recovery mechanism itself is becoming less certain.
  4. A further credit-rating downgrade at any of the three agencies (S&P is already at the lowest investment-grade notch, BBB-, with a negative outlook — the next downgrade step is speculative grade).
  5. Management reverses the "no new common equity through 2030" position — a concrete, checkable statement made on 2026-09-23 that would be a material negative surprise if walked back.
  6. An adverse verdict or damaging evidentiary finding at the January 2027 bellwether trial.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-27 (Q3 2026, 32 days from data cutoff). A possible special California legislative session before year-end 2026 to revisit wildfire liability reform (CEO Pizarro: "a possibility," per the 2026-09-23 interview) — genuinely dated and binary. Bellwether jury trial, January 2027 (first of what will likely be several, covering 8 plaintiffs). Ongoing: SCE's internal review of the fire's cause remains "complex and ongoing" per the 10-Q, so a company-side causation update could land at any time.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Felony liability: the 10-Q explicitly discloses exposure to "felony liability with regards to the Eaton Fire," and states any resulting fines/penalties would not be recoverable from insurance, the Wildfire Fund, or rates (i.e., fully shareholder-borne). This is disclosed as a risk-factor-level exposure, not a confirmed charge — but it is a materially different (and more severe) category of risk than a civil damages exposure and should be tracked separately.
  • Going-concern language: none found; the 10-Q and MD&A liquidity discussion assume continued access to capital markets, consistent with an investment-grade (if weak) rated entity.
  • Auditor changes / restatements / SEC-DOJ matters: none identified this pass.
  • Insider selling pattern: not pulled this pass (FMP insider-trading endpoints hit a session rate limit) — flagged not available, an open item for follow-up.
  • Litigation beyond Eaton: the 10-Q separately discloses ongoing reserved exposure for 2017/2018 Wildfire/Mudslide Events (Thomas/Koenigstein/Montecito-era), including a still-unresolved CAL OES public-entity claim in the "TKM" litigation with a tolled statute of limitations — a smaller, longer-tail item layered on top of the much larger Eaton Fire exposure.

dossiers.EL:
EL — The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.

Most recent period incorporated: FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-19) and the Q4/FY2026 earnings release (8-K Ex-99.1, filed 2026-08-19). Checked SEC EDGAR for events to 2026-09-25: found and incorporated a 2026-09-08 8-K (routine board-nominee disclosure, immaterial to the investment case). Next earnings (fiscal Q1 2027) not yet formally scheduled in the sources checked; estimated late October 2026 by cadence (see §10).

Basis: all figures are consolidated GAAP (The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. and its subsidiaries), USD. EL's fiscal year ends June 30, so "FY2026" = July 2025–June 2026. All headline figures are GAAP/as-reported unless labeled "Adjusted," "Organic" or "Non-GAAP" (the company's own definitions), and the two are never blended into one number below.

1. Verdict

WATCH — overturning the triage's implicit "advance" optimism on valuation discipline grounds, not on business quality. One-sentence reason: the FY2026 turnaround is real and primary-source-confirmed (organic sales accelerating quarter over quarter, FCF nearly doubled, adjusted EPS +24–34% guided for FY2027), but only one fiscal year into it, and the reverse DCF shows the 2026-09-25 price already embeds more sustained FCF growth than a fair base case supports — a great business, one year into proving itself, priced for more than one year of proof can justify. Condition to revisit: two more quarters of organic growth ≥3% and adjusted operating margin tracking toward the FY2027 12.7–13.5% target with no incremental litigation charge.

2. Business in plain English

Estée Lauder makes and sells prestige beauty products — skin care (La Mer, Estée Lauder, Clinique), makeup (MAC, Estée Lauder), fragrance (Jo Malone, Le Labo) and hair care (Aveda) — through department stores, specialty retailers, travel retail (airport/duty-free) and its own e-commerce, mostly outside the mass-market channel. It makes money on gross margins near 73–76%, monetized through a mix of North America/EMEA "The Americas"/"Europe, Middle East & Africa" and Asia/Pacific regions, with mainland China and travel retail (notably Hainan) historically an outsized swing factor. Competitive position rests on brand equity and department-store/travel-retail distribution relationships built over decades; new CEO Stéphane de La Faverie (since 2025) is executing a company-wide restructuring ("One ELC") targeting cost savings and operating-margin recovery after several difficult years.

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

Quant context (b1_live_scores.csv): decile 5 / quintile 3 (mid-pack composite), but momentum 61st percentile and SUE (earnings surprise) 80th percentile — the model is picking up the real, recent earnings beats. Quality-family reads are mixed: ROE 87th percentile (flattered by a genuinely small equity base post-impairments — see §6 — not by superior returns on a normal balance sheet) and asset-growth 40th percentile. Durable: three straight quarters of accelerating organic sales growth (Q1 FY26 +3%, Q2 +4%, Q4 +5% [Corrected 2026-10-08: omits Q3 FY26 at +2%; path was +3, +4, +2, +5, not steady acceleration] — see §4/§5) and FCF nearly doubling YoY are real, filed, primary-source facts, not narrative. Not yet proven durable: the 49% one-year volatility (triage's own flag) and the fact that FY2026's GAAP operating result was still a loss in the final quarter (Q4 FY26, driven by continued restructuring cash charges — see §4) show the turnaround is not yet fully clean even on management's own numbers.

4. Last two fiscal years of results (GAAP, USD millions except per-share)

FY2026 gross profit grew faster than revenue (details in Q4 release), consistent with the mix/cost-savings story management describes.

5. Guidance track record (last four releases)

Q2 FY2026 (2026-02-05) FY2026 organic net sales growth tightened to 1%–3%; adjusted EPS and operating margin raised Raised/tightened

Q4/FY2026 (2026-08-19) FY2026 delivered Adjusted EPS $2.51 (beat the May $2.35–$2.45 guide); FY2027 initial guide: organic sales +3–5%, adjusted operating margin 12.7%–13.5% (raised from a preliminary May 2026 outlook of 12.5%–13.0%), Adjusted EPS $3.10–$3.35 (+24–34% YoY), GAAP EPS $2.52–$2.85 (+100%+ off the depressed FY2026 base) Beat and raised

This is a clean, consistent beat-and-raise pattern across all four of the last releases — the single strongest piece of evidence for the turnaround thesis, and it is corroborated by the accelerating organic-growth print in §4, not just a multiple re-rating.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP vs. Adjusted gap is large and requires care: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS $0.50 vs. Adjusted EPS $2.51 — a $2.01/share gap, reconciled in the filing as $1.83/share of restructuring/other charges plus $0.18/share of securities class-action settlement, net of a small FX item. FY2027 guidance keeps a smaller but still real gap (GAAP $2.52–$2.85 vs. Adjusted $3.10–$3.35), because restructuring charges continue into FY2027 ("vast majority of the full run-rate benefits still expected to be realized during fiscal 2027"). This dossier treats GAAP as primary and Adjusted as a labeled reconciliation, per the sector playbook — never the reverse.
  • FCF conversion improved sharply: FY2026 operating cash flow $1,773m (FY2025: $1,272m) less capex $457m (FY2025: $602m) = FCF $1,316m (FY2025: $670m) — FCF nearly doubled YoY, a genuinely strong, primary-source-confirmed cash improvement, not just an accounting narrative.
  • Balance sheet: cash $3,498m (FY2025: $2,921m); long-term debt $6,803m (FY2025: $7,314m) plus ~$503m current portion; net debt ≈ $3,808m. TTM EBITDA ≈ operating income $780m + D&A $796m = $1,576m → net debt/EBITDA ≈ 2.4x, improved from the prior year and moderate for the sector. Stockholders' equity fell to ~$3.9–4.0bn (from a much larger base pre-impairment) — the FY2025 goodwill/intangible impairments (§4) permanently reduced the equity base, which is why ROE now screens unusually high; this is a genuine artefact of past write-downs, not current-period outperformance, and should discount the quant Quality-family ROE score accordingly.
  • Dividend: $1.40/share declared for FY2026 ($0.35/quarter), paid throughout the restructuring — not cut, a modest positive signal on management's confidence in the cash outlook.
  • Litigation/impairment history is real and recent, not merely historical: $159m Talcum-litigation settlement charges (FY2025), $911m Americas goodwill impairment + $375m Asia/Pacific intangible impairment (FY2025), and an $84m loss-contingency (net of insurance) for a pending securities class-action settlement recorded in FY2026 — see §11.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

NTM P/E ~27.3x, trailing GAAP P/E ~189x (distorted by the depressed $0.50 GAAP EPS base — the trailing multiple is not a meaningful cheap/expensive signal this year and should be disregarded in favor of NTM). No V1 systematic valuation row exists for EL in v1_valuation_table.csv — v1_verdict is null; this section is this dossier's own reverse DCF. Method: two-stage DCF (10-year explicit FCF growth + 3% terminal growth) on FY2026 as-reported FCF ($1,316m — no restructuring normalization applied, a deliberately conservative choice given the litigation/impairment history in §6). Cost of capital: CAPM cost of equity = 5.17% + 1.274 (sourced beta, FMP profile) × 4.14% ERP = 10.4%; after-tax cost of debt ≈ 3.7%; weights from EV (10.0% debt / 90.0% equity, EV ≈ $38.0bn = $34.2bn market cap + $3.8bn net debt) → WACC ≈ 9.8%.

Implied 10-year FCF growth at the 2026-09-25 close ($94.47): ≈ 11.7% [Corrected 2026-10-08: recomputed on equity basis with SBC deducted ($1,006m FCF): about 10.0% at 10.4% cost of equity; still above the 7-8% base] (sensitivity: 8.6% at WACC 8.5%, to 13.2% at WACC 10.5% — highly sensitive because FY2026 FCF is still coming off a depressed, one-year-old base).

My base case: ~7–8%/yr — supported by the FY2027 guide (organic sales +3–5%, margin expanding toward 12.7–13.5% from ~10.7–11.0% in FY2026 [Corrected 2026-10-08: FY2026 adjusted operating margin was 11.2%], i.e. meaningful but not unlimited margin-recovery runway versus EL's pre-crisis ~18–20% operating margins) — but clearly below the ~11.7% implied at the central WACC estimate, and below the implied growth even at the low end of the WACC sensitivity range (8.6%). This is the core of the WATCH call: the market is pricing a faster, more complete margin/growth recovery than one year of (genuinely good) evidence can yet support.

Bear/base/bull (3-year annualized total return, dividend-inclusive): - Bear (g = −5%: China/travel-retail relapse, incremental litigation charge, restructuring benefits disappoint): −42%/yr - Base (g = 7.5%): −2%/yr (a directly disciplined result of the price already embedding faster growth than the base case) - Bull (g = 14%: turnaround fully succeeds, margins return to high-teens ahead of schedule): +24%/yr

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: 1. Four consecutive quarters of beat-and-raise, with organic sales growth accelerating each quarter (Q1 +3% to Q4 +5%) — the turnaround has real, improving primary-source momentum, not just a low base. 2. FCF nearly doubled YoY ($670m to $1,316m) while still absorbing $813m of restructuring cash costs — underlying cash generation is stronger than the headline GAAP loss quarters suggest. 3. MAC back to #1 in color cosmetics and travel retail (Hainan) growth resumed double digits per the triage's cited sources — brand-level share gains, if durable, support the margin-recovery thesis independent of macro.

Bear: 1. Reverse DCF: at a fair, sourced-beta WACC, the price already embeds sustained double-digit FCF growth for a decade — a lot to ask of a company one year into a restructuring, with restructuring charges still running into FY2027. 2. Litigation and impairment history is recent and real: $911m + $375m of impairments and $159m of Talcum-litigation charges in FY2025, plus a fresh $84m securities-class-action settlement recorded in FY2026 — this is not a company with a clean recent record, and 49% one-year volatility (triage) reflects genuine, not merely sentiment-driven, uncertainty. 3. China/travel-retail — historically EL's biggest swing factor — must prove durable beyond the quarters reported so far; the FY2027 guide itself flags "a lower base of travel retail shipments in the first half of fiscal 2026" as one of the reasons FY2027 organic growth should look strong in H1, meaning some of the guided growth is a base-effect, not pure demand acceleration.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Organic net sales growth falls back below 3% for two consecutive quarters (it has ranged 3–5% for the last four quarters; [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: last four quarters ranged 2-5% (Q3 FY26 +2%)] a reversal would break the accelerating trend).
  2. Adjusted operating margin fails to reach at least 12.0% for FY2027 (vs. the guided 12.7–13.5%).
  3. Any new goodwill/intangible impairment or litigation settlement charge exceeding $100m is recorded in FY2027.
  4. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.0x (vs. ~2.4x now).
  5. GAAP operating income is negative for two consecutive quarters in FY2027 (it was negative in Q4 FY2026 alone due to restructuring cash costs — a repeat pattern would suggest the restructuring is not on the disclosed timeline).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: fiscal Q1 2027 results — not yet formally scheduled in the sources checked; estimated late October 2026 by the prior three years' cadence (2023/2024/2025 Q1 releases were all on/near Oct 30).
  • Annual meeting of stockholders expected 2026-11-17 (per the 2026-09-08 8-K), at which two new director nominees (Rolex CEO Jean-Frédéric Dufour and Matthew E. Rubel) stand for election — a minor governance catalyst, not fundamental to the thesis.

11. Red-flag scan

Real, disclosed adverse facts, not merely historical: a $84m loss contingency (net of insurance recoveries) for a pending securities class-action settlement was recorded in FY2026 (10-K/earnings release, filed 2026-08-19) — the underlying allegations were not detailed in the sources checked this pass and should be read directly in the FY2026 10-K's legal-proceedings item before sizing any position; a $159m Talcum-litigation settlement was recorded in FY2025; and $1,286m of combined goodwill/intangible impairments were recorded in FY2025 (Americas goodwill $911m + Asia/Pacific intangibles $375m). No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language was found in the FY2026 10-K sections reviewed. Insider Form 4 pattern was not exhaustively reviewed this pass (time-boxed; disclosed limitation, not a clean bill of health).

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), horizon 12–36 months. The 25 Sep price implies only ~3.1% 10-year cash-earnings growth against my base of ~6.5%, because the market still prices ELV as if the 2025–26 medical-cost reset (adjusted net income $7,694m in 2024, ~$33.0 a share derived, -> $30.29 in 2025 -> guided at least $27.00 in 2026) never recovers. Named reservation: ELV's profit now hinges on government-program medical cost trend (Medicaid, ACA, Medicare Advantage) and on an unresolved DOJ False Claims Act suit, and guidance is written as "at least", so a cost-trend relapse would break the case. The quick triage ("neither quality nor growth clears the bar", advance=false) is overturned on price-versus-delivery, not on quality: the business is lower-quality than a year ago, but priced for less.

2. Business in plain English

Elevance is a Blue Cross Blue Shield licensee (Anthem brand; the 10-K says its licences give it "exclusive, and in certain areas, non-exclusive" use of the Blue names in assigned territories) and sells health insurance to ~44.9m medical members (employers, individuals/ACA, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid) and, through Carelon, pharmacy benefit management (CarelonRx) and care services (Carelon Services) sold inside and outside its own plans. Its edge is Blue-brand territory exclusivity plus a vertically integrated pharmacy/care arm; its weakness is that premiums are set a year ahead while medical costs are not.

dossiers.EME:
EME — EMCOR Group, Inc.

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). [Corrected 2026-10-08: verdict now WATCH after FCF-based reverse DCF, see Correction section] Thesis horizon 12–24 months. Exceptional current execution (three consecutive full-year guidance raises, record backlog, 40% ROE, net cash) but the growth driver is a concentrated, cyclical, project-based capex wave (AI/data-center construction), sell-side coverage is thin (7 analysts), and the stock has already re-rated to near the top of its own 10-year multiple range — the reservation is durability of the driver past the next 2–3 years, not current quality.

2. Business in plain English. EMCOR is the largest U.S. mechanical and electrical construction and building-services contractor: it designs, installs and maintains the electrical, HVAC, plumbing and low-voltage systems inside data centers, hospitals, manufacturing plants, and commercial/institutional buildings, and separately runs industrial/facilities-services businesses. It earns fixed-price and cost-plus construction margins plus recurring service/maintenance revenue, with almost no owned real estate or heavy equipment (asset-light). Competitive position: #1 by revenue in U.S. specialty construction, currently the prime beneficiary of hyperscaler/AI data-center buildout because very few contractors are pre-qualified and staffed to execute at this scale and speed.

3. Why the model likes it. b1 percentiles: earnings momentum (SUE) 89th percentile, momentum 54th, quality mixed (leverage percentile not computable — net cash, no meaningful debt; ROE not scored in this snapshot but is 40.3% per Yahoo), value modest (ep 61st, book/price 37th — the stock is not statistically "cheap"). The triage read (revenue +19.8%, ROE 40%, net cash, 21.3x NTM P/E "underappreciated" vs FIX/PWR at 29–34x) is directionally right on quality but the valuation gap versus higher-multiple peers narrowed materially between the 2026-08-18 triage snapshot and today: EME now trades at 20.7x forward P/E (see §7), closer to, not "underappreciated" relative to, that peer set.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet. Per the finance-skills infrastructure/capital-goods playbook, U.S. E&C names should be read on Net Service Revenue-equivalent margin, cash conversion, and backlog quality rather than headline OPM alone; full pass-through/NSR disclosure was not available in the sources reviewed here, so margin figures above are gross (a stated limitation). Cash conversion needs a caveat: operating cash flow was $1,302mm in FY2025, down from $1,408mm in FY2024 despite EPS growth, and Q1 2026 OCF was essentially zero ($0.558mm) before rebounding to a $289.9mm H1-2026 cumulative figure by Q2 — consistent with working-capital consumption (unbilled receivables/contract assets building ahead of billing) as the backlog ramps, which is normal for a growing contractor per the sector playbook but should be watched: unbilled revenue growing materially faster than revenue for multiple quarters is the sector's standard early-warning sign and was not independently verified here (data limitation — would require the segment/contract-asset footnote, not pulled in this pass). Balance sheet is a clear strength: total debt just $548mm vs $924mm cash (net cash) [Corrected 2026-10-08: the $548mm is lease liabilities, not borrowings; no funded debt, cash $924.4M], FY2025 buybacks $586mm and dividend yield only 0.21% (buybacks, not dividends, are the primary capital-return vehicle). No debt-funded acquisition or securitization risk comparable to DPZ's.

7. Valuation snapshot. Price $762.21; market cap $33.6bn; EV $32.79bn (net cash, so EV < market cap). FY2026-guidance-midpoint P/E (EPS $32.63 midpoint) = 23.4x. Forward (NTM consensus) P/E 20.7x; trailing P/E 23.7x. FCF (Yahoo TTM) $978mm → FCF yield 2.9% on market cap, 3.0% on EV — modest, consistent with a business still reinvesting working capital into backlog growth rather than harvesting cash. No V1 row exists for EME (outside the top-70 quant-ranked universe covered by the systematic valuation model), so v1_verdict is null. Own-history context: EME traded in the mid-teens P/E (14–18x) through 2019–2023; the move to 20–24x since the AI data-center buildout began represents a genuine re-rating, now sitting near the top of its 10-year range. A simple reverse Gordon-growth back-out at 20.7x forward P/E and ~9% cost of equity (beta 1.13) implies roughly 4% perpetual growth priced in [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong method: EPS treated as cash and 9% rate below 10.3%; FCF-based two-stage at 9.67-10.3% needs 13.7-15.1% a year for ten years] — but a single-stage perpetuity model understates the right framework here: the correct read is a two-stage model with several years of backlog-driven double-digit growth fading to a GDP-like terminal rate, which a 4%-equivalent back-out is arguably consistent with, not obviously excessive. Given the genuine uncertainty in normalizing a mid-cycle project-construction growth rate, this dossier's view is "fair" (not cheap, not obviously expensive) and implied_vs_base = in_line. [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated to above; verdict now WATCH, see Correction section]

8. Bull case / Bear case. Bull: (1) RPO backlog (+32.9% YoY) provides 2–3 years of revenue visibility even without further order intake; (2) EMCOR is one of a handful of contractors with the scale and pre-qualification to win the largest hyperscaler jobs, a structural (if narrow) moat; (3) net-cash balance sheet gives capacity for further tuck-in M&A or buybacks without dilution. Bull risk flagged as reservation, not dismissed: the same concentration that drives the upside — AI/data-center capex — is the single largest identifiable risk if hyperscaler capex plans are cut or delayed. Bear: (1) Data-center capex is famously lumpy; a pause or reallocation by 2–3 large customers would hit a business now guiding to $20bn+ revenue built partly on that vertical; (2) labor availability and wage inflation are called out by management as ongoing constraints even amid the guidance raises; (3) working-capital consumption (Q1'26 near-zero OCF) could compound if the backlog conversion cycle lengthens.

9. Kill criteria (measurable) -- what would break the thesis. 1. RPO/backlog growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +32.9% YoY as of 2026-03-31) [Corrected 2026-10-08: now +43.9% at 2026-06-30]. 2. Full-year revenue or EPS guidance is cut, breaking the current three-release raise streak. 3. Consolidated operating margin falls below 8.5% for two consecutive quarters (vs 8.7–12.7% range over the last 8 quarters). 4. Net cash position flips to net debt exceeding 1.0x EBITDA. 5. Cumulative operating cash flow over any trailing 4 quarters falls below 50% of cumulative EBITDA over the same period (working-capital/cash-conversion red flag per the sector playbook).

10. Catalysts & calendar. Next earnings: estimated 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29 (Q3 2026; exact date not yet confirmed by company press release as of 2026-09-25 — used 2026-10-27 as the point estimate in the summary JSON, flagged as an estimate).

11. Red-flag scan. No SEC/DOJ investigation, restatement, auditor change, or going-concern language found. As a government contractor EMCOR is routinely subject to U.S. government audits/investigations per its own risk-factor disclosure, but nothing specific to a current material matter was found. Analyst coverage is thin (7 analysts per the live snapshot), which increases estimate/model risk on both sides. No unusual insider-selling pattern identified (insiders hold 0.7% of shares, typical for a long-public industrial).

EOG is a genuinely low-cost, disciplined operator (company-disclosed sub-$50/bbl WTI breakeven covering both its full capital program and its regular dividend) with a successfully integrating Encino/Utica acquisition. The named reservation, and the reason this is not a plain INCLUDE: current TTM and even NTM earnings are elevated by a live, unresolved Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz war oil-price spike (WTI briefly exceeded $110–112/bbl in April 2026 and was still ~$92–93/bbl at this review's cutoff, versus EOG's own realized ~$65–73/bbl in the year before the conflict began). "Cheap on 9x NTM P/E" is a fair headline but should not be read as cheap on a normalized, through-cycle basis. EOG is also now a named defendant in a fresh, unquantified shale-antitrust class action that survived a motion to dismiss three weeks before this review's cutoff.

2. Business in plain English

EOG Resources explores for and produces crude oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas from US shale plays (Delaware Basin/Permian, Eagle Ford, Utica, plus international exploration), selling hydrocarbons at prevailing market/benchmark-linked prices. It makes money on the spread between realized commodity prices and its (low) all-in cost to find, develop and produce a barrel. Its competitive position is cost leadership: EOG has spent over a decade emphasizing "premium" drilling returns and capital discipline over pure production growth, which shows up in its dividend/breakeven framework (section 7).

dossiers.EQIX:
Equinix, Inc. (EQIX) — Diligence Dossier (F32, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 24–36 months. One-sentence reason: the dominant interconnection-density data-center REIT is compounding AFFO/share faster than the price implies, but a capex program that is about to roughly double annual spend (funded partly by more debt/equity issuance) and a residual, if now-resolved, accounting-scrutiny history argue for a starter position rather than full weight.

Thesis (≤25 words): The world's most interconnected data-center network, benefiting from AI/hyperscaler demand, growing AFFO faster than its rich-looking headline P/E suggests.

2. Business in plain English

Equinix owns and operates 270+ carrier-neutral data centers (International Business Exchanges, "IBX") where enterprises, cloud providers (hyperscalers) and network carriers colocate equipment and interconnect directly with each other. It earns recurring rent for cabinet/space ("colocation") plus per-connection interconnection fees — the interconnection business is the moat, since the value of being in an Equinix facility rises with the number of other networks already there (a network effect that is very hard for a new entrant to replicate). It also earns development fees and equity income from xScale, a joint-venture vehicle built specifically to fund hyperscale (large single-tenant) capacity without putting all of that capex on Equinix's own balance sheet.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q13_triage.json) scored EQIX quality 5, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4, flagging net debt/EBITDA of "4.9x amid a $4–5bn/year capex plan to double capacity through 2029" as the key diligence item, and noting the required growth under a simple FCF-yield heuristic (~5.2%) is "well below Equinix's actual mid-teens-to-20% growth trajectory." The pre-registered quant composite agrees and ranks it strongly: decile 8, live_rank 106 of 503, composite 0.79 (b1_live_scores.csv). Quality percentiles are genuinely high (ROE pct 0.71, OCF/assets pct 0.81) and reflect a durable, structurally growing business (AI/hyperscaler demand for interconnected capacity, not a one-off). One caveat on the "value" family score: EQIX's book/price percentile is very high (0.95, i.e. screens "cheap" on book value) — this is a REIT-accounting artefact (real estate carried at depreciated historical cost, not fair value) rather than genuine cheapness, and should not be read as the stock being statistically undervalued on that basis; the momentum score (pct 0.71) and the AFFO-based valuation work in §7 are the more trustworthy reads.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP; source: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK0001101239, cross-checked to 8-K press releases)

Long-term guidance was also raised at Q2'26: 2027–2029 annual revenue growth to 10–13% (from 7–10%) and AFFO/share growth to 9–12% (from 5–9%) — a structural upgrade to the multi-year algorithm, not just an in-quarter beat. 6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

AFFO is the correct cash-flow lens here (GAAP FCF is structurally negative — 1H'26 free cash flow was −$560m, adjusted FCF −$336m — because "free cash flow" as reported nets ~$2.9bn of 1H'26 non-recurring/development capex against $1.78bn of operating cash flow; this is normal for a REIT in a heavy build-out phase and is why AFFO, which separates recurring maintenance capex [~1.6% of revenue] [Corrected 2026-10-08: recurring capex is guided at ~3% of revenue ($290-310m)] from growth capex, is the metric management, analysts and this dossier all use). Key balance-sheet fact validating the triage's own flag: full-year 2026 total capex guidance is now $5.0–$6.0bn, roughly double the prior ~$3.8bn non-recurring-capex run-rate, and the long-term 2027–2029 capex range was raised to $5.0–$7.0bn/year. Total debt principal was $22.15bn at Q2'26 (senior notes $19.69bn) vs $21.42bn at YE'25, funding this build-out; cash was only $979m. Using Q2'26-guided adjusted EBITDA ($5.21–$5.27bn annualized) and net debt (~$21.2bn), net debt/EBITDA ≈4.0x by this dossier's method — lower than triage's cited 4.9x, likely because triage used a trailing (rather than forward-guided) EBITDA base or a gross-debt denominator; both readings agree leverage is moderate-to-elevated for a REIT and will need continued external funding (debt and/or equity) to sustain the capacity-doubling plan, which is dilution risk to per-share AFFO growth if funded disproportionately with equity. Dividend ~$2.04bn expected FY2026 (dividend yield ~1.9%, d4), and management said dividend growth should "approximate AFFO per share growth" going forward.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

Price (2026-09-25 close) $1,008.08; GAAP trailing P/E 65.0x / NTM P/E 54.7x (d4) — both distorted by heavy real-estate depreciation, the classic reason GAAP P/E is the wrong lens for a REIT. The economically relevant multiple is price/AFFO: $1,008.08 ÷ FY2026-guided AFFO/share midpoint ($42.99) ≈ 23.4x, versus FCF yield 3.8–4.2% (d4). Peer DLR (Digital Realty, a direct data-center-REIT comparator) trades at an even richer NTM P/E of 62.1x with a lower FCF yield (5.6% — Yahoo methodology differs from AFFO) and dividend yield 2.7% (d4, 2026-09-25); sell-side mean target for EQIX is $1,233.48 (+22%, d4). No V1 row exists for EQIX → v1_verdict = null; valuation view is independently derived.

Reverse DCF (AFFO basis): EV = market cap $99.47bn + net debt ~$21.17bn = $120.6bn; AFFO₀ = FY2026-guided $4.27bn; WACC 8.3% (cost of equity = rf 4.2% + β0.97×ERP 5% = 9.1%; post-tax cost of debt ≈4.5%; debt weight ≈17.5%) [Corrected 2026-10-08: rf should be the 5.17% 10-year Treasury (25 Sep 2026); AFFO adds back SBC and excludes growth capex; restated Ke 9.5%, WACC 8.8%]; terminal growth 3%. Solving for the 10-year AFFO growth rate that reproduces today's EV gives implied growth ≈7.8% p.a. [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated to ~10.7% p.a. on AFFO less SBC at WACC 8.8%] My evidence-based base case is ~10% p.a. — the midpoint of management's own just-raised, credible (three-consecutive-raise track record) 2027–2029 AFFO/share growth guide of 9–12%. Implied (7.8%) is below base case (10%) → the stock is not priced above what the evidence supports; if anything it screens modestly cheap relative to the newly raised long-term algorithm. [Corrected 2026-10-08: withdrawn: restated implied ~10.7% vs base ~10% is in line] Bear case 4%/yr (AI-capex demand cools, heavy equity issuance to fund the doubled capex program dilutes per-share AFFO growth well below aggregate growth, exit multiple compresses to 18x): 3-yr annualized return ≈ −3%. Base case 10%/yr, exit multiple ~23x (roughly stable): ≈ +11%/yr. Bull case 13%/yr (top of the new long-term range sustained, multiple re-rates to 26x): ≈ +18%/yr.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) the interconnection network effect (record 9,700 net interconnections added in Q2'26, third consecutive quarter of double-digit MRR growth) is arguably the hardest-to-replicate moat among data-center REITs — a new entrant cannot buy its way into an existing web of carrier/cloud relationships; (2) management just raised its long-term (2027–2029) growth algorithm across revenue, AFFO/share and EBITDA margin, backed by record bookings, not merely a forecast; (3) xScale JVs let EQIX capture hyperscale demand while keeping a meaningful share of that capex off its own balance sheet, partially mitigating the funding/dilution risk in §6. Bear: (1) the capex step-up is real and large — guided FY2026 total capex of $5–6bn is roughly double the prior non-recurring run-rate, and it must be funded by some mix of debt (pushing leverage higher) and equity (diluting per-share AFFO growth) for years; (2) a March 2024 short-seller report (Hindenburg Research) alleged Equinix was misclassifying maintenance capex as growth capex to inflate AFFO — a direct challenge to the exact metric this dossier's valuation relies on (§11); although the company's own investigation and the SEC/DOJ inquiries have since closed with no restatement and no enforcement action, the underlying capex-classification judgment calls that prompted the allegation still exist and deserve ongoing scrutiny, not blind trust; (3) AI-driven hyperscaler demand for interconnected colocation, while currently accelerating, is a newer and less-tested growth driver than EQIX's historically stable enterprise-colocation base — a slowdown in hyperscaler capex plans (already debated across the sector) would hit the highest-growth, highest-multiple part of the bull case first.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. AFFO/share guidance cut (a reduction to the low end of the then-current full-year range) at a subsequent quarterly release.
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 5.0x (from ~4.0x currently) without a credible funding plan disclosed alongside it.
  3. Recurring (monthly recurring revenue) growth decelerates below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from 11% currently).
  4. Any restatement of prior AFFO or capex classification, or a new SEC/DOJ enforcement action (distinct from the closed 2024 matter).
  5. Annualized gross bookings decline YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +23% YoY currently).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-28 (Q3'26, per d4 next_earnings_date). Watch for: bookings trend continuation, any update on xScale JV funding/equity stakes, and the pace of the capex step-up (guided $5–6bn FY2026) actually landing within range.

11. Red-flag scan

Material, now-resolved: on 20 March 2024 short-seller Hindenburg Research published a report alleging Equinix engaged in "accounting manipulation" — specifically, misclassifying capex necessary to sustain existing operations as growth/expansion capex to inflate AFFO. The Audit Committee launched an independent investigation (WilmerHale/AlixPartners); Equinix received subpoenas from the SEC (30 April 2024) and the US Attorney's Office, N.D. California. The investigation "didn't identify any accounting inconsistencies or errors that would require an adjustment to previous financial statements" per the company; on 19 November 2025 the SEC notified Equinix it had concluded its investigation with no enforcement action recommended, and the company said it expects no further NDCA action. A related shareholder securities class action was settled for $41.5m. No auditor change, going-concern language, or restatement was found. Read-through: the underlying dispute (recurring vs. non-recurring capex classification) is exactly the judgment call behind the AFFO figure this dossier's valuation depends on — the matter is legally closed but the modeling sensitivity it exposed is not, and warrants continued monitoring each quarter (§9, kill criterion 4).

12. Data basis, recency and disclaimer

Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 10-Q and 8-K ex-99.1, both filed 2026-07-29. Events checked to 2026-09-25 (litigation/regulatory search, guidance history). All figures are consolidated (US GAAP, single-entity reporter, no separate standalone statements filed). GAAP figures are labelled GAAP; AFFO/FFO are Equinix's own non-GAAP measures (industry-standard NAREIT-style definitions) and are labelled as such — never conflated with GAAP net income or EPS.
