7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

Price (2026-09-25 close) $35.41; market cap ≈$18.3bn (d4); EV ≈$38.6bn (net debt ≈$20.5bn). FY2026 P/E on the just-revised guided adjusted EPS midpoint ($6.20) ≈5.7x — very cheap on an adjusted basis, though the wide GAAP-to-adjusted gap (§4) means this multiple should be read with the earnings-quality caveat in mind, not as a clean P/E. No V1 row exists for FIS (checked v1_valuation_table.csv — no row) → v1_verdict = null; valuation view is independently derived.

Reverse DCF: EV = FCF₁×(1+g)/(WACC−g). Using FCF₁ = $2.2bn (FY26 guide midpoint) and WACC ≈8.5% (a CAPM-mechanical WACC using FIS's pre-deal beta of 0.80 would understate the risk of the new, much higher post-deal leverage, so a judgmentally higher 8.5% is used — cost of equity ≈8.2% via CAPM plus a leverage-risk add-on, blended with a ≈4.3% post-tax cost of debt at a ≈53% debt weight), solving for g against EV $38.6bn gives implied perpetual FCF growth ≈2.6–2.7%/yr. [Corrected 2026-10-06: FCF of $2.2bn is after about $0.8bn of interest yet is set against EV, and stock-based compensation ($101M in H1) is added back; unlevered, after SBC (about $2.64bn) the same formula gives about 1.5% a year; still far below the 8-10% base, implied_vs_base stays below, verdict unchanged (DVH5)] My evidence-based base case is ~8–10%/yr over the medium term (synergy capture toward the disclosed $150M+ 2028 EBITDA target, mid-single-digit organic bank-tech growth once Capital Markets stabilizes, and deleveraging-driven interest-expense relief) — well short of management's own implied ~15%/yr FCF path to "$3bn+ by 2028," but comfortably above the ~2.6% the price implies. Implied growth is below base case: this reads cheap even after discounting management's own target for the usual optimism. Bear case (integration stumbles, Capital Markets stays soft, leverage stays near 3.5x for the full window, buybacks stay paused, EPS grows only ~3%/yr, multiple stays at a distressed-adjacent ~4.5–5.7x): 3-yr annualized return ≈ +1–2% (dividend yield roughly offsets a modest de-rating). Base case (EPS compounds ~8–9%/yr as the 2028 targets are partly delivered, multiple re-rates from 5.7x toward 7.5x as leverage nears target and buybacks resume): ≈ +20–21%/yr. Bull case (synergies exceed target, leverage falls faster, multiple re-rates toward bank-tech-peer levels of ~10–11x): ≈ +34–36%/yr.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) The Issuer Solutions/Worldpay swap is a real strategic upgrade — a large, high-margin recurring-revenue processing business replacing a passive minority stake — with management guiding to $150M+ of EBITDA synergies and $3bn+ FCF by 2028, and synergy capture already tracking "ahead of plan"; (2) at ~5.7x guided adjusted EPS and a ~5.7% FCF yield on EV, the market prices in almost no execution success from a deal management itself frames as transformative; (3) FIS's core large-bank issuer-processing franchise shows an "85% win rate" against newer entrants (e.g., Visa's Pismo), evidence the moat (deep, sticky bank-core integrations) is intact even as smaller/fintech-focused rivals target the low end of the market. Bear: (1) Gross leverage of 3.5x (vs. a 2.8x target) is real and current, not hypothetical — it has already forced a buyback and tuck-in-M&A pause, and adjusted-EPS guidance was cut (from 8–10% growth to 7.0–8.5%) just one quarter after the deal closed; (2) disclosed organic softness is current-quarter, not distant risk: pro forma revenue/EBITDA growth guidance was cut 60–150bps, Capital Markets professional-services revenue fell 17%, and UBS/Credit Suisse-related client attrition is cutting ~1 point off 2026 revenue growth; (3) GAAP earnings are dominated by non-recurring items (a $2.2bn one-time gain inflated Q1'26 GAAP EPS to $4.58, while Q2'25 was a GAAP loss of −$0.90/share) — "adjusted EPS" is doing most of the work in the cheap-valuation case, and a resolved-but-relevant $210m securities-fraud settlement (§11) shows the company has previously been found to have over-stated integration/synergy disclosures around a prior (Worldpay) acquisition.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

Any of the following would break the thesis; each is a specific, observable, time-bound signpost to monitor at each earnings release, not a vague worry: 1. Adjusted-EPS guidance is cut again at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release (any reduction to the low end of the current $6.15–6.24 range). 2. Gross leverage fails to decline toward the 2.8x target — stays at or above 3.5x for two consecutive quarters after Q2'26. 3. Client attrition (UBS/Credit-Suisse-style losses) widens beyond the currently disclosed ~1-point drag on 2026 revenue growth. 4. Capital Markets segment professional-services revenue declines for a third consecutive quarter (currently −17% in the most recent disclosed quarter). 5. Share buybacks remain fully paused beyond FY2027 — i.e., management fails to resume "meaningful" repurchases once leverage nears its own 2.8x target, contradicting its own stated plan.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-11-04 (Q3'26, per d4 next_earnings_date). Key things to watch: whether the pro forma organic growth cut stabilizes, Capital Markets segment trend, and any update on the deleveraging path toward 2.8x.

Securities Litigation," M.D. Fla., filed March 2023) alleged FIS and certain officers made misleading statements about the prior Worldpay acquisition's valuation, integration and synergies between May 2020 and February 2023. FIS agreed to a $210M settlement, substantially covered by insurance; the court granted final approval on July 9, 2026. This relates to prior management-era disclosures about the earlier Worldpay deal, not the current Issuer-Solutions/Worldpay-stake-sale transaction, but it is directly relevant context given the current transaction's own integration and synergy claims are similarly central to today's thesis. dossiers.FITB:
FITB — Fifth Third Bancorp — Diligence Dossier (Agent F44, wave 2, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (reservation: Comerica integration is ~60% through a multi-quarter systems/synergy conversion, and the market has already re-rated the stock for a good chunk of the expected outcome). Thesis horizon: 12–24 months (integration completion + synergy realization).

2. Business in plain English

Fifth Third is a Cincinnati-based regional bank that, on 2 Feb 2026, completed an all-stock merger with Comerica, becoming the ~9th-largest US bank by assets (~$294B, per opening-balance disclosure of $86B of Comerica assets added to Fifth Third's prior ~$208B base). It makes money the way any bank does — taking in deposits cheaply and lending them out at a spread (commercial & industrial, commercial real estate, auto, mortgage, and Comerica's historically strong middle-market and wealth franchise) — plus fee income from wealth/asset management, commercial payments, and capital markets. Competitive position: a top-10 US regional with a legacy Midwest/Southeast retail franchise now layered with Comerica's Texas/California/Michigan commercial-banking strength.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q06) flagged +67% forward EPS growth and +52% revenue growth from the deal and an 11.8x NTM P/E. That growth is not organic — it is the arithmetic effect of consolidating a similarly-sized bank via an all-stock deal (diluted share count rose from 669.2M avg (Q4 2025) to 916.0M avg (Q2 2026), +37%). The durable part of the thesis is real: NIM has expanded for two straight quarters (3.13%→3.30%→3.36%) on repricing and deposit-cost discipline, and credit quality improved through the deal (NCO ratio 0.45%→0.37%→0.30%, the best since 2Q23). The artefact risk is real too: ~65% of expected full-year merger charges were already booked through Q2 2026, and the "growth" figures triage cited will normalize to flat/low-single-digit once the merger comparison rolls off.

4. Results — last five reported quarters (GAAP unless noted; FTE = fully taxable-equivalent)

5. Guidance track record

Fifth Third's earnings press releases do not carry quantitative full-year EPS/revenue guidance (typical for large US banks — guidance is qualitative and given on the earnings call, which was not transcribed within this time-box). Qualitative commentary across the three reviewed releases has been consistently constructive and specific: Q4 2025 emphasized standalone momentum ahead of the deal; Q1 2026 said integration was "progressing as we expected"; Q2 2026 said the Comerica systems conversion was on track for Labor Day 2026 (the last major integration milestone) and reiterated the "on-track" synergy language without a dollar figure change. No guidance was cut in the reviewed window. This is a gap, not a clean pass: I could not verify a specific cost-synergy target ($ millions) against delivery because it was never quantified in the press releases I read; flagged as a confidence limiter.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP vs adjusted: Q1 2026 GAAP EPS $0.15 vs an implied ~$0.83 adjusted (reported as "a net negative $0.68 impact from certain items"); Q2 2026 GAAP $0.83 vs adjusted $1.02 (0.19 of certain items). The gap is real and merger-related — not a case of recurring non-GAAP add-backs masking weak organic results — but the size of it (over 5x reported EPS in Q1 2026) means GAAP EPS is not usable as a run-rate for at least two more quarters.
  • Capital: CET1 fell from 10.81% (Q4 2025) to 9.96% (Q1 2026, deal close: $12.3B of common stock issued as merger consideration, $6.2B of goodwill/intangibles created, $73B of RWA added) and has been roughly stable since (9.93% at Q2 2026). No share repurchases in 1H26 — capital is being conserved to rebuild the ratio, a sensible but confidence-limiting signal (management is not yet confident enough in excess capital to resume buybacks).
  • Credit: NPA ratio actually rose slightly (0.57%→0.60% Q1 2026→Q2 2026) even as NCOs fell — a mild, disclosed divergence ("modest growth in consumer and commercial NPAs") worth watching, though ACL coverage remains strong (303% of NPLs).
  • Funding: Average deposits rose $209.4B→$231.5B q/q (Comerica full-quarter effect); consumer deposits +$4.6B, interest-bearing deposit costs down 2bp to 2.13% — funding cost discipline is intact.
  • Debt/capital markets: Routine debt management only in the red-flag window — a senior-notes exchange-offer registration completed 23 Sep 2026 and an early redemption notice (24 Sep 2026) for $500mm of 1.707% notes due Nov 2027, called one year early. Both are ordinary treasury operations, not distress signals (SEC 8-Ks, filed 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24).
  • Share count: diluted shares +37% (669.2M→916.0M) from the all-stock deal — durably dilutive unless synergies close the gap, which is exactly the open question this thesis rests on.

7. Valuation

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for FITB (not yet run by the valuation agent) — v1_verdict is null in the summary JSON; nothing to reconcile against. Own reverse-engineered view: banks are valued on P/TBV, not FCFF DCF (P/TBV = (ROE−g)/(COE−g) is the standard identity; a mechanical FCFF reverse-DCF is inappropriate for a lender per sector convention). At the 25-Sep-2026 close of $52.10 and TBVPS of $23.15, FITB trades at 2.25x tangible book. Solving the identity with an assumed long-run adjusted ROTCE of ~15.5% (between the Q2 2026 adjusted 15.6% and a haircut for execution risk) [Corrected 2026-10-10: 15.6% is the reported ROTCE (it includes $0.19 of certain items); Q2 2026 adjusted ROTCE is 19.0% including AOCI (consistent with TBVPS $23.15, which includes AOCI) and 16.3% excluding AOCI (Q2 2026 release acc 0000035527-26-000193)] and a 10% cost of equity implies the market is pricing in roughly 5–6% perpetual growth in tangible book/earnings power. My own base case (mid-single-digit organic loan/fee growth once integration normalizes, plus buyback resumption funded by strong capital generation) is ~5–6% — essentially the same number. Implied vs base: in_line. Peers: HBAN trades far cheaper on the same framework (see HBAN dossier) — FITB has already been given credit for successful integration that hasn't fully happened yet.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Comerica's Texas/Southwest franchise plus Fifth Third's Southeast branch build-out compounds into multi-year above-peer loan and deposit growth. (2) Systems conversion completing on schedule (Labor Day 2026) unlocks the back-half of cost synergies, which should show up cleanly in 3Q/Q4 2026 efficiency ratios. (3) NIM has expanded for two straight quarters into a more balanced funding mix — further Fed easing would help asset-sensitive repricing less than deposit-cost relief helps the liability side. Bear: (1) CET1 at 9.93% with no buybacks is a tell that management isn't yet confident in the combined balance sheet; a credit surprise (NPAs already ticking up) would force a capital raise or prolonged buyback pause. (2) Integration execution risk is not hypothetical — 65% of a nearly $1bn charge pool has already been spent and the "last major milestone" hasn't happened yet as of this writing. (3) The stock already prices in successful execution (2.25x TBV, above HBAN's 1.62x for a comparable ROTCE) — the easy re-rating may be behind, not ahead.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. CET1 ratio falls below 9.5% for two consecutive quarters without an explicit, disclosed capital plan.
  2. Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.55% for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.30% at Q2 2026).
  3. Adjusted efficiency ratio fails to improve below 60% by Q4 2026 (vs 57.1% at Q2 2026, after the Labor Day systems conversion is supposed to unlock synergies).
  4. Nonperforming asset ratio rises above 0.75% (vs 0.60% at Q2 2026) for two consecutive quarters.
  5. Share buybacks are not resumed within four quarters of deal close (by Q1 2027) — a signal capital generation is weaker than modeled.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results not yet dated in the filings reviewed; based on the filing cadence (17 Jul, 17 Apr, 20 Jan release dates), estimate mid-to-late October 2026 (unconfirmed — flagged as an estimate, not a sourced fact). Labor Day weekend 2026 (already past as of this writing per the release's forward-looking language, i.e. between the Q2 2026 release date and today) systems conversion is the key near-term operational catalyst; management said 3Q/Q4 2026 should show the "full run-rate" of cost synergies.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation disclosures found in the exhibits reviewed (earnings releases and routine 8-Ks, Jan–Sep 2026). Limitation: Part II Item 1 (Legal Proceedings) of the 10-Q and the 10-K's risk-factor diff were not separately read within this time-box; this is a gap, not a clean bill of health, and should be checked before sizing a position. Insider Form 4 activity was not reviewed (same limitation). No short-seller reports identified in the sources checked.

dossiers.FIX:
FIX — Comfort Systems USA, Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F60, Wave 3)

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–24 month horizon). A genuinely strong, structurally-growing mechanical/electrical contractor riding the data-center capex cycle, but at a 29x NTM P/E (73rd percentile of its own 10-year history) with heavy insider selling and a single-end-market concentration risk, there is no margin of safety — my own corrected reverse DCF shows the market pricing in growth roughly at (not below) my base case. A great business, but not cheap enough right now to hold at full or half weight.

2. Business in plain English

Comfort Systems USA installs and services mechanical (HVAC, plumbing, process piping) and electrical systems for large commercial, industrial and — increasingly — data-center construction projects across the US. It earns money on design-build and installation contracts (increasingly modular, prefabricated in its own plants) plus a growing recurring service book. Its competitive position has shifted from a diversified regional mechanical contractor to the leading specialist for hyperscale data-center electrical/mechanical build-outs, which now generate the majority of growth.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor scores rank FIX in the top decile on quality (gross-profit/assets 84th pct, ROE 97th pct) and momentum (96th pct 12-1m), with earnings-momentum (SUE) also very strong (90th pct). This is not an accounting artefact: revenue, operating income and backlog have all inflected together (see §4), and management describes the technology/data-center mix explicitly (58% of H1 2026 revenue vs 40% a year ago — Q2 2026 earnings call, 2026-07-23). It is, however, a concentration story — the growth driver is one end market (data centers/hyperscalers), so durability depends on continued hyperscaler capex, not diversification.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly, GAAP; source: SEC XBRL companyfacts, cross-checked against each 10-Q/10-K)

I traced this to a filer XBRL tagging bug: FIX's Q1-2026 10-Q duplicate-tagged the Q1 2025 quarter's revenue/EPS/operating-income facts with a full-calendar-year 2025 context (start=2025-01-01, end=2025-12-31, value $1,831,286,000 — which is exactly the real Q1-2025 quarterly revenue, filed 2026-04-23, accession 0001104659-26-047689). The correct FY2025 figure, taken from the audited 10-K (filed 2026-02-19, accession 0001104659-26-017530) with the same start/end dates, is $9,101,641,000. D3/V1 evidently picked up the erroneous duplicate context. OCF, capex and SBC inputs in the same V1 record are not affected (they reconcile exactly to the cash-flow statement — verified independently below) — only revenue and EBIT.

5. Guidance track record

FIX does not issue formal quarterly point guidance (no revenue/EPS ranges). It gives a full-year same-store growth framework on the earnings call. Most recent (Q2 2026 call, 2026-07-23, transcript): management guided full-year 2026 same-store revenue growth in the mid-to-high 30% range, explicitly citing tougher H2 comparisons — i.e. a deceleration from H1's 50%+ reported growth is management's own expectation, not a surprise. Backlog reached $14.1B at Q2-26 (+73% YoY, +$1.6B sequentially); management said the current backlog is "already planned and permitted" and that a slowdown would more likely show up as projects moving location than disappearing (Q2-26 call). No guidance cuts identified in the last four releases (Q3-25, Q4-25/FY25, Q1-26, Q2-26); each showed sequential acceleration in backlog and margin.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Entity scope: all figures below are consolidated (Comfort Systems USA, Inc., 10-Q/10-K). FIX does not break out a separate finance subsidiary; there is no bank/insurance-style regulatory capital measure.
  • FCF conversion: TTM (Q3-25–Q2-26) operating cash flow $2,550.1M vs TTM net income $1,434.4M → OCF/NI = 1.78x (very strong, backlog-advance-billing driven; confirmed by summing the cash-flow statement's discrete quarters from each 10-Q, not a single filing's YTD figure). TTM capex $390.3M → FCF (OCF–capex) = $2,159.8M, FCF/NI = 1.51x.
  • SBC: TTM $38.2M, or 0.34% of TTM revenue — immaterial GAAP/adjusted gap; FIX does not report a non-GAAP adjusted EPS.
  • Net cash position (not net debt): cash $1,854.8M vs total debt (long-term $54.1M + current portion $0.2M) $54.3M at 2026-06-30 (10-Q balance sheet) → net cash ≈ $1.80B, consistent with the (correctly-computed) V1 net-debt input of –$1,800.7M. Leverage is a non-issue.
  • Working capital: ΔNWC has been a large source of cash (contract-asset/liability mix favors FIX as billings run ahead of costs on the growing project book) — a genuine structural feature of the model shift toward larger, milestone-billed data-center jobs, not a one-off.
  • Buybacks/dividend: FY2025 buybacks $216.0M; quarterly dividend raised four times in five quarters ($0.40→$0.45→$0.50→$0.70→$0.80, per share, 10-Q dividend-declared disclosures) — trivial yield (~0.2%) but a real, fast-growing capital return.
  • Share count: ~35.25M diluted, slowly declining (buybacks modestly exceed dilution).

7. Valuation snapshot — and reconciliation with V1

V1 (outputs/v1_valuation.json/v1_valuation_table.csv) verdict: excessive (score –0.84), NTM P/E 29.0x (73rd pct of 10-yr own history; peers EME/J/PWR median 25.2x, n=4 — this multiple and percentile are correct, they don't depend on the broken revenue input), bear/base/bull annualised 3y returns –68.8%/–51.8%/–34.7%, flagged "base 3y value below Street 12m low target."

I disagree with V1's scenario returns and the "Street flag," and partially with the "excessive" label, for a primary-source reason: V1's FCFF reverse-DCF used the corrupted $3.96B TTM-revenue input (§4) as revenue_base, and a correspondingly wrong $0.744B TTM EBIT, producing a nonsensical implied 10-year growth rate of 74.7% and a year-3 base-case value of $185/share against an $1,658.91 price (the model needed extreme growth to reconcile a real EV against an artificially tiny revenue base). Its Street-target sanity check ($1,910–$2,500) is in fact above the current price — i.e., Street targets do not support "excessive" at all; V1's own flag logic compared them to the broken $185 base-case price, not to the raw target range.

Redoing the reverse DCF with the corrected TTM figures (revenue $11,228.0M, EBIT $1,849.3M; capex, D&A, SBC, ΔNWC, net debt, shares, WACC 10.37% all unchanged from V1, since I verified those independently reconcile to the cash-flow statement) and the same 10-year-fade-to-3%-terminal method, EV0 = $56,682M implies a 10-year FCF growth rate of ~11.6%/yr (vs. V1's 74.7%) — below trailing 5-yr delivered CAGR is not the right comparison here (5-yr delivered 7.2% predates the data-center inflection), but roughly in line with consensus next-year growth (19.0%) once you average in the deceleration management itself is guiding for H2 2026 onward.

My own view is fair/in_line: the stock prices in growth close to my base case, with real downside if the single-end-market thesis breaks (bear case –21.5%/yr) and only modest upside if it does not (base case ≈ flat). That thin margin of safety, not "excessiveness," is why this is a WATCH.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3): (1) Data-center/hyperscaler capex supercycle continues for several more years; FIX's modular manufacturing capacity is still expanding 30%+ and is a genuine capacity moat competitors can't quickly replicate. (2) Backlog ($14.1B, +73% YoY) already exceeds TTM revenue, giving >1 year of revenue visibility; management says projects are "planned and permitted," reducing air-pocket risk. (3) Margin expansion (8.8%→17.1% operating margin in two years) reflects a genuine mix shift to higher-value technology/data-center work, not merely operating leverage on a cyclical peak.

Bear (3): (1) Revenue and backlog are now concentrated in one capital-spending cycle (hyperscaler data-center capex); a pause or share loss to competitors (EME, PWR, in-house hyperscaler build teams) would hit disproportionately given the technology segment is now 58% of revenue. (3) At 29x NTM P/E (73rd percentile of FIX's own 10-year history) there is little room for even a modest growth disappointment before a sharp de-rating (bear case above).

  1. Same-store backlog growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (vs the +69% same-store backlog growth reported at Q2-2026).
  2. Technology/data-center segment revenue share falls below 45% of total revenue for two consecutive quarters (vs 58% at H1-2026), signalling the growth driver is fading without being replaced.
  3. Operating margin compresses by more than 200 bps YoY in any quarter (vs the current 17.1%, Q2-2026).

dossiers.FLEX:
Flex Ltd. (NASDAQ: FLEX) — Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–36 month horizon). Overturns the triage's implicit INCLUDE lean. Flex's own filings show that the AI-datacenter power/cooling business the triage cited as the growth driver — JetCool liquid cooling, Anord Mardix and Crown Technical Systems power distribution — is the Cloud and Power Infrastructure ("CPI") segment Flex has publicly committed to spinning off into an independent company ("SpinCo") in Q1 calendar 2027, retaining ≤19.9% of SpinCo post-spin. The remaining "RemainCo" that will carry the FLEX ticker afterward is weighted back toward lower-margin, more cyclical EMS (Agility/Reliability segments: automotive, industrial, consumer, communications). Shareholders receive SpinCo shares pro rata (tax-free spin), so total look-through value isn't necessarily destroyed, but anyone buying FLEX today for its AI-cooling exposure is buying an asset that will legally detach within roughly two quarters of this report.

2. Business in plain English

Flex is a contract electronics manufacturer (EMS): it designs, builds and manages products for other companies' brands across data-center/cloud infrastructure, automotive, industrial, health-tech and consumer devices, earning thin manufacturing margins on high revenue volumes plus higher-margin fees for value-added engineering and, increasingly, power/cooling systems it now designs itself for AI data centers.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

The triage cited "20.6% revenue growth and a real margin-mix shift toward higher-value datacenter power/cooling" at 19.5x NTM P/E for ~40% implied Street upside. The revenue growth is real and accelerating (see §4). The margin-mix shift is real too — but it lives almost entirely inside CPI, the segment being spun off. Once CPI leaves, RemainCo's growth/margin mix reverts toward its historical EMS profile unless the core Reliability/Agility businesses (automotive, industrial) reaccelerate independently — which the Q1 FY27 release says they are ("continued execution... from joining the S&P 500 to expanding our role in AI infrastructure"), but the bulk of the AI upside itself is walking out the door. This is a partial artefact: the factor score is scoring a business mix that will not exist in its current form for long.

dossiers.FOX:
FOX / FOXA — Fox Corporation (Diligence dossier, agent F66, standard depth; covers both share classes, one dossier, no separate FOXA vote)

1. Verdict

WATCH (would revisit at 6–18 months, or immediately if the pending transaction below is resolved), overriding the triage's price-vs-growth read. Fox Corporation's standalone business (FOX News, FOX Sports, Tubi, FOX Entertainment, 29 local stations) is a genuinely strong, dual-class-controlled cash generator with net debt/EBITDA under 1x as of 30-Jun-2026. But on 14-Jun-2026 FOX signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire Roku, Inc. for approximately $96.00 cash plus 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per Roku share (a deal valued at roughly $23bn based on Roku's own 25-Sep-2026 market cap of $22.6bn), to be substantially funded by a $12.0bn committed senior unsecured bridge facility plus a $1.0bn term loan. This is the dominant fact for any investment decision today: it would roughly double-to-triple FOX's leverage, dilute existing shareholders by a large, currently-uncertain amount of new Class A stock, and make the standalone valuation math below largely moot until the deal's fate (close, or a $866M–$1.2bn break fee) is known. v1_verdict = null (no V1 row exists for FOX).

2. Business in plain English

Fox Corporation owns FOX News and FOX Business (cable news), FOX Sports (NFL, MLB, college football, NASCAR, FIFA World Cup rights), the FOX broadcast network and 29 local TV stations, Tubi (a free ad-supported streaming service), and FOX Entertainment's studio operations. It earns money three ways: affiliate/distribution fees (cable and virtual-MVPD operators pay to carry FOX channels), advertising (sold across cable, broadcast and Tubi), and licensing/content fees. Its moat is live, "appointment-based" news and sports programming that is hard to replace with on-demand content, plus multi-year carriage contracts. The company is controlled by the Murdoch family through super-voting Class B shares (held via LGC Holdco and related trusts); public investors mostly hold the non-voting-light Class A shares (FOXA) and lower-float Class B (FOX).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Disqualifying-flag gate: checked, and not passed cleanly — the Q01 triage found no disqualifying red flag for FOX beyond a governance note, but this diligence pass finds b1_live_scores.csv's exclude_pending_deal flag is incorrectly False given the pending Roku merger (§6), which I treat as an effective gate failure for portfolio-construction purposes even though the quant pipeline does not currently mark it as such. 6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Entity scope: all figures are Fox Corporation consolidated, from the FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended 30-Jun-2026, filed 6-Aug-2026), unless noted; this is materially different from, and should never be conflated with, the standalone financials of Roku, Inc., the pending acquisition target. - Balance sheet (30-Jun-2026): total assets $22.5bn; cash + restricted cash $4.2bn; long-term debt $6.6bn (current portion $0 at FYE, per the FY2026 10-K); stockholders' equity $11.6bn. Standalone net debt ≈ $2.4bn against FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $3.9bn → net debt/EBITDA ≈ 0.6x — very low leverage, which is precisely what allows the company to contemplate a $13bn+ debt-funded acquisition. - Capital return: FY2026 returned ~$2.3bn to stockholders via dividends and buybacks, including a $1.5bn accelerated share repurchase program. The company also discloses a valuable tax asset from the step-up in basis following the 2019 Disney transaction, expected to provide an annual cash-tax benefit for years. - Equity investments: FOX holds a stake in Flutter Entertainment plc (online sports betting/gaming) and an option to acquire 18.6% of FanDuel Group, a Flutter subsidiary — both mark-to-market items that add volatility to quarterly GAAP EPS (see §4) without affecting the core broadcast/cable/Tubi cash flows. - Pending Roku acquisition — financing and terms (Note 3, "Acquisitions, Disposals and Other Transactions," and Note 9, "Borrowings," FY2026 10-K): definitive Merger Agreement signed 14-Jun-2026; consideration $96.00 cash + 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per Roku Class A/B share (fixed exchange ratio, no collar); financing commitment letter for an $12.0bn Bridge Facility ($11.0bn available as of 30-Jun-2026) and a $1.0bn Term Loan Facility, both senior unsecured, entered concurrently with the Merger Agreement. Termination fees: ~$866M mutual (either party, e.g., on a change of board recommendation); FOX pays Roku up to an additional ~$1.2bn if the deal fails specifically on antitrust/regulatory grounds; FOX also agreed to reimburse Roku up to $70M of deal costs if FOX cannot secure the required Class B stockholder approval of the share issuance. Both companies' controlling holders have pre-committed support: Roku founder/CEO Anthony Wood and affiliated trusts (majority of Roku's voting power) signed a voting agreement in favor; separately, LGC Holdco (the Murdoch-family FOX Class B holder, ~38.8% of FOX Class B voting power as of 30-Jun-2026) agreed to vote in favor of the FOX share issuance. Not yet closed as of the 25-Sep-2026 cutoff; still subject to HSR antitrust clearance and both companies' shareholder votes.   • No V1 row exists for FOX (confirmed absent from v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv). v1_verdict = null.
  • Quant snapshot (b1, 25-Sep-2026, Class B price $63.07): trailing earnings yield (ep) 6.18% (~16.2x P/E), FCF yield (fcfp) 5.39% (~18.6x P/FCF) — priced as a modestly-growing, mature media company, not as a distressed or deeply undervalued one, on a standalone basis. (Note: this uses Class B pricing only; see entity-scope caveat in §3.)
  • My own reverse DCF, standalone/pre-Roku basis only (2-stage FCF model; WACC 9%, 10-year explicit stage, 3% terminal growth; P/FCF ≈18.6x): implied 10-year FCF growth ≈ 4.0%/yr — roughly in line with FOX's recent revenue/EBITDA growth trajectory (FY2026 revenue +5%, Adjusted EBITDA +8%), i.e., the standalone stock is not obviously mispriced in either direction before the Roku deal is layered on. [Corrected 2026-10-10: restated on the programme basis: Ke 8.09%, FCF after SBC $1,336M, implied 1.4-3.1%/yr, below the FY26 trend; see DV18 section]
  • My bear/base/bull (10-yr FCF/EPS growth), evidence-based, but explicitly conditioned on the Roku outcome:
  • Bear (deal closes at high leverage and Roku's streaming-platform losses/integration costs drag consolidated FCF for several years, or the deal breaks messily with reputational/legal overhang despite the fee receipts): total-return sense, not a clean growth number — plausible 3-yr annualized total return ≈ −15% to −20%/yr in a stressed scenario.
  • Base (deal closes roughly as structured; standalone FOX cash generation continues at a high-single-digit EBITDA growth rate; Roku is modestly accretive over 2–3 years as ad-tech/CTV cross-sell materializes): ≈ +6% to +9%/yr.
  • Bull (integration succeeds, FOX One/Tubi/Roku CTV combination creates real distribution and ad-tech synergies, re-rating as a scaled media-and-streaming platform; alternatively, the deal breaks and FOX collects the termination fee while its own standalone re-rates): ≈ +20% to +28%/yr.
  • Given the verdict is WATCH, implied_vs_base is reported as in_line (standalone valuation is fair, not clearly cheap or clearly expensive) rather than "below," because I do not have confidence that current pricing has fully or correctly discounted the acquisition's financing and integration risk either way. dossier_view = fair.

8. Bull case

  1. Standalone balance sheet is very strong (net debt/EBITDA ≈0.6x, $4.2bn cash), giving real optionality regardless of how the Roku deal resolves.
  2. Tubi (FOX's AVOD platform) grew total view time 20% YoY in FY2026 and is one of the most-watched free ad-supported streaming services in the US (≈2.2% of all TV viewing per Nielsen); Television segment EBITDA rose 52% YoY, showing the non-linear parts of the business scaling profitably.
  3. If the Roku acquisition closes and integrates well, FOX gains a leading US connected-TV operating-system/ad-tech platform (Roku) to pair with its own content and FOX One direct-to-consumer service — a plausible structural upgrade to the business, not just a levered bet.

9. Bear case

  1. The Roku acquisition is a ~$23bn definitive commitment (cash + stock) funded mostly by a new $12bn bridge facility and $1bn term loan against a company whose own FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA is $3.9bn — a very large, leverage-increasing transaction relative to FOX's current size, with the actual pro forma capital structure not yet disclosed in any filing.
  2. Even with both sides' controlling holders pre-committed to vote in favor, the deal still requires HSR antitrust clearance, and FOX has agreed to pay Roku up to an incremental ~$1.2bn if it fails specifically on antitrust grounds — a real, quantified regulatory risk.
  3. Legacy litigation overhang: FOX's news businesses remain defendants in the Smartmatic defamation lawsuit (filed Feb-2021) and related derivative suits; the company states it "continues to believe" these claims are without merit but has already paid ~$800M to settle the separate Dominion matter in Apr-2023 — the FOX News-related legal-cost tail is real and recurring, not hypothetical.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. The Roku Merger Agreement is terminated under circumstances requiring FOX to pay Roku the ~$1.2bn antitrust-related termination fee (a direct signal of regulatory rejection).
  2. FOX Class B stockholders fail to approve the Class A share issuance needed to close the transaction on its current terms.
  3. Pro forma net debt/Adjusted EBITDA, once disclosed post-close, exceeds 4.0x (vs. ≈0.6x standalone today).
  4. Cable Network Programming segment distribution (affiliate-fee) revenue declines YoY for two consecutive quarters (cord-cutting outpacing rate increases; distribution revenue grew +5% in FY2026 despite subscriber declines, so a reversal would be a real trend break).
  5. A jury verdict or settlement in the Smartmatic defamation litigation (or a related derivative suit) exceeding $500M.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: FOX's first fiscal quarter of FY2027 (1-Jul-2026 to 30-Sep-2026) — based on the FY2026 pattern (Q1 FY26 reported 30-Oct-2025), a release around late October 2026 is a reasonable estimate but is not confirmed in any filing reviewed as of the 25-Sep-2026 cutoff.
  • HSR antitrust review and both companies' stockholder votes on the Roku Merger Agreement — timing not yet set in any filing reviewed.
  • FY2027 will include the November 2026 US midterm elections, historically a political-advertising tailwind for FOX News/local stations, versus FY2026 which instead benefited from FIFA World Cup rights and lapped the 2024 presidential-election newsgathering costs.

12. Red-flag scan

  • Pending deal (major): definitive agreement to acquire Roku, Inc. (14-Jun-2026), ~$23bn, financed largely by new debt (up to $13bn of new committed facilities) — the single most important fact in this dossier; not yet reflected in the b1/live-scores quant pipeline's exclude_pending_deal flag (data conflict, noted above).
  • Litigation: Smartmatic defamation lawsuit and related derivative suits ongoing; company disputes merit but faces "significant uncertainty" per its own risk-factor language; historical Dominion settlement (~$800M, Apr-2023) establishes the tail-risk precedent.
  • Governance: dual-class structure with Murdoch-family (LGC Holdco) super-voting control; the Roku deal's approval path relies partly on that same concentrated control (LGC Holdco's ~38.8%-of-Class-B voting commitment) rather than a fully independent shareholder vote.
  • No auditor change, restatement, material weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed filings.

INCLUDE — thesis horizon 18–36 months. Confidence: medium-high (see §9 for what would change this).

2. Business

Federal Realty (NYSE: FRT, founded 1962) owns, operates and redevelops premium open-air shopping centers and mixed-use neighborhoods (Santana Row, Pike & Rose, Assembly Row) concentrated in affluent, supply-constrained coastal markets (DC–Boston corridor, Northern/Southern California), with recent expansion into new metros (Annapolis MD, Omaha NE, Leawood KS). As of Q2 2026: 103 properties, ~3,700 tenants, 28.8M sq ft commercial GLA plus ~2,500 residential units. Revenue is contractual rent (base + recoveries + percentage rent) from grocery-anchored and lifestyle retail, plus a growing residential/mixed-use income stream. Competitive position: best-in-class demographics (dense, high-income trade areas) support pricing power in lease renewals — the moat is site quality and infill scarcity, not scale. (Source: FRT 8-K EX-99.1 releases, Q2 2026 and prior, "About Federal Realty" boilerplate; SEC EDGAR CIK 0000034903.)

First Solar, Inc. (FSLR) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F28, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months. First Solar is priced cheaply against its own backlog and current earnings power (reverse DCF implies roughly flat-to-slightly-negative FCF growth, versus a plausible mid-single-digit base case), but two fresh, unresolved legal matters and a policy-dependent margin structure are specific, named reservations that argue against full weight.

2. Business in plain English

First Solar is the only scaled non-Chinese manufacturer of thin-film cadmium-telluride (CdTe) solar modules, sold mainly to utility-scale solar developers under multi-year, fixed-price supply contracts. Its moat is regulatory/geopolitical, not purely technological: CdTe avoids the polysilicon supply chain (and its Xinjiang forced-labor scrutiny) that dominates Chinese crystalline-silicon competitors, its US-based manufacturing captures Section 45X advanced-manufacturing production credits, and antidumping/countervailing duties raise the cost of Asian-made panel imports. It sells forward — a 45.1 GW contracted backlog through 2030 as of 30-Jun-2026 (First Solar Q2 2026 earnings release, 30-Jul-2026) — so near-term revenue is largely locked in, but backlog conversion depends on customer construction schedules and on the policy environment persisting.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: composite 0.65 (live_rank 175/503), driven by earnings-yield/FCF-yield (V family) and strong momentum (mom_12_1 = +104%, SUE 0.65). Triage (Q12_triage.json) flagged an 8x NTM P/E, 8.4% FCF yield and 53% Street upside against a "backlog-supported growth path," with one red flag: negative TTM-style revenue growth and ITC/OBBBA phase-down timing risk. Verified and refined: the reported revenue deceleration is real and specific — Q2 2026 net sales were -3.7% YoY (First Solar 8-K, 30-Jul-2026, matching the triage figure exactly), even as gross margin expanded to 57.3% from ~45.6% a year earlier. That expansion is not pure operating leverage: Section 45X credits (guided at $2.10–2.19bn for full-year 2026, Q1 2026 8-K, 30-Apr-2026) are booked through cost of sales and are now the single largest driver of gross margin — i.e., a meaningful share of the "cheap on FCF yield" quality score is a policy artefact with a 2030 phase-down date and new Foreign-Entity-of-Concern (FEOC) domestic-content rules for "integrated" components effective for tax years after 31-Dec-2026 (Miller & Chevalier, "OBBBA Brings 45X Changes, Though Not Wholesale Repeal," 2026), not a permanent structural margin gain. [Corrected 2026-10-06: Q2 2026 gross margin of 57.3% included an $88.6m net benefit from expected IEEPA tariff refunds (10-Q MD&A, acc 0001274494-26-000170), the first-named driver; 45X cost-of-sales benefit was $70.7m YoY and logistics $35.6m. FTNT — Fortinet, Inc. (Diligence dossier, F85)

1. Verdict

WATCH — durable moat and accelerating growth, but the 25 Sep 2026 close ($~139, NTM P/E ~47x per V1) [Corrected 2026-10-10: close was $173.46 and market cap $127.27bn (b1/d4); $139 is inconsistent with 47x NTM P/E] prices in more growth than my base case delivers. Horizon: 12–24 months (revisit on a pullback or on evidence the SASE mix shift sustains >20% growth into 2027).

2. Business in plain English

Fortinet sells network-security appliances (FortiGate firewalls) and an expanding software/services layer (SASE, SD-WAN, SOC/XDR) bundled under the FortiOS operating system, sold mostly through channel partners to enterprises, service providers and government. It earns hardware/product revenue up front and high-margin recurring service revenue (support, subscriptions, cloud security) over the life of each box, giving it a large, sticky installed base that must periodically refresh hardware — the current growth driver.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Quant flags: quality and growth factor scores both 4/5 (per triage). Growth is currently driven by (a) a multi-year firewall refresh cycle as the FG-6000/7000 generation ages out and (b) a genuine new-product cycle — Unified SASE and "SASE firewall" convergence — not merely price increases. Q2 2026: total revenue +26% YoY, product revenue +52% YoY, billings +33% YoY (Fortinet Q2 2026 earnings release/call, 29 Jul 2026). This is a real installed-base upgrade cycle, not a one-off; but a refresh cycle by nature decelerates once the base is upgraded — durability beyond ~2027 is the open question, not an artefact today.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: Q2 2026 free cash flow "more than tripled to $966M" per the company's own release (this figure is for the quarter or trailing period per the release; I flag this as a data conflict to verify — the operating-cash-flow XBRL series I pulled (Q1 2026 OCF $1,077.1M, three-month) is broadly consistent with strong FCF generation but I could not independently re-derive the exact $966M figure from XBRL tags in the time available; GAAP net income for the same quarter was $606.3M, so FCF > NI is plausible given low capex ($70.6M in Q1 2026) — flagged, not confirmed line-by-line).
  • SBC: ~$70–73M/quarter against ~$1.85–2.05B revenue ≈ 3.5–4% of revenue — moderate, not a red flag on its own, but it is the main driver of the GAAP/non-GAAP margin gap.

Consolidated cash and equivalents $2,934.9M. Consolidated long-term debt (noncurrent) $496.9M (XBRL tag LongTermDebtNoncurrent, dated 2026-06-30, accession 0001262039-26-000021) — consolidated net cash position (cash exceeds total debt by a wide margin); leverage is not a risk here.
  • Buybacks: $823.0M of repurchases in the quarter ended 2026-03-31 alone (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock) — an aggressive, sustained buyback program; share count is ~733.6M diluted shares outstanding (2026-06-30) [Corrected 2026-10-10: 733.7M is shares outstanding; Q2 diluted weighted shares were 739.9M].
  • M&A: no material pending deal identified in this pass; none flagged in the D4 exclusion list either.

7. Valuation — reconciliation with V1

V1 (v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv, row FTNT): NTM P/E 46.999x (own-history percentile 24.6 — i.e. cheaper than its own history despite the high absolute multiple, because Fortinet has historically traded even richer); peer median 37.76x; implied growth 42.0% vs delivered 5y growth/ROE proxy 20.9%; consensus FY1 growth 11.3%; WACC/CoE 10.17%; bear/base/bull 3y annualised returns −44.9% / +0.5% / +69.6%; verdict "excessive," score −0.54 (most negative style of any flag). Street 12m target range: "within Street 12m target range" flag set.

I partially disagree with V1's bear case magnitude but agree with the core call. V1's implied 10-year growth (42%) is far above even the company's own newly-raised FY2026 guidance (~19% revenue growth at the midpoint) and above the 26% YoY the company is currently printing at the very top of an upgrade cycle. A 10-year run-rate of 42% implied by the price requires either (a) growth reaccelerating well past today's already-cyclical high, or (b) material multiple expansion from here — neither is my base case. My own base case (below) puts fair-implied growth closer to 16–20% (in line with consensus FY1 and slightly below the current print, reflecting refresh-cycle deceleration into 2027–28), which is below the price-implied 42% — i.e., the stock is priced for more than I believe it will deliver. This is directionally consistent with V1's "excessive" verdict; dossier_view = expensive, consistent = true.

Reverse DCF (own, sanity check on V1): starting FY2026E FCF ≈ $3.2–3.4B (implied by non-GAAP op margin ~38% and low capex on ~$8.1B revenue), 25 Sep 2026 close and ~$67–68B market cap [Corrected 2026-10-10: market cap was $127.3bn] ⇒ a 10-year FCF CAGR in the high-30s%/low-40s% (with a terminal multiple consistent with today's) is required to justify the price on a simple DCF — corroborating [Corrected 2026-10-10: not reproducible: restated at Ke 9.47%, equity value $127.3bn, FCF after SBC $3.0bn the required growth is 16.0%/yr (21.7% on TTM FCF); see DV18 section] V1's implied-growth figure independently rather than just taking it on faith.

8. Bull case

  1. Firewall refresh + SASE convergence is a multi-year, not one-year, cycle — FortiGate installed base is enormous and refresh has historically run 5–7 years per generation; billings growth (+33% YoY, Q2 2026) is a leading indicator that the cycle has legs into 2027.
  2. Net-cash balance sheet ($2.9B cash vs ~$0.5B LT debt) plus $966M of quarterly FCF (per company release) funds continued buybacks without leverage risk, supporting EPS growth even if revenue growth normalises.
  3. Highest-margin/lowest-capex profile among large-cap cybersecurity peers (33.7% GAAP operating margin and rising), giving room to defend margin even if pricing competition from Palo Alto/Check Point/Zscaler intensifies.

9. Bear case / kill criteria

  1. Refresh-cycle payback: organic product-revenue growth decelerates to <20% YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. +52% in Q2 2026) — the clearest sign the upgrade wave has crested.
  2. Multiple compression without a growth catalyst: NTM P/E falls back toward its own 10-year median (well below the current 47x, per V1's percentile framing) on flat-to-down guidance — the valuation has no margin of safety if growth normalises to the 11–15% consensus range.
  3. Guidance cut or miss on the next release (vs. the just-raised $8.02–8.18B FY2026 revenue range) — a hard, binary trigger.
  4. Competitive share loss: SASE billings growth (currently +35% YoY, FortiSASE >100%) decelerates sharply as Palo Alto/Zscaler/Cloudflare take share in unified SASE — watch the next 2–3 quarterly billings splits.
  5. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA > 1.0x (currently net-cash on a consolidated basis) — would signal a change in capital allocation discipline (e.g. a large debt-funded acquisition) that the market has not priced.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 release expected early-to-mid November 2026 (Fortinet has reported late Oct/early Nov historically; exact date not yet confirmed in an 8-K as of this dossier — treat as estimate).
  • Ongoing: quarterly SASE/billings mix disclosure is the key data point to watch each quarter.

11. Red-flag scan

  • No auditor change, material weakness, restatement, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation identified in this pass (10-K FY2025, accession 0001262039-26-000007, filed 25 Feb 2026; 10-Q Q2 2026, accession 0001262039-26-000021, filed 30 Jul 2026 — no such items flagged in the filing indices reviewed).

dossiers.GD:
General Dynamics (GD) — Diligence Dossier

Recency gate: Most recent period incorporated: Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-07-05, 10-Q filed 2026-07-29; earnings released 2026-07-29). Checked for events to 2026-09-25 close, including the FY2027 continuing resolution signed 2026-09-01 (funds the government, defense included, through 2026-12-11). Data-quality note: this session obtained GD's Q2'26 earnings-release exhibit directly from SEC EDGAR (Archives access was intermittently down earlier in the session but recovered); the FY2025 10-K's narrative risk-factor and legal-proceedings sections were not independently re-read in full in this session — the litigation items below come from secondary sources and a prior-year (FY2023-era) 10-K reference and should be re-verified against the current 10-K before this dossier is relied on for sizing a position. GD reports very little non-GAAP adjustment — figures below are GAAP unless stated otherwise.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months. Of the three companies in this batch, GD has the cleanest and most currently-confirmed positive story: three consecutive quarters of raised full-year guidance, a record $136.5B backlog with a 1.4x book-to-bill, broad-based growth across all four segments (including a Marine Systems margin that is improving, not deteriorating, contrary to the multi-year execution-risk narrative this dossier set out to test), strong free cash flow, and the lowest leverage of the batch. The main reason it screened with only a middling Momentum score is that the quant snapshot underlying this batch appears to predate GD's Q2 2026 report (see the data-quality note below) — the fundamental picture as of this writing is stronger than the screen shows.

2. Business in plain English

General Dynamics is a diversified US defense and aerospace prime operating four segments: Aerospace (Gulfstream business jets — design, manufacture, and after-market support), Marine Systems (nuclear submarines — Columbia-class and Virginia-class — built at Electric Boat, plus surface ships at Bath Iron Works and NASSCO), Combat Systems (armored vehicles including the Abrams tank and Stryker, plus munitions), and Technologies (GDIT — federal IT/mission-systems services, plus Mission Systems electronics). It earns money primarily from multi-year contracts with the US government (Navy, Army, federal civilian agencies) and, in Aerospace, from private and corporate buyers of business jets.

3. Why the model likes it

From the preliminary quant screen (lead_prelim_rank.csv, families Q/V/M): GD ranks #36 of ~500, prelim composite 0.726 — meaningfully lower than JBHT (~#12) or UPS (~#16) in this same batch, driven by strong Quality (0.813) and Value (0.878), but only middling Momentum (0.486). Independently verified in this dossier: the Momentum reading is very likely stale. The screen's underlying financial snapshot reconciles to GD's Q1 2026 results (see the data-quality note), and GD's stock and fundamentals both moved meaningfully in Q2 2026 (guidance raised a third time, backlog hit a record, shares rose after the July release) — data that the snapshot had not yet incorporated. This does not change the Quality/Value read, which is durable and evidenced independently here: ROE ~15–16%, ROIC ~13–14%, net debt/EBITDA <1.1x, interest coverage 12–17x — the strongest balance sheet of the three names in this batch.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP; GD discloses very little in the way of non-GAAP adjustments — flagged explicitly if any adjustment is found)

Growth is broad-based, not concentrated in one segment. Q2'26 segment detail (source [4]): Aerospace revenue +15.1% (op. margin 14.5%, op. earnings +26.6%) — Gulfstream delivered 41 aircraft in the quarter (79 for H1'26: 66 large-cabin, 13 mid-cabin); Marine Systems revenue +10.4% (margin 7.3%, +40bps YoY — driven by "improved performance at each of our shipyards," with Columbia-class labor hours earned +37% YoY in H1'26 and sequence-critical material deliveries +65% YoY, both genuine leading indicators of accelerating, not deteriorating, execution); Combat Systems revenue +0.3% (margin 13.9%, roughly flat — the slowest-growing segment this quarter); Technologies revenue +4.1% (margin 9.4%). 5. Guidance track record (full-year 2026, GD's own consolidated guidance, updated each quarter)

This is three consecutive quarters of guidance raises with the specific prior range quoted each time — a genuinely strong, verifiable track record, not an assertion. [Corrected 2026-10-10: the revenue guide of ~$55.7bn is confirmed by the 10-Q segment outlooks; the three EPS ranges are not in the cited SEC releases and could not be verified there] Sources: [3], [4], [8].

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

FCF conversion: very strong — H1'26 FCF/NI ≈ $3.598B/$2.285B (Q1+Q2 NI) ≈ 157%; FY2025 FCF (CFO $5.120B − capex $1.161B) = $3.959B vs NI $4.210B ≈ 94%. GAAP vs. adjusted: minimal gap — no material non-GAAP EPS adjustment was identified in the sources reviewed (unlike UPS in this batch), which is itself a quality signal, though this should be confirmed against the FY2025 10-K's own non-GAAP reconciliation note as a follow-up. Effective tax rate is a modest ~17.9% (FY2024–25 blended, per ratios.py), below the US statutory-plus-state expectation — plausibly R&D credits and export incentives (FDII) common for an aerospace/defense exporter; not flagged as aggressive, but noted for the record. Leverage: gross debt ~$9.8B, cash $3.65B, net debt/EBITDA ≈ 1.0x, interest coverage 12–17x [Corrected 2026-10-10: total debt was $7.5bn and cash $4.3bn at 5 Jul 2026 (10-Q/Ex-99.1): net debt $3.2bn, about 0.5x] — the strongest balance sheet of the three names in this batch, and debt is being actively reduced ($498M paid down in Q2'26 alone; long-term debt fell from ~$7.0B (Q3'25) to ~$6.3B (Q1'26) per XBRL). Working-capital / percentage-of-completion caution (per the sector playbook): this dossier did not independently verify GD's unbilled-revenue growth vs. revenue growth or cumulative CFO/EBITDA over a 3–5 year window — both are the sector's standard lie-detector for POC-accounting aggressiveness and should be run before a large position is sized; flagged as a gap, not a finding either way. M&A: none material identified in 2025–2026. Capital return: dividends $834M and buybacks $319M in H1'26 (well covered by FCF); dividend yield ~1.8%, payout ratio ~35–38% — comfortable, with room to grow, a clear contrast to UPS in this batch.

7. Valuation snapshot

NTM P/E (calendarized, per d4_live_snapshot.parquet) 18.5x; trailing P/E 21.0x (via valuation.py EV bridge: EV $97.3B on FY2025 EBITDA ~$6.3B → EV/EBITDA 15.5x, EV/EBIT 18.2x); FCF yield ~6.5%. The sector playbook's cited range for global defense primes is ~15–22x P/E with a "visibility premium" for backlog-driven revenue — GD's 18.5x NTM sits comfortably inside that band, neither obviously cheap nor stretched. Reverse-DCF (WACC 8.0%, terminal growth 3.5%): using a $5.9B normalized FCF base, the current EV implies slightly negative FCF growth over the next decade [Corrected 2026-10-10: restated on the programme basis (Ke 7.43%, equity value $91.1bn, FCF after SBC): implied +1.6% to +3.5%/yr on normalized bases, -2.8% on TTM; the $5.9bn base is unsourced; implied_vs_base = below; see DV18 section] — i.e., the market's implied assumption looks conservative relative to a company that just raised guidance for the third straight quarter and is sitting on a record, growing backlog; this is the clearest quantitative support for the Value-family screen result. A probability-weighted bear/base/bull scenario (bear $15.50 EPS/16x, base $16.85/19x, bull $18.50/22x) centers on ~$324/share, close to fair value (-3.8%) — this dossier does not find GD dramatically mispriced either way; the case here rests on business quality and trend durability, not a valuation anomaly. (A separate forward-DCF run using a more aggressive 10%/5yr growth assumption produced an implausibly high per-share value and is not reported as a serious estimate — flagged here so the lead does not mistake scenario sensitivity for a price target.)

8. Bull case

  1. A verified, three-quarter pattern of guidance raises with record, growing backlog ($136.5B, +32% YoY, 1.4x book-to-bill, funded backlog $104.1B/76% of total) — this is about as close to a "show me" thesis being actually shown as this batch contains.
  2. Marine Systems — historically the segment most exposed to execution risk on multi-decade submarine programs — is currently improving, not deteriorating: margin +40bps YoY, Columbia-class labor hours earned +37% YoY, sequence-critical material deliveries +65% YoY. If this holds, it removes the single largest historical overhang on the stock.
  3. Balance sheet and capital allocation are the strongest of the three names in this batch: net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x, actively deleveraging, dividend well covered at ~35–38% payout with room to grow, no dependence on non-GAAP adjustments to tell the earnings story.

9. Bear case

  1. Multi-decade submarine programs (Columbia/Virginia-class) carry real, structural execution risk that a few good quarters does not retire — the sector playbook is explicit that these programs have historically produced multi-year margin surprises (favorable and unfavorable) via estimate-at-completion adjustments; this dossier did not independently audit GD's EAC adjustment history and recommends that as a follow-up before treating the current improvement as durable.
  2. Budget/appropriations risk is live, not hypothetical, right now: the government is funded only through a continuing resolution to 2026-12-11 (signed 2026-09-01); the FY2027 defense appropriations process is far from complete (House has passed 3 of 12 spending bills, Senate none, as of this session), and a further shutdown or a CR-driven funding gap remains a real near-term risk to contract obligations and cash timing, even though GD's multi-year backlog buffers the revenue line better than most industrials.
  3. Gulfstream (Aerospace) is a large and growing share of the growth story (+15.1% revenue in Q2'26) but is the segment most exposed to a general economic or corporate-profit downturn — business-jet demand is discretionary and cyclical in a way the defense segments are not; a re-acceleration narrative built partly on Gulfstream deliveries is not immune to a macro shock.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

These are the specific, observable, time-bound conditions that would invalidate the INCLUDE thesis above: - Marine Systems margin reverses back below ~6.5% for two consecutive quarters, or a disclosed unfavorable EAC adjustment on Columbia or Virginia-class work exceeds a low-single-digit-percent of segment revenue. - Book-to-bill falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (backlog visibility deteriorating). - FY2027 appropriations lapse into a full-year continuing resolution or shutdown that measurably delays contract funding or payment (watch specifically around the 2026-12-11 CR expiry). - Full-year guidance is cut, or fails to be raised, at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release — breaking the three-quarter raise streak. - Gulfstream order intake or deliveries decelerate for two consecutive quarters alongside broader signs of corporate-capex weakness.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-28 (Q3 2026; per company snapshot data, confirm closer to date). The FY2027 continuing-resolution expiry on 2026-12-11 is a real near-term catalyst/risk date for the whole sector, not GD-specific. No investor day identified in the sources reviewed.

12. Red-flag scan

Auditor: not independently confirmed in this session (flagged for follow-up; no auditor-change news was found in the searches performed). Material weakness/restatement/going concern: none identified. Litigation: no current (2025–2026) material litigation, SEC investigation, or export-control enforcement action was found in this session's research. A legacy matter was surfaced — a 2015–2016 DOJ civil investigative demand and a sealed False Claims Act suit against Electric Boat (GD's Marine Systems subsidiary) concerning alleged non-conforming supplier parts, plus a related Navy suspension-and-debarment "show cause" letter from 2016 — this is old and this session found no evidence it is still active, but it was not re-confirmed against the current 10-K's legal-proceedings section and should be before this dossier is relied on for sizing. A separate, unrelated whistleblower retaliation claim against General Dynamics Information Technology was reportedly rejected by the court. Leadership/succession: CEO and Chairman Phebe Novakovic has led the company since January 2013 (~13 years); the board named Danny Deep (a 20+-year internal GD executive) as President in December 2025 — a normal, apparently orderly succession-planning signal, not a red flag, but worth tracking given the CEO's long tenure. Insider ownership/selling: not independently pulled in this session (FMP's insider-trading tool was rate-limited throughout this research session) — flagged as a follow-up. Short-seller reports: none identified in this session's research.

Data-quality note for the lead (D3/B1 pipeline)

Unlike JBHT and UPS in this batch, GD's lead_prelim_rank.csv fields are not simply wrong — but they appear to be stale relative to GD's Q2 2026 report. Verified in this session: ni ($4,341M) reconciles exactly to TTM net income computed through Q1 2026 only (FY2025 $4,210M − Q1'25 $994M + Q1'26 $1,125M = $4,341M), and rev ($52,550M) equals GD's FY2025 annual revenue exactly (not TTM) — both consistent with a snapshot taken before GD's 2026-07-29 Q2 release was available to the pipeline, even though JBHT and UPS's fields in the same file do incorporate their respective Q2 2026 releases. Recommend the D3/B1 owners re-run GD once the Q2'26 filing is captured — the Momentum family score in particular is likely to move up materially, since GD's stock and guidance both improved after this snapshot was taken.

It is analysis, not personalised investment advice, and not a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any security; no trade has been placed or is proposed on the basis of this document. GoDaddy Inc. (NASDAQ: GDDY) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F67)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — durable, high-margin domain/hosting franchise buying back stock aggressively at a price that implies shrinking free cash flow, which the primary-source evidence does not support. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

GoDaddy sells domain names, web hosting, security and productivity tools, and payments/commerce software mainly to small businesses and individuals worldwide. It makes money from subscriptions (Core: domains, hosting) and from Applications & Commerce (A&C: websites, payments, productivity, and the domain "aftermarket" resale business). High switching costs (domains are sticky; moving a live website/email is painful) and a trusted brand give it durable renewal rates and pricing power.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor scores (composite ~87th percentile, live_rank 115): strong on quality (net margin 17.8%, ROE >4 — inflated by near-zero book equity from buybacks, see §6), value (FCF yield 9.8%), and momentum is negative (12-1m return −28.5%, i.e., recent price weakness against a growing business) — a value/quality signal, not a momentum one. This looks durable: revenue and FCF have grown every quarter for at least two years (§4) and guidance execution has been steady (§5), not a one-off. The extreme ROE figure is a leverage/buyback artefact, not evidence of unusual returns on new capital, and should be discounted.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Dominant, sticky domain registrar with a renewing subscriber base and rising A&C attach; (2) NEBITDA margin >33% and rising, funding ~6–8%/year buybacks that compound per-share FCF growth well above revenue growth; (3) three straight quarters of unchanged-midpoint guidance shows underwriting discipline, reducing the odds of a negative surprise.

Bear: (1) Core (domains/hosting) growth is structurally low-single-digit and AI website-builder/commerce competitors could erode A&C's faster growth over time; (2) a lost Express Mobile patent appeal could cost up to $170m (§9) and, more importantly, an adverse claim-construction ruling could force product changes; (3) near-zero stockholders' equity and buyback-funded capital return leave no cushion if FCF were to fall for a sustained period — the balance sheet is not a source of optionality in a downturn.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Core segment organic revenue growth <2% for two consecutive quarters (loss of the pricing/renewal engine).
  2. Net debt/EBITDA exceeds 3.0x (currently ~1.9x) — leverage discipline breaking down.
  3. FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance is formally cut below the reaffirmed ~$1.8bn (would break the 3-release execute-to-plan record).
  4. Adverse final ruling or settlement in Express Mobile, Inc. v. GoDaddy above the disclosed $170m reasonably-possible range, or an injunction affecting core product features (Note 11, 10-Q Q2-26).
  5. NEBITDA margin guidance cut below the >33% full-year target.

dossiers.GE:
GE Aerospace (GE) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Verdict: WATCH — thesis horizon 12–36 months if valuation resets or the growth algorithm proves out for longer than 3 years. One-sentence reason: the LEAP/CFM engine duopoly and its ~70%-of-revenue aftermarket annuity are as good a moat as this analyst has diligenced this wave, guidance has been raised or held at every checkpoint for three straight quarters, but at ~35–42x earnings the stock already prices in about 17%/yr FCF growth for a decade versus a ~13%/yr evidence-based base case, so it is a "great business, full price," not a name to add at the current price.

1. Business in plain English

GE Aerospace designs, manufactures and services jet engines for commercial aircraft (Commercial Engines & Services, "CES" — LEAP via the 50/50 CFM International joint venture with Safran, plus GEnx, GE90) and military/defense propulsion (Defense & Propulsion Technologies, "DPT" — T700, F110, Avio Aero). It makes most of its money the way razor-blade businesses do: engines are often sold near breakeven, and the real profit comes from decades of high-margin spare parts, overhaul and repair ("shop visits") on an installed base of ~50,000 commercial and ~30,000 military engines. GE Aerospace is the standalone industrial successor to the old General Electric conglomerate, following the 2023 spin-off of GE HealthCare and the April-2024 spin-off of GE Vernova; the consolidated entity still carries a legacy run-off insurance block and a Polish mortgage portfolio (Bank BPH) from the old GE Capital, which are not part of the aerospace operating business (see §6, §12 for entity-scope detail).

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1 quant composite is moderate (composite 0.413, decile 5, live_rank 292) — Quality (fam_Q 0.599) and Momentum/Earnings-momentum (fam_M 0.522, fam_S 0.524) are all mid-to-upper range, but Value (fam_V 0.262) is weak (earnings yield 2.6%, FCF yield 2.5%, both raw and low) reflecting the rich multiple. The fundamental triage independently scored quality 5/5, growth 4/5 with no disqualifying red flags — "21% revenue growth on the LEAP ramp and a widening services backlog justify a 35x NTM P/E." The durability case (a duopoly moat, a multi-decade aftermarket annuity as the young LEAP fleet ages into its first shop visits) is well evidenced in the filed backlog and delivery data below and is genuinely different in kind from a cyclical growth story.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — a genuine oligopoly imaging/diagnostics franchise with record orders and backlog, but the reservation is specific and named: full-year 2026 guidance was cut once already (tariffs, input-cost inflation, a struggling Patient Care Solutions segment) and first-half free-cash-flow conversion is unusually weak (~19% of net income), so near-term earnings quality is softer than the headline 16.5% EPS growth suggests. GE HealthCare designs, makes and services medical imaging equipment (CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray/mammography), patient-monitoring hardware, and pharmaceutical imaging agents (contrast media, radiotracers) used by hospitals and clinics worldwide. dossiers.GEV:
GEV — GE Vernova Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F44, wave 2, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH — overturns triage's implicit "price is fine" read (price_vs_growth 4/5). This is a genuinely strong, accelerating business (backlog $176bn, orders +88% organically in 2Q26, guidance raised in each of the last three quarters), but the 25-Sep-2026 close prices in roughly 20%+ annualized growth for a decade — well above a defensible base case. Per the wave-2 mandate, a great business priced for more than it can deliver is WATCH, not INCLUDE. Thesis horizon: revisit if the multiple de-rates or backlog conversion confirms the 2028 outlook is on track without relying on Wind-segment improvement that the numbers don't yet show.

2. Business in plain English

GE Vernova (spun off from General Electric in 2024) makes the equipment that generates and moves electricity: gas turbines and related services (Power segment), grid/transformer/switchgear equipment increasingly sold into AI data centers (Electrification), and wind turbines (Wind, structurally loss-making). It sells to utilities, independent power producers, grid operators and, increasingly, data-center developers and their power suppliers — riding the AI-driven electricity-demand buildout.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q09) cited a $176B backlog, gas-turbine backlog growing from 100 to 116+ GW, data-center electrification orders exceeding all of 2025 in Q1'26 alone, and guidance raised each of the last two quarters, concluding the elevated 36x NTM multiple was supported. Diligence confirms every one of those facts from primary sources (2Q26 press release, filed 2026-07-22) and adds a third consecutive guidance raise (see §5) — the momentum is real and durable in the sense that it is order-book-driven, not accounting-driven, in Power and Electrification. The valuation conclusion does not survive contact with the numbers, however (see §7): the market is not pricing "strong growth," it is pricing growth at a pace GE Vernova's own long-range outlook does not project past 2028.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Balance sheet: $3.72bn total debt vs $12.72bn cash and short-term investments (d4 snapshot, 2026-09-25) — net cash of roughly $9bn, minimal leverage risk. Capital returned to shareholders: $3.6bn (FY2025), $1.4bn (1Q26), a further $2.5bn (2Q26, cumulative $3.9bn YTD) — includes a $0.50/share quarterly dividend and buybacks; dividend yield is negligible (~0.2%) so this is predominantly buybacks.
  • Segment quality — Wind is a live, unreconciled red flag: FY2025 Wind segment EBITDA loss was −$598mm (full year).   • Segment strength: Power segment EBITDA margin 18.8% (2Q26) and Electrification 18.4% (2Q26), both expanding meaningfully y/y (+245bps and +357bps respectively on the quarter) — the parts of the business actually driving the guidance raises are executing well.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (own model; no V1 row exists for GEV)

No V1 systematic valuation row exists for GEV — v1_verdict is null. Standard capital-goods valuation (EV/EBITDA, not FCFF DCF given the WC-driven FCF noted above) at the 25-Sep-2026 close of $957.63 (market cap $255.0bn; EV ≈ $246.1bn using $3.72bn debt and $12.72bn cash, per d4 snapshot) against FY2026 guidance-midpoint adjusted EBITDA of ~$5.98bn (46bn revenue × 13% margin midpoint) implies ~41x forward EV/EBITDA. Reverse-DCF: solving for the 10-year EBITDA CAGR that justifies this EV at a 10% discount rate and a 14x exit multiple (a reasonable mid-cycle multiple for a scaled, still-growing capital-goods/grid-equipment franchise) requires ~22–23% annualized EBITDA growth for 10 straight years; even generous assumptions (16x exit multiple, 9% discount rate) still require ~20%. My own base case — GE Vernova's own 2028 outlook ($56bn revenue, 20% margin ≈ $11.2bn EBITDA, implying ~37%/yr for the next two years) decelerating over years 3–10 toward a still-strong 8–10%/yr as the AI-power capex supercycle normalizes toward broader grid/utility capex growth — blends to roughly ~14%/yr over 10 years. Implied vs base: above. The stock is priced for continued hyper-growth well beyond the company's own explicit two-year outlook; per the eligibility rule, this makes GEV ineligible for INCLUDE/INCLUDE-SMALL regardless of how good the underlying business is.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Orders +88% organically (2Q26) and backlog +$13bn sequentially for two consecutive quarters show the AI/data-center power buildout is, if anything, still accelerating, not decelerating. (2) Power segment margin expansion (18.8% and rising) shows genuine operating leverage, not just volume. (3) Net cash balance sheet plus $12bn+ of FCF guided gives enormous flexibility to fund capacity expansion (management's own 20 GW→24 GW→30 GW gas-turbine output ramp) without dilution. Bear: (1) The valuation (~41x forward EV/EBITDA, ~20%+ implied 10-year growth) leaves no room for even a modest disappointment — a single guidance miss would likely produce a large de-rating. (2) Wind segment losses are running well ahead of the company's own stated full-year guidance with no public reconciliation — either a forecasting problem or an undisclosed 2H26 assumption; either way it is evidence the guidance numbers deserve more scrutiny than the "raised every quarter" headline suggests. (3) The FY2026 FCF guide nearly doubled in one quarter on a much smaller revenue/margin guide change — consistent with a working-capital/progress-billing tailwind from backlog growth that would reverse if order intake decelerates, meaning today's FCF yield may overstate sustainable cash generation.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Quarterly order growth (y/y, organic) falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (vs +71% 1Q26, +88% 2Q26).
  2. Adjusted EBITDA margin fails to reach the 12–14% FY2026 guided range in either 3Q or 4Q2026.
  3. FY2026 Wind segment EBITDA loss is confirmed (at FY2026 results) to exceed $700 million (vs the standing ~$400mm guide), i.e., the current guidance/actuals gap is never reconciled.
  4. Free cash flow for 2H2026 comes in below $5 billion combined (i.e., the raised $11.5–12.5bn FY guide is not met), confirming the 2Q26 FCF jump was working-capital timing rather than sustainable.
  5. EV/forward-adjusted-EBITDA multiple compresses below 25x without a corresponding fundamental deterioration (a valuation-only de-rating would be the point at which this name becomes newly investable on the same fundamentals).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results not yet dated in the filings reviewed; based on the 22 Jul / 22 Apr / 28 Jan release cadence, estimate mid-to-late October 2026 (unconfirmed — flagged as an estimate). CEO Scott Strazik's stated near-term milestones: 20 GW annual gas-turbine output run-rate by 3Q2026, "at least 125 GW" of gas equipment under contract by year-end 2026.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, restatements, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation disclosures found in the press-release exhibits reviewed. The Wind-segment guidance/actuals gap (§6) is the primary quantitative red flag from this diligence pass and was not identified by triage. Limitation: the 10-Q/10-K Legal Proceedings sections and insider Form 4 activity were not separately reviewed within this time-box — flagged as gaps.

dossiers.GILD:
GILD — Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Diligence dossier, F85)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — durable HIV franchise plus a genuine new blockbuster (Yeztugo) supports the thesis, but I size this smaller than a plain INCLUDE because (a) Q2 2026 shows Gilead is deploying very large sums into early-stage oncology/IPR&D (Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro Medicines) with a $1.75B Trodelvy impairment in the same quarter, raising execution and capital-allocation risk, and (b) no V1 systematic valuation row exists yet to cross-check against. Horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Gilead is a biopharmaceutical company best known for HIV treatment (Biktarvy, the market-leading single-tablet regimen) and, since mid-2025, HIV prevention (Yeztugo/lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable PrEP shot — the first of its kind). It also owns Kite (CAR-T cell therapies for blood cancers), a liver-disease franchise, and is building an oncology pipeline through recent acquisitions. It makes money selling patented drugs mostly to US/European health systems and payers, with patent-protected pricing power on its lead HIV products.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage flagged quality 4/5, growth 4/5, but noted the trailing margin/ROE looked negative and needed confirming as a one-off (Q06_triage.json, GILD entry). Confirmed: Q2 2026 GAAP net loss of −$10.496B (EPS −$8.45) was driven by $11.2B of acquired IPR&D expense (Arcellx $7.0B, Tubulis $3.1B, Ouro Medicines ~$1.0B net) plus a $1.75B Trodelvy NSCLC impairment after the Phase 3 EVOKE-03 trial was discontinued (company Q2 2026 earnings release/ prepared remarks, 4 Aug 2026; corroborated by SEC 10-Q for period 2026-06-30, accession 0000882095-26-000031, filed 2026-08-06). This is a real, one-time (non-recurring) accounting charge on top of real cash M&A spend — the underlying commercial business (revenue +10% YoY in Q2 2026 to $7.803B) is healthy and growing. The quant model's negative trailing ROE is therefore an artefact of this charge, not a signal of core deterioration — but the cash cost of the acquisitions themselves (and the debt raised to help fund them) is real and increases balance-sheet risk versus a year ago.

4. Last 8 quarters (GAAP, USD; SEC XBRL companyconcept, CIK 0000882095)
