1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). [Corrected 2026-10-08: verdict restated INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH: the dossier's own probability-weighted value ($155, 31% below the price) and a reverse DCF that needs about 7.9% a year at the programme cost of equity do not support inclusion; see Correction DV23] Thesis horizon: 12–24 months. JBHT is a genuinely high-quality, low-leverage, non-union logistics franchise showing real evidence of a freight-cycle inflection (Q2 FY26 revenue +19% YoY, intermodal operating income +58%), but the stock's 31x trailing / ~24x NTM P/E already prices a durable recovery that is one quarter old, management itself declined to extrapolate ("careful in ensuring Intermodal is the correct long-term answer" rather than chasing volume — CFO/COO on the Q2'26 call), and two of five segments (Final Mile, Truckload) are shrinking or losing money. Half-weight reflects strong conviction on business quality, low conviction on the entry price.

2. Business in plain English

J.B. Hunt is a US surface-transportation and logistics company operating through five segments: Intermodal (JBI — the largest, moving freight in containers via rail plus company-owned drayage trucks), Dedicated Contract Services (DCS — trucks and drivers committed to a single customer's network), Integrated Capacity Solutions (ICS — an asset-light freight brokerage matching shippers with third-party carriers), Final Mile Services (big-and-bulky home delivery), and Truckload (JBT — traditional over-the-road trucking). It makes money by charging shippers (retailers, manufacturers, e-commerce companies) for capacity and network reliability, competing on service and price against rail-owned intermodal competitors, other asset-based truckers, and brokers.

3. Why the model likes it

From the preliminary quant screen (lead_prelim_rank.csv, families Q/V/M; official point-in-time scores not yet live): JBHT ranks #12 of ~500 S&P names, prelim composite 0.814, driven by top-decile Quality (0.968) and top-decile Momentum (0.978), with only middling Value (0.495 — it is not cheap). The Quality score is durable and evidenced independently here: ROE ~16–19%, ROIC ~13.5–15%, net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x, zero unionized labor, strong buybacks funded from internally generated cash (see §6). The Momentum score is largely an artefact of one quarter — FY2025 segment revenue was essentially flat (Intermodal +0.3%, DCS -0.6%, Final Mile -9.5%) and the acceleration is entirely a 2026 phenomenon (Q1'26 revenue +4.6% YoY, Q2'26 +19.4% YoY) tied to a specific, checkable cause: industry-wide truckload capacity tightening plus "road-to-rail" conversion, not a structural re-rating of the whole business. Whether this is durable is precisely the open question this dossier flags as the central risk.

Acceleration is real but narrow and recent. Segment detail for Q2'26 (per the Q2'26 earnings release, source [4]): Intermodal revenue +22% (load volume +10%, i.e. real volume growth, not just price/fuel), operating income +58%; Dedicated +9% revenue; ICS (brokerage) +49% revenue and flipped from a loss to a small profit; Final Mile -6% revenue (management disclosed a deliberate $90M revenue headwind from "disciplined account management" — i.e., walking away from unprofitable volume, per the Q2'26 call, source [5]); Truckload +35% revenue but an operating loss (source [4]), as purchased-transportation cost inflation outpaced the segment's own rate increases. Adverse fact, not softened: operating cash flow was down year-over-year in H1'26 ($723.3M vs $806.2M in H1'25, per source [3] XBRL) despite higher earnings — consistent with working-capital consumption (receivables) from the volume surge; FCF was still up YoY only because capex fell even faster (H1'26 capex $144.9M vs H1'25 $399.1M, a 64% cut, source [4]) [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong figures: $144.9M and $399.1M are net cash used in investing (after equipment sale proceeds); gross additions to property and equipment were $227.2M vs $462.3M, a 51% cut; the FCF figures of $496.1M and $343.9M do use gross additions].

5. Guidance track record

JBHT does not issue formal quantitative revenue or EPS guidance — consistent across all of the last four releases (Q3'25, Q4'25/FY25, Q1'26, Q2'26 earnings calls) — so there is no "raised/maintained/cut vs. prior range" table to build for the headline numbers, and no prior report should have claimed otherwise. The one quantified, trackable guidance item is the effective tax rate: full-year 2026 guidance was narrowed on the Q2'26 call to 24.0%–24.5%, versus an effective rate of ~25.4% realized in Q2'26 itself and ~24.8% for FY2025 — a modest tightening, not a raise or cut of substance. Beyond that, management gives only qualitative color: on Q2'26 it guided to demand "remain[ing] strong" through H2 2026 and a peak season "similar" in timing/shape to 2025, explicitly declining to quantify the intermodal volume outlook when pressed by analysts (Evercore's Jon Chappell asked directly whether June's growth rate could hold; management would not commit to a number).

FCF conversion: FY2025 FCF/NI = 947.6/598.3 = 158% (capex well below D&A in a low-investment year); TTM-through-Q2'26 conversion is even higher given the capex pullback — but see the OCF-decline point in §4, which is the more important quality signal than the FCF/NI ratio in isolation. SBC: not separately broken out in the sources reviewed here — flagged as a gap [Corrected 2026-10-08: share-based compensation was $71.8M in FY2025 and $38.1M in H1 2026 (companyfacts); TTM FCF of about $1.10bn is about $1.03bn after SBC]; recommend the valuation/quant team pull ShareBasedCompensation from XBRL directly. GAAP vs. adjusted: minimal gap — JBHT does not report a separate adjusted EPS; the only routinely-cited non-GAAP figure is "revenue excluding fuel surcharge" for volume/mix analysis. 7. Valuation snapshot

NTM P/E (calendarized) 24.1x; trailing P/E 31.4x (via valuation.py EV bridge: EV $22.39B on TTM EBITDA $1.67B → EV/EBITDA 13.4x, EV/EBIT 23.4x); FCF yield 4.3–4.5%. Against its own history, JBHT has historically traded in a wide range (high-single-digit to mid-20s trailing P/E, richest at earnings troughs and cheapest at peaks — a cyclical inversion the sector playbook explicitly warns about), so today's multiple sits at the rich end even before judging the recovery's durability. Against peers, JBHT is actually the cheapest of the large-cap truckers on forward P/E — Old Dominion Freight Line ~35–39x forward, Knight-Swift ~34–36x forward, versus JBHT's ~24–30x depending on source — but "cheapest of an expensive peer group" is not the same as cheap. Reverse-DCF (via valuation.py, WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3%): the current EV already implies ~6% per-year FCF growth for a full decade [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated: at the programme cost of equity 10.11% (5.17% + Blume beta 1.193 x 4.14%), TTM FCF after SBC about $1.03bn and market cap about $21.3bn, the price implies about 7.9% a year for ten years then 3% (the 6% at WACC 8.5% could not be reproduced: 4.3% at 8.5% on the same inputs)] — a plausible but non-trivial hurdle for a historically cyclical trucker whose FY2025 revenue was flat. A probability-weighted bear/base/bull scenario (bear $5.50 EPS/16x, base $7.20/22x, bull $8.50/27x) centers on $155/share, ~31% below the current price — i.e. the market is already underwriting meaningfully more than this dossier's base case.

Valuation reconciliation with V1 (added 2026-09-26): V1 rates JBHT "fair" (score −0.03, essentially neutral), with a base-case 3-year annualized return of +6.4% — implying a price near $266 in three years versus $225.46 spot — and notes this stays inside the Street's 12-month target range ($182–370, so no internal street-flag caution is raised). This dossier's own probability-weighted bear/base/bull scenario above centers on $155/share, about 31% below the current price, and §3/§7 state plainly that the stock's 31.4x trailing / 24.1x NTM P/E already "prices a durable recovery that is one quarter old" and that "the market is already underwriting meaningfully more than this dossier's base case." The two are not reconcilable as a rounding difference: V1 sees modest further upside, this dossier sees material downside risk to fair value. This dossier's more cautious reading is better supported, because it rests on current, concrete facts a trailing-multiple model does not see: the freight-cycle inflection is one quarter old and management itself declined to extrapolate it (§3/§9); two of five segments (Truckload, Final Mile) are shrinking or unprofitable (§4/§9); and H1 FY26 operating cash flow fell year-over-year despite higher earnings (§4/§9). V1's own-history percentile (36.7%, on NTM P/E) is not itself a red flag, so the two models are not flatly contradictory on every input — but on the bottom-line valuation call, the dossier's downside-weighted scenario is the better-evidenced one, consistent with this dossier's smaller, INCLUDE-SMALL sizing.

8. Bull case

  1. Verified, real freight-cycle inflection, not just a comp effect: Q2'26 intermodal load volume +10% (units, not just price) alongside operating leverage (JBI operating income +58% on +22% segment revenue), and management cites industry-wide capacity tightening (safety enforcement, driver-market tightness) as the structural driver — a classic late-cycle-to-recovery signal for a bellwether name.
  2. Balance sheet and capital discipline are genuinely excellent: net debt/EBITDA ~1x, zero union exposure, debt down ~$570M YoY, and $135M of structural cost already removed with "additional runway" cited by management — this is a company that used the freight downturn to get leaner, not just survive it.
  3. Record dedicated-fleet sales pipeline ("record level in terms of number of trucks," per DCS president, exceeding COVID-era peaks) and record "mini-bid" frequency across the network suggest share-of-wallet gains are still to come through 2027, independent of the broader freight cycle.

9. Bear case

  1. One good quarter does not confirm a cycle turn, and management itself would not commit to extrapolating June's growth rate — the stock has already re-rated as if it has. A reversion of intermodal pricing/volume in H2'26 (management flagged rail-service "moderation" as volumes accelerated, a potential constraint) would be a straightforward disappointment against a 24x NTM multiple.
  2. Two of five segments are structurally weak right now: Truckload is losing money on purchased-transportation inflation despite 35% revenue growth (a genuine earnings-quality flag — growth funded by higher-cost outsourced capacity, not owned assets), and Final Mile revenue is shrinking by management's own choice. A "sum of the parts" investor would not pay a premium multiple for either.
  3. OCF fell year-over-year in H1'26 even as earnings rose — working-capital consumption from the volume surge is a real, current adverse fact, not a hypothetical risk, and the FCF improvement it's paired with was capex-driven (capex -64% YoY) rather than earnings-driven; capex cannot fall indefinitely if volume growth is to be sustained.

10. Key risks & kill criteria

These are the specific, observable, time-bound conditions that would invalidate the INCLUDE-SMALL thesis above: - Intermodal revenue growth (ex-fuel) decelerates back below ~5% YoY for two consecutive quarters — the core recovery thesis fails. - Truckload (JBT) segment operating losses persist for more than two more quarters without a clear path to breakeven from pricing actions. - Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x (would indicate the buyback/capex-cut strategy has outrun cash generation). - OCF conversion (OCF/NI) stays below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters, signaling the working-capital drag is structural rather than transitory. - Any loss of the "record" DCS sales pipeline translating to signed, revenue-generating fleet growth within the stated 12–18 month cycle.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-15 (Q3 2026, per company snapshot data; confirm closer to date). 2027 intermodal bid season commentary (management flagged growing optimism into it) is the next major qualitative catalyst, likely discussed on the Q3'26 and Q4'26 calls. No investor day identified in the filings reviewed.

dossiers.JBL:
Jabil Inc. (NYSE: JBL) — Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon), reservation: the model's growth read is real and guidance has been raised in back-to-back quarters, but core EMS operating margins remain thin (GAAP operating margin 5.1% in FQ3 FY26) and the balance sheet has taken on incremental debt and a doubling of goodwill/intangibles in nine months to fund M&A (Hanley Energy Group and others), while equity has been shrunk to near-parity with liabilities by aggressive buybacks — a structurally low-equity-cushion balance sheet even though liquidity and cash generation are currently fine.

2. Business in plain English

Jabil is an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company: it builds and assembles electronics — from data-center power/cooling gear to automotive electronics to healthcare devices — under contract for other companies' brands, and is increasingly selling its own higher-value power, thermal and networking infrastructure content into AI data centers (via its Intelligent Infrastructure segment and the 2025/26 Hanley Energy Group acquisition).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Triage cited "11.8% revenue growth and 111% EPS growth from AI-related mix shift" at 18.8x NTM P/E with 36% Street upside, flagging "thin core EMS margins (2.6%)... high ROE partly reflects a small equity base from buybacks rather than pure business quality." The revenue and EPS growth are corroborated by the primary filings and have accelerated, not decelerated, over the last two quarters (see §4) — durable in the sense that management is raising guidance on it every quarter, not a one-off beat. However, the triage's own caution about a shrunken equity base is confirmed and, if anything, understated: total Jabil Inc. consolidated stockholders' equity fell from $1,513M (Aug-25) to $1,323M (May-26) even as total consolidated assets grew from $18.5B to $23.8B, i.e. consolidated leverage (assets/equity) rose from ~12.2x to ~18.0x in nine months — this is a genuine artefact risk for any ROE-based factor score.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) guidance raised in both of the last two quarters on revenue, margin, EPS and FCF simultaneously; (2) core operating margin trend is improving (4.5%→5.3%→5.8% quarter over quarter into FQ4 guide); (3) FCF conversion stayed >100% of core earnings even while investing heavily in M&A. Bear: (1) core EMS margins remain structurally thin and cyclical — a swing in AI-capex sentiment would hit Intelligent Infrastructure hard; (2) consolidated stockholders' equity has been run down to $1.3B against $22.5B of consolidated total liabilities, an unusually thin cushion that limits room for a downside surprise without a covenant or rating concern; (3) debt-funded M&A (Hanley Energy Group and others) roughly doubled consolidated goodwill/intangibles in nine months, adding both integration risk and future amortization/impairment risk.

  1. Core operating margin (Non-GAAP) falls below 5.0% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 5.8% FQ3 FY26 actual and 5.8% FY26 full-year guide).
  2. Total Jabil Inc. stockholders' equity (consolidated) falls below $1.0 billion at any quarter-end.
  3. Consolidated net debt (notes payable and long-term debt, less cash) exceeds $3.5 billion at any quarter-end (vs. ≈$2.0B at May-26).
  4. FY26 or FY27 guidance is cut (not raised) versus the immediately prior range at any quarterly release.
  5. Adjusted free cash flow conversion (adjusted FCF / core earnings) falls below 70% for two consecutive quarters.

KeyCorp is the holding company for KeyBank, National Association, a regional bank operating mainly in the Northeast, Midwest, Mountain West and Pacific Northwest. 1. Verdict

Keysight designs and sells electronic test-and-measurement instruments and software used to validate chips, wireless networks (5G/6G), satellites, and defense electronics before they ship. Implied growth (~13%) is above my base case (~8–9%) — this is a good business priced for a cycle that doesn't mean- revert, which per the mandate makes it WATCH, not INCLUDE, even though the trend is genuinely strong right now.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) AI-accelerator and 6G R&D test-capex is a multi-year, not one-year, upswing — backlog/orders could keep surprising high. (2) Net-cash balance sheet gives room to buy back stock or bolt on software/IP without dilution. (3) Software/subscription mix shift raises structural margins over time.

Bear: (1) Semiconductor capex is famously cyclical — a 2019- or 2023-style capex air pocket would hit orders before revenue, and the stock is priced at ~50x TTM EPS for a hardware-heavy business. (2) A single-customer or single-node (e.g., leading-edge AI chip) slowdown could remove a large slice of the current growth. (3) Multiple compression risk: even flat fundamentals at a normalized ~30–35x multiple implies material downside from $362.

9. Kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Quarterly revenue growth decelerates below +15% YoY for two consecutive quarters (signals the AI/test capex cycle has crested).
  2. Order backlog or book-to-bill ratio (next earnings release) falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Diluted EPS growth YoY drops below +15% for two consecutive quarters.
  4. Net cash position turns negative (i.e., debt-funded buyback/M&A that changes the balance-sheet risk profile).
  5. Forward P/E stays above 45x TTM EPS while revenue growth decelerates below 15% — valuation/fundamentals gap widening rather than closing.

dossiers.KKR:
KKR & Co. Inc. (KKR) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F111, Wave 7)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (12–36 month horizon). Reason: durable, compounding fee/AUM franchise trading at a valuation that, on a reverse-DCF basis, implies far less growth than KKR has delivered or guides toward [Corrected 2026-10-08: KKR gives no numeric guidance; implied growth is ~8-10%, in line with the 10-12% base, see Correction sections] — but the Global Atlantic insurance/annuity book adds real earnings volatility and duration risk that the quant model's worst-in-batch rank (per Q04 triage) is at least partly pricing correctly, so full weight is not warranted.

2. Business in plain English

KKR is a global alternative-asset manager (private equity, credit, infrastructure, real assets, capital markets) that earns management and performance fees on ~$796bn of assets under management (AUM), plus balance-sheet investment gains. Since 2021 it has also owned 100% of Global Atlantic, a fixed-annuity/life-insurance platform whose "spread" income (investment yield minus policyholder crediting rate) is now folded into KKR's "Insurance Operating Earnings." It makes money from (a) recurring management fees on locked-up capital, (b) performance fees ("carry") when funds exit investments profitably, and (c) insurance float invested into KKR's own credit strategies. Competitive position: top-3 global alternative manager alongside Blackstone and Apollo, differentiated by the insurance-balance-sheet flywheel that funds origination.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Q04 triage flagged 13.6x NTM P/E and strong forward growth, but the worst statistical-model rank in the batch (495/500) and negative 12-month momentum (-15%), largely attributable to Global Atlantic's private-credit/annuity exposure and sector-wide insurance-affiliate concerns (flagged alongside Apollo in Mar 2026 press). My read: the low-multiple, high-growth combination is durable at the segment level — Total Operating Earnings (management fees + insurance + strategic holdings; management's preferred "more durable and recurring" metric) rose 19% LTM to $5.5bn (2Q'26 LTM) from $4.7bn (2Q'25 LTM), and 84% of segment earnings now come from these more-recurring sources per the 2Q'26 earnings release. The negative momentum/model rank looks like a market discount for insurance-book opacity, not a break in the fee-earning franchise — but it is not an "artefact" either; it is a real, currently-unresolved risk (Section 6).

dossiers.KLAC:
KLA Corporation (KLAC) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F28, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH — not now, on valuation discipline, not business quality. KLA is the best-moat business of the three names in this batch, and the triage's quality/growth scores (5/5) are well supported by primary data. But the reverse DCF shows the price already assumes a growth rate this industry has never sustained for a full decade, even in this AI-capex supercycle. A great business priced for more than it can plausibly deliver is a WATCH under this program's own pre-committed rule, not an INCLUDE. Horizon if it re-rates or grows into the multiple: 24–48 months.

2. Business in plain English

KLA makes process-control and yield-management equipment (inspection and metrology tools) that semiconductor fabs use to find defects during manufacturing. It holds the leading share in this sub-segment of semicap equipment — every advanced logic and memory fab, and increasingly every advanced-packaging line, needs its tools regardless of which chipmaker wins the underlying race, which gives it a toll-booth-like position on the entire industry's capital spending rather than exposure to any single customer's success.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: composite 0.46 (live_rank 270/503 — a lower composite than FSLR/GEN because KLA scores weakly on the Value family at today's price, which is exactly the tension this dossier resolves). Triage (Q12_triage.json) called it the "best moat in semicap," citing a 33x NTM P/E as fair for 15% revenue and 83% EPS growth. Verified: the growth numbers are real and accelerating — Q1 FY26 revenue +13.0% YoY, Q2 +7.2%, Q3 +11.5%, Q4 FY26 +15.2% YoY (all SEC XBRL, cross- checked against earnings releases), and FY2026 GAAP net income grew to $4.83bn (FY2025: $4.06bn, FY2024: $2.76bn) — a genuine acceleration, not a one-quarter blip. China revenue concentration has been falling, not rising, as a risk (29.8% of FY2026 revenue vs 33.3% FY2025 and 42.8% FY2024, per the FY2026 10-K), which reduces (does not eliminate) the export-control tail risk. What needs adjustment: the "33x NTM P/E is fair for 83% EPS growth" framing understates how much growth is already priced in over a full decade, not just next year — see §7. It is durable near-term, not an artefact, but the multiple is pricing perpetuity-level assumptions onto a single strong year.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Cash conversion — data conflict corrected: FY2026 (annual) operating cash flow = $4,143.1m (SEC XBRL, 10-K); FY2026 capex = $375.9m. Primary-sourced TTM FCF ≈ $3,767.1m. Investment-grade-quality balance sheet.
  • Capital return: dividend raised to $2.30/share annualised [Corrected 2026-10-10: $2.30 is the new QUARTERLY dividend, pre-split (Q3 FY26 release, acc 0000319201-26-000014); post-split that is $0.23 a quarter, $0.92 annualised, about 0.5% yield] — the 17th consecutive annual increase — plus a new $7bn buyback authorisation and $2.29bn of FY2026 repurchases. 7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

Price 25-Sep-2026 close: $187.92 (post-split). Market cap $245.24bn. EV (net debt $1.25bn) ≈ $246.49bn. Trailing P/E 50.8x (elevated by the lower-margin early part of FY2026 still sitting in the trailing window); NTM P/E per d4's headline (reliable) field ≈ 28.0–32.7x depending on the exact forward-EPS vintage used. Trailing P/FCF on the corrected FCF figure = 65.4x; FCF yield 1.5%.

Reverse DCF (WACC 10.0%, terminal growth 3.5%, 10-year horizon, base FCF = corrected TTM $3,767.1m, EV anchor $246.49bn): implied stage-1 FCF growth ≈ 22.5% per year for 10 years. [Corrected 2026-10-10: FCF of $3,767.1m adds back stock-based compensation of $310.2m; with SBC treated as a cost (FCF $3,457m) the implied growth is about 23.6%, still above base] This is the key finding of this dossier: sustaining ~22–23% compound FCF growth for a full decade would require KLA's FCF to grow roughly 8x by 2036, in an industry that is structurally cyclical (semicap equipment order books historically swing with the 3–5 year memory/logic capex cycle). An evidence-based base case of roughly +12–14%/yr over 10 years (front-loaded high-teens-to-20% growth through the current AI-capex upcycle for 2–3 years, fading to high-single-digit growth as the cycle normalises and China-related headwinds persist) is well below the ~22.5%/yr the market is paying for. Implied vs base: above (expensive) — this is the reason for the WATCH verdict despite best-in-class business quality. No V1 systematic valuation exists for this name yet.

Scenario table (post-split GAAP EPS basis, 3-year horizon, dividend yield ~0.4%/yr added): | Scenario | Prob. | 3y-forward EPS | Exit P/E | Value/share | 3y annualised total return | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Bear | 30% | $5.00 | 20x | $100 | ~-19.5%/yr [Corrected 2026-10-10: recomputed from the table inputs: about -18.6%/yr] | | Base | 45% | $7.50 | 25x | $187.50 | ~+0.4%/yr | | Bull | 25% | $9.50 | 30x | $285 | ~+15.3%/yr |

Bear reflects a semicap-cycle downturn (memory/logic capex digestion after the current AI build-out) compounded with a tighter China export-control regime; base assumes the current growth trajectory moderates to a sustainable mid-teens rate and the multiple normalises from its currently elevated trailing level; bull assumes the AI capex cycle extends without a digestion phase.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Structurally the best-positioned company in semicap equipment — process control/inspection is needed regardless of which chipmaker or foundry wins the AI race, and KLA's share in this sub-segment is the highest in the industry (triage assessment, consistent with the accelerating, broad-based revenue growth seen across all four FY2026 quarters). (2) China revenue concentration is falling (42.8%→33.3%→29.8% over three fiscal years) even as absolute China revenue held roughly flat — the mix is diversifying away from the single largest geopolitical risk. (3) Fortress balance sheet (net debt ~$1.25bn against $245bn market cap) and a 17-year dividend-growth streak fund growth and buybacks simultaneously.

Bear: (1) The reverse DCF shows the market pricing ~22.5%/yr FCF growth for a decade — a bar this cyclical industry has not cleared over any historical 10-year window, including the most recent AI-driven upswing (KLA's own 3-year revenue CAGR into FY2026 is well under half that rate). (2) Export-control risk to China is not resolved, only reduced in relative weight — the FY2026 10-K explicitly attributes flat China revenue to export-control restrictions offsetting legacy-node capex, meaning further tightening could still cut absolute dollars, not just share. (3) Trailing P/FCF of ~65x (corrected figure) means the stock is priced overwhelmingly on the next several years' growth, not today's cash generation — a classic setup for a sharp de-rating if the semicap cycle turns even briefly.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Quarterly revenue YoY growth below 5% for two consecutive quarters (a classic early semicap-cycle-turn signal; currently accelerating at 7–15%).
  2. GAAP diluted EPS guidance cut at any subsequent release (currently 2-for-2 met/beaten in this pass's sample).
  3. China revenue share or absolute dollars fall further in a way the company attributes explicitly to new export restrictions (as opposed to the already-disclosed, gradually diversifying trend).
  4. Net debt/EBITDA (currently trivial) rises above 1.0x without a value-accretive reason disclosed (would signal a large, possibly dilutive, capital-allocation shift).
  5. Trailing P/FCF (corrected basis) stays above 50x for more than two quarters after revenue growth decelerates below 10% YoY — the combination that would confirm the market has not yet re-rated the stock down to the base case.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 28-Oct-2026 (Q1 FY2027, quarter ended 30-Sep-2026; company guided revenue $4.0bn ±$200m, GAAP diluted EPS $1.14 ±$0.10 at the Q4 FY26 release). No investor day identified in the sources reviewed.

  • No auditor changes, going-concern language, restatements, or unusual insider-selling pattern identified in the sources reviewed this pass.

KO — The Coca-Cola Company

Agent: F125 (wave 8 standard diligence). Price basis: 2026-09-25 close $87.81 (d4 snapshot, Yahoo); 4,302.5m shares -> mkt cap ~$377.8bn.

1. Verdict

WATCH — an exceptional, guidance-raising franchise, but at $87.81 (26.7–26.9x the implied 2026 comparable EPS of $3.27–3.30; ~3.3% FCF yield) the price implies ~6.5% 10-year FCF growth against my base of ~6%. Triage ("quality but wait for a pullback") is confirmed and the FCF-yield flag (1.4%) is explained: FY25 GAAP FCF carried a ~$6.1bn fairlife payment; normalised 2026 FCF guide is $12.4bn. Horizon 12–36 months. Would move to INCLUDE-SMALL near ~$78–80 (implied <= base) or on sustained 2027 EPS growth above 8% currency-neutral.

2. Business in plain English

Coca-Cola sells concentrates, syrups and finished beverages (Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Powerade, smartwater, Costa, fairlife) in 200+ countries, mostly via independent bottlers who buy concentrate; it earns a high margin (Q2'26 GAAP operating margin 34.9%) on brand and distribution, with low capital needs (capex ~$2.2bn). It is shedding capital-heavy bottling (African bottling operations sale to Coca-Cola HBC, held for sale).

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable

Quality and stability factors plus a +36% 12-month run (triage). Durable: unit case volume +5% in Q2'26, price/mix +2%, value share gains. Less durable: currency added ~2–3 points to EPS growth, Q1 had six extra days, and Q2 includes World Cup activation timing.

Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-10-21 (estimate; last year 2025-10-21, not confirmed in a filing); Africa bottling sale closing by end-2026; Eighth Circuit/Tax Court appeal steps; Feb 2027 2027 outlook; ex-dividend mid-Nov 2026 (Yahoo).

LDOS — Leidos Holdings, Inc.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months. A diversified US federal-government IT/defense/intel/health/civil contractor with a $48.7bn backlog, a clean four-quarter beat-and-raise FY2026, and a genuinely cheap valuation (9.8x NTM P/E, 7.4% FCF yield — a reverse DCF implies only ~3.6%/year 10-year FCF growth against guided ~7% FY2026 EPS growth even before crediting further M&A) [Corrected 2026-10-06: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint $12.35 vs FY2025 actual $11.99 is +3.0%, not 7%]. The named reservation: leverage jumped from ≈2.0x to ≈2.45x net debt/EBITDA [Corrected 2026-10-06: per the 10-Q and releases net debt is $5,283M on TTM adjusted EBITDA of $2,417M = 2.2x, up from 1.5x at year-end 2025] after a debt-funded $2.4bn acquisition (ENTRUST, closed 30 March 2026) that meaningfully changes the company's risk profile, and the triage's own flagged red flag — US federal budget/DOGE-era spending-cut policy risk to contract awards — is real, ongoing, and only partially tested so far (Leidos has weathered DOGE cancellations better than peers, but a 93-person WARN-notice layoff tied to a CBP contract change in March 2026 shows the risk is not merely theoretical). Half-weight reflects genuine business quality and a real margin of safety, offset by event-driven leverage and policy risk that a full-weight holding should not carry.

2. Business in plain English

Leidos is one of the largest US government IT-services and defense-technology contractors, organized into four reporting segments: Intelligence & Digital ($1,499m of Q2 2026 revenue, the largest segment — intelligence-community IT, cyber, digital modernization), Health ($1,086m — health IT and managed health services, including large VA/DHA contracts), Homeland ($1,018m — border/security/aviation screening technology, including TSA-related work), and Defense ($955m — defense systems, sensors, and the Dynetics missile-defense/hypersonics business). It earns money almost entirely from multi-year US federal government contracts (cost-plus, fixed-price, and time-and-materials mixes), competing on cleared personnel, incumbency, and technical differentiation rather than on price alone. The March 2026 acquisition of ENTRUST Solutions Group (energy-infrastructure engineering, ~3,100 professionals) is a deliberate diversification move — it roughly doubles Leidos' presence in electric-grid and natural-gas engineering, a non-federal, utility-customer revenue stream that reduces (modestly, at this scale) the company's near-total dependence on US government appropriations. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the pending divestiture of Security Enterprise Solutions and Industrial Automation into the Analogic JV (41.5% retained; assets held for sale $935M; closed 5 Oct 2026) is not mentioned anywhere in this dossier and will deconsolidate part of Homeland revenue]

3. Why the model likes it — and is it durable?

B1 composite is below the program median (live_rank 359/~2,300, decile 3, quintile 2; composite 0.277) — LDOS is not a broad quant favorite; it is here because of the triage's independent quality+growth+price-vs-growth screen. Family drivers: Value (fam_V ≈0.99, essentially the highest percentile in the program) — cheap on earnings yield, FCF yield and EBIT/EV; Quality (fam_Q ≈0.47, average); Momentum (fam_M ≈0.08, weak) and Earnings momentum (fam_S ≈0.15, weak) — the stock has not re-rated and recent EPS surprises have been unremarkable, consistent with a name the market is treating as a low-growth "value trap" candidate rather than rewarding for its guidance beats.

Durability check: the guidance beats are real and filed (see §5) — four straight raises through FY2026 [Corrected 2026-10-06: three raises (Q3 2025 EPS, Q1 and Q2 2026) plus one initial guide, no cuts], with FY2026 book-to-bill running 1.1–1.3x and funded backlog up sequentially. But a meaningful share of the FY2026 guidance raise (the +$500m revenue step-up between the initial February guide and the May Q1 guide) is explicitly attributed by management to the ENTRUST acquisition closing, not organic acceleration — organic growth in Q2 2026 was 4% against 7% total reported growth. The cheap valuation is durable relative to the current, verified profile (double-digit-percent free cash flow yield, growing backlog); whether the growth rate underlying it is durable depends materially on federal-budget/appropriations outcomes that are outside the company's control.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: company-guided FY2026 operating cash flow ≈$1.85bn against guided non-GAAP net income roughly consistent with $12.20–12.50 diluted EPS on ~126m shares (~$1.55bn) — FCF conversion above 100% on a non-GAAP basis, though GAAP net income (which includes acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs from ENTRUST) will run lower; TTM GAAP net income per the quant snapshot is $1,376m against TTM operating cash flow of $1,147m [Corrected 2026-10-06: actual TTM operating cash flow to 3 Jul 2026 is $2,300M (1,750 - 544 + 1,094) and TTM capex $137M; the $1,147m figure matches no trailing period] (a snapshot taken mid-transition, before Q2 2026's $793m OCF quarter is fully reflected in the trailing-twelve-month figure — treat the quant-snapshot FCF/OCF numbers as stale by one quarter).
  • SBC: not separately re-derived in this pass from XBRL (a scope limitation); Leidos discloses SBC in its 10-K and it has historically run in the low-single-digit percent of revenue range for this business model — not independently verified here.
  • GAAP vs adjusted: Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS $2.81 vs non-GAAP $3.26 — a $0.45/share gap (~14%), driven primarily by intangible-asset amortization (elevated post-ENTRUST) and acquisition/integration costs. This gap is disclosed by the company and is typical for a serial-acquirer government-services model, but it means the "12% EPS growth" language in guidance refers to the non-GAAP figure — GAAP diluted EPS growth is not equivalent and was not separately re-confirmed in this pass.
  • Net debt/leverage — the central balance-sheet finding of this dossier: LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations (XBRL) was $4,628m at 2026-01-02 (year-end 2025) and jumped to $6,014m at 2026-04-03 (Q1 2026) and $6,009m at 2026-07-03 (Q2 2026) — a ~$1.4bn increase that exactly matches the $1.4 billion senior notes offering (per Davis Polk/TipRanks reporting: $600m 4.100% notes due 2029 and $800m 5.000% notes due 2036, priced 2 March 2026, ~$1.387bn net proceeds) issued specifically to fund the ENTRUST acquisition. Against TTM EBITDA of $2,382m (quant snapshot, likely to rise post-ENTRUST), total debt/EBITDA is now ≈2.5x (cash $748m nets it to ≈2.45x) [Corrected 2026-10-06: 6,031 less 748 = 5,283 / 2,417 = 2.2x] — up from a comfortably lower ratio pre-acquisition. Not covenant-threatening for an investment-grade-rated government contractor, but a real, disclosed step-change in leverage that a half-weight (not full-weight) position should price in.
  • M&A: ENTRUST Solutions Group, ~$2.4bn, closed 2026-03-30, funded by the debt raise above; the notes carried a special mandatory redemption clause (101% of principal) if the deal had not closed — it did close, so this contingency lapsed. WARN notice: 93 employees laid off at an Ashburn, VA security-operations-center in March 2026 following a change to a US Customs and Border Protection contract — a small, specific, disclosed instance of the DOGE/contract-recompete risk the triage flagged.

7. Valuation snapshot — no V1 row; own reverse DCF

No systematic V1 valuation row exists for LDOS; v1_verdict is null in the summary JSON per program convention.

Quant snapshot (d4, as of 2026-09-25 close $123.61): NTM P/E 9.77x (pe_ntm), TTM FCF yield 7.4% (fcf_yield), EV/EBITDA ≈9.0x (EV $21,361m / EBITDA $2,382m — both likely to shift once ENTRUST is fully reflected in trailing EBITDA). Consensus targets: mean $157.27, range $132–225 (17 analysts, "buy" average).

Own reverse DCF (10-year explicit FCF growth + 2.5% terminal growth, 8.5% discount rate): solving EV = $21,361m for a constant annual FCF growth rate on a $1,147m (quant-snapshot TTM, likely conservative/stale — see §6) FCF base implies ≈3.6%/year for ten years. [Corrected 2026-10-06: that figure reproduces only on levered, partly stale FCF of $1,147m set against EV; on guided FY2026 operating cash flow less capex and SBC ($1.62bn) against the $15.6bn market cap the price implies about -5% a year (about -2.8% unlevered); still far below base] Against a base case of ~7% non-GAAP EPS growth (per FY2026 guidance, itself boosted by ENTRUST) and mid-single-digit organic growth even before M&A, the implied growth sits meaningfully below what the evidence supports — consistent with the triage's own "7.4% FCF yield against a required growth of only ~1.6%" framing (my own model, with a slightly different discount rate and terminal-growth assumption, arrives at a similar conclusion: cheap).

Bear/base/bull cases (own construction, 3-year horizon, exit-multiple method): - Bear: non-GAAP EPS growth slows to 2%/year (a DOGE/budget-driven contract-cancellation or extended government-shutdown scenario, plus ENTRUST integration friction), exit multiple compresses to 9x NTM (a further de-rate on federal-budget fear, below today's already-low 9.8x) → EPS ≈$13.44, price ≈$120.9, annualised total return ≈+0.7% including dividends. - Base: non-GAAP EPS growth 7%/year (consistent with FY2026 guidance and the company's stated long-term algorithm of mid-single-digit organic growth plus accretive M&A) [Corrected 2026-10-06: FY2026 guidance implies only about +3% EPS growth; at 4% a year the base scenario return is about +9.2%, not +12.4%], exit multiple 11x (a mild re-rate toward defense-IT peer averages, still below the broad market) → EPS ≈$15.51, price ≈$170.6, annualised total return ≈+12.4%. - Bull: non-GAAP EPS growth 11%/year (continued accretive M&A, margin expansion, and Golden Dome/cyber demand tailwinds referenced on the Q3 2025 call), exit multiple 13x → EPS ≈$17.31, price ≈$225.1, annualised total return ≈+23.0%.

The implied 10-year growth (3.6%) sits well below my own base case (7%/year) [Corrected 2026-10-10: the base case is about 4% a year after the DVH5 correction; implied (about -5%) remains below], satisfying the INCLUDE test — but the half-weight reflects that the quality of the "cheap" signal is weaker than BR's: post-acquisition leverage and unresolved federal-budget-policy risk are real, current-period concerns, not merely valuation caution.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Four consecutive quarters of guidance raises in FY2026 (revenue and non-GAAP EPS both raised at Q1 and Q2) [Corrected 2026-10-10: three raises (Q3 2025 EPS, Q1 and Q2 2026) plus one initial guide, no cuts], a 1.1–1.3x book-to-bill and $48.7bn total backlog ($10.2bn funded) — real, filed evidence of demand, not merely a cheap multiple. 2. NTM P/E of 9.8x and a 7.4% FCF yield are genuinely inexpensive for a company guiding to high-single-digit EPS growth [Corrected 2026-10-10: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint $12.35 is +3.0% on FY2025 $11.99] — the reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in almost no growth. 3. The ENTRUST acquisition is a disclosed, deliberate diversification into non-federal, utility-customer revenue (energy-grid engineering) that — if integration goes to plan — reduces Leidos' near-total dependence on US federal appropriations over time, a structural de-risking the market has not yet given credit for.

Bear (3): 1. The triage's own flagged red flag is real and only partially tested: US federal budget/DOGE-era spending-cut policy risk to contract awards and backlog conversion. Leidos has weathered DOGE cancellations better than named peers (Accenture Federal, Deloitte Federal, IBM all lost more in disclosed cancellations), but the March 2026 WARN notice (93 jobs, Ashburn VA, tied to a CBP contract change) is a concrete, dated instance of the risk materializing at a small scale — a larger recompete loss or a prolonged government shutdown (a risk explicitly flagged by analysts per Federal News Network reporting) remains a live, unhedged exposure. 2. Net debt/EBITDA rose from a comfortable level to ≈2.45x in a single quarter via a $1.4bn debt-funded acquisition [Corrected 2026-10-10: net debt $5,283M over TTM adjusted EBITDA $2,417M is 2.2x, up from 1.5x at year-end 2025] — a real, disclosed change in risk profile that increases sensitivity to any combination of margin pressure and rate resets on the new notes (4.10% and 5.00% coupons). 3. A DOJ/SEC investigation stemming from a 2021 internal FCPA-related inquiry (international operations, third-party representatives) remains only partially resolved: the DOJ closed its investigation with no further action in December 2024, but the SEC investigation was still open as of the most recent 10-K reviewed in this search — an unresolved legal overhang, low in probability of material impact but not yet formally closed.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable) -- signposts that would change our verdict

  1. FY revenue or non-GAAP EPS guidance is cut versus the immediately prior quarter's guidance (zero cuts across the last four releases; four consecutive raises) [Corrected 2026-10-06: three raises and one initial guide, no cuts].
  2. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ≈2.45x currently) without a disclosed deleveraging plan.
  3. Organic revenue growth (excluding ENTRUST and any further M&A) falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters.
  4. A single contract recompete loss, cancellation, or government-shutdown-driven revenue disruption exceeding $300 million of annualized revenue is disclosed (calibrated as roughly 1.5x the scale of the March-2026 Ashburn WARN-notice event).
  5. The SEC's FCPA-related investigation (open since 2021) results in a formal enforcement action, fine, or admission of wrongdoing (currently: DOJ closed with no action Dec-2024; SEC status not confirmed closed as of the most recent 10-K reviewed). [Corrected 2026-10-06: replace with the DOJ Antitrust Division criminal investigation (Aug 2022 subpoena, 10-K and 10-Q Note 11): formal charge, plea, fine or accrual]

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, estimated 2026-11-03 (per d4 snapshot).
  • FY2026 year-end results (expected mid-February 2027) — first full read on ENTRUST's contribution and whether the FY2027 initial guide shows organic acceleration or continued M&A-driven growth.
  • Any federal budget/appropriations resolution or further government-shutdown risk in Q4 2026/Q1 2027 (a recurring, calendar-driven catalyst for the whole govcon sector).
  • Resolution (open or closed, with or without action) of the SEC's FCPA-related investigation.

11. Red-flag scan

  • SEC investigation (open, unresolved): stemming from a self-reported 2021 internal FCPA-related inquiry into international operations, third-party representatives and subcontractors; DOJ closed its parallel investigation with no further action in December 2024; the SEC investigation's current status was not confirmed as closed in the sources reviewed for this dossier — treated as an open item, not resolved. [Corrected 2026-10-06: not supported by the FY2025 10-K or Q2 10-Q, which contain no SEC/FCPA investigation; the disclosed live matter is an Aug 2022 grand jury subpoena in a criminal DOJ Antitrust Division investigation of three Intelligence Group procurements, still open with fines not estimable]
  • Workforce/contract-driven layoff: March 2026 WARN notice, 93 employees at an Ashburn, VA security-operations center, tied to a change in a US Customs and Border Protection contract — a small, dated, but concrete instance of DOGE/recompete risk.
  • Government-shutdown exposure: analysts have flagged shutdown risk to Leidos' execution/outlook (per Federal News Network reporting on vendor austerity measures, October 2025); no quantified company-specific impact was disclosed in the sources reviewed.
  • Leverage step-change: disclosed above (§6); not a red flag in the sense of concealment — fully disclosed via 8-K Items 1.01/2.01/2.03 and the 424B2 notes prospectuses — but a material, real change in risk that this dossier flags explicitly.
  • No auditor change, restatement, or going-concern language identified in the filings and news reviewed. Insider Form-4 activity was not separately reviewed in this pass (scope limitation, disclosed).

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL — thesis horizon: 12–24 months

Lennox is a high-quality, high-ROE HVAC compounder (Home Comfort Solutions residential/light-commercial plus a fast-growing Building Climate Solutions commercial arm) trading at a below-peer-group multiple. The triage's thesis — "best-in-class capital efficiency, priced cheaper than HVAC peers because of soft residential demand" — is largely confirmed, but this diligence pass surfaces one thing the triage's red-flag list did not capture: FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance was cut at the Q2 2026 release (to $23.00–$24.00 from $23.50–$25.00, i.e., the top end down $1.00/−4%, midpoint down ~3%), even as revenue-growth guidance was simultaneously raised (to ~8% from 6–7%, driven by a bigger acquisition contribution). LIN — Linde plc — Diligence Dossier (Agent F53, wave 3)

1. Verdict

WATCH — the world's largest industrial-gas company, an genuine oligopoly (with Air Liquide, Air Products) with a record, largely contracted project backlog and a real, evidenced string of guidance raises. But the reverse DCF implies growth above Linde's own guided long-term earnings algorithm, and the current elevated-capex phase (funding that backlog) is temporarily depressing free cash flow, making today's price look even more demanding on an FCF basis. A great business, priced for more than its own guidance says it will deliver — the addendum's own standard for WATCH, not INCLUDE. Horizon: revisit if the multiple de-rates or backlog conversion accelerates growth above the current guided range.

2. Business in plain English

Linde produces and distributes industrial and medical gases (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon, CO2, specialty gases) via on-site plants built next to large customers (steel, chemicals, refining, electronics/semiconductor fabs, healthcare), pipeline networks and bulk/cylinder delivery. On-site contracts are typically 15–20 year take-or-pay agreements passing through energy costs — very low volume/price risk once built. Moat: capital intensity, pipeline network density and long-term contracts make it nearly impossible for a new entrant to replicate a regional gas network; Linde, Air Liquide and Air Products effectively split the global on-site/merchant market.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv: pct_leverage 0.604 (moderate — Linde does carry meaningful debt to fund its capital-intensive network, discussed in §6), pct_roe 0.688, pct_accruals 0.271 (no accrual red flag). Value percentiles are weak (pct_ep 0.396, pct_fcfp 0.1875) — correctly flagged as expensive, driven by heavy current-year growth capex (see §6/§7) more than by earnings weakness. 8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) record $11B project backlog (record $8.1B sale-of-gas backlog) is largely contracted/take-or-pay, de-risking multi-year growth visibility; (2) three consecutive guidance raises show real execution momentum into a historically defensive, oligopolistic business; (3) electronics/semiconductor and clean-hydrogen end-markets provide a genuine secular growth optionality layer on top of the base industrial-gas business (data-center/AI-driven electricity and gas demand is a plausible tailwind, though not confirmed in Linde's own Q2 2026 release, which discussed "electronics" strength generically without naming AI/hyperscaler demand specifically — flagged as an unconfirmed narrative some investors use). Bear: (1) the reverse DCF and the company's own long-term EPS algorithm disagree by ~3-4 points a year — the market is pricing execution above what Linde itself promises; (2) net debt/EBITDA of 1.67x plus capex guidance raised to $5.5–6.0B (from an original $5.0–5.5B) means the balance sheet is being leaned on harder to fund growth, at a time global industrial production (steel, chemicals — core end markets) is only modestly growing; (3) Q4 2025 GAAP net income fell 11% YoY on purchase-accounting/restructuring items — a reminder that the 2018 Linde AG/Praxair merger still carries real amortization drag on GAAP results, and "adjusted" EPS is doing a lot of the guidance-beat work.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Net debt/EBITDA > 2.25x (vs. 1.67x today) without a disclosed, value-accretive reason (e.g., large M&A).
  2. Full-year adjusted-EPS guidance cut (vs. the immediately preceding range) — would break the three-quarter raise streak that is central to the bull case.

2. Business

Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defense prime, organized in four segments: Aeronautics (F-35, F-16, F-22 sustainment, C-130J, classified programs — largest segment), Missiles and Fire Control/MFC (PAC-3, THAAD, HIMARS, JASSM, LRASM, PrSM — fastest-growing, highest-margin segment), Rotary and Mission Systems/RMS (Sikorsky helicopters: Black Hawk, Seahawk, CH-53K, plus naval/radar systems), and Space (national-security space, GPS III, NASA Orion/Artemis). 8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Backlog at an all-time high ($230.4B, +31% in two quarters), with MFC backlog nearly doubling on funded, multi-year missile-production framework agreements against a structurally elevated global missile-defense demand backdrop. (2) The FY24/Q2'25 charge quarters appear to be flowing through (reach-forward-loss accounting front-loads the full remaining loss), and post-charge quarters (Q3'25 EPS $6.95, Q4'25 $5.80, Q2'26 $7.94; OCF/FCF rebounding to $2.8–3.7B/quarter) show real recovery, with guidance raised twice in 2026. (3) Capital-return discipline intact through the charge-heavy period: 23 consecutive years of dividend growth, $3.0B FY25 buybacks against a $10.3B authorization, FY26 FCF guide raised to $7.0–7.2B. [Corrected 2026-10-06: no shares were repurchased in H1 2026 (10-Q), so 'discipline intact' applies to FY25 only; a $3.45bn acquisition to be funded with cash and new financing is pending]

Bear: (1) The charge pattern spans two consecutive fiscal years and at least four programs/business units (Aeronautics classified ×2, MFC classified, RMS/Sikorsky ×2, plus newly disclosed F-16/C-130J issues) — a genuine, recurring pattern of cost-estimation and execution risk, and by definition classified-program specifics cannot be independently verified from public filings. (2) F-35 delivery cadence decelerated sharply in H1 2026 (-47% YoY) exactly as Aeronautics segment backlog has declined for two straight periods — the largest, historically most stable program may be plateauing in volume terms. (3) A single quarter (Q2 2025) saw ~$1.5B of segment-operating-profit guidance and ~$5.35/sh of EPS guidance cut at once — a scale of in-year revision that is a fair challenge to how much program-level visibility management has when it first frames annual guidance.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Any newly disclosed reach-forward/classified-program charge exceeding ~$300M pretax in a single quarter.
  2. Aeronautics segment backlog falling below the 2026-06-30 level of $54.4B at the next 10-Q (a third consecutive decline).
  3. Full-year 2026 F-35 deliveries pacing materially below the ~150–155 unit run-rate implied by FY2025's 191 (e.g., under ~100–110 units through Q3 2026).
  4. A guidance cut (not reaffirmation) to FY2026 sales, segment operating profit, or FCF at either of the next two earnings releases.
  5. A continuing resolution or government shutdown lasting beyond one quarter that management explicitly attributes a revenue/cash shortfall to.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Q3 2026 earnings expected on/about 2026-10-20 (unconfirmed estimate from historical mid-to-late-October pattern). Pending Ultra Maritime acquisition (announced, excluded from FY26 guidance) — closing/financing terms are a near-term catalyst; the 2026-08-28 8-K (items 1.01/9.01) likely relates to this and was not reviewed this pass. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the 8-K is a $2.25 billion 364-day revolver renewal (acc 0001193125-26-371750); the Ultra Maritime agreement dates from 6 Jul 2026] FY2027 budget/appropriations process (CR vs. full-year enactment) is a recurring Q1-timed macro risk. Further pension risk-transfer transactions have been flagged by management as recurring optionality.

11. Red-flag scan

Two consecutive fiscal years of large classified/international-program losses across ≥4 programs (§6) is the dominant, already-disclosed red flag — not a future risk but a present, repeated pattern. C-130J deliveries collapsed 21→2 units on disclosed supply-chain ("diminishing manufacturing sources") issues. No auditor change, restatement, going-concern language, or SEC/DOJ investigation was identified in sources reviewed, but a full FY2025 10-K critical-audit-matters, related-party, and Form 4 insider-pattern review was not completed this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as a coverage gap, not a clean bill. Agent: F103 | As of: 2026-09-25 close ($63.60, Nasdaq) | Wave: 6

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon: 24–48 months (regulated-utility compounding thesis). One-sentence reason: a well-run Midwest regulated electric/gas utility with a genuine, contracted data-center demand tailwind and above-peer ROE, held to half weight because the growth case is funded by a large, dilution-risk-bearing capex plan and the dividend-implied valuation already prices in most of the near-term growth.

2. Business in plain English

Alliant Energy owns two regulated utility subsidiaries — Interstate Power and Light (Iowa) and Wisconsin Power and Light — that generate and sell electricity and natural gas to homes and businesses under state-regulated rates. It earns a return set by regulators on the capital it invests in the grid and power plants; growth comes from rate-base expansion (new generation, transmission, grid upgrades) approved by the Iowa Utilities Commission and Public Service Commission of Wisconsin. The current growth driver is large hyperscale data-center customers (Microsoft, Meta, Google have facilities on its Iowa grid) signing long-term electric-service agreements.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 composite 0.399 (decile 4), driven by Value (book/price 0.452, the highest of the three names here — LNT trades cheaply to book, typical for a regulated utility) and a strong positive earnings-momentum (SUE +0.204, the best of the three). Quality: ROE 11.1% (d4/b1), which the triage card correctly notes is best-in-class among Midwest utility peers — this is durable in the sense that it is regulator-approved and rate-base-driven, not a cyclical or accounting artefact, though it is capped by rate-case outcomes rather than a market-share moat.

5. Guidance track record

  • New demand contracted: a new electric-service agreement for ~370 MW of contracted Iowa data-center demand was signed and disclosed at the Q2 2026 release, on top of a stated 2–4 GW pipeline of large-load opportunities (data centers, primarily Iowa/Wisconsin).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet — entity scope stated explicitly

  • Leverage: debt/equity ≈ 1.41x; this is a normal, regulator-sanctioned capital structure for a rate-based utility and should not be compared to an industrial company's leverage norms — flagged here explicitly per the wave-6 entity-scope requirement.   • Capex-funding / dilution risk: a $13.4B four-year capital plan at a company with ~$7.5B of equity implies substantial ongoing external financing — a mix of debt and, very likely, further common-equity issuance (ATM programs are typical for utilities in this position). [Corrected 2026-10-08: issuance is already under way: 929,759 shares sold under the ATM programme in H1 2026 (the $1.3bn 2025 programme was fully used in March 2026 and a new programme of up to $1bn filed), shares outstanding 257.1M to 259.3M (10-Q Note 5)] This is the main dilution risk to the EPS-growth thesis and was not flagged in the original triage card, which noted only the demand tailwind, not its funding cost.
  • No pending M&A identified.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

No V1 row exists for LNT yet — v1_verdict = null. - NTM P/E (d4): 17.3x; trailing P/E ~20.1x; dividend yield ≈ 3.4% (dividend rate $2.14 ÷ price $63.60). - Utilities are valued on earnings/dividends, not FCF (FCF is structurally negative during a capex ramp — d4 shows TTM FCF of −$1.14B, which is expected and not a red flag for a utility mid-buildout, not comparable to the FCF-based reverse DCF used for JNJ/MCK). - Reverse DCF via dividend-discount approach (own calc): using price $63.60, current indicated annual dividend $2.14 (dividend yield 3.37%) and a cost-of-equity estimate of ~7.5% (utility beta ~0.53 per d4/y_beta; CAPM with ~4.2% risk-free and ~5% ERP would give ~6.85%, so 7.5% is a conservative/round estimate), a Gordon-growth solve gives an implied perpetual dividend growth rate of ≈4.1% (7.5% − 3.37% yield). [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 4.2% risk-free rate is stale (10-year Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep 2026); Ke = 5.17% + Blume beta 0.69 x ERP 4.14% = 8.0% (8.6% with a 5% ERP) gives implied dividend growth of 4.5% (5.1%) vs the 5.5-6.5% base: "below" holds on the programme ERP with a smaller margin] Management's own guided EPS growth (7%+ for 2027–2029) is well above this implied 4.1%, even allowing for a payout ratio that grows slower than EPS during the capex ramp. Verdict: priced "below" my base case (I'd underwrite realistic base-case long-run EPS/dividend growth at 5.5–6.5%, below management's own 7%+ guide but above the ~4.1% the current price implies) — genuinely attractive if the data-center-driven capex plan executes on schedule and rate cases are constructive, which is the key uncertainty (see kill criteria). - Caveat: this is a simplified one-stage DDM, not a full multi-stage utility rate-base model; treat the 4.1% figure as directional, not precise.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: 1. Genuine, contracted (not speculative) hyperscale data-center demand in Iowa (370 MW signed this quarter alone, 2–4 GW pipeline) — a real, multi-year rate-base growth driver most peer utilities lack at this scale. 2. Best-in-class ROE (11.1%) among the Midwest utility peer set, reflecting constructive regulatory relationships in both Iowa and Wisconsin. 3. Guidance tracking the upper half of the 2026 range and a 7%+ EPS CAGR guide for 2027–2029, both reaffirmed as of the most recent quarter.

Bull case is priced generously already given the dividend-yield-implied growth of only ~4.1% versus a 7%+ guide — most of the upside case requires believing management and believing regulators approve the associated rate increases without pushback.

Bear: 1. The $13.4B four-year capital plan requires heavy external financing; slower-than-planned equity issuance timing, higher-than-expected interest costs, or a credit-rating pressure event would compress the EPS-growth delivery below the 7%+ guide. 2. Data-center demand pipelines are frequently oversold industry-wide (multiple utilities citing overlapping hyperscaler pipeline MW); if even a portion of the 2–4 GW pipeline fails to convert to signed agreements, the growth re-rating reverses. 3. Regulatory/rate-case risk: Iowa/Wisconsin commissions could slow-walk the large capex-driven rate increases needed to fund the plan without harming affordability optics, especially with data-center customers seen as beneficiaries.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Adjusted/ongoing EPS growth falls below 5% for a full fiscal year (vs. the 7%+ 2027–29 guide).
  2. A signed data-center service agreement (any of the ~370MW+ pipeline) is cancelled or materially downsized before energization.
  3. Debt/equity ratio rises above 1.8x (from ~1.41x today [Corrected 2026-10-08: 1.61x on total debt of $12,118M]) without a corresponding equity raise, signalling capex is outrunning the planned financing mix.
  4. A rate case in Iowa or Wisconsin is rejected or approved at less than 70% of the requested revenue increase.
  5. Guidance is cut (not just reaffirmed) at either of the next two quarterly releases (next: 2026-11-05).

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-11-05 (Q3 2026).
  • Any new large-load/data-center service-agreement announcements (management has signalled more are likely given the 2–4 GW pipeline).
  • Iowa/Wisconsin rate-case filings and decisions tied to the capex plan (no specific docket/decision date identified in this pass).

11. Red-flag scan

  • No triage-listed red flags for LNT (triage card listed none); this dossier's own review found no litigation, accounting, or regulatory red flags in the sources reviewed.
  • The main risk this dossier surfaces that the triage did not is financing/dilution risk from the capex plan, not a "red flag" in the misconduct sense but a material underwriting consideration.
  • No auditor changes, restatements or going-concern language identified.

dossiers.LOW:
LOW — Lowe's Companies, Inc. (Diligence dossier, agent F69, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (24–36 month horizon), with a specific reservation: comparable sales growth has decelerated for three straight quarters (+1.3% → +0.6% → +0.2%) and fiscal-2026 guidance has been trimmed to the low end of every metric twice in six months [Corrected 2026-10-08: once; the 20 May 2026 release affirmed the outlook unchanged and the only trim was on 19 Aug 2026], even as headline sales growth (+8–10% YoY the last two quarters) is now mostly acquisition-driven (Foundation Building Materials, Artisan Design Group), not organic. The #2 U.S. home-improvement retailer is priced for very little growth — a real margin of safety — but momentum is fading, not building, into a still-pressured DIY/housing macro.

2. Business in plain English

Lowe's operates ~1,760 big-box home-improvement stores in the U.S., selling building materials, appliances, tools and home décor to both do-it-yourself (DIY) consumers and professional contractors (Pro). It competes head-to-head with Home Depot. Its "Total Home" strategy is shifting the mix toward Pro, online and installed/home-services revenue (all growing) to offset a structurally weaker DIY segment tied to existing-home-sales activity and discretionary renovation spend, which has been depressed by high mortgage rates for several years.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Disqualifying gates: checked — not a pending-deal exclusion, exclude_pending_deal=False confirmed (both FBM and ADG M&A are completed, not pending); volatility gate removed program-wide per STATE.md amendment (i). b1 (2026-09-25): composite decile 2/10, live_rank 444/503 — a weak overall quant signal, driven mainly by value (pct_ep 0.67, pct_fcfp 0.65, pct_ebit_ev 0.67) and quality-cash-flow signals (pct_gp_a 0.65, pct_ocf_a 0.54), offset by very poor book/price (pct_bp 0.09 — a direct artefact of the deeply negative book value from decades of buybacks, discussed in §6, not a quality problem) and weak asset growth/leverage percentiles (also mechanically driven by the negative-equity capital structure). 7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

  • No V1 row exists for LOW (v1_valuation_table.csv has no LOW entry). v1_verdict = null.
  • Price $189.28 (2026-09-25 close, per b1/d4 snapshot); market cap ≈ $106.2bn (b1); shares ≈ 561M.

  • My own reverse DCF (10-year two-stage FCF model; cost of equity 8.0% [large, stable retailer, moderate beta]; terminal growth 2.5%; solved against EV ≈ $140.6bn [market cap + net debt ≈ $34.4bn]; FCF0 = FY2025's $7.65bn): implied 10-year FCF growth ≈ 2.3%/yr — a very undemanding bar, close to pure terminal-value pricing. [Corrected 2026-10-08: 8.0% is too low against the 5.17% Treasury (Blume beta 0.90 x ERP 4.14% = Ke ~8.9%) and EV was paired with levered FCF; on consistent bases the implied growth is about 0.6% (equity value vs levered FCF at 8.9%) or -0.4% to +0.7% (EV vs unlevered FCF ~$8.65bn at WACC 7.5-8.0%), below even the bear case; "below" is strengthened]
  • My bear/base/bull (10-yr FCF growth), evidence-based:
  • Bear (DIY/housing stays depressed for years, comp deceleration continues into negative territory, FBM integration disappoints): ≈ 0–1%/yr.
  • Base (Pro/online/installation mix shift continues at its current pace, modest comp growth resumes as rates ease, FBM contributes a full year with integration largely complete, buybacks gradually resume): ≈ 4–6%/yr.
  • Bull (housing turnover recovers meaningfully, Pro market-share gains accelerate, FBM and future bolt-ons compound Pro-channel scale): ≈ 8–10%/yr.
  • The implied ~2.3%/yr sits clearly below even the bear case. implied_vs_base = below (cheap).
  • valuation_view_vs_v1: no v1 row to reconcile against (null); dossier_view = cheap.

8. Bull case

  1. Pro/online/home-services growth is real and multi-quarter: online sales +15.5% (Q1 FY26) and +15.7% (Q2 FY26) YoY; this is the fifth consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales, even if the magnitude is now very small.
  2. Reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in almost no growth (~2.3%/yr) — even a modest, evidence-based base case (Pro mix shift + eventual housing-turnover recovery) clears that bar comfortably.
  3. Balance sheet, while nominally "negative equity," reflects decades of shareholder-friendly capital return from a durable, profitable business (FCF ≈ $7.65bn in the year just ended) rather than operating losses — management has now demonstrated the discipline to pause buybacks (from $4.05bn to $0.21bn) to delever after a large acquisition, rather than over-leveraging further.

9. Bear case

  1. Comparable sales growth has decelerated in three straight quarters (+1.3% → +0.6% → +0.2%), and FY2026 guidance has been trimmed to the low end of every metric twice in six months [Corrected 2026-10-08: once, on 19 Aug 2026] — the "positive comp streak" the company emphasizes is arithmetically true but directionally weakening.
  2. Reported headline sales growth (+8–10% YoY, last two quarters) is now substantially acquisition-driven (FBM/ADG), masking much weaker underlying organic performance — investors reading only the headline sales-growth number would overestimate organic momentum.
  3. Net debt (~$34.4bn) rose materially to fund the FBM deal at a rich 13.4x EBITDA multiple; if DIY/housing stays weak for longer, deleveraging (and the buyback resumption bulls are counting on) could be delayed well beyond current expectations.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable — what would break this thesis / invalidation triggers)

  1. Comparable sales turn negative (below 0.0%) for two consecutive quarters (trend has already gone +1.3%→+0.6%→+0.2%).

LRCX — Lam Research Corporation (diligence agent F29, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–36 month thesis horizon). Lam is a genuinely excellent, share-gaining wafer-fab-equipment (WFE) franchise riding a real AI/leading-edge/HBM-packaging capex wave with record margins — but at $315.21 (25-Sep-2026 close) the stock is priced, on V4's own systematic reverse DCF, for sustained growth roughly 2.5–4x its own trailing history, and the triage's "override to advance" rationale (net-cash balance sheet, ~8% required growth) does not match V1's own math. I side with V1's "excessive" verdict, not the triage override.

2. Business in plain English

Lam Research makes wafer-fab-equipment — principally etch and deposition tools — used by memory and logic chipmakers to build semiconductors. It is one of a handful of companies (with Applied Materials, KLA, Tokyo Electron, ASML) that customers have no real alternative to for advanced nodes and, increasingly, HBM/advanced-packaging manufacturing steps. Roughly a quarter of revenue still comes from China, a share that has been shrinking under US export controls.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 quant (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, 2026-09-25): composite 0.906 (decile 10, but live_rank 47 — outside the top-30 momentum/earnings tier that MU sits in), driven again mostly by momentum (fam_M 0.983, mom_12_1 +126%) and earnings-surprise (fam_S 0.942, SUE 3.55); fam_V is very low (0.021 — the model sees LRCX as expensive on every value metric, which is the correct read given a NTM P/E of 31.4x). This is a real, filing-verified upcycle (record revenue, record non-GAAP operating margin 38.4% in FQ4'26), but the WFE sub-sector is the most cyclically amplified link in the chain (sector playbook: "a 15% cut in foundry capex can mean a 30%+ decline in tool orders, and the reverse on the way up") — the current growth rate is a cycle peak, not a new trend line, even though the underlying AI-capex driver is real for several more years.

This is a genuine gap in this dossier's coverage — flagged, not glossed over.

7. Valuation — reconciling with V1

V1 (outputs/v1_valuation.json, priced 2026-09-25): verdict "excessive" (score −0.881), reverse-DCF FCFF, WACC 11.8%. NTM P/E 31.4x, at the 80th percentile of its own 177-month (14.75-year) history — i.e., this is one of the more expensive points in Lam's own trading history, not a discount. V1's implied 10-year FCFF growth is 48.5%/yr, against a historical 5-year CAGR of only 9.7% and 10-year CAGR of 14.7%, and even the sell-side's own next-fiscal-year consensus growth is 18.1% — a fraction of the 48.5%/yr implied. V1's base case (20.3% assumed growth, 20.4x exit multiple) still produces a 3-year annualised return of −20.2%, its bull case (28.1% growth) only reaches +2.4%/yr, and its street-flag again notes the base case sits below the Street's own 12-month low target ($290 vs $315.21 spot). My reconciliation: the triage's "override to advance" argument (net-cash balance sheet and "net-cash-implied required growth of ~8%") looks like it referenced a different, easier hurdle than V1's actual reverse-DCF framework — the ~8% figure resembles a bond-like "growth needed to cover the multiple via earnings yield alone" heuristic, not the 10-year FCFF-growth-at-WACC reverse DCF V1 (and this dossier) actually solve for. On the harder, filing-grounded test, implied growth (48.5%/yr) is well ABOVE any defensible base case (my own base case: high-teens to low-20s%/yr, i.e., roughly consensus-to-slightly-above, allowing 2–3 more years of AI/HBM-driven WFE strength before the capex cycle normalises). valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "above".

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Genuinely record, company-verified non-GAAP operating margin (38.4% FQ4'26) and gross margin (52.0%) from pricing actions, mix and efficiency, not just volume. (2) HBM/advanced-packaging and leading-edge etch/deposition steps are structurally gaining share of the WFE dollar as chipmakers add process steps — a real, multi-year tailwind, not merely a spending-cycle peak. (3) China revenue mix has fallen from 43% to 26% of sales in three quarters, and the company says Taiwan (27%) and Korea (20%) demand "more than offsets" the loss — i.e., the China de-risking that many feared is already mostly priced through the P&L rather than a future shock. Bear: (1) WFE is the most amplified link in the semiconductor value chain; the forward guide implies the largest single-quarter sequential jump (+20.5%) in the two-year data reviewed — a hard bar to clear twice in a row. (2) A Shanghai-based, state-backed Chinese toolmaker has begun shipping homegrown immersion DUV lithography systems (5 units in 2026, 20 planned for 2027) to SMIC/CXMT/Hua Hong, and the pending US MATCH Act would tighten export controls further — a two-sided China risk (less addressable China revenue, and slowly emerging Chinese-equipment competition at the margin) that is not fully reflected in a 31.4x, 80th-percentile multiple. (3) V1's own reverse DCF, using Lam's own trailing cash flows and a conservative 11.8% WACC, requires the company to more than triple its own 10-year historical growth rate for the next decade to earn the current price.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Reported (GAAP or non-GAAP) revenue growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters (roughly half the current run-rate).
  2. China revenue share stabilises or reverses its decline (i.e., a further adverse export-control tightening) and Taiwan/Korea demand fails to keep offsetting it, evidenced by a guidance cut.
  3. Non-GAAP gross margin falls back below 48% (below the FY26 average) for a full quarter.
  4. Book-to-bill (or qualitative order commentary) turns negative for two consecutive quarters — the sector's cleanest leading indicator of a WFE downturn.
  5. The MATCH Act or a further export-control tightening is enacted with a disclosed revenue impact beyond the ~$600M/year headwind already guided.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: ~2026-10-21 (est.), LRCX's fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ending ~2026-09-27, essentially concurrent with this dossier's cutoff) — date sourced from third-party earnings calendars, not yet confirmed via an LRCX press release at the time of this pull.   • Litigation/SEC: no material litigation, SEC/DOJ investigation, restatement or going-concern language found in the sources reviewed for this pass.
  • Insider selling: several Form 4 sales in 2026 (Chief Legal Officer Ava Harter, $1.51M, 2026-08-31, under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-04-28; directors/SVPs selling $6.1–20.0M across mid-2026) — these read as routine, plan-based diversification against a large stock-price run rather than a cluster of opportunistic, un-planned sales, but the magnitude (director sale of $20.0M) is worth monitoring next quarter.

1. Verdict

WATCH. Statistically cheap (8.3x TTM GAAP EPS; 11.6x the underlying FY26 guide; net cash $1.39bn), and the price implies free cash flow shrinking about 5% a year for ten years, below my base case (+3%). But earnings are still falling faster in the second half than in the first (Q3 guide: EPS $0.93-0.98 vs $2.59 a year ago), full-year guidance has been cut twice, Americas comparable sales are -12%, and a new CEO started only on 8 Sep 2026. lululemon designs and sells premium technical athletic apparel (yoga, running, training) through 825 company-operated stores, e-commerce and some licensed partners, in North America (Americas), China and the rest of the world. It earns a high gross margin (about 55-60%) because customers pay full price for the brand, and it has grown by opening stores and entering new markets. The problem now is the United States: demand for its core products has weakened, discounting and tariffs have squeezed margins, and international growth, which used to offset it, has slowed.

dossiers.LUV:
LUV - Southwest Airlines Co. (NYSE: LUV) - standard-depth diligence (agent F134)

1. Verdict: WATCH. Horizon 12-24 months. Triage said not to advance because of negative free cash flow and an unproven revenue overhaul. Primary sources partly overturn the "unproven" point (Q2 2026 adjusted revenue +20.3%, adjusted operating margin 6.7% vs 3.4%) but confirm the risk: full-year guidance was cut at the midpoint ($3.25-4.25 from "at least $4.00") and is back-half loaded, earnings swing on fuel, and trailing free cash flow is negative. Condition that would move it to INCLUDE-SMALL: Q3 adjusted EPS at or above $0.75 and the full-year range narrowed to a low end of at least $3.75, or net capex held at or below $3.0B with positive free cash flow for two quarters.

2. Business in plain English. Largest US low-fare domestic airline (803 aircraft, 30 Jun 2026). Until 2025 it had open seating, free bags and no fare tiers. In 2025-26 it added bag fees, basic economy, assigned and extra-legroom seating (launched 27 Jan 2026), loyalty changes and a richer Chase co-brand card deal. About 60% of customers bought up from the base fare in Q1 2026 (vs about 20% in 2025, Q1 release). Moat is network density and brand; weakness is a single aircraft type, Boeing delivery dependence, and a fuel-exposed cost base.

3. Why the model likes it. Cheap on forward earnings (about 11x the midpoint of the "$3.25 to $4.25" range) with strong 12-month price momentum and improving margins; earnings revisions are the driver. Durable or artefact? The improvement is real but the 2026 comparison is flattered by a weak 2025 base (Q1 2025 GAAP loss) and by very high unit revenue growth (+16% in Q2) that will lap in 2027; the quality scores are distorted by the equity decline after $2.25B (H1 2025) and $1.25B (H1 2026) of buybacks.

(b) Cost discipline: CASM-X +3.4% vs guide above; fleet renewal (64 deliveries, about 60 retirements in 2026). (c) Every $0.50 a gallon fuel move is worth about $1.7 of EPS (my estimate from about 2.2B gallons), so fuel relief is large upside. (b) Back-half loaded guide and seasonal Q4; revenue growth laps the 2025 bag-fee start in H2 (Q3 RASM guide is lower than Q2's +20%).
