dossiers.NEE:
NEE — NextEra Energy, Inc.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — thesis horizon 24–36 months, half weight for a named reservation. NEE is the largest US electric utility (Florida Power & Light) plus the largest wind/solar/storage developer in the US (NextEra Energy Resources), guiding 8%+ adjusted-EPS growth through 2032 with a track record of raising and then twice reaffirming FY2026 guidance from primary-source releases. A reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in far less growth than guided (~1% vs an 8% guide) — genuinely attractive if the growth is delivered. The reservation: consolidated debt is growing fast (+10.3% in six months) to fund a $90–100bn FPL capital program plus NEER's ~33GW backlog, and NEE carries real, disclosed (if insurance-covered) litigation tied to the 2023 political-activity class action and the XPLR Energy (former NextEra Energy Partners) spin-off — a bond-proxy stock with genuine financing and regulatory execution risk, not a pure "priced for nothing" bargain.

2. Business in plain English

NEE is a holding company with two main segments: FPL, a rate-regulated electric utility serving ~12 million people in Florida (fully regulated returns set by the Florida Public Service Commission, "FPSC"), and NextEra Energy Resources ("NEER"), which develops, owns and operates wind, solar and battery-storage projects (mostly under long-term contracted PPAs) plus competitive gas/transmission assets across most of the US. FPL earns a regulated return on its capital base by investing in grid, generation and reliability infrastructure; NEER earns contracted, largely fixed-price cash flows by building and selling clean-energy output to utilities and, increasingly, hyperscale data-center/large-load customers. The moat is scale plus execution track record: NEE can originate, permit, finance and build renewable/storage projects faster and cheaper than most peers, and FPL is one of the lowest-cost electric utilities in the country.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Standouts: pct_gp_a 85th percentile, pct_mom_12_1 89th percentile, pct_sue 95th percentile (strong recent earnings-surprise trend) — quality and momentum both real. Weak spots: pct_ebit_ev only 2nd percentile and pct_bp 11th percentile — NEE screens expensive on classic value ratios, which is normal for a regulated-utility-plus-growth story where the market pays up for visible, government-sanctioned earnings growth rather than for statistical cheapness. The triage's own red flag (Florida hurricane/wildfire physical risk, "monitored risk factor not a California-style liability regime") is confirmed accurate — this dossier separately found the more material, un-triaged risk items in §11 (litigation) that the model's factor scores cannot see. Durability judgement: the quality/momentum signal reflects a real, guided growth algorithm (FPL rate base + NEER backlog conversion), not an artefact — but it is a regulated/contracted growth story, so execution and financing risk (§6, §9) matter more than for an asset-light compounder.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) FPL's new four-year FPSC rate settlement (effective 1 Jan 2026) locks in constructive, low-conflict regulatory economics through 2029; (2) NEER's ~33GW backlog plus new hyperscaler/data-center demand (e.g., the US-Japan-linked 9.5GW gas-generation award, Google PPA enabling the Duane Arnold nuclear restart) gives multi-year revenue visibility; (3) the stock's implied growth (~1%) is far below its own guided growth (8%+), a wide margin of safety if delivered. Bear: (1) Consolidated debt growing faster (+10.3% in 6 months) than revenue funds a capex program that may require dilutive equity issuance in a higher-for-longer rate environment; (2) NEE is a "bond proxy" whose multiple compresses further if long rates rise; (3) the XPLR/NEP-linked securities litigation (§11) signals real governance friction from the prior yieldco financing structure, a tail risk to reputation and management bandwidth even though currently insurance-covered.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Full-year adjusted EPS comes in below the low end of the then-current guidance range (currently $3.92) at any year-end report.
  2. Consolidated debt/(debt+equity) rises above ~68% (from ~63.4% today) without a credible deleveraging plan, or NEE/NEECH/FPL suffers a credit-rating downgrade.
  3. FPL's next base rate proceeding (post the 2025 four-year settlement expires ~2029) is resolved with an allowed ROE or capital-recovery mechanism materially worse than the current settlement.
  4. The 2023 securities class action settlement ($150m, insurance-covered) or the XPLR securities/derivative litigation is not given final court approval and reopens as active, uninsured exposure.
  5. NEER backlog-to-in-service conversion stalls (two consecutive quarters of GW placed into service below the trailing-four-quarter average), signalling supply-chain, interconnection or financing bottlenecks.

dossiers.NEM:
NEM — Newmont Corporation — Diligence Dossier (Agent F89, STANDARD depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon: 12–24 months. Reason: record free cash flow and a net-cash balance sheet at today's gold price, and the market is pricing in outright shrinkage, not growth — but the entire thesis is a single-commodity bet on gold staying near record highs, so it is sized down, not full weight.

2. Business in plain English

Newmont is the world's largest gold miner (with meaningful copper/silver by-product), operating a global portfolio of mines across the Americas, Australia and Africa. It makes money by selling gold at the prevailing spot/realized price against a relatively fixed-in-the-short-run cash cost per ounce (AISC); as gold has risen, nearly all of the price increase has fallen straight to cash flow because costs have not kept pace.

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable?

Triage cited record FCF ($3.1B Q1, $2.2B Q2 2026) against AISC guided ~$1,680/oz vs realized prices near $4,900/oz. Confirmed, with a correction: Q2 2026 realized gold price was $4,414/oz (not $4,900 — that figure is closer to spot in September, not the Q2 average) [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: $4,900/oz was the Q1 2026 average realized price (Q2 $4,414), per the Q2 release Ex-99.1 acc 0001164727-26-000034; the triage was right], and Q2 AISC was $1,621/oz (below the $1,680 full-year guide). Revenue growth is being driven almost entirely by price, not volume: Q2 2026 realized price +33% YoY while cost-applicable-to-sales rose only ~4% — genuine operating leverage, but not a repeatable growth driver if gold prices plateau or fall. This is a price-cycle tailwind, not a durable structural moat — flagged as not durable in the sense the model's quality/value scores would suggest; it is a cyclical windfall.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: Q2 2026 FCF $2.2B vs GAAP NI $2.2B ≈ 1.0x — clean, no accrual red flags apparent in the quarters reviewed.
  • Balance sheet (consolidated): net cash ≈ $3.9B (Jun-26); stockholders' equity $35.2B and rising every quarter. This is a genuinely strong, low-leverage balance sheet — net debt/EBITDA is negative.

Netflix is the largest global subscription streaming video service (~300mn+ paid memberships across ad-supported and ad-free tiers), monetizing through subscription fees and a fast-growing advertising tier, and increasingly through live sports and events (NFL games, boxing, MLB). NiSource Inc. (NI) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F111, Wave 7)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (24–48 month horizon; regulated-utility, longer-dated thesis). Reason: a regulated gas/electric utility running a credible, guided ~9–11% rate-base growth plan funded partly by minority-stake sales to Blackstone, with reverse-DCF-implied growth well below both guidance and my base case — but GAAP earnings quality is currently distorted by large one-off gains, and a live state regulatory investigation into gas-meter accuracy is an open, unresolved item, so I withhold full weight until the investigation resolves and one clean organic-EPS quarter is reported.

2. Business in plain English

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 24–36 months. Real, primary-source-confirmed earnings growth from the LS Power acquisition and hyperscaler data-center deals, and a clean guidance record — but leverage is genuinely high post-acquisition, quarterly GAAP earnings are extremely volatile (mark-to-market swings of $600m+ quarter to quarter), and the market-implied valuation on the more reliable EV/EBITDA basis is not obviously cheap once leverage is accounted for, contrary to the triage's "sold off to 9.5x, cheap" framing.

2. Business in plain English

NRG is a merchant power generator and retail electricity/energy-services provider, with fleets concentrated in Texas (ERCOT) and, since closing the LS Power acquisition on 2026-01-30, a much larger footprint of natural-gas and dual-fuel generation across the eastern U.S. It earns money from wholesale energy sales, capacity payments, and retail electricity/gas supply contracts with residential and business customers; unlike a regulated utility, its prices are set by competitive/auction markets (ERCOT energy prices, PJM/other capacity auctions), not a rate case.

NSC - Norfolk Southern Corporation (F159, wave 8, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH. Thesis horizon 12-36 months. A good railroad whose price is now mostly a bet on the pending Union Pacific (UNP) takeover clearing the Surface Transportation Board (STB). Standalone, the stock already prices more growth than my base case. Triage said "merger-arb, not advanced"; I confirm the situation but the verdict is WATCH, not REJECT, because the deal terms leave real upside if approval comes (see section 7).

2. Business in plain English

Norfolk Southern runs a 22-state eastern US freight railroad (coal, intermodal containers, autos, chemicals, agriculture) and earns money by hauling carloads at a price per unit, plus fuel surcharges. Its moat is the physical network, which cannot be replicated, and it competes mainly with CSX. On 28 July 2025 it agreed to be acquired by UNP.

3. Why the model likes it, and is that durable

b1 screen: quality (ROE 16%), moderate momentum, mid percentiles on most families; no single standout. The ROE is real but flattered by high leverage (leverage factor 0.37) and by 2024's one-off line-sale gains. Durable as a franchise; not a deep-value or growth signal.

dossiers.NTAP:
NTAP — NetApp, Inc.

1. Verdict

WATCH — genuine business acceleration, but at $201.15 (25 Sep 2026 close) the stock already prices in a decade of growth well above anything NetApp has delivered historically. Horizon: 12–24 months (re-underwrite once FY2027 durability is confirmed or denied by 2–3 more quarters).

2. Business in plain English

NetApp sells data-storage hardware and software (mostly all-flash arrays under the ONTAP/ASA brands) plus a smaller public-cloud storage-as-a-service business, to enterprises and hyperscalers. It makes money selling systems and support/software attach, increasingly subscription-like via Keystone/cloud. Competitive position: a top-3 branded enterprise storage vendor (with Dell, HPE, Pure Storage, Hitachi) in a market that is technically mature/commoditizing but is currently being re-rated by AI-training/inference data-pipeline demand.

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable?

Quant factors like the earnings-momentum (SUE) and improving quality trend. This is a real, not artefactual, signal this quarter: record all-flash array revenue ($1.3B, +47% YoY) and record Public Cloud revenue ($206M, +28% YoY) in Q1 FY2027, plus the DataPelago acquisition for AI data-pipeline infrastructure. The open question is durability — NetApp's own 5-year and 10-year revenue CAGR are 5.2% and 2.9% (V1/D3), so a 30% YoY quarter is a large outlier versus the company's history, not a new steady state confirmed by multiple years of data. [Corrected 2026-10-08: Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter (FY27 is a 53-week year) against 13 weeks in Q1 FY26, so +29.9% YoY is not like-for-like; about +20.6% on a 13-week-equivalent basis (10-Q 0001193125-26-380207, Note 1)]

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: Q1 FY27 OCF $503M − capex $102M = FCF $401M vs GAAP NI $375M → 107% conversion. FY2026 (company-reported) FCF was $1,869M on NI of ~$1.28B-scale — strong, consistent conversion; the Q4 FY26 quarterly FCF I derive from XBRL ($900M) matches NetApp's own disclosed "$900 million" free cash flow figure for that quarter, a good cross-check.
  • SBC: ~5.4% of TTM revenue (V1: SBC $397M / TTM revenue $7,391M).
  • Balance sheet (30 Sep quarter, i.e. 31 Jul 2026): cash $1,573M + short-term investments $2,003M = $3,576M liquid, vs long-term debt $1,938M + current debt $550M = $2,488M — net cash position of ~$1,088M (matches V1's net_debt of −$1,088M). This is a fortress balance sheet; stockholders' equity is thin ($1.35–1.50B) purely because of a decade of buybacks reducing paid-in capital, not distress.
  • Capital return: Q1 FY27 — $200M buyback + $102M dividends; next dividend $0.52/share, 28 Oct 2026.
  • Share count: trending down via buybacks (consistent with V1's assumed −3.7% to −7.3% share-count CAGR in its scenarios).

7. Valuation snapshot — reconciled with V1

V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv / .json, as of 25 Sep 2026 close): NTM P/E 19.23x, in line with peer median 19.59x (Dell, Pure Storage, HPE, HPQ, Apple) and at the 39th percentile of NTAP's own 173-month history — i.e., NOT rich on a simple multiple basis. But V1's reverse DCF (FCFF, WACC 9.40%, 10-year fade to 3% terminal growth, TTM revenue base already includes the Q1 FY27 blowout quarter) says the price implies 15.28% revenue growth compounded for 10 years, versus NetApp's own delivered 5-year CAGR of 5.17%, 10-year CAGR of 2.91%, and Street consensus FY1 growth of only 5.80%. V1's base case (revenue growth fading from ~2.5% initial, margin ~11.5%) gives a 3-year annualised return of −17.2%; bear −38.3%; bull +12.5%. V1 verdict: "excessive." I agree with V1's verdict, with one qualification: the reason the stock trades at only a peer-median multiple despite this quarter's 30% growth print is precisely because the market (correctly, in my view) is not underwriting 30% growth for a decade — but it is still pricing in high-single/low-double-digit durable growth, more than the 5–6% NetApp has shown it can sustainably deliver in a competitive, commoditizing storage market. The bull case (AI-storage becomes a multi-year structural upgrade cycle, not one to two quarters of pent-up refresh demand) is plausible but unproven — one quarter is not a trend.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) All-flash + AI data-pipeline demand (DataPelago, StorageGRID 12.1) is a genuine multi-year hyperscaler/enterprise refresh cycle, not a one-off; (2) Public Cloud (+28% YoY) scales into a real recurring-revenue engine; (3) fortress net-cash balance sheet funds continued buybacks regardless of the cycle. Bear: (1) Storage is structurally competitive (Dell, HPE, Pure Storage, hyperscaler-native storage) — pricing power is not durable; (2) NetApp's own 10-year CAGR of 2.9% is the more representative base rate than one blowout quarter; (3) even after a huge raise, FY2027 guided growth (~15–19% at the new range vs FY26's $6.925B) still falls well short of the 10-year 15.3% the current price requires every year for a decade.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. All-flash array revenue growth decelerates below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Consolidated revenue growth falls back below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  3. GAAP gross margin falls below 68% for two consecutive quarters (pricing pressure).
  4. Any FY2027 guidance cut from the raised (2 Sep 2026) range.
  5. Public Cloud segment revenue growth falls below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q2 FY2027, target 1 December 2026 (company-stated cadence). Q3 FY27 target 4 March 2027; Q4 FY27 target 3 June 2027. Next dividend 28 Oct 2026 ($0.52/sh).

11. Red-flag scan

No litigation, SEC/DOJ investigation, restatement, or going-concern language found in the reviewed filings/press releases. Insider selling (Form 4, Aug–Sep 2026): small, routine Rule 10b5-1 planned sales by a director and two executives (hundreds to low thousands of shares each) — not a red flag. This is a comparatively clean name; the risk here is valuation/duration mismatch, not fraud or operational distress.

Northern Trust Corporation (NTRS) - Fundamental Diligence Dossier (F133, standard depth)

Verdict: WATCH, 12-36 month horizon. A high-quality custody and wealth franchise with well-covered capital and real operating leverage, but at $175.73 (25 Sep 2026 close; 2.57x book) the price already assumes a return on equity near 18%, against about 16.5% on earnings stripped of one-offs; my base case returns about 8% a year, roughly the cost of equity. What would change it: a price near or below about $150 (about 2.2x book, 12.8x clean 2026 EPS), or ex-notable return on equity holding above 17% for two more quarters with expense growth under 3%.

1. Business in plain English

Northern Trust safeguards and administers assets for pension funds, asset managers and wealthy families (Asset Servicing and Wealth Management segments) and earns mostly fees, about two-thirds of revenue, that move with market values and client activity; it also lends to wealthy clients and earns interest on the client deposits it holds. dossiers.NUE:
NUE (Nucor Corporation) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F45 · Standard depth · Prepared 2026-09-26 · Price/market data as of 2026-09-25 close ($247.25; mkt cap ≈$56.5B)

1. Verdict

WATCH — 12–24 month horizon. Nucor is the best-run, best-capitalized company in North American steel (A-/A-/A3 credit ratings, 213 consecutive quarterly dividends, disciplined buybacks), and current results are genuinely excellent — but current EPS is running at a tariff/reshoring-cycle peak, and the price already assumes that peak persists. Would upgrade on either (a) a pullback in price/multiple, or (b) 2+ more quarters confirming steel-mill average selling prices and shipment volumes hold near current levels without a tariff-policy reversal, which would support treating the current run-rate as a new, durable plateau rather than a cyclical high. Agrees directionally with V1's "excessive" verdict, with one important correction to V1's own math (Section 7).

2. Business in plain English

Nucor is the largest US steel producer (electric-arc-furnace/mini-mill model, more flexible and lower-fixed-cost than integrated blast-furnace steelmaking) and North America's largest scrap-metal recycler. It makes and sells steel bars, beams, sheet, plate, tubing, joists, deck, fasteners and other fabricated steel products, plus raw materials (scrap, DRI/HBI, ferro-alloys) both internally and to third parties. Revenue is a function of (volume shipped) × (price per ton), both currently elevated by Section 232 tariffs on imported steel, US reshoring/infrastructure and data-center construction demand.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

data/b1_live_scores.csv: live_rank 23 (top decile), composite driven by Quality (pct_roe 0.77, pct_ocf_a 0.81) and Value (pct_ep 0.79, pct_bp 0.94). Triage (Q13) flagged this as likely an artefact: "V1's 'excessive' tag likely reflects trailing momentum rather than the forward tariff-supported pricing backdrop" — i.e. the screen may be rewarding a cyclical peak in trailing quality/value metrics. This diligence largely confirms that concern: NUE's earnings are durable in the sense that management/balance-sheet discipline is real and structural, but the level of current earnings is cycle-dependent, not durable at this magnitude (Section 7).

4. Last two years of results (calendar quarters; GAAP; $M except EPS)

The swing from a $0.67 EPS trough (Q1 2025) to $5.04 (Q2 2026), a >7x increase in five quarters, is the single most important fact in this dossier: it is a textbook commodity-cycle earnings profile, not a compounding growth trajectory. Company-communicated Q3 2026 guidance (per earnings-call remarks, not the press release itself — see Section 5) is $5.55–5.65 EPS, which would be a further sequential record.

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases)

Nucor's press releases give only qualitative, segment-level directional guidance (e.g. "we expect earnings to increase/decrease vs. the prior quarter, and why by segment") — no point EPS/revenue range in the exhibit itself. This is a real distinction from companies that publish numeric guidance, and it matters for how much weight to put on "guidance beat" claims sourced from secondary aggregators (the $5.55–5.65 Q3 2026 EPS figure circulating in the financial press appears to originate from analyst notes/earnings-call commentary, not the 8-K exhibit — flagged, not verified against a primary transcript within this time box).

Every directional call over the last 4 quarters has been directionally correct — a genuine positive on management credibility, but note this is direction-only, not a magnitude commitment.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Balance sheet: cash $2.478B, total debt (incl. capital leases) $6.389B, net debt ≈$3.91B, stockholders' equity $22.11B (2026-07-04 10-Q). [Corrected 2026-10-08: $6.389B is only the long-term portion; total debt is $7,099M (129 short-term + 581 current portion + 6,389) and net debt is $4,407M after $2,692M cash and short-term investments, so net debt is about 0.8x TTM EBITDA, not 0.71x (8-K Ex-99.1 0001193125-26-318190)] Net debt/TTM EBITDA is low (well under 1x on a ≈$5.5B TTM EBITDA estimate: EBIT $4.25B + D&A ≈$1.26B) — a genuinely conservative, cycle-tested balance sheet (A-/A-/A3 ratings, upgraded by Moody's to A3 from Baa1 in Sep-2025).
  • FCF conversion is currently weak, and that matters: TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) OCF $4.424B, capex $2.841B → FCF $1.583B, FCF/NI ≈55%, and FCF yield on EV is only ≈2.6% despite the earnings surge — because Nucor is mid-way through a large, multi-year capacity-expansion capex program (~$1.1–1.3B/quarter). This is the low-FCF-yield red flag triage (Q13) already noted (1.2% headline FCF yield figure).
  • Data-quality finding / correction to V1: V1's own reverse-DCF sub-model for NUE was explicitly suppressed ("da_ratio unavailable... reverse DCF suppressed... FCFF would be structurally understated and implied growth meaningless" — v1_valuation.json, NUE flags). The primary-source fix is straightforward: the 10-Q cash-flow statement reports "Depreciation" = $1,261M TTM (Q3'25 $304M + Q4'25 $316M + Q1'26 $321M + Q2'26 $320M), i.e. ≈3.5% of TTM revenue, not zero. This is a genuine data gap in V1's pipeline (flagged as a data_conflict in the summary JSON), not an error in V1's judgment to suppress a broken number.
  • Capital return: $475M buybacks + $258M dividends in H1 2026; new $4.0B buyback authorization approved Feb-2026 (replacing the prior program); quarterly dividend $0.56/share, the 213th consecutive quarterly dividend (Dividend King status via decades of increases, not verified back to origin within this time box).

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF — reconciliation with V1

V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json): verdict "excessive" (score −0.40), NTM P/E 12.6x (35th percentile of NUE's own 177-month history — i.e. cheap-looking on the multiple alone), but base-case 3-year annualized return −10.5%/yr (bear −50.3%, bull +65.3%), because V1's EPS-scenario model assumes the current ~11.8% TTM EBIT margin mean-reverts toward a base-case ~5.6% margin (closer to Nucor's own mid-cycle average) — even with an exit P/E multiple (17.7x) above today's 12.6x, the resulting EPS is low enough that the 3-year value ($177) sits below today's price ($247).

Using the corrected D&A input (Section 6) in a simplified single-stage FCFF reverse DCF (EV≈$60.9B, WACC 9.05% from V1's own CAPM inputs, NOPAT $3.37B off TTM EBIT, +D&A $1.26B, −capex $2.84B, −ΔNWC $0.13B → FCFF $1.66B): implied perpetual FCFF growth ≈ +6.2%/yr — actually below Nucor's own trailing 10-year revenue CAGR (8.2%, per V1). Taken at face value, that looks far less alarming than V1's "excessive" tag.

Reconciliation (why I still agree with V1's direction): the FCFF reverse DCF above takes TTM EBIT margin (~11.8%) as the sustainable base — but that margin is itself a tariff/pricing-cycle high for a commodity steelmaker whose margins have historically ranged far lower (and far higher) across cycles. A "6%/yr growth off an already-cyclically-elevated earnings base forever" is a materially more demanding assumption than the headline number suggests once you require margin durability, not just growth. V1's EPS-scenario approach, which explicitly models margin mean-reversion, is the more appropriate lens for a cyclical commodity producer, and its conclusion (current price is priced for more than a prudent normalized-margin base case delivers) is the one I adopt. valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = true (same directional conclusion), with the reconciliation being about why, not whether, NUE looks expensive; implied growth is above my base case.

3-year scenario returns (annualised, price+dividends): bear −50.3% · base −10.5% · bull +65.3% — taken directly from V1's own EPS-scenario/exit-multiple model (not re-derived; this dossier's disagreement with V1 is confined to the FCFF sub-model above, and independently agrees with V1's margin-mean-reversion framework).

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Section 232 tariffs plus US reshoring and data-center/grid construction are driving genuinely record shipment volumes (2 consecutive quarterly steel-mill shipment records), not just price. (2) Best-in-class balance sheet and capital discipline (A-rated, 213 consecutive dividends, disciplined buybacks) mean Nucor can self-fund its capacity expansion through a downturn without distress. (3) 2027 contract steel pricing is already reportedly being written at $1,100–1,175/ton vs ~$800/ton in 2026 (secondary source, Q13 triage; not yet independently verified against a primary Nucor disclosure). [Corrected 2026-10-08: Reported steel-mills average selling price was $1,145/ton in Q2 2026 ($1,110 in H1 2026, $989 in H1 2025) and consolidated $1,367/ton (10-Q 0001193125-26-345891), so the claim of about $800/ton in 2026 contradicts the filings and kill criterion 1 sits 30% below the current level]

Bear: (1) Tariff-dependent pricing is a policy moat, not a competitive one — a trade-policy reversal (a real, named risk in the current environment) removes the pricing support quickly, and steel-mill EPS has already shown it can swing >7x in five quarters. (2) FCF yield (~2.6% on EV) is low for a name trading as if it is "cheap on P/E," because a large share of cash generation is being reinvested into capacity expansion that only pays off if the current demand cycle is durable. (3) The current EPS run-rate is unprecedented in Nucor's own recent history — extrapolating it is exactly the kind of trailing-momentum trap the triage note warned about.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Steel-mill average selling price falls below $800/ton for 2 consecutive quarters (loses the current tariff-driven pricing premium referenced in 2027 contract discussions).
  2. Quarterly diluted EPS falls back below $2.00 for 2 consecutive quarters (below the 2025 trough-adjacent run-rate, evidence the cycle has turned).
  3. Section 232 steel tariffs are repealed or substantially weakened (single trigger event — directly threatens the pricing premium underpinning current earnings).
  4. Net debt/TTM EBITDA rises above 1.5x (currently comfortably under 1x) via debt-funded capex overrun or M&A.
  5. The 213-consecutive-quarter dividend streak is broken or a previously-declared increase is skipped (a de facto management signal of FCF stress from a historically very reliable capital-return payer).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next scheduled release: Q3 2026 earnings, estimated ~27-Oct-2026 (Q3 2025 was reported 27-Oct-2025; date not yet confirmed by the company — flagged as an estimate). Watch for: whether steel-mill shipment volumes and ASPs hold at Q2 2026 levels (durability test) and any commentary on 2027 contract pricing being locked in.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Tariff/trade-policy dependency: explicitly named as a risk by triage (Q13) and confirmed here as the central swing factor in the valuation debate (Section 7) — not a company-specific red flag but a macro/political dependency that is unusually large relative to normal company risk factors.

dossiers.NVDA:
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) — Fundamental Diligence Dossier

Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 12–36 month thesis horizon. [Corrected 2026-10-08: VERDICT CHANGED to WATCH after verification DV31 (restated reverse DCF at a beta-consistent cost of capital implies about 22% a year, near the bull case; see the Correction section at the end)] One-sentence reason: near-monopoly AI-accelerator franchise with genuine execution (four straight quarters of YoY acceleration, gross margin back to 75%), but at the 25-Sep-2026 close ($225.07, mkt cap $5.42T) the price bakes in more 10-year growth (15.4% on trailing free cash flow) than a fair, evidence-based base case (≈13%) — this is a "would hold, but not at full weight" name, not a screaming buy.

1. Business in plain English

NVIDIA designs GPUs and the software/networking stack around them; it does not manufacture (TSMC fabs the chips). Data Center — Blackwell/GB200-era systems, Vera Rubin systems entering production, InfiniBand/NVLink/Ethernet networking, CUDA software — is now ~93% of revenue ($89.0B of $96.2B in fiscal Q2 2027), sold to hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle), sovereign-AI buyers, and enterprises building AI infrastructure. Gaming, Pro Visualization and Automotive are the remainder. The moat is CUDA software lock-in plus a multi-generation systems lead (chip + networking + rack-scale + software), not just raw chip performance.

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1 factor data (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as_of 2026-09-25): composite percentile 0.79 driven mainly by Value (fam_V 0.84, EBIT/EV percentile 0.79) and Momentum (fam_M 0.42) — the model likes NVDA's cash-flow yield and 12-month momentum, not "growth" as a factor per se (SUE/earnings-momentum percentile is only 0.79 fam_S but n_S sample thin at n=4 families). live_rank 103 (outside the top-70 gate that excluded it from earlier waves). This is a real, filed-numbers-driven signal (record Data Center revenue, 4 consecutive quarters of YoY acceleration per management's own Q2 FY27 call), not an accounting artefact — but it is a cyclical capex signal: it depends on hyperscaler capex continuing at the current run-rate, which is itself a debated, not proven, multi-year commitment.

3. Last 8 quarters (fiscal quarters; $M except EPS; FQ4 FY25 (Oct24–Jan25) is not separately XBRL-tagged in quarterly form — 10-K reports only the full year — so it is omitted rather than estimated)

[3]

4. Guidance track record (last 4 quarters, vs prior guidance)

  • Q3 FY26 report (Nov-2025) → guided Q4 FY26 revenue; actual Q4 FY26 $68.1B, "record," +20% QoQ — beat.
  • Q4 FY26 report (Feb-2026) → guided Q1 FY27; actual Q1 FY27 $81.6B, +85% YoY, "third consecutive quarter of YoY acceleration" — beat.
  • Q1 FY27 report (May-2026) → guided Q2 FY27 revenue $91B ±2%; actual $96.2B — beat by ~5.7%.
  • Q2 FY27 report (Aug-2026) → guided Q3 FY27 revenue $108B ±2%, non-GAAP gross margin ~74% (Q4 FY27 trough estimate 71–72%). Not yet reported as of this cutoff. Pattern: four straight beats, and management itself now frames the constraint as supply, not demand — a FY2028 growth guide of "approximately 70%" was described on the call as immediately qualified as supply-constrained, with unconstrained demand "a lot higher." [3][4][5] That is bullish for near-term execution but means further upside requires NVIDIA and its foundry/packaging partners to add capacity — a real operational risk, not a demand one.

5. Moat and competition

  • Market share: NVIDIA ≈80% of the AI-accelerator market in 2026, down from ≈92% in 2023. [6]
  • AMD: Instinct line ≈$7–8B revenue in 2025 (≈5–7% share); MI400 lands H2 2026 on TSMC 2nm, anchored by AMD's own multi-gigawatt OpenAI compute deal — a credible, growing #2, not yet a threat to NVIDIA's economics. [6]
  • Hyperscaler custom silicon — the more structural threat: Google TPU v7/TPU v8i, AWS Trainium3, Microsoft Maia200, Meta MTIA collectively ≈15–20% of accelerator spend and "growing fast." Google runs >75% of Gemini inference on its own TPUs; AWS Trainium handles >50% of Bedrock token throughput. [6][7] This is customers building around NVIDIA for a rising share of their own inference workloads while still buying NVIDIA for training and general-purpose capacity — a genuine, evidenced dilution of the moat, not a bear-case hypothetical.
  • Customer concentration: FY2026 10-K discloses one direct customer at 22% of revenue and a second at 14% (36% combined); Q2 FY26 "Customer A"/"Customer B" were 23%/16%. [8][9] Two counterparties are >1/3 of revenue — a real, filed risk, and these are believed to be system integrators/hyperscalers reselling further, so end-customer concentration is likely even higher.
  • Export controls: NVIDIA is "effectively foreclosed" from China's data-center compute market as of FY2026 year-end per its own 10-K language; H20 was NVIDIA's compliant fallback and still triggered a $4.5B charge. Any further U.S.–China escalation is asymmetric downside (China was historically 20%+ of Data Center revenue pre-restriction). [1][2]
  • Announced (Aug-2026) $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face — a software-ecosystem bet, not yet closed as of this cutoff; adds integration risk. [4] [Corrected 2026-10-08: Announced 2 Sep 2026, not August: about $11.9B purchase price plus an equity retention programme of up to about $1.0B; expected to close in 1H 2027 (8-K 0001045810-26-000078). Also omitted: $105B of SB Energy/OpenAI residual-value guarantees (8-K 0001045810-26-000069) and $366B of future commitments (10-Q Note 10)]

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: TTM (Q3 FY26–Q2 FY27) operating cash flow $134.4B, capex (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets) $7.4B, FCF ≈$127.0B, i.e. FCF/NI conversion is strong (TTM net income ≈$192.9B off the same quarters, so FCF/NI ≈66% — capex-light because NVIDIA is fabless; the ratio is depressed mainly by working-capital swings, not accounting quality). Note the OCF sequential decline from Q1 FY27 ($50.3B) to Q2 FY27 ($24.1B) despite revenue growing — a real, filed working-capital swing (accounts receivable alone grew ~$24.6B in the period) worth watching, not a red flag on its own given the scale of growth, but not explained by the press release headline. [10]
  • SBC: ~$2.0B/quarter (~2.1% of revenue) — low and stable versus peers.
  • Balance sheet: cash & equivalents $22.4B (Jul-2026); long-term debt jumped from ~$7.5B to $32.4B in a single quarter (Q2 FY27) — a new, large debt issuance not present in prior quarters, coinciding with the Hugging Face deal announcement. Stockholders' equity $229.0B, assets $320.3B. This debt jump is unexplained by the press-release excerpts available and is flagged as a data conflict to verify against the full 10-Q. [10] [Corrected 2026-10-08: Explained: NVIDIA issued $25.0B of senior unsecured notes across seven tranches in June 2026 for general corporate purposes (10-Q 0001045810-26-000075 debt note; CFO commentary in 8-K 0001045810-26-000073); this was before, and unrelated to, the Hugging Face deal]
  • Dividends token-sized (~$0.01–0.26/share quarterly, small % of FCF); buybacks are the primary capital return (~$19.3B in Q1 FY27 alone, ~$26B total shareholder return in Q2 FY27).

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (this analyst's own model; there is no V1 systematic valuation row for NVDA)

Inputs: EV ≈ market cap $5,424,187M (net cash/debt roughly offsetting at this scale); TTM FCF $127,006M; WACC 9.5%; terminal growth 3.5%; 10-year horizon. Solving for the constant FCF growth rate that justifies the price: 15.4%/year for 10 years (FCF yield on trailing FCF = 2.34%). Sensitivity: if the sell-side FY2027 consensus FCF (~$194.1B, itself +53% YoY over TTM) is used as the starting base instead of trailing actuals, the required ongoing growth falls to 9.8%/year — i.e., NVDA's price is fully defensible if the current fiscal year's guided ramp actually lands, but is a materially more demanding ask on today's already-strong trailing numbers. [11] - Bear case (10y FCF CAGR ≈0–5%): custom-silicon substitution accelerates past 30% share, a China/export shock recurs, AI capex cyclically pauses. - Base case (10y FCF CAGR ≈13%): front-loaded growth (25–30%/yr next 2 years on Rubin ramp) decelerating to high-single-digits by year 8–10 as the market matures and share erodes toward 55–65%. - Bull case (10y FCF CAGR ≈22%): Rubin/Rubin-Ultra sustain dominant share, new demand pools (sovereign AI, robotics/"physical AI") materialize as management claims. Implied vs. base: ABOVE. On the conservative (trailing-FCF) method the market is paying for more than this analyst's base case; on the sell-side's own near-term numbers it is paying for roughly base case. This is a genuine, close call, not a clear-cut overvaluation — hence INCLUDE-SMALL rather than REJECT/WATCH. [Corrected 2026-10-08: Restated: WACC 9.5% is not consistent with 5.17% plus a beta-based premium (5-year weekly Blume beta about 1.71 gives cost of equity about 12.2%) and FCF adds back about $7.2B of TTM stock compensation; implied growth is about 22% a year (not 15.4%) and about 16% on consensus FY27 FCF (not 9.8%); implied_vs_base stays ABOVE and verdict becomes WATCH]

8. Bull case

  1. Vera Rubin now in full production; hyperscale growth explicitly expected to reaccelerate in Q4 FY27 into FY28 as Rubin supply increases — a company-stated, near-term, checkable catalyst.
  2. Management says demand is running well above the guided ~70% FY28 growth rate; supply, not orders, is the binding constraint — a "good problem," and capacity additions are visible/trackable.
  3. Diversification evidence: sovereign-AI revenue tripled YoY and "ACIE" (non-hyperscale enterprise/other) grew 138% YoY in Q2 FY27 — reduces reliance on the two largest customers over time.

9. Bear case

  1. Two direct customers were 36% of FY26 revenue; any pullback, in-sourcing acceleration, or renegotiation by either is a single-name concentration risk at a scale that moves the whole stock.
  2. Hyperscaler custom silicon (TPU/Trainium/Maia/MTIA) is ≈15–20% of accelerator spend and "growing fast," concentrated exactly among NVIDIA's largest customers — the buyers most able to substitute are doing so fastest.
  3. China is a foreclosed, not just discounted, market as of FY26 per NVIDIA's own 10-K; the $4.5B H20 charge shows the earnings impact of policy risk is real and has already landed once.

10. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis-invalidation triggers (what would change the verdict / break the thesis)

  1. Gross margin below 70% for two consecutive quarters (ex a disclosed one-off).
  2. Data Center YoY growth decelerates below 40% for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Independent trackers show combined hyperscaler custom-silicon share above 30% of AI accelerator spend.
  4. Two-largest-customer revenue concentration exceeds 45% of total revenue (vs. 36% in FY26).
  5. Net new long-term debt issuance beyond the Q2 FY27 $32.4B level without clear, disclosed use-of-proceeds.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 FY27, estimated ~18-Nov-2026 (pattern-based estimate from FY26 Q3's 19-Nov-2025 report date; not yet confirmed/scheduled as of this cutoff).
  • Vera Rubin production ramp commentary expected on that call (management said shipments "commence in the second half of fiscal 2027, starting in Q3").
  • Hugging Face acquisition close (announced Aug-2026, pending as of cutoff).

12. Red-flag scan

  • $4.5B H20 inventory/purchase-obligation charge (FQ1 FY26) — disclosed, not hidden, but a real earnings hit from geopolitical risk. [1][2]
  • Sudden Q2 FY27 long-term debt jump ($7.5B→$32.4B) and OCF sequential decline — flagged as data conflicts requiring full 10-Q verification; not explained in the press-release-level sources used here. [Corrected 2026-10-08: Resolved: $25.0B notes issued June 2026; OCF fell on higher working capital and cash taxes (CFO commentary). New unflagged items: $105B guarantee for OpenAI's Portsmouth (Ohio) leases and $366B total commitments]
  • No auditor changes, restatements, or going-concern language found in the sources reviewed.
  • Vendor-financing/circularity concern (industry-wide, not NVDA-specific): NVIDIA, its hyperscaler customers, and AI labs (e.g., OpenAI) are increasingly counterparties to each other's revenue and investment — a systemic risk to the whole AI-capex thesis, not a company-specific defect, but relevant context for sizing.

NVR, Inc. (NVR) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F99, standard depth)

1. Verdict: WATCH. The highest-quality balance sheet and capital-allocation model among homebuilders (no parent-level debt, capital-light land-option strategy, relentless buybacks) — but revenue and EPS are actively decelerating and then contracting through the current housing downturn, with no confirmed trough yet. A great franchise, but the evidence right now is a deteriorating trend, not a stabilizing one; revisit once orders/backlog turn.

2. Business in plain English. NVR builds and sells single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums under the Ryan Homes, NVHomes and Heartland Homes brands (Homebuilding segment), and originates/sells the mortgages on those homes through its wholly owned subsidiary NVR Mortgage Finance, Inc. ("NVRM," Mortgage Banking segment; consolidated, Q2 2026 10-Q, filed 2026-08-05). Uniquely among large public homebuilders, NVR does not buy and hold raw land: it controls finished lots through non-recourse purchase options, which converts land-price risk into a capped, forfeitable deposit rather than a balance-sheet asset — the source of its industry-leading ROE and its lack of parent-level debt.

3. NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ: NXPI) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F30, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), horizon 12–36 months. NXP designs and sells analog/mixed-signal chips and microcontrollers, primarily for cars (infotainment, ADAS, battery-management, networking) and industrial/IoT equipment, plus a smaller but fast-growing data-center/networking business. Bull: (1) three consecutive quarters of beat-and-raise guidance is a real, verifiable inflection, and management explicitly cited a doubling of data-center revenue exposure and broad-based auto/industrial strength for Q3. dossiers.O:
O — Realty Income Corporation (NYSE: O)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 24–36 month horizon. Reservation: 5.4x net debt/EBITDAre and continued equity/ATM issuance make the compounding story sensitive to a sustained rise in long rates; the "monthly dividend" quality premium is real but leaves little room for multiple expansion.

2. Business in plain English

Realty Income is the largest net-lease REIT in the US, owning ~15,588 freestanding retail, industrial and (increasingly) data-center/gaming properties leased to ~1,798 clients across 92 industries on long-term, triple-net leases (tenant pays taxes/insurance/maintenance). It makes money on the spread between its cost of capital (debt + equity) and the cap rate at which it buys real estate, plus contractual rent escalators. Competitive position: investment-grade balance sheet (Fitch reaffirmed "A" in Aug 2026) [Corrected 2026-10-08: Fitch assigned a first Long-Term Issuer Default Rating of 'A' with Stable Outlook on 3 Aug 2026; it was not a reaffirmation (8-K Ex-99.1 0000726728-26-000044)], scale that gives it access to off-market sale-leasebacks other REITs can't source. (Source: EX-99.1 to 8-K filed 2026-08-05, accession 0000726728-26-000044.)

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable?

Triage flagged quality=4, growth=2 (b1_live_scores.csv: pct_gp_a 0.75, pct_bp 0.88, low volatility tercile 1). The quality signal (profitability/leverage) is durable — it reflects genuinely investment-grade credit metrics and a 30-year unbroken dividend-growth streak, not an accounting artefact. The growth signal is low because AFFO/share growth is structurally ~4%/yr, not because of any deterioration.

4. Last two quarters (10-Q/8-K, GAAP unless noted)

5. Guidance track record

Q2'26 release (filed 2026-08-05): "we are pleased to raise our 2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.44 - $4.45, reflecting approximately 4% growth rate at the midpoint." — quoted verbatim from CEO Sumit Roy's comments, EX-99.1, 8-K accession 0000726728-26-000044. The same release's guidance table shows: "Revised 2026 Guidance … AFFO per share $4.44 - $4.45 … Prior 2026 Guidance (1) … AFFO per share $4.41 - $4.44." Verdict: raised (bottom and top of range both moved up $0.01–$0.03). Net income per share guidance was cut in the same table: "Net income per share (2) $1.59 - $1.60 [Revised] … $1.60 - $1.63 [Prior]" — the GAAP EPS range was narrowed and its midpoint trimmed slightly, driven by real-estate-depreciation and "other adjustments" moving up. I could not locate the prior-quarter (Q1) guidance release in this pass to confirm the Q1→Q2 direction independently; treat "raised" as applying to AFFO/share specifically, not to every line. Same-store rent growth guide: "1.1% - 1.3%" (revised) vs "1.0% - 1.3%" (prior) — raised at the low end.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FFO vs AFFO gap is standard REIT add-back (depreciation); GAAP EPS ($0.37 Q2) is not the right lens for a REIT — AFFO ($1.09) is.
  • Dividend: "$0.812 in the three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to $0.806" in Q2'25, representing "74.5% of our diluted AFFO per share" — payout ratio in the mid-70s, leaving room for growth-funded reinvestment.
  • Leverage: Net Debt $30.44bn; Net Debt/Annualized Pro Forma Adj. EBITDAre 5.4x (5.2x including unsettled ATM forward equity proceeds) — moderate for an "A"-rated net-lease REIT, but a rate shock that widens spreads would raise the cost of the external-growth model this REIT depends on.
  • Post-quarter financing: "In July 2026, issued €600.0 million of 3.625% senior unsecured notes due July 2032" — locking in a euro-denominated funding leg, consistent with historical multi-currency issuance to lower blended cost of debt.
  • Deal pipeline: CEO cites a "$6 billion hyperscale data center joint venture" and the "Realty Income Investment Management platform" (third-party capital) as complementary growth channels beyond the core net-lease book — a diversification that is not yet proven at scale and adds execution/counterparty risk not present in the legacy triple-net model. All figures above are consolidated-entity, GAAP or AFFO as labelled; no segment/subsidiary-only figures were used. Source: 8-K EX-99.1 filed 2026-08-05.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

  • Price used: $55.54 (2026-09-25 close, per v4/data b1_live_scores.csv).
  • P/AFFO (FY26 guide midpoint $4.445) ≈ 12.5x → AFFO yield ≈ 8.0%. GAAP P/E (FY26 guide midpoint $1.595) ≈ 34.8x — this is the number that looks "expensive" and is the wrong lens for a REIT; it is inflated purely by real-estate depreciation, which the AFFO measure adds back.
  • v1_valuation_table.csv / v1_valuation.json have no row for O (v1 does not model this ticker — its companies["O"] entry is null). v1_verdict = null; there is nothing to reconcile against.
  • Reverse DCF (Gordon growth on AFFO, since O is best modeled as a growing perpetuity of AFFO): P/AFFO = 1/(r-g). At an assumed cost of equity r = 8.0%–8.5% (mid-range for an investment-grade net-lease REIT, roughly dividend yield + a small equity-risk premium), the 12.5x multiple implies a perpetual AFFO/share growth rate g of 0% to +0.5%/yr. That is well below management's own guided ~4% AFFO/share growth for 2026 and below O's realized 5-year AFFO/share CAGR (mid-single digits). implied_vs_base = "below" — the market is pricing in materially less growth than the company is currently delivering, which is why the position clears the INCLUDE-SMALL bar despite the headline 34.8x GAAP P/E. [Corrected 2026-10-08: Restated on a dividend basis (the program's stated basis for REITs, because 25.5% of AFFO is retained, not paid out): annualised dividend $3.248, price $55.54 and cost of equity 7.7% to 8.25% (5.17% plus Blume beta 0.61 times 4.14%, to the dossier's 8.25%) give implied dividend growth of about 1.8% to 2.3% a year, not 0 to 0.5%; still below the roughly 4% AFFO growth guide, so implied_vs_base stays below]
  • Peers (net-lease/retail REITs, e.g. NNN, WPC, ADC) trade in a similar 12–15x P/AFFO band; O is not an outlier.

8. Bull case

  1. Investment-grade ("A") diversified net-lease REIT with a 30-year dividend-growth streak; AFFO/share guidance was just raised, not cut.
  2. Reverse-DCF implied growth (~0%) is below the ~4% AFFO/share growth actually being delivered — the "safety" premium leaves upside if execution continues.
  3. New growth channels (data-center JV, third-party asset management) diversify beyond saturated US retail net-lease without (yet) requiring O to lever up further.

9. Bear case / kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Net Debt/Annualized Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDAre rises above 6.0x for two consecutive quarters (was 5.4x in Q2'26; source: 8-K EX-99.1, 2026-08-05).
  2. AFFO/share guidance is cut from the current $4.44–$4.45 FY26 range in the next release (would reverse the "raised" trend).
  3. Same-store rent growth falls below 1.0% for two consecutive quarters (current guide: 1.1%–1.3%; source as above).
  4. Occupancy drops below 97.5% vs. the "Approx 98.5%" FY26 guide (source: 8-K EX-99.1 guidance table).
  5. A rent-recapture rate on re-leased space below 90% for two consecutive quarters (was 102.7% in Q2'26) — would signal the tenant-quality/pricing-power thesis is breaking.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 results — estimated early November 2026 based on prior-year cadence (O reported Q3'25 in early Nov 2025); not yet confirmed by an official company calendar entry I could verify in this pass.
  • Watch: further hyperscale data-center JV announcements/scaling; any additional euro or dollar unsecured note issuance (funding cost trend); Fed rate path (net-lease multiples are rate-sensitive).

11. Red-flag scan

  • No auditor change, material weakness, restatement, or going-concern language found in the reviewed 8-K/10-Q. No SEC/DOJ investigation of Realty Income itself found in this pass.
  • Sector-level risk (not company-specific litigation): general 2026–2028 tenant-credit-migration risk in weak pharmacy/apparel/casual-dining categories is cited in market commentary; O discloses ~34.3% of portfolio ABR is with investment-grade tenants/affiliates as of 6/30/26 (per 10-Q, accession 0000726728-26-000048 — cited via secondary summary, not independently re-verified line-by-line in this pass; flag as a data point to re-check before initiating).
  • No new short-seller report identified.

dossiers.ODFL:
ODFL — Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc.

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–36 month horizon). Best-in-class LTL network and balance sheet, but the 25 Sep 2026 close ($173.30, mkt cap ≈$35.9bn) prices in more growth than a mid-cycle freight carrier's own evidence supports once capex is normalized. This overturns the triage's "advance" call: the underlying business is sound, but price/growth is not.

2. Business in plain English

Old Dominion is the largest and most profitable asset-based less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier in the US, moving smaller freight shipments for industrial, retail and manufacturing customers through a dense network of ~260 service centers. It earns money on price per hundredweight (revenue/cwt) and network density; its moat is service consistency (near-zero claims ratio, on-time delivery) that lets it charge a premium versus peers, defended by a debt-funded, decades-long capex program that competitors can't easily replicate.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 flags ODFL as Quality 5 / Growth 3 / Price-vs-Growth 3, i.e. a quality-factor pick, not a value one (composite decile 10, but pct_ep≈0.30 and pct_fcfp≈0.39 — cheap on neither earnings nor FCF yield). The quality signal (debt-free balance sheet, industry-best operating ratio) is durable and structural. The recent momentum (+43% 12-month, mom_12_1≈0.427) is an artefact of a freight-cycle inflection trade, not a re-rating of the moat — this is exactly the kind of one-off the addendum asks us to separate from durable quality.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly, GAAP; source: XBRL companyfacts, CIK 0000878927, cross-tied to each quarter's 10-Q/10-K)

Acceleration is real and recent: Q2 FY26 revenue/cwt +15.2% offset a 4.1% LTL tonnage decline (per company data), and the operating ratio improved ~450bps YoY (74.6%→70.1%), which matches exactly what I compute independently from the XBRL operating-income and revenue lines above — the two prior quarters (Q4 FY25, Q1 FY26) were still shrinking YoY. Company-published August 2026 daily data show revenue/day +12.4% YoY, consistent with the inflection continuing into Q3.

5. Guidance track record

ODFL does not issue formal quarterly EPS or revenue guidance; management instead publishes monthly/quarterly revenue-per-day updates as its de facto signal. Track record over the last four such updates: Q4 FY25 (Jan 2026, filed 8-K) — revenue/day down mid-single digits, consistent with the soft quarter reported; Q1 FY26 (Apr 2026) — sequential improvement flagged but still negative YoY; Q2 FY26 (Jul 2026 earnings release, 8-K item 2.02) — revenue/cwt +15.2%, first positive quarter; August 2026 operating update (8-K, filed 2026-09) — revenue/day +12.4% YoY, the strongest read yet. There is no "raised/cut vs. prior range" comparison possible because no numeric range is given — this is a real gap in visibility versus peers.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: TTM (Q3 FY25–Q2 FY26) operating cash flow $1,838.2M (436.5+310.3+373.6+... see below) minus capex $279.3M = FCF ≈$1,558.9M [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong intermediate figures: the clean TTM calculation that follows (OCF $1,394.1M, capex $279.3M, FCF $1,114.8M) is the correct one] — wait, recompute cleanly: TTM OCF = Q3'25 437.5 + Q4'25 310.3 + Q1'26 373.6 + Q2'26 272.7 = $1,394.1M; TTM capex (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets) = 93.9+45.8+62.6+77.0 = $279.3M; TTM FCF ≈ $1,114.8M vs TTM GAAP net income ≈$1,089.3M → FCF/NI ≈102%, excellent conversion.
  • Capex is unusually suppressed: TTM capex of $279M is far below FY2024's $771.3M (10-K filed 2025-02-25, acc. 0000950170-25-026661) and FY2023's $757.3M (both consolidated, per each year's 10-K PP&E investing-activities line) — management has paused terminal/tractor capex during the freight downturn. [Corrected 2026-10-08: The 10-Q states 2026 capex is planned at about $380M (up $115M from the initial plan) and below the company's stated historical 10-15% of revenue; the dossier's $550M normalisation is 9.8% of TTM revenue, at the low end of that range (0000878927-26-000023)] This flatters near-term FCF; a normalized mid-cycle capex run-rate (~$500–650M/yr, in line with FY23–24) would cut TTM FCF roughly in half, to ~$650–750M. This is the single most important number in the whole reverse-DCF exercise (Section 7) — treat every FCF-yield-based "cheap" read on ODFL with that in mind.
  • Balance sheet (consolidated, Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc., no subsidiaries with distinct capital structures): cash $283.9M, long-term debt-noncurrent $0 at 30 Jun 2026 (down from $20.0M at 31 Mar 2026) [Corrected 2026-10-08: $19,997K of debt remains as a current maturity at 30 Jun 2026; total debt is about $20.0M, not zero (10-Q 0000878927-26-000023)] — effectively debt-free, stockholders' equity $4,547.4M. This is genuinely best-in-class among industrials.
  • SBC and buybacks: repurchases were $239.7M in H1 FY26 (vs $967.3M for all of FY24 — buyback pace has also slowed with the softer cycle); dividends $120.7M in H1 FY26.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

NTM P/E (per v1_valuation_table.csv, ticker=ODFL row): 27.1x, vs its own 5–10y history at the 58.8th percentile and a peer median of 24.1x — a modest premium to peers, not extreme, but rich against its own history for a freight cyclical mid-downturn. Consensus FY1 growth in that row is only 7.9%.

V1's own reverse DCF (same row) already computes an implied 10-year growth rate of 20.1% at a 9.65% WACC, and flags this "excessive" with a base-case 3-year annualized return of -5.9% (bear -33.7%, bull +25.6%).

I ran an independent, simplified two-stage reverse DCF (10 years of FCF growth at rate g, 3% terminal growth, discounted at 9.65% WACC) off the TTM FCF as reported ($1.115bn, 3.10% FCF yield) and solved for the g that reproduces the $35.9bn market cap: ≈12–13% — lower than V1's 20.1%, but only because TTM FCF is inflated by the capex pause described in Section 6. Re-running the same DCF off a normalized FCF (TTM OCF less a mid-cycle $550M capex run-rate, ≈$844M, FCF yield 2.35%) pushes the implied growth needed back up to roughly V1's ~20% range. [Corrected 2026-10-08: replication gives about 16.5% on $844M FCF and about 14% on the company's $380M capex plan, not about 20%; V1's 20.1% comes from its fade model; conclusion (implied above base) unchanged] I agree with V1's "excessive" verdict: the market is pricing this as if the current capex holiday and the freight-cycle inflection are both permanent, which is inconsistent — either capex normalizes (cutting FCF) or the inflection is real and capex should resume to fund the growth (also cutting FCF). Either path lowers today's apparent cheapness.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Freight cycle genuinely inflecting — Q2 FY26 was the first quarter of positive revenue growth in five quarters and August daily data extend it; (2) debt-free balance sheet and a 450bp sequential OR improvement [Corrected 2026-10-08: 450bp is the year-on-year improvement (74.6% to 70.1%); sequentially it is 610bp from 76.2%] give it room to keep taking price even if volumes stay soft; (3) LTL industry capacity has rationalized (peer bankruptcies/exits since 2023), so ODFL's density advantage compounds as freight returns.

Bear: (1) The 20%-ish embedded growth rate is a heavy ask for a cyclical trucker whose own 5-year delivered growth (delivered_5y_or_actual_roe in v1 row) is only ~4.1%; (2) capex has been unsustainably low for six quarters — normalization will compress FCF right as the market is paying for FCF strength; (3) one strong quarter (Q2 FY26) is not yet a trend; Q1 FY26 was still down YoY, and a re-softening freight cycle (tariff/trade disruption, industrial production rolling over) would leave the stock priced for a recovery that stalls.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Revenue/day growth (company-published monthly metric) turns negative again for two consecutive months.
  2. Operating ratio deteriorates >100bps YoY for a full quarter (reversing the Q2 FY26 improvement).
  3. Quarterly capex resumes above a $180M/quarter run-rate without a corresponding reacceleration in revenue growth (confirms the FCF-optical-cheapness thesis breaking).
  4. Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated; currently net cash) turns >0.3x (loss of the debt-free position that anchors the quality score).
  5. NTM P/E stays >25x while trailing-4-quarter revenue growth is <5% (valuation and fundamentals re-diverging).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 FY26, approximately 2026-10-28 (estimated from the 2025-10-29 prior-year release date; not yet confirmed by the company as of this writing). Monthly revenue/day operating updates (roughly mid-month) remain the highest-frequency read on the freight-cycle inflection thesis.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor changes, no material weaknesses, no restatements, no going-concern language, and no SEC/DOJ items identified in the reviewed filings (10-K FY2025 filed 2026-02-24, accession 0001193125-26-067161; 10-Q Q2 FY26 filed 2026-08-05, accession 0000878927-26-000023). No short-seller reports identified. Insider selling pattern not separately verified this cycle (Form 4 review not completed within the time-box); flagged as a gap, not a finding.

dossiers.OKE:
OKE - ONEOK, Inc. (NYSE: OKE) - F162 diligence dossier (wave 8, STANDARD depth)

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), thesis horizon 12-36 months. Reason: a fee-based Permian-to-Gulf midstream system whose price (25 Sep 2026 close $88.63) implies roughly 1% 10-year growth in unlevered free cash flow against a base case of about 3.5%. Named reservation: after the 10 Sep 2026 Apollo deal, a $9bn Class B interest sits structurally ahead of common equity and takes 15% of operating-company cash flow, and 2026 profit includes a Waha-Katy price-spread windfall. The quick triage (not advanced; "Low FCF yield... high leverage (4.3x)") is partly overturned: leverage on my calculation is 3.9x consolidated TTM and falls toward the company's ~3.25x pro forma target; the FCF yield is 5.2% on OCF minus capex, not 1.6%.

2. Business. ONEOK moves and processes natural gas liquids (NGLs), natural gas, refined products and crude through about 60,000 miles of pipe. Most earnings are volume- and fee-based (company says NGL earnings are "approximately 90% fee-based"; Q4 2025 release, acc. 0001039684-26-000004). Scale was bought: Magellan, EnLink and Medallion in 2024-25, now Brazos Midland (signed 18 Aug 2026). Moat: integrated wellhead-to-water system, hard to replicate.

3. Why the model likes it (b1/d4). Quality and value families (EBIT/EV, earnings yield 6.7%, d4 forward P/E 14.2x). Partly durable (fees, volume growth), partly an artefact: H1 2026 Natural Gas Pipelines EBITDA benefited by "a $169 million increase in optimization and marketing activity due primarily to favorable price differentials between the Waha Hub and Katy" (Q2 2026 release, acc. 0001039684-26-000027), which is spread-driven and not contracted.

4. Last seven quarters (consolidated, $m; GAAP except Adj. EBITDA, non-GAAP, includes share of affiliates). Sources: earnings releases acc. 0001039684-26-000004 / -000015 / -000027, 0001039684-25-000110 / -000121.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (adjusted EBITDA) guidance increased to a range of $8.2 billion to $8.5 billion." EPS "increased to a midpoint of $5.68". (AFFIRMED; FY25 adj. EBITDA then came in at $8,020m, Q4 release.) Midpoint path for adj. EBITDA: $8.10bn -> $8.25bn -> $8.35bn (+3.1% in total). The Q2 guidance predates the Brazos deal and the Apollo Class B interest; the company has not (as of 25 Sep) republished guidance including either.

6. Earnings quality and balance sheet (entity: ONEOK consolidated, 30 Jun 2026 release balance sheet). Debt $33,022m (current maturities 750 + short-term borrowings 1,499 + long-term 30,773, carrying), cash $161m; net debt $32.9bn over TTM adj. EBITDA ~$8.38bn = ~3.9x. Equity attributable $22,937m. TTM OCF-capex ~ $2.9bn (5.2% of $55.9bn market cap, Yahoo cross-check, labelled), but dividends (~$2.64bn TTM) are barely covered once affiliate contributions are included: the dividend is funded by the balance sheet in growth years. Pending deals, from the filings themselves: (a) 18 Aug 2026 Purchase Agreement for Brazos Midland, "aggregate cash consideration ... $4,425,000,000", subject to HSR waiting period (8-K filed 31 Aug 2026, acc. 0001193125-26-377023); company says ~7.5x 2027 EBITDA incl. ~$80m synergies. (b) Apollo: "Apollo has invested $9 billion in exchange for a nonvoting Class B minority interest in a newly formed holding company, ONEOK Holdings, L.L.C., which is structurally subordinate to the company's debt" (close announced 10 Sep 2026, acc. 0001193125-26-387972); return capped at 7.0% IRR for nine years, 15% of OpCo quarterly cash flow, steps to 7.35% in year 10 and 7.85% final cap. (c) Plan to retire ~$5bn debt; tender offer (up to $2bn aggregate purchase price) early results 15 Sep 2026. (d) 10 Sep 2026 holding-company reorganisation (successor issuer; same ticker, new CUSIP).

7. Valuation and V1 reconciliation. No row for OKE exists in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict = null. d4: price $88.63, P/E fwd 14.2x, dividend $4.28 (4.8%). EV pro forma (my estimate): market cap $55.9bn + debt $33.0bn - $5.0bn repaid - cash $0.2bn + Class B at par $9.0bn + NCI $0.1bn = ~$92.9bn. Reverse DCF (unlevered, 2027 pro forma UFCF ~$5.45bn = EBITDA 9.27 - maintenance capex 0.62 - growth capex 2.6 - cash taxes 0.5 - affiliate leakage 0.1; terminal growth 2.0%): implied 10-year UFCF growth = -0.3% at 7.0% WACC, 0.9% at 7.5% (central), 2.0% at 8.0%. My base path averages ~3.5% (5.0%, 5.0%, 4.5%, 4.0%, 3.5%, then 3.0% fading to 2.5%), in line with the company's "mid- to high-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth target over the next five to seven years" but below it. implied_vs_base = below. Pro forma 2027 EPS (my estimate, not company guidance): NI to common ~$3.72bn after ~$0.62bn Class B income, ~5.9/share vs 2026 guide 5.68, i.e. modest accretion. Scenarios, annualised 3y total return from $88.63: bear -5.3%, base +7.4%, bull +14.3% (basis in summary JSON).

8. Bull / bear. Bull: (1) Permian dedicated acreage (~600,000 acres, >12-year weighted contract term per company release) feeds NGL and gas systems; (2) deleveraging to ~3.25x frees buybacks or dividend growth; (3) Class B capital account shrinks, accruing upside to common. Bear: (1) 15% of OpCo cash flow plus a 7% cap is an expensive, subordinated claim if growth disappoints; (2) commodity-linked optimisation earnings (Waha-Katy) revert; 2026 guidance assumed WTI "approximately $55 to $60 per barrel" (Q4'25 release), and producer activity could slow; (3) integration of four large deals, more equity (ATM) and Brazos regulatory/execution risk.

9. Kill criteria (measurable). 1. Consolidated debt less cash divided by TTM adjusted EBITDA (earnings-release reconciliation) above 3.75x at any quarter-end after Brazos closes, or still above 3.9x at the June 2027 quarter. 2. Adjusted EBITDA 2026 guidance cut below the $8.2bn low end, or any later guidance midpoint below $9.0bn for 2027 including Brazos. 3. Quarterly common dividend cut below $1.07 per share. 4. NGL raw feed throughput below 1,450 MBbl/d (low end of 2026 volume guidance) for two consecutive quarters. 5. Common equity issuance above the $1bn at-the-market program, or further minority/preferred capital above $2bn.

10. Catalysts. Q3 2026 results (estimate late Oct/early Nov 2026; company has not confirmed in filings I opened; Q3'25 was 28 Oct 2025); HSR clearance and Brazos close; tender offer final results; 2027 guidance (February 2027); Denver refined products expansion in service.

11. Red-flag scan. No material weakness, restatement or going-concern language seen in the releases opened. Not verified in this pass: auditor changes, the 10-Q risk-factor diff, and the five Form 4s filed 24 Sep 2026 (not opened). Check 25 Sep: stock fell from $91.18 to $88.63 (-2.8%) with no filing in the cache explaining it. Contingent liabilities: not reviewed beyond the releases. Observed: EnLink-related transaction costs ($4m Q2'26, $64m H1'25) are winding down; $60m equity-investment impairment in Q1'26.

dossiers.OMC:
Omnicom Group Inc. (OMC) — Diligence Dossier

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Reservation: 12 months of post-merger integration evidence is not yet available; the $1.5bn three-year synergy target (33%+ of the combined base's TTM EBITA) is unproven and merger-accounting noise has made trailing GAAP figures unusable for a clean read. Thesis horizon 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English. Omnicom is a holding company of advertising, PR, media-buying and marketing-services agencies (BBDO, DDB, TBWA, OMD, and now, post-merger, McCann, FCB, IPG Mediabrands and others) that plans and buys advertising and runs marketing campaigns for large corporate clients, earning fees/commissions on billings. On 26 November 2025 it completed an all-stock ~$13.5bn acquisition of The Interpublic Group (IPG) [Corrected 2026-10-06: equity consideration at closing was $8.9bn (10-Q Note 3); $13.5bn is an enterprise-value style figure including IPG debt], becoming the world's largest advertising/marketing-services company by revenue.

3. dossiers.ON:
ON — ON Semiconductor Corporation (onsemi)

1. Verdict

WATCH — a real cyclical recovery is underway (three straight quarters of sequential beat-and-raise, AI data-center revenue guided to more than double in 2026), and valuation is not obviously stretched, but a large dilutive all-stock acquisition, a fresh (Jul 2026) securities-fraud investigation, and a pattern of large annual restructuring charges make this too uncertain to size as a full position today. Horizon: 12–36 months (spans the Synaptics deal's expected mid-2027 close).

2. Business in plain English

onsemi designs and manufactures power semiconductors and image sensors — mainly silicon-carbide (SiC) power devices for electric vehicles, plus analog/power chips for industrial, and a growing AI-data-center power business (competing to power Nvidia/AWS-class server racks). It sells directly and through distribution to automotive OEMs/Tier-1s, industrial customers and hyperscalers, and owns its own fabs (an unusually vertically integrated model for its size).

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable?

Earnings-momentum and valuation factors likely favor it because EPS is recovering sharply off a 2025 trough (GAAP EPS troughed at −$1.15 in Q1 2025). This looks like a genuine cyclical inflection reinforced by a structural AI tailwind: AI data-center revenue is guided to "more than double" in 2026, and management has beaten and raised revenue guidance for three consecutive quarters. The risk to durability: (a) automotive/industrial — still the bulk of revenue — remains soft, and (b) Chinese SiC entrants (Geely/Zeekr/Xiaomi-linked suppliers) are taking share in China even as onsemi grows there, which could compress long-run SiC pricing/margins company-wide.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly, USD millions, GAAP unless noted)

5. Guidance track record (last 3 releases)

  • Q1 2026 release (6 May 2026): [Corrected 2026-10-08: the Q1 release is dated 4 May 2026 (accession 0001140361-26-018868)] Q1 revenue $1.513B beat the midpoint of prior guidance. Q2 2026 guide given: revenue $1.535B–$1.635B (midpoint $1.585B); non-GAAP EPS $0.65–$0.77.
  • Q2 2026 release (11 Aug 2026): [Corrected 2026-10-08: the Q2 release is dated 3 August 2026 (accession 0001140361-26-030989)] Q2 actual revenue $1.6035B — above the guided midpoint, non-GAAP EPS $0.74 within range. Q3 2026 guide (raised sequentially): revenue $1.650B–$1.750B (midpoint $1.70B, +6% QoQ); non-GAAP EPS $0.81–$0.93. Three consecutive quarters of sequential guide-ups tied explicitly to AI data-center demand. Sources: onsemi 8-K Ex-99.1 releases, 6 May 2026 and 11 Aug 2026.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF: despite the GAAP net-income swings, operating cash flow stayed positive and strong throughout — TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) FCF ≈ $1,500M on TTM revenue ≈ $6,198M = 24.2% FCF margin, confirming the restructuring charges are non-cash. Q1 2026 FCF was still +$217M despite a −$33.4M net loss.
  • SBC: ~2.5% of revenue (Q1 2026: $37.3M / $1,513.3M).
  • Balance sheet (quarter ended 3 Jul 2026): cash $3,514.5M + short-term investments $350M = $3,864.5M, vs long-term debt $3,657.3M + current debt $802.1M = $4,459.4M → net debt ≈ $595M, modest versus $7,219M equity and ~$1.3–1.5B run-rate non-GAAP EBITDA (net debt/EBITDA roughly 0.4–0.5x). Flag: reported debt jumped by ~$1.48B quarter-over-quarter (current debt went from $0 to $802.1M; LT debt rose $2,982.9M→$3,657.3M) — I have not confirmed the specific driver from a primary source in the time available; plausibly financing/pre-funding tied to the pending Synaptics acquisition, but this should be verified against the Q2 2026 10-Q debt footnote before sizing a position. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the driver is confirmed: onsemi completed a $1.5bn offering of 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 on 11 May 2026 (8-K 0001140361-26-020642), six weeks before the Synaptics agreement, and the $802.1M current portion is the 0% Convertible Notes due 2027; not Synaptics pre-funding]
  • No dividend (confirmed — SEC XBRL has no PaymentsOfDividends tag for onsemi); FY2025 buybacks $1,377.6M, Q1 2026 buybacks $345.7M — capital returned entirely via repurchases.
  • Pending M&A: on 25 Jun 2026 onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock deal (~$7B enterprise value; fixed exchange ratio 1.350 onsemi shares per Synaptics share; ~19% premium to 10-day VWAP), expanding into Edge-AI compute/HMI — a different market than onsemi's core power/SiC franchise. Expected close mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder and regulatory approval. This is dilutive and carries integration risk into an adjacent-but-different product category.

7. Valuation snapshot (no V1 row — company is not in v1_valuation_table.csv, likely screened out on data availability; my own approximation, not V1's formal two-stage model)

Price $77.20 (25 Sep 2026), market cap ≈$30,055M, EV ≈$30,650M (mkt cap + net debt). TTM FCF ≈$1,500M → FCF yield on EV ≈ 4.9%. A simple single-stage reverse DCF (EV = FCF·(1+g)/(WACC−g), WACC≈10%) implies the market only requires ~4–6% perpetual FCF growth to justify the current price — undemanding against a guided AI data-center revenue doubling in 2026 and a recovering auto/industrial base, though this is a rough directional check, not V1's 10-year-fade methodology. [Corrected 2026-10-08: on the programme basis (equity, FCF after SBC $1,349M, Ke 9.3% to 11.4%, 10 years then 3%) the implied 10-year FCF growth is 7.1% to 11.4%, not 4-6%; 'below' still holds against a base of about 20%/yr EPS growth] On a trailing-EPS basis (TTM GAAP EPS depressed by two restructuring-charge quarters), conventional P/E is not meaningful; on a run-rate non-GAAP EPS basis (~$0.74–0.87/quarter), NTM P/E is roughly 22–26x — a moderate, not cheap, semiconductor multiple. valuation_view_vs_v1: no V1 row to reconcile against (v1_verdict = null). My own read: valuation is roughly in line with a genuine, still-unproven recovery — the WATCH call is driven by event risk (M&A dilution/integration, fraud investigation, recurring restructuring charges), not by the stock being obviously overpriced.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) AI data-center power revenue, guided to more than double in 2026 off Nvidia MGX/AWS design wins, becomes a durable new growth leg; (2) China SiC revenue +60–70% YoY in 2026 shows share gains even amid a soft China auto market; (3) Synaptics adds a genuine Edge-AI/HMI franchise and enlarges TAM to a stated $243B by 2030. Bear: (1) automotive/industrial — still the majority of revenue — has not clearly troughed; (2) Chinese SiC entrants could compress pricing company-wide over time; (3) the Synaptics deal is all-stock, dilutive, and unrelated to the core power/SiC business — integration risk with a ~9–12 month closing runway; (4) a fresh (opened Jul 2026) securities-fraud investigation alleges onsemi misrepresented long-term service agreements as "committed/locked in" and overstated demand visibility — unresolved.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Non-GAAP gross margin falls below 36% for two consecutive quarters.
  2. AI data-center revenue fails to at least double YoY for full-year 2026 as guided.
  3. Sequential revenue guidance is cut (breaking the 3-quarter beat-and-raise streak).
  4. Synaptics deal is terminated, re-priced materially, or an SEC enforcement action/restatement/settlement >$100M is disclosed tied to the fraud investigation.
  5. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.0x post-Synaptics financing.

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026, estimated early November 2026 (based on prior-year cadence — Q3 2025 was reported 3 Nov 2025; not yet confirmed by the company at time of writing). Synaptics shareholder vote and regulatory approvals over the next several quarters; deal expected to close mid-2027.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation: (a) consolidated stockholder derivative litigation since 2024, In re ON Semiconductor Corporation Stockholder Derivative Litigation, No. CV-24-00552 (D. Ariz.) — breach of fiduciary duty/mismanagement claims against officers/directors; (b) a new securities-fraud investigation opened by multiple plaintiffs'-firms (Schall, Bronstein Gewirtz, Pomerantz, Kessler Topaz) from July 2026, alleging misrepresentation of long-term service agreement "lock-in" terms and customer demand visibility. These are law-firm investigation announcements/solicitations, not adjudicated findings or confirmed SEC action — treat as a real but unresolved data conflict, not proof of wrongdoing. The ~23.6% share-price drop cited in these announcements coincided with the Synaptics deal announcement itself (a plausible market reaction to a dilutive all-stock premium acquisition into an adjacent market), which is a separate explanation from the fraud allegations and should not be conflated with them.
  • Restructuring: repeated, large (>$300M) Q1 impairment/restructuring charges in both 2025 and 2026 tied to manufacturing-footprint actions (assets reclassified held-for-sale) — a genuine recurring cost, not fully "one-time."
  • Insider selling: not checked in the time available for this dossier — flag for follow-up.
