PPG — PPG Industries, Inc.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Thesis horizon: 24–36 months. Reason: of the three names in this batch, PPG has the cleanest recent execution record — six consecutive quarters of positive organic sales growth and three consecutive quarters of FY2026 guidance reaffirmed, never cut — at a valuation (≈12.7–13.6x forward earnings) that implies less 10-year growth than a reasonable base case [Corrected 2026-10-06: INCLUDE reduced to INCLUDE-SMALL; at a 9.6% cost of equity the price implies slightly more growth than the evidence-based 5% base; see Re-assessment (RA8)], with small, well-disclosed legacy liabilities rather than open-ended ones.

2. Business in plain English

PPG is a global paints and specialty-coatings maker (automotive OEM and refinish coatings, architectural/decorative paints, aerospace, protective and marine, packaging and specialty coatings) selling to auto makers and body shops, homeowners and contractors, aircraft makers, and industrial manufacturers worldwide. It makes money through brand strength, a large direct/distributor network, and formulation/technology know-how that supports price realization; it competes with Sherwin-Williams, AkzoNobel and RPM in an oligopoly-like global coatings market with high customer-switching costs (regulatory qualification cycles in automotive/aerospace coatings in particular).

3. Why the model likes it, and durability

b1_live_scores.csv: ROE 19.3%, FCF/P 5.1%, EBIT/EV 9.1%, book/price 33.8%, live rank 210/503, 12-month momentum +9.5%. The primary-source check (§4–5) shows organic growth is modest but has now been positive for six straight quarters and improved sequentially (1% Q1 2026 → 4% Q2 2026), which is a more durable signal than the triage's cautious framing suggested — the quality read holds up.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

Quant card (25-Sep-2026 close): price $107.52, NTM P/E 12.7x, trailing P/E 15.4x, FCF yield 4.6%, dividend yield 2.7%, net debt/EBITDA 2.2x, 12-month momentum +9.5%, Street target upside 17.5% (21 analysts). No V1 systematic valuation row exists for PPG (outside V1's ~92-name coverage); v1_verdict is null.

Illustrative reverse DCF (own model, not V1): FCF₀ = 4.6% × $23.9bn ≈ $1.10bn; discount rate 8.5% (industrial/specialty chemicals, moderate cyclicality); 10-year explicit growth then 2.5% terminal growth. Solving for the FCF growth rate that reproduces the $23.9bn market cap gives ≈5.6%/yr for 10 years. [Corrected 2026-10-06: discount rate 8.5% was not consistent with the 5.17% Treasury: CAPM with Blume beta 1.03-1.07 gives 9.45-9.6%; at 9.6%, owner FCF $1.25bn (after SBC) and 3.0% terminal growth the implied growth is 5.75% (4.6%-7.3% across TTM and FY2025 cash flow bases); see Re-assessment (RA8)] - My base case: ~6–7%/yr blended 10-yr EPS/FCF growth, extrapolating the current trajectory (six straight quarters of organic growth, guidance reaffirmed three times, aerospace and Latin America architectural strength offsetting automotive-refinish softness). [Corrected 2026-10-06: base restated to 5%: FY2026 guidance midpoint $7.90 is +4.2% on FY2025 adjusted EPS of $7.58, H1 2026 adjusted EPS grew 3%, and organic growth is low single digit] Implied (~5.6%) is below my base case (~6–7%) → "below," though the margin of safety is modest, not a screaming bargain. [Corrected 2026-10-06: with the corrected discount rate and base, implied (5.75%) is above the 5% base: in_line, with no margin of safety] - Bear case (~1%/yr): the organic-growth streak breaks as auto OEM/refinish and China-linked demand weaken further, margin gains stall, multiple compresses toward 11x on a cyclical de-rate. - Bull case (~12%/yr): aerospace and Latin America momentum broadens to more of the nine underlying businesses, cost/portfolio actions under CEO Tim Knavish continue to lift margins, multiple re-rates toward 16x as the growth/quality combination is recognized.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Six consecutive quarters of positive organic sales growth, improving sequentially (1%→4% quarter over quarter in H1 2026) — a real, primary-source-verified trend, not a one-quarter blip. (2) FY2026 guidance has been reaffirmed, not cut, in both quarters reported so far this year — a cleaner signal than either other name in this batch. (3) Legacy liabilities (asbestos $42M, a small environmental consent-order matter) are modest and well-quantified, reducing tail risk relative to some coatings/chemicals peers. Bear: (1) Organic growth, while positive, is still low-single-digit and uneven — automotive refinish/OEM softness is a real drag not yet resolved, and the "8 of 9 businesses" framing means one business is still declining. (2) At 12.7–13.6x forward earnings the stock is cheap in absolute terms but not screamingly so once the modest (5.6%) implied-growth margin of safety versus a 6–7% base case is taken into account. (3) A cyclical global economy (especially China-linked industrial/auto demand) could turn the current sequential improvement back down.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Consolidated organic sales growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the streak is currently 6 positive quarters).
  2. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($7.70–$8.10) is cut.
  3. Net debt / EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~2.2x currently).
  4. Asbestos-related reserves increase by more than 2x the current $42M.
  5. Automotive OEM/refinish organic sales decline for 3 or more consecutive quarters.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: ~27-Oct-2026 (estimated from the FY2025-Q3 report date of 28-Oct-2025; not yet confirmed by a company announcement).
  • Ongoing portfolio/cost-action program under CEO Tim Knavish (referenced in 2026 earnings-release commentary); specific divestiture milestones not itemized in the releases reviewed.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Legacy liabilities: asbestos-related reserves of $42M as of 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q, Note, accession 0000079879-26-000252) — "the Company believes that... the total reserves for asbestos-related claims will be sufficient." Small relative to PPG's ~$18bn annual revenue base.
  • Environmental/litigation: a legacy waste-disposal site in Cadogan/North Buffalo Townships, PA (former Ford City glass-manufacturing facility disposal area, used until the early 1970s) is subject to a 2019 consent order with Pennsylvania's DEP (a $1.2M civil penalty for past unauthorized discharges) and a related citizens' suit (Sierra Club/PennEnvironment) partly settled (injunctive relief + a $250,000 donation); a separate Clean Water Act civil-penalty trial on the remaining claims was pending per the 10-Q (accession 0000079879-26-000252, Item 1 Legal Proceedings). Financially immaterial at PPG's scale but an open legal matter.
  • Data conflict — activist/new-CEO claim: the triage read cited "general knowledge of PPG activist involvement/portfolio review" alongside a new-CEO catalyst. A search of SEC EDGAR for PPG (CIK 0000079879) found no SC 13D or SC 13D/A on file — no activist stake could be confirmed via a primary ownership filing. Tim Knavish is confirmed as current Chairman and CEO from his being quoted as such in the Q1 and Q2 2026 earnings releases; the specific timing/circumstances of his appointment and any activist campaign were not independently verified against a primary filing in the time available for this pass.
  • Insider Form 4 patterns and short-seller reports were not separately pulled in this standard-depth pass (time-boxed); no red flag identified from other sources reviewed.

PPL — PPL Corporation

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon: 12–36 months. Reservation: the growth thesis is real, primary-source-verified, and currently ahead of schedule (Section 4–5) [Corrected 2026-10-08: ongoing EPS grew only +3% in Q2 and +4% in H1 vs a 6%-8% target; growth is guided to be second-half weighted, not ahead of schedule], but it is financed by a rapid, debt-funded capex ramp (long-term debt +$1.8bn in one quarter) [Corrected 2026-10-08: the +$1.8bn is the six-month non-current change (17.99bn to 19.79bn); Q2 alone was +$0.77bn] against structurally negative free cash flow; the multi-gigawatt data-center pipeline is mostly signed-agreement-stage rather than in-service, and the largest incremental opportunity (the Invitium Energy generation JV) is explicitly excluded from current guidance and is a 2029–2032 story, not a near-term one. Full weight is not warranted until the financing plan and at least one more data-center in-service milestone are confirmed.

2. Business in plain English

PPL Corporation owns three regulated, wires-and-pipes utilities: PPL Electric Utilities (Pennsylvania transmission and distribution), Louisville Gas & Electric and Kentucky Utilities (Kentucky regulated electric and gas, including generation), and Rhode Island Energy (electric and gas, acquired 2024). All three earn a regulator-approved return on their asset base; PPL does not sell into a competitive retail market. The current investment story is a wave of data-center and other large-load demand in Pennsylvania and Kentucky that is driving a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar transmission/generation build-out, funded through customer-protected tariffs designed so new large loads — not existing residential/commercial customers — pay for the infrastructure built to serve them.

From b1_live_scores.csv: composite rank 319/~500 (decile 4, i.e. below-average overall on the pre-registered model), with fam_S (earnings momentum / SUE) the standout at 0.756 — the strongest score of the three names in this batch — against weaker fam_Q (0.303) and weak fam_M (0.210, mom_12_1 −5.96%, i.e. the stock has underperformed on a trailing 12-month basis despite the operational acceleration described below). Read together with the primary-source results in Section 4 (accelerating EPS growth, beaten-and-raised-feeling quarter even though guidance was technically "reaffirmed"), the earnings-momentum signal looks durable — it is being driven by real NII/rate-base growth and cost discipline, not a one-off. Prudential sells retirement products (pension risk transfer, annuities), group and individual life insurance in the US, life insurance in Japan and Brazil, and runs PGIM, a $1.49 trillion asset manager (PGIM AUM, 30 Jun 2026). Agent: F14 | As of: 2026-09-25 close (price $287.97) | Classification: Self-Storage REIT

WATCH — thesis horizon 18–36 months. Condition to upgrade: two consecutive quarters of positive same-store NOI growth, AND at least one full reported (not guided) quarter of NSA-inclusive Core FFO per share confirming the deal is accretive as promised. Public Storage has an excellent balance sheet (2.9x net debt/EBITDA, A2/A rated) and just closed a transformative, industry-leading acquisition, but its core same-store business is genuinely shrinking, not merely decelerating, Core FFO per share has been flat-to-down for a year, and the systematic valuation model's inputs are stale on two separate counts (a capex-proxy error and a pre-merger share count) — there is no reliable, current valuation anchor to underwrite a full position today.

2. Business in plain English

Public Storage owns and operates the largest self-storage platform in the U.S. — 3,584 facilities pre-merger (June 2026), now 4,500+ facilities / 327M+ sq ft after closing its acquisition of National Storage Affiliates (NSA) on July 22, 2026 — plus a 35% stake in Shurgard (Europe, 335 facilities) and a pending ~$1.2B acquisition of Public Storage Canada (68 facilities, expected to close Q3 2026) [Corrected 2026-10-08: PS Canada closed on 1 Sep 2026 (8-K accession 0001193125-26-377690)]. It makes money renting small storage units to households and small businesses on flexible month-to-month leases, monetized further through tenant-insurance/reinsurance fees and third-party property management. Competitive position: #1 by scale against Extra Space Storage (EXR) and CubeSmart (CUBE), both of which are also acquisitive; the sector just consolidated further via PSA/NSA.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Gates: the formal Stage-1 intake-gate script was not re-run for this dossier within the time box; no disqualifying findings (auditor change, going-concern language, restatement) surfaced during the manual primary-source review in §11, aside from the routine NSA-merger shareholder litigation noted there. This is durable but double-edged: the quality (high margin, low churn) is real and verified in the same-store data (74–78% NOI margins), but the model's love for PSA is a bet on quality/momentum continuing, not on the stock being statistically cheap — and I find the momentum leg increasingly questionable given the fundamentals in §4.

  3. Q1'26 (Apr 27, 2026): FY2026 guidance reaffirmed unchanged ($16.35–$17.00, mid $16.675) despite a Core FFO beat in the quarter (+2.4% YoY) — management held the line rather than raising, with the NSA deal newly announced (Mar 16, 2026) and pending.
  4. Q2'26 (Jul 29, 2026): guidance raised: Core FFO/share to $16.75–$17.05 (mid $16.90, +$0.225); SS Revenue growth raised to -0.2% midpoint (from -1.1%); SS Expense growth guidance worsened (+0.4pt, to 2.5% midpoint); SS NOI growth raised but still negative (-1.15% midpoint, from -2.2%). Management explicitly attributed only $0.02/share of the raise to "accretion from financing" the NSA/PS Canada deals — i.e., minimal M&A benefit has shown up yet. Even after this raise, the FY2026 Core FFO/share guidance midpoint ($16.90) is barely above FY2025's actual ($16.97) — essentially flat, not the +18%/yr V1 base case.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP vs Core FFO gap: Q2'26 GAAP diluted EPS +44.9% YoY ($2.55 vs $1.76) vs Core FFO/share -2.6% YoY ($4.17 vs $4.28). The GAAP gain is almost entirely a foreign-currency swing on Euro-denominated notes (+$17.2M gain in Q2'26 vs a -$146.1M loss in Q2'25 — a ~$163M swing), which Core FFO correctly excludes. Operating income itself fell -6.7% YoY in Q2'26 ($466.7M vs $500.0M) — the core business got weaker, not stronger, even as headline GAAP EPS surged.
  • Cash-flow quality: 1H26 operating cash flow $1,563.2M, down 0.9% YoY ($1,577.8M in 1H25) despite GAAP net income up 33.7% — same FX-driven divergence. FAD (PSA's AFFO-equivalent, deducting maintenance capex) was $1,389.7M, -1.1% YoY (1H26 vs 1H25) — a cleaner, still-declining cash-flow measure.
  • G&A: Q2'26 G&A +72.5% YoY ($44.4M vs $25.7M), driven by NSA/PS Canada transaction and integration costs, a "corporate transformation" restructuring program ($6.9M of costs YTD, against a $954K opening reserve), and CEO-transition costs (Tom Boyle became CEO April 1, 2026; Ron Havner → Shankh Mitra as Chairman). Core FFO excludes these, so headline Core FFO understates the near-term cash G&A drag.
  • Capex: 1H26 "capital expenditures to maintain real estate facilities" were $86.5M (~3.5% of revenue annualized); including property-enhancement and energy-efficiency capex, ~$269M annualized (~5.5% of revenue) — see §7, a direct conflict with V1's capex assumption.
  • Leverage (own-reported): Net Debt to EBITDA 2.9x; Net Debt-and-Preferred-Equity to EBITDA 4.2x (up from 4.1x YoY); EBITDA-to-Fixed-Charges 6.6x (down from 6.9x). Credit ratings A2/S&P A, unchanged. This is a genuinely strong, investment-grade balance sheet — the clearest bull-case pillar. Preferred stack is large: $4.35B pre-merger, plus new Series T (~$957M) and Series U (~$567M) issued to former NSA preferred holders.
  • Debt maturities: total debt $10.25B, weighted-average rate 3.30%, only 6.3% maturing in 2026 ($650M); no cliff before "thereafter" ($4.93B, mostly 2033+). $3.0B new unsecured revolver (undrawn) + $500M delayed-draw term loan + $1.0B commercial paper program, replacing a smaller $1.5B facility.
  • Recent/pending M&A and its financing — the central fact of this dossier: PSA closed the all-stock acquisition of National Storage Affiliates (NSA) on July 22, 2026 (0.14 PSA shares per NSA share; ~$10.5B enterprise value at announcement). Public Storage issued ~11.2M new common shares, ~9.57M Series T preferred shares, ~5.67M Series U preferred shares, plus ~4.1M OP units and 0.66M Series T-1 preferred OP units. A "Dropdown JV" holding 313 of the acquired properties (~$3.2–3.3B value) was formed with legacy NSA unitholders owning ~80% (PSA 20%); the JV raised ~$2.0B of secured mortgage debt (Goldman Sachs/Wells Fargo, matures Aug 2027) plus a $237M mezzanine loan from a PSA subsidiary. Expected synergies: $110–130M run-rate over 3–4 years; expected full accretion $0.35–0.50/share per share at stabilization — not yet. Separately, PSA has agreed to acquire PS Canada for ~US$1.2B (~$889M in OP units + ~$310M cash; 68 properties, 5.3M sq ft), expected to close Q3 2026 — a sitting PSA board member, Tamara Hughes Gustavson, and her family hold the (non-controlling, "less than 0.1%") equity interest in PS Canada being acquired, a related-party dynamic disclosed in the 10-Q. YTD through Q2'26: $5.9B of debt capital-markets activity and $6.0B of common/OP-unit issuance — an unusually large financing year. Subsequent to Q2'26: $900M of senior notes issued July 20, 2026 (4.855% effective); C$400M (~US$290M) of notes issued Sept 16, 2026 (4.540%, likely partly funding the pending Canada deal). Three shareholder lawsuits were filed against NSA/PSA over the merger seeking injunctive relief and additional disclosures — company states the claims lack merit and supplemented its disclosures; this is routine "disclosure" litigation typical of large stock-for-stock deals, not evidence of fraud, but a real (low-severity) legal/cost overhang.
  • Share count trend: essentially flat pre-merger (175.4M→175.6M shares, Dec'25→Jun'26; small net issuance via LTIP/ATM), then +11.2M (~6.4%) in one step from the NSA close — not yet reflected in trailing per-share metrics or in V1's inputs.

7. Valuation snapshot — reconciliation with V1

V1's verdict: "fair," score 0.242, base 3-yr annualised return +18.2%/yr (bear +7.6%, bull +27.8% — notably, even V1's own bear case is positive, unusual for this framework). V1's method: P/FFO(proxy) 15.8x vs the stock's own history's 9.6th percentile (statistically cheap vs its own past); reverse-DCF implied 10-year growth of +25.3% (vs consensus FY1 +7.3%, delivered 5y CAGR +9.64%) — a very large "achievable minus implied" gap that is the main reason V1's score is only "fair" rather than "attractive" despite the cheap-vs-history read.

I find V1's inputs unreliable on two separate, quantifiable counts, and the true picture is more uncertain than either "fair" or "attractive."

(a) Capex proxy error. Because D3's capex_ttm field was null for PSA, V1 proxied capex with full trailing D&A ($1.164B, 23.8% of revenue). The Q2'26 10-Q cash-flow statement shows actual maintenance-type capex (maintain + enhancements + energy) of ~$269M annualized (~5.5% of revenue) — roughly a quarter of what V1 assumed. Overstated capex understates FCFF, which mechanically inflates the reverse-DCF's implied growth rate (25.3%). A corrected calculation would show materially lower implied growth — quite possibly close to or below the ~7–10% achievable/delivered range — which would flip the "achievable minus implied" score component from strongly negative toward neutral or positive, and push V1's composite score up, not down. In other words, correcting this input alone would likely make V1 say PSA looks more attractive on the reverse-DCF, not less.

(b) Stale, pre-merger share count and financials. V1's inputs (diluted_shares = 176,512,000; market_cap = $50.83B) are the Q2 2026 weighted-average share count for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 — i.e., before the July 22, 2026 NSA close. They do not include the ~11.2M new common shares (nor the new preferred, nor NSA's assets, earnings, or assumed/JV debt). At the reviewed $287.97 price, the corrected market cap (~175.5M pre-merger shares + ~11.2M NSA shares ≈ 186.7M shares, before PS Canada) is roughly 6% higher than V1's figure, before even accounting for NSA's own FFO contribution or integration costs. V1's entire valuation snapshot for PSA is therefore built on a company that, as of the 2026-09-25 cutoff, no longer exists in that form — it was superseded two months earlier by a transformative, already-closed acquisition.

These two errors point in different directions (the capex fix would raise V1's score; the share-count/business staleness makes the whole computation moot until pro forma NSA financials are available), so I cannot simply "correct" V1's number — I can only flag that no reliable, current systematic valuation exists for PSA right now, on top of a same-store business that is independently showing declining revenue and NOI (§4, §6). Peer comparison: V1's peer_median (28.1x) is EXR's NTM GAAP P/E (peer_n=2, i.e. just EXR vs PSA), not a true P/FFO comparison — also flagged as unreliable by V1 itself; I did not have time to independently rebuild true peer P/FFO multiples for EXR/CUBE.

valuation_view_vs_v1: dossier view = fair; consistent = false. I do not simply defer to V1's "fair" label — I arrive at a more cautious place (WATCH, not INCLUDE-SMALL) via a different, evidence-based route: deteriorating same-store fundamentals and integration risk on an unproven, complex mega-merger, layered on top of a valuation model I know to be stale on two independent counts. This is a case where the correct action is to withhold conviction, not to average two wrong numbers into a number that sounds "fair."

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) Best-in-class, investment-grade balance sheet (2.9x net debt/EBITDA, A2/A) gives PSA capital-markets access no self-storage peer can match, evidenced by $5.9B of 2026 debt issuance at reasonable spreads; (2) the NSA deal creates the clear #1 global self-storage platform (4,500+ locations) with a credible, quantified synergy plan ($110-130M) and PS Next operating-margin uplift (PSA's 78% same-store margin vs NSA's historical 70%); (3) PS Canada extends the platform into a new, currently-unconsolidated market at a modest incremental cost.

Bear: (1) The core (same-store) business is shrinking in 2026 — revenue and NOI both negative YoY for two straight quarters, with full-year guidance still pointing to negative same-store NOI even after being raised; realized rent per square foot has now declined for two consecutive quarters; (2) Core FFO per share has fallen for three straight quarters (from $4.31 to $4.17) and FY2026 guidance implies essentially flat per-share cash flow versus FY2025 — not the +18%/yr V1 base case; (3) integration risk is real and unproven: a >$10B all-stock deal, a complex 80/20 "Dropdown JV" with $2.2B of new JV-level debt, routine-but-real shareholder litigation, and a simultaneous second acquisition (PS Canada) and CEO/Chairman transition all landing in the same 12 months.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

The specific, observable, time-bound conditions that would invalidate this thesis:

  1. Same-store NOI growth remains negative for full-year 2026 as reported (confirming the current -1.15%-midpoint guidance rather than a further raise into positive territory).
  2. NSA merger fails to show positive Core FFO accretion in the first full reported quarter of combination (Q3 or Q4 2026 reported Core FFO per share, pro forma for the enlarged share count, below what a standalone-PSA trajectory would have produced).
  3. Net Debt-and-Preferred-Equity to EBITDA rises above 5.0x (from 4.2x now).
  4. Same-store realized annual rent per occupied square foot declines for four consecutive quarters (currently two: Q1'26 and Q2'26).
  5. The pending Public Storage Canada acquisition fails to close, or closes on materially worse terms, by year-end 2026. [Corrected 2026-10-08: moot: the acquisition closed on 1 Sep 2026; replace with leverage after the $500M delayed-draw term loan and $310M cash outlay]

  • My pro forma arithmetic (derived, not guidance): net debt about $77B (Paramount $13.6B net + WBD $29.7B + about $34B new debt for the $80.9B equity price less $46.7B equity, plus fees); pro forma 2026 EBITDA about $11.2B before synergies (about 6.9x net debt/EBITDA) versus the company's "net debt-to-EBITDA of 4.3x on a synergized basis" (8-K 27 Feb 2026, acc 0001104659-26-021911); share count about 5.0B (1.12B + $46.7B / $12.00).

7. Valuation and reverse DCF

V1 row: none for PSKY, so v1_verdict = null. - d4 (25 Sep 2026): price $9.96, market cap $11.1B, EV $27.0B (standalone), NTM P/E about 13x-18x ("caution": FY1 EPS dispersion extreme), Street mean target $9.95 (range $2-$16, 16 analysts), dividend $0.20. d4 FCF of $17.6B is a data error (filings: H1 FCF $354M). - Reverse view (pro forma, because the deal is the investment): market cap on about 5.0B shares = about $49.9B; adding about $77B net debt gives EV about $127B, i.e. 11.3x pre-synergy EBITDA and 7.4x with the full $6B. For a 11% cost of equity and 2.5% growth, $49.9B of equity needs about $4.2B of steady levered FCF; pre-synergy pro forma levered FCF is only about $0.3B (Paramount about $0.4B before transformation costs, WBD about $2.3B, less about $2.4B extra interest on new debt, derived). The gap must come from after-tax synergies of $4.7B (79% of $6B pre-tax): the price needs about 83% of the plan, from the start. Base case here: about 58% of synergies ($3.5B EBITDA) by 2029. - Required (83%) exceeds base (58%): implied_vs_base = above. - 3-year annualised total return, per share, price only (ignores the pending warrant distribution): bear -58.8%, base -0.9%, bull +25.2%. Basis: 2029 EBITDA $11.5B / $14.7B / $18.0B (Paramount 4.0/4.2/4.5 + WBD 6.5/7.0/7.5 + synergies 1.0/3.5/6.0), EV/EBITDA 7x / 8x / 9x, year-3 net debt $77B / $69B / $64B, 5.0B shares.

8. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) the antitrust barrier is gone: States Consent Decree entered 30 Sep 2026 (8-K acc 0001104659-26-112347, post-cutoff) and 65 jurisdictions cleared; (2) streaming scale (Paramount+ revenue +16% in Q2) plus HBO Max in one platform and "$6 billion in synergies" (27 Feb 8-K); (3) the equity buyers pay a $12.00 floor against a $9.96 market price, and existing holders receive warrants (record date 5 Oct 2026, expected issue about 13 Oct 2026). Bear: (1) leverage: about $77B net debt on about $11B EBITDA and falling WBD revenue (-11%); (2) linear TV is shrinking (TV Media revenue -9%, advertising -14%) and a large part of 2026 EBITDA growth is accounting-driven; (3) a media-quality and governance overhang: Ellison/RedBird hold all voting stock, the consent decree imposes 30+ film releases a year, a $1.5B extra US-production spend, a news-independence board and divestiture triggers (Miramax, six cable channels).

9. Key risks and kill criteria

  1. Consolidated net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA above 6.0x at the first post-close quarter end (company target 4.3x synergised).
  2. Consolidated free cash flow (OCF less capex) negative in any two consecutive post-close quarters.
  3. Run-rate realised synergies below $2.0B twelve months after close (target over $6B).
  4. Paramount+ paid subscribers below 80.0M for two consecutive quarters (81.6M at Q2 2026).
  5. TV Media revenue decline worse than -12% y/y for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: -9%).

10. Catalysts and calendar

NYSE listing transfer about 6 Oct 2026; warrant record date 5 Oct 2026 and issue about 13 Oct 2026 (8-K acc 0001104659-26-111034; may be cancelled or postponed); WBD close any time after 30 Sep 2026 order (agreement termination date 4 Mar 2027, extendable to 4 Jun 2027; ticking fee of "$0.00277778 for each day after September 30, 2026"); Q3 results about 9 Nov 2026 (d4: confirmed, not estimate); notes pricing; first post-close guidance.

11. Red-flag scan

Deal cost: $2.8B Netflix termination fee paid; $7.0B "Regulatory Termination Fee" owed to WBD if the deal fails on antitrust grounds (funded by Ellison parties buying shares at $16.02). dossiers.PSX:
PSX - Phillips 66 (NYSE: PSX) - standard-depth diligence (agent F140)

1. Verdict: WATCH. Horizon 12-36 months. The triage "no advance" is confirmed, but for a sharper reason than "cyclical": the stock is priced at roughly my bull case. Q2 2026 earnings of $3.8B came from a refining margin spike (3:2:1 crack spread $41.63 a barrel against $21.65 a year earlier) caused by Middle East supply disruption, and the 25 Sep 2026 price of $255.75 needs free cash flow to stay near $8.5B a year for a decade, against my base of $4.5B once margins normalise. A well-run integrated refiner, midstream and chemicals group, priced for a disruption to last. Condition that would change this: a price near or below about $160 (my base-case DCF value), or evidence that refining margins have structurally reset (for example two more quarters with realized margin above $20 a barrel and a multi-year supply loss).

2. Business in plain English. Phillips 66 turns crude oil into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel at its refineries, moves and processes natural gas liquids (NGLs) through pipelines and fractionators, owns half of Chevron Phillips Chemical (CPChem, plastics), markets fuels and lubricants, and makes renewable diesel. Refining and Marketing earn money from the spread between product and crude prices, which swings enormously; Midstream and Chemicals are the steadier part. The Q2 2026 segment split (pre-tax adjusted, 8-K accession 0001534701-26-000030): Refining $3,086M, Midstream $785M, Marketing and Specialties $514M, Renewable Fuels $544M, Chemicals $404M, Corporate -$407M. Competitive position: scale in the US Central Corridor after buying the other 50% of WRB Refining (Wood River and Borger) on 1 Oct 2025, and an integrated NGL wellhead-to-export chain; no pricing power on refined products.

3. Why the model likes it. b1 composite decile 5 (rank 252). The drivers are not value or quality: family percentiles are quality 0.28, value 0.26, momentum 0.88, earnings surprise 0.61, with a 12-1 month price return of about +87% and an earnings surprise score of 2.26. Durable or artefact? Artefact of a commodity shock. The earnings surprise is the spread spike itself; the momentum is the price response to it. Neither persists if crack spreads mean-revert.

4. Results, last quarters (company releases, Ex. 99.1; GAAP EPS and company-adjusted EPS labelled; I opened five quarterly releases, Q2 2025 to Q2 2026; Q3 and Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 were not opened).

5. Guidance track record. Phillips 66 does not publish numeric earnings, margin or throughput guidance in its earnings releases, so there is no range to compare with a prior range, and I do not infer one. What it does state are targets and budgets: - Q4 2025 release, 4 Feb 2026 (0001534701-26-000003): "Announced 2026 capital budget of $2.4 billion, including $1.1 billion for sustaining capital and $1.3 billion for organic growth capital." Q2 2026 10-Q: capital budget "$2.4 billion" unchanged. - Q2 2026 10-Q (0001534701-26-000032): "We are targeting reductions of total debt to $17 billion and reductions of our debt-to-capital ratio by the end of 2027." Debt was $20.6B at 30 Jun 2026 (consolidated), down from a $27.1B peak at 31 Mar 2026. - Same 10-Q: "Our financial target aims to return greater than 50% of net cash provided by operating activities, excluding working capital, to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends." Q2 2026 return: $887M against $4,317M cash from operations ex-working capital (21%), so the stated 50% target was missed in the quarter while debt was repaid. - Q1 2026 release (0001534701-26-000020): "Increased the annualized quarterly dividend by 7%"; dividend $1.27 a quarter. Board added $10B to the buyback authorization on 29 Jul 2026.

6. Earnings quality and balance sheet (entity: consolidated Phillips 66 at 30 Jun 2026, 10-Q). Consolidated total debt $20,565M (short-term $1,797M, long-term $18,768M); consolidated cash $4,099M; company-defined net debt $16,466M; consolidated total equity $32,703M; debt-to-capital 39%, net debt-to-capital 33%; $6.4B of committed credit capacity, no revolver draw. The debt-reduction path looks strong but part of it is timing: debt rose to $27.1B at 31 Mar 2026 because working capital and a $2.25B 364-day term loan (borrower Phillips 66 Company, a subsidiary, parent-guaranteed; 8-K 0001193125-26-114070, 18 Mar 2026) financed higher crude costs, then reversed. Covenant on that loan and the revolver: maximum consolidated net debt-to-capitalization of 65%. Receivables securitization facility (subsidiary Phillips 66 Company, 8-K 0001193125-26-361266) raised to a $2B committed size and extended to 19 Aug 2027. Share count: about 399.0M outstanding (d4 cross-check). Legal accrual: the Propel Fuels trade-secret case is a consolidated accrued liability of $928M at 30 Jun 2026 ($867M at 31 Dec 2025) against a final judgment of $833M entered 5 Aug 2025 that carries 10% post-judgment interest; appeal opening brief filed 10 Jul 2026 (10-Q, Legal Proceedings note). Earnings quality: GAAP and adjusted earnings were close in Q2 2026 ($9.55 vs $9.41), but Q1 to Q2 swings include "favorable mark-to-market impacts" and inventory/derivative effects that reverse.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1. V1 (v1_valuation_table.csv) classifies PSX "operating", metric NTM P/E 9.94x at the 38th percentile of its own history vs a peer median 9.54x, verdict "excessive" (score -0.43), 3-year annualised returns bear -46.8%, base -20.0%, bull +45.2%, and flag "base 3y value below Street 12m low target". I agree with the direction and verdict, and disagree with the size: a -46.8% bear implies a price near $40, which is below any outcome the filing history supports (trough EPS $2.97 in 2021, $4.99 in 2024). My base is -12.7% a year, so V1 is consistent with the dossier.

Reverse DCF (10% discount rate, 3% terminal growth, consolidated free cash flow; my start point $8.5B = consensus NTM EPS $24.90 (aggregator) x about 400M shares = about $10.0B, less about $1.5B for growth capex net of depreciation; this is my estimate, not a company figure): the $102.0B market cap needs that $8.5B to hold roughly flat for ten years (implied +0.2% a year; -1.7% at a 9% discount rate). Put differently, a steady-state free cash flow of about $6.9B growing 3%. My cases (free cash flow path, PV at 10%): bear $5.5B, $3.8B, $3.5B then +3% (PV $49.5B, CAGR -6.6%); base $6.5B, $5.0B, $4.5B then +3% (PV $63.2B, CAGR -4.2%, equal to about $158 a share and 2029 EPS near $14); bull $8.5B, $8.5B, $8.0B, $7.5B then +3% (PV $101.3B, CAGR +0.5%). The market cap of $102.0B equals the bull PV. Implied is above base: the price demands more than my evidence supports. Peers NTM P/E (d4): MPC 8.3x, VLO 10.2x, PSX 10.3x on consensus that still embeds elevated margins. Street mean target $251.9 (19 analysts; aggregator; low $173).

8. Bull and bear. Bull: (1) Midstream and Chemicals growth and cost actions (Golden Triangle polymers and Ras Laffan start in 2027, Iron Mesa gas plant Q1 2027, record NGL volumes) lift through-cycle earnings; (2) if the Middle East supply loss persists, refining margins stay wide and buybacks ($10B new authorization) retire shares; (3) debt falling toward $17B de-risks the equity. Bear: (1) crack spreads of $41.63 are at an extreme; if they return to the 2025 level ($21.65 in Q2 2025) earnings fall sharply (adjusted EPS was $2.38 in Q2 2025 against $9.41 in Q2 2026); (2) refining earnings in Q1 2026 were only $208M, so the Q2 figure shows how violently the segment swings; (3) insiders sold heavily into the rally (Section 11) and the $928M Propel accrual could rise if the appeal fails.

9. Key risks and kill criteria (for any position or upgrade from WATCH). 1. Realized refining margin below $12 a barrel in two consecutive quarters ($24.08 in Q2 2026, $10.11 in Q1 2026). 2. Consolidated total debt (short-term plus long-term, carrying value) above $22B at any quarter-end before 2027 ($20.565B at 30 Jun 2026), or the $17B target withdrawn. 3. Consolidated net debt-to-capital ratio above 40% at any quarter-end (33% at 30 Jun 2026). 4. Propel Fuels accrual raised above $1.2B or an appellate ruling affirming the $833M judgment (accrual $928M). 5. Return of capital below 35% of operating cash flow excluding working capital for two consecutive quarters, other than when debt reduction targets are still unmet (Q2 2026: 21%).

10. Catalysts. Q3 2026 earnings expected about 28 Oct 2026 (estimate from the 29 Oct 2025 pattern; not confirmed). California Court of Appeal ruling on Propel (no date). Crack-spread path and OPEC/Middle East headlines. Golden Triangle polymers startup (late 2026 to 2027). Western Gateway pipeline progress.

11. Red-flag scan. Auditor Ernst & Young LLP; 10-K critical audit matter: the WRB Refining LP acquisition (accession 0001534701-26-000006). No material weakness seen. Litigation: Propel (above); Dakota Access Pipeline easement decision in May 2026, compliance costs "minimal". Insider Form 4 pattern since 25 Mar 2026 (my parse of open-market sales): EVP Refining 52,100 shares (about $11.7M), EVP 56,700 (about $13.4M), CFO Kevin Mitchell 56,650 (about $10.2M), Controller 7,834 (about $1.7M), and a director's 175-share purchase (about $0.03M). Heavy selling near the peak is a mild negative. No going-concern, restatement or auditor-change language found. Short interest 6.8M shares (about 1.7%, d4).

dossiers.PTC:
PTC Inc. (NASDAQ: PTC) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F98 | As of 2026-09-25 close (px $138.12) | Fiscal year ends Sept 30

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — durable, high-margin PLM/SaaS franchise; the FY26 GAAP "revenue decline" that triggered triage is a divestiture accounting artifact, not organic decay; ARR growth is healthy and guidance was raised twice this year. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: verdict is now WATCH (pending takeover). PTC signed a definitive merger agreement with Schneider Electric on 4 Oct 2026 for $205 per share in cash (8-K Item 1.01, filed 5 Oct 2026); the 12–36 month equity-compounding horizon no longer applies and merger arbitrage is out of mandate.]

2. Business in plain English

PTC sells product-lifecycle-management (PLM), CAD and industrial IoT/AI software — Windchill (PLM), Creo/Onshape (CAD), Codebeamer (ALM) and ServiceMax (field service) — to industrial manufacturers (aerospace, medtech, auto, electronics) who need a single digital record of a product from design through service. Revenue is subscription-based (ARR), high-switching-cost (multi-year implementations embedded in engineering workflows), sold direct and via a growing partner channel (Rockwell, Microsoft).

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 live factor file (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as_of 2026-09-25): Quality percentile 0.74 (gp/assets 0.69, ROE 0.75 — both strong and structural: PTC's margin profile is a function of the SaaS mix shift, not a one-off), but Momentum percentile 0.093 and SUE percentile 0.136 — both weak, and Value percentile is mixed (ep 0.71 high, fcfp 0.81 high, but ebit_ev 0.093 low, reflecting GAAP operating-income compression from the Q2'26 divestiture). Composite decile 5/10 (composite_raw 0.477), live_rank 290 — not a top-quant name; it qualified for diligence on the quality+cheapness combination the triage flagged, not on momentum. Durable: the quality signal is fundamentals-driven (recurring ARR, ~80%+ gross margin business). Data conflict: b1's ebit_ev and momentum scores understate the business because they are computed on GAAP operating income/EPS, which is depressed in FY26 by the Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture (see §4) — this is exactly the kind of GAAP-vs-adjusted distortion the conventions ask us to flag.

dossiers.PYPL:
PYPL — PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: PYPL)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 18–30 month horizon. Reservation: branded-checkout share loss and margin compression are real and ongoing; the position is a bet that a 10x-ish multiple already discounts a turnaround that hasn't yet shown up in the numbers, not a bet that the turnaround is confirmed.

2. Business in plain English

PayPal operates a two-sided digital-payments network — merchants accept PayPal/Venmo/Braintree, consumers pay with them — monetizing via take-rate on payment volume, plus interest income on customer balances and lending. Its moat is network effects (more merchants → more consumers → more merchants) and stored-credential convenience, but that moat is eroding at the point of sale as Apple Pay, card-network click-to-pay, and embedded checkout reduce PayPal's branded-checkout advantage. New CEO Enrique Lores (since 2025) [Corrected 2026-10-06: Lores was appointed on 2-Feb-2026, effective 1-Mar-2026, replacing Alex Chriss (8-K Item 5.02, acc 0001193125-26-035860)] is running a stated "transformation" focused on branded-checkout stabilization, Venmo monetization and Braintree/financial-services diversification. dossiers.Q:
Qnity Electronics, Inc. (NYSE: Q) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F78 | As of: 2026-09-25 close | Depth: Standard

1. Verdict

WATCH, thesis horizon 12–24 months. Reason: a real, evidenced business (revenue +18–22% YoY, Adjusted EBITDA growing faster, guidance raised twice in its first two standalone quarters) sitting at a valuation that requires ~17%/yr free-cash-flow growth for a decade to be justified — well above this analyst's own base case (~12%/yr) for a materials supplier exposed to the historically cyclical semiconductor-capex cycle. Add a brand-new (~10-month) standalone track record, GAAP net income falling in both quarters since the spin-off (on new leverage), and an as-yet-unrated/thinly-covered credit, and the combination argues for full diligence to keep tracking, not for buying at full or half weight yet.

2. Business in plain English

Qnity Electronics is DuPont's former Electronics & Industrial segment, spun off as an independent public company on 1-Nov-2025. It makes the specialty materials semiconductor fabs consume to build chips — photoresists, CMP (chemical-mechanical planarization) slurries and pads, and other process chemistries (Semiconductor Technologies segment) — plus flexible circuit materials, thermal-management and connector/interconnect products used in advanced packaging and electronic assemblies (Interconnect Solutions segment). Its products are "qualified into" a customer's manufacturing process (a multi-quarter approval process), which is the source of its switching-cost moat: once a fab qualifies a given photoresist or slurry chemistry for a process node, changing suppliers requires re-qualifying the whole line. It sells into the same AI/HPC-driven capex upcycle as the semicap-equipment names (AMAT, KLAC, LRCX) the triage also flagged, but as a consumable materials supplier rather than a capital-equipment maker.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor data (25-Sep-2026) flags Q with coverage_flag = insufficient_families_no_composite and blank Momentum/SUE scores — the model could not fully score this name because it has under 12 months of standalone price/return history (spun off 1-Nov-2025), so the "why the model likes it" question is only partly answerable from b1: Quality percentiles are middling (gp/assets pct 21%, ROE pct 17%, ocf/assets pct 15% — all modest, likely depressed by post-spin interest expense — see §6), leverage percentile 44% (moderate). The triage's "advance" call was driven by growth and price-vs-growth judgement (quality 3, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4), not a strong quant composite — this ticker was advanced on a qualitative/growth thesis, not a validated quant signal, which is itself worth flagging: there is essentially no track record to statistically lean on yet.

4. Last two years of results — entity-scope caveat first

Pre-1-Nov-2025 quarters are DuPont's Electronics & Industrial segment / carve-out financial statements, not an independent public company's results; post-spin quarters are Qnity Electronics, Inc. standalone, with a new ~$4.0bn debt capital structure the carve-out periods never carried. This is the single most important comparability fact in this dossier: GAAP net income falls YoY in both standalone quarters even though revenue and segment-level Adjusted EBITDA both grew, because interest expense went from $0 in the carve-out periods to ~$61m/quarter standalone (see §6) — a capital-structure effect, not an operating deterioration. The Company's own earnings releases label the 2025 comparative periods "pro forma" for this reason and this dossier follows that labelling.

Revenue growth is real and accelerating in dollar terms (+17.6% Q1'26, +22.1% Q2'26 vs. pro forma prior year), and both segments grew double digits in Q1'26 and Q2'26. But GAAP net income fell 18.6% (Q1'26) and 31.3% (Q2'26) YoY over the same periods — the widening gap is the new interest expense (see §6), not a revenue or margin problem at the operating level (Adjusted Operating EBITDA grew 22% and 24% YoY respectively, faster than net sales).

Source: Qnity 8-K exhibit 99.1 earnings releases (dates below); SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 2058873).

5. Guidance track record

Only two standalone quarterly releases exist (spin-off was 1-Nov-2025), so only two data points are available; the initial FY2026 guide (likely issued alongside the Feb-2026 FY2025 10-K/earnings release) was not independently pulled within this diligence window — noted as a limitation, not asserted.

Release FY2026 guidance given vs. prior range Actual/next data point
Q1'26 (12-May-26) "Raises full-year guidance": Net Sales $5.225–5.375bn; Adj. Operating EBITDA $1.535–1.625bn; Adj. EPS $3.80–4.14; Adj. FCF $500–600m Raise (vs. an earlier range not independently verified here) Q2'26 results (below) beat the run-rate implied by this guide
Q2'26 (4-Aug-26) "Raises full-year guidance" again: Net Sales $5.55–5.65bn; Adj. Operating EBITDA $1.675–1.725bn; Adj. EPS $4.40–4.60; Adj. FCF $600–700m Verified raise vs. the Q1'26 range above (every line item up) FY2026 not yet complete

Two consecutive, verified guidance raises across every metric in a company's first two quarters as a standalone public company is a genuinely positive, evidenced execution signal — the concern in this dossier is valuation and capital structure, not near-term execution.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • New debt from the spin: long-term debt was $0 at 31-Dec-2024 (as part of DuPont) and $4.0bn at 31-Dec-2025 and since (spin-related notes issued around the Nov-2025 separation). Interest expense (InterestAndDebtExpense) went from $0 in pro forma 2025 quarters to $61m in both Q1'26 and Q2'26 (~$244m annualised — roughly a 6.1% effective rate on the $4.0bn), which is the primary driver of the GAAP EPS decline in §4.
  • Cash: $961m at 30-Jun-2026 (up from $166m at 31-Dec-2024, pre-spin) — a large post-spin cash cushion, partly from the spin-off's own cash allocation and partly from FCF retained since.
  • Net debt/EBITDA: net debt ≈ $3.04bn (30-Jun-2026). Against trailing 4-quarter Adjusted Operating EBITDA (Q3'25 pro forma + Q4'25 349 + Q1'26 411 + Q2'26 431 ≈ $1.5–1.55bn, Q3'25 figure interpolated as it was not independently pulled) ≈ ~2.0x; against the FY2026 guide-midpoint Adjusted EBITDA (~$1.70bn) ≈ ~1.8x. The triage's cited "2.3x" is in the same neighbourhood; the small difference is which EBITDA base (trailing vs. forward guide) is used — flagged as a reconciled, not conflicting, data point. Either way, leverage is moderate for an industrial spin but the credit is new and thinly covered (triage notes only ~8 sell-side analysts), so there is limited external validation of the capital structure's durability through a cycle.
  • Adjusted vs. GAAP gap: Adjusted Earnings were up 33% (Q1'26) and 53% (Q2'26) YoY even as GAAP net income fell 19–31% — a large and widening GAAP/adjusted gap. Management's add-backs (per the releases) are chiefly the pro forma interest-expense/standalone-cost normalisation for the comparative period and items in the current period the Company treats as non-recurring (integration/separation costs, intangible-amortisation from spin-related basis step-up). This dossier has not independently re-derived the full non-GAAP reconciliation table line-by-line within the time budget — flagged as a limitation; the direction (adjusted diverging positively from GAAP) is itself the fact worth monitoring, regardless of which side is "more right."
  • Stockholders' equity fell from $10.64bn (31-Dec-2024, as part of DuPont) to $7.10–7.26bn post-spin — consistent with a leveraged spin-off (debt-funded distribution back to former parent/shareholders is typical in these structures) rather than any operating loss of equity value.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

  • Price 25-Sep-2026: $124.69; market cap ≈ $26.09bn; shares ≈ 209.2m; EV (mkt cap + net debt) ≈ $29.12bn.
  • Forward P/E on FY2026 Adjusted EPS guide midpoint ($4.50): ≈ 27.7x. EV/Adjusted EBITDA on FY2026 guide midpoint (~$1.70bn): ≈ 17.1x — both rich multiples, consistent with the market pricing Qnity like a growth semicap name (comparable to the AMAT/KLAC/LRCX multiples the triage cites) rather than a "specialty materials/chemicals" multiple.
  • No V1 systematic valuation row exists for Q (checked v1_valuation_table.csv — ticker absent, unsurprising given the sub-12-month listing history); v1_verdict = null.
  • Reverse DCF (own build): EV ≈ $29.12bn, FCF0 = FY2026 Adjusted FCF guide midpoint ($650m — a forward guide, not a trailing actual, since standalone history is under a year; this already gives the company credit for expected near-term growth), WACC 9.5% (newly-levered industrial spin, elevated but not extreme risk), terminal growth 3%, 10-year horizon. Implied 10-year FCF CAGR required ≈ 16.8%/yr. This analyst's base case (below) is ~10–12%/yr average over the same horizon (current growth is faster, but a decade of double-digit growth for a company selling into a historically cyclical semiconductor-capex market is a demanding, not a conservative, assumption). Implied growth is above base case → does not qualify for INCLUDE/INCLUDE-SMALL under this program's rule, regardless of how well the business is executing near-term. Dossier view: expensive/full. [Corrected 2026-10-08: method restated: FCF0 $650M is levered (after about $244M interest) and was divided into EV with a 9.5% rate not tied to the 10y UST of 5.17%; on an equity basis (market cap $26.09B, Ke 10-11% = 5.17% + about 5-6% premium for a newly levered cyclical, FCF $600M after about $50M stock compensation) implied 10-year FCF growth is about 18-20%/yr (about 14% on an unlevered EV basis at WACC 9.5%); implied_vs_base stays above, WATCH unchanged]

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: 1. Two consecutive quarters of guidance raised across every metric (sales, EBITDA, EPS, FCF) is a strong, evidenced execution signal for a company only ~10 months old as a standalone reporter. 2. Both segments (Semiconductor Technologies +15.5% and Interconnect Solutions +30.2% YoY in Q2'26) are growing double digits, and the qualified-into-the-process nature of photoresists/slurries/CMP consumables gives genuine switching-cost protection once a fab has adopted a given chemistry. 3. The AI/HPC-driven "shrink and stack" trend management describes (more process layers per chip = more materials intensity per wafer) is a real, structural tailwind specific to advanced packaging, not just a generic semicap-cycle call.

Bear: 1. GAAP net income has fallen YoY in both quarters since the spin (−19%, then −31%), and while this dossier attributes it chiefly to new interest expense, a newly-listed, thinly-covered (~8 analysts), leveraged (~1.8–2.0x net debt/EBITDA) credit with under a year of standalone filings is inherently harder to underwrite with confidence than an established issuer. 2. The valuation (27.7x forward P/E, 17.1x forward EV/EBITDA, and a reverse-DCF-implied ~17%/yr decade-long FCF growth requirement) is priced for the current AI-capex upcycle to persist without the cyclicality that has historically characterised semiconductor capital spending (a risk the triage separately flags for the semicap-equipment names AMAT/KLAC/LRCX/STX/WDC — the same macro driver applies here). 3. Standalone track record is ~10 months; there is no independently-verified evidence yet of how the business performs through a downcycle, a refinancing, or a period without guidance raises.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable signposts that would break this thesis)

  1. Net debt/trailing-4-quarter Adjusted Operating EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~1.8–2.0x currently).
  2. FY2026 guidance (raised twice: Adj. EBITDA to $1.675–1.725bn, Adj. EPS to $4.40–4.60) is cut in a future release — a reversal of the current two-for-two raise streak.
  3. GAAP net income declines YoY for a third consecutive standalone quarter (two consecutive already: Q1'26 −19%, Q2'26 −31%).
  4. Semiconductor Technologies or Interconnect Solutions segment revenue growth decelerates below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from the current 15–30% range) — a proxy for the AI-capex cycle turning.
  5. A major customer publicly cuts capex/capacity guidance materially, given Qnity's short standalone credit history and thin (~8-analyst) sell-side coverage.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026, estimated early-to-mid November 2026 (not officially confirmed as of this dossier) — based on the ~13-week cadence from Q1'26 (12-May) and Q2'26 (4-Aug) reports.
  • Watch: the 10-K for FY2026 (expected ~Feb-2027) for the first full-year standalone report and any credit-rating action on the ~$4.0bn notes.
  • Recent 8-Ks (10-Sep-2026, 21-Aug-2026) not yet reviewed in depth within this diligence window — flagged for the next update.

11. Red-flag scan

  • No auditor change, restatement, or material weakness identified in the reviewed filings (10-Q, 30-Jun-2026).
  • No securities litigation or SEC/DOJ investigation identified in the sources reviewed — but Qnity has under a year of trading history, so the absence of litigation to date carries less evidentiary weight than it would for an established issuer. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 10 Sep 2026 8-K (Item 8.01, acc 0002058873-26-000037) records a PFAS settlement in which Qnity established a $43M indemnification liability (44% share of DuPont's after-tax liability); the 21 Aug 2026 8-K (acc -26-000033) names Ken Rizvi CFO effective 1 Oct 2026 replacing an interim CFO; the 1 Jul 2026 8-K (acc -26-000025) repriced the $2,338M term loan to SOFR+1.75% from +2.00%]
  • The GAAP-vs-adjusted earnings gap (§6) is real and should be re-underwritten line-by-line (not just directionally) before any position sizing.

dossiers.QCOM:
Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) - Fundamental Diligence Dossier (F133, standard depth)

Verdict: WATCH, 12-36 month horizon. The business is strong and its data-centre and car push is real, but at $201.97 (25 Sep 2026 close) the price asks for roughly 14% a year of free-cash-flow growth after charging for stock pay, against about 5% in my base case; the quick triage said the same thing for a thinner reason. What would change it: a price near or below about $165 (about 16x the FY27 consensus of $10.18 non-GAAP EPS), or two quarters showing disclosed data-centre revenue while handset revenue stabilises and TTM free cash flow recovers above $9B.

1. Business in plain English

Qualcomm designs the chips and modems inside most premium Android phones (QCT segment: handsets, automotive, IoT) and licenses its patents to nearly every phone maker (QTL segment, about 70% pre-tax margin). QCT is 86% of quarterly revenue; handsets still gave $5.1B of $8.5B QCT revenue in Q3 FY26. Its biggest customer, Apple, is replacing Qualcomm modems with its own; the 10-Q (0000804328-26-000086) says it expects Apple "will increasingly use its own modem products". Growth is now meant to come from automotive (+61% YoY in Q3), IoT (+9%) and a new data-centre business.

2. Why the model likes it, and whether it lasts

b1 composite 0.614, live_rank 193, family scores Quality 0.89 (GP/A percentile 0.76, ROE 33%), Value 0.78 (earnings-yield percentile 0.76, FCF-yield 0.71), Momentum 0.37 (12-1 month percentile 0.36) and Surprise 0.12 (SUE percentile 0.12; a weak earnings-surprise trend). The quality and value reads rest on TTM figures that are already rolling over: non-GAAP EPS fell 20% YoY in Q3 FY26 and TTM cash flow is down. Triage (Q12) said revenue -4%, forward EPS growth 17%, about 20x NTM. Filings confirm revenue -4% in Q3. The "17% forward growth" is not in the consensus data: d4 shows FY27 EPS 10.18 versus FY26 10.48, i.e. -3%. The 17% looks like a mis-basing; I treat it as a data conflict (see summary).

6. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

d4 (Yahoo, cross-check only): price $201.97; market cap about $215.7B on 1,068M shares; NTM P/E 19.8x; FY26 P/E 19.3x on $10.48 (my sum of three reported quarters, 3.50 + 2.65 + 2.21, plus the $2.15 midpoint of the Q4 range quoted in section 4, = $10.51); FCF yield 4.7%; consensus target mean $194 (range 100-400, 30 analysts), i.e. the price is above the average target. Peers NTM P/E (same source): AVGO 18.9x, MCHP 19.2x, ON 18.5x, NXPI 13.8x, ADI 24.6x, TXN 28.7x; QCOM is priced like high-growth analog and AI peers with negative FY27 EPS growth. V1: no row exists for QCOM, so v1_verdict is null. EV about $222.7B (market cap + consolidated net debt $6.97B); EV/TTM non-GAAP operating income about 15.6x, /GAAP about 21.8x. Own 5-10 year multiple history not computed in this pass. Reverse DCF (10 years, growth held years 1-5 then fading to 3% terminal, cost of equity 9.5%): starting free cash flow of $10.4B (not charging SBC) implies about 7.8% a year; charging SBC ($7.17B) implies about 14.5% a year (11.3% at 8.5%, 17.5% at 10.5%). Base case: non-handset revenue about $24B by FY29 (60% of the $40B target; FY26 about $12-13B), handsets down to about $17B from about $23B, QTL flat at about $5.5B, non-GAAP operating margin about 29%, about 1.0B shares: FY29 non-GAAP EPS about $12.0, a 4.6% CAGR from $10.5, i.e. about 5% free-cash-flow growth. Implied growth is well above base, so implied_vs_base = above. - Bear (FY29 EPS $8.5, 13x, dividends $11.0): about -15.6% a year. Base ($12.0, 17x, $11.6): about +2.2% a year (20x gives +7.6%, 15x gives -1.7%). Bull ($15.5, 20x, $12.0; company targets largely hit): about +16.8% a year. Dividend $3.68 a share (1.9%).

7. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) Automotive revenue $1,588M in Q3 (+61%; "23 Consecutive Quarters of Double-Digit Year-Over-Year Growth") and data centre: on 3 Sep 2026 Qualcomm issued an Amazon affiliate a warrant tied to "up to a maximum amount of $60 billion in payments" of server-chip purchases (8-K 0001104659-26-105718), a named customer commitment. (2) Management says China handset revenue bottomed in Q3 FY26 and pricing actions should lift gross margin. (3) $20B buyback authorisation and a 1.9% dividend. Bear: (1) Handsets, still 60% of QCT, fell 20% in Q3 and Apple roll-off continues; FY27 consensus EPS is below FY26. (2) The Amazon warrant is customer compensation: 25M shares at $161.26 against $201.97 is about $1.0B of intrinsic value (2.3% dilution) before any purchases beyond the 3,750,000 shares vested at issue; economics of the chips are not disclosed. (3) Cash conversion fell, inventory is up 28%, R&D and SG&A are growing 17-27% against falling revenue, and GAAP operating margin fell to 16%.

8. Key risks and kill criteria (for an existing or later position)

  1. Non-GAAP diluted EPS below $2.05 for Q4 FY26 or below $1.80 in any later quarter.
  2. QCT handset revenue falls below $4.5B in any quarter of FY27, or China handset revenue has not returned to sequential growth by Q1 FY27 as the April 2026 release (quoted in section 4) said it would.
  3. TTM free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, consolidated) below $8.0B at any quarter-end.
  4. Consolidated debt (short- plus long-term, carrying value) above $20B, or inventory above $9.5B while revenue is below $10B a quarter.
  5. No disclosed data-centre revenue (reported as its own line) by the FY27 Q2 report (May 2027), or the Amazon warrant vesting above 12,500,000 shares without matching disclosed revenue.

9. Catalysts and calendar

Q4 FY26 results expected 2026-11-04 per d4 (Yahoo; not company-confirmed). The Qualcomm v. Arm trial is scheduled to begin 5 Oct 2026. Initial shipments of the hyperscaler custom silicon were said to be "later this calendar year" (0000804328-26-000060). Apple modem transitions through the fiscal 2027 handset cycle. QTL licence agreements with key OEMs "expiring at varying dates between fiscal 2027 and 2031" (10-K 0000804328-25-000085): renewal risk.

10. Red-flag scan

No auditor change or material weakness found: the Q3 10-Q states disclosure controls effective. Litigation (10-Q 0000804328-26-000086 commitments note): Arm Ltd. v. QUALCOMM (filed 31 Aug 2022; jury on 20 Dec 2024 found Qualcomm did not breach the Nuvia licence; final judgment for Qualcomm 30 Sep 2025; Arm appealed to the Third Circuit on 1 Oct 2025), Qualcomm's own suit against Arm (trial scheduled to begin 5 Oct 2026) and ParkerVision (Federal Circuit hearing held 1 Jun 2026). No accrual for contingent losses at 28 Jun 2026; the 10-Q says losses are "reasonably possible, are not probable". Customer concentration: two customers were 23% and 20% of Q3 revenue. Insider pattern (Form 4, 1 Mar to 25 Sep 2026, 38 filings): sales about $12.1M, no purchases; the CEO sold 10,000 shares at $195 on 2026-09-23 and 10,000 at $200 on 2026-09-25. Plan status (10b5-1) was not checked. Form 144 notices Sep 2026 (0001628280-26-063526, 0001628280-26-062919). The stock rose 37% from $147.61 on 31 Jul to $201.97 on 25 Sep, so the price has moved far more than the fundamentals since the last print.

dossiers.RCL:
RCL — Royal Caribbean Group (Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.)

Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-28) and the Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex-99.1, filed 2026-07-28). Checked SEC EDGAR (10-K/10-Q/8-K index) for events to 2026-09-25: found and incorporated the 2026-09-23 8-K announcing the Sandals/Beaches Resorts joint venture (Q3 2026 results are not yet released; next release 2026-10-27).

Basis: GAAP figures are consolidated, USD, as filed with the SEC (CIK 0000884887). "Adjusted EPS," "Adjusted Net Income," "Adjusted EBITDA" and "Net Yields" are the company's own non-GAAP definitions, labeled every time they appear, and are never blended with GAAP figures in the tables below.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 12–36 months. One-sentence reason: an industry-leading cruise operator executing a genuine beat-and-raise cycle on primary-source numbers, but the reverse DCF shows the price already embeds roughly as much sustained growth as a fair base case can justify, and the newly announced, fully debt-financed ~$3bn Sandals/Beaches resorts joint venture (2026-09-23, unaudited/pending, closing early 2027) adds leverage and diversification risk on top of an already elevated balance sheet from the newbuild cycle — the specific reservation for the half-weight sizing. [Corrected 2026-10-08: verdict restated to WATCH after the reverse DCF was rebuilt on free cash flow instead of net income; see the correction section at the end and F21_summary.json]

2. Business in plain English

Royal Caribbean Group operates 71 cruise ships under three wholly owned brands — Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea — plus a 50% joint-venture stake in TUI Cruises (Mein Schiff/Hapag-Lloyd brands), sailing to more than 1,000 destinations. It sells vacation packages (transportation, lodging, food, entertainment) directly and through travel agents to mostly North American and European consumers, monetized through ticket price ("Net Yield") plus onboard/pre-cruise spend. Its competitive edge is the newest, largest-capacity ships in the industry (the Icon-class, e.g. Icon of the Seas, Star of the Seas, Legend of the Seas) combined with owned private destinations (Perfect Day, Royal Beach Club), which let it charge premium prices and fill ships above nominal capacity (110% load factor in Q2 2026). It is now diversifying beyond cruise: entering river cruising in 2027 (Celebrity River Cruises) and, per the 2026-09-23 announcement, acquiring a 50% stake in Sandals and Beaches Resorts (Caribbean all-inclusive land resorts).

3. Why the model likes it — and whether that's durable

Quant context (b1_live_scores.csv, as of 2026-09-25): composite rank 460/~1,172 (decile 7, quintile 4 — mid-pack overall), but strong on individual families: momentum (12-1m) 78th percentile, SUE (earnings surprise) 61st percentile, EBIT/EV 34th, gross-profit/assets 26th, ROE 65th. Value-family scores (E/P −16%, B/P −58% raw) are actually negative/weak in the raw quant panel — the model does not flag RCL as statistically cheap on book-value or plain earnings yield; the "cheap" read in the triage (12.4x NTM P/E) is a forward-multiple observation, not a systematic value-factor signal, and the two should not be conflated. Durable: four consecutive quarters of Adjusted-EPS guidance raises or beats built on real booked-position strength and record demand (see §5). Less durable / worth discounting: the ROE percentile and asset-growth score partly reflect the still-recovering post-COVID capital base (equity of only $10.2bn against $44.6bn of assets) rather than a structurally higher return on capital; leverage remains a real constraint (see §6).

4. Last two years of results (GAAP, USD millions except per-share; "Adj." = company's non-GAAP Adjusted EPS)

Revenue growth decelerated from double digits (Q1/Q4 2025/26, boosted by capacity growth and itinerary mix) to +6.5% in Q2 2026 — still healthy, and management's own capacity-growth glide path (below) explains most of the deceleration; it is not, on the primary-source evidence, a demand problem. GAAP and Adjusted EPS have converged to within a few cents every quarter for the last five quarters — an unusually clean GAAP/non-GAAP reconciliation for the sector (the FY2025 adjustment was mostly routine debt-extinguishment/FX items, not large one-offs).

5. Guidance track record (last four releases, FY Adjusted EPS)

Release (date) Guide given vs. prior guide

Q1 2026 (2026-04-30) FY2026 cut to $17.10–$17.50, driven by a disclosed $0.62/share fuel-cost increase and softer Mediterranean/West-Coast-Mexico bookings from "prolonged geopolitical activity" Cut from the January initial guide
Q2 2026 (2026-07-28) FY2026 raised to $17.73–$17.87, "better than expected...driven by strong close-in demand, lower costs" Raised from the April guide, and back above the January initial midpoint

This is a genuine cut-then-raise pattern with an identified, disclosed cause (geopolitical/demand softness in specific itineraries, then recovery) — not a smoothed "always raised" narrative. It is real evidence that demand is not fully insulated from geopolitical shocks, a fact the bull case should not paper over (see kill criteria).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion is currently negative — a genuine adverse fact, not a quality-of-earnings gimmick: TTM (Q3'25–Q2'26) operating cash flow $6,786m less capex $7,202m = –$416m FCF, driven by the Icon-class newbuild programme (FY2026 capex guided ~$4.7bn, of which $1.6bn is "non-newbuild"; Legend of the Seas delivered Q2 2026, Icon VI/VII ordered with committed financing in April 2026). This is a temporary, disclosed capital cycle, not an operating problem — TTM GAAP net income of $4.4bn and Adjusted EBITDA of ~$6.9bn (TTM op income $5.1bn + TTM D&A $1.8bn) are both healthy and growing — but it means the stock cannot currently be judged on an FCF-yield basis; we use TTM (GAAP/Adjusted) net income as the reverse-DCF base instead (§7), labeled accordingly.
  • Leverage: total debt incl. current maturities $23,407m, cash $875m → net debt $22,532m; net debt/EBITDA (TTM) ≈ 3.26x — elevated for the sector, moving in the right direction only slowly given continued heavy capex. Debt maturities per the Q2 2026 release: 2026 $0.9bn, 2027 $2.7bn, 2028 $3.4bn, 2029 $1.2bn, 2030 $1.3bn. Liquidity $6.9bn (cash + undrawn $6.6bn revolver, increased by $250m in July 2026).
  • Capital return: $199m of buybacks + $404m dividends in Q2 2026 alone (>$600m/quarter); $805m remaining under the current repurchase authorization; share count down from 274m (FY2025 average) to 268m (Q2 2026).
  • Pending M&A — the key new fact (2026-09-23 8-K, checked to cutoff): Royal Caribbean Group will acquire a 50% equity interest in Sandals and Beaches Resorts (Caribbean all-inclusive land resorts) for approximately $3.0bn at ~10x forward EBITDA, funded entirely by committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley — no equity issuance disclosed. Expected to close early 2027, "accretive to earnings next year." This is unaudited, self-reported deal economics (no independent fairness opinion or financing terms disclosed yet) and will push net debt/EBITDA higher just as the newbuild capex cycle is supposed to ease — the single biggest incremental balance-sheet risk in this dossier.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

NTM P/E ~12.4x (triage_cards.csv), FCF yield not meaningful this year (§6). No V1 systematic valuation row exists for RCL in v1_valuation_table.csv — v1_verdict is null; this section is this dossier's own reverse DCF. Method: two-stage DCF (10-year explicit growth + 3% terminal growth), owner-earnings base = TTM Adjusted Net Income (~$4.38bn = $16.36 TTM adjusted EPS × 268m diluted shares) substituted for FCF because FCF is temporarily negative from the newbuild cycle (§6) — a deliberate, disclosed methodology choice, not a mix of GAAP and adjusted figures (the FCF proxy itself is the adjusted metric throughout). Cost of capital: CAPM cost of equity = 5.17% (10yr UST) + 1.75 (sourced beta, FMP profile) × 4.14% ERP = 12.4%; after-tax cost of debt 4.74% (6% pretax, 21.9% tax rate); weights from EV (25.7% debt / 74.3% equity) → WACC ≈ 10.4%.

Implied 10-year owner-earnings growth at the 2026-09-25 close ($242.70): ≈ 8.0% (sensitivity: 6.1% at WACC 9.5%, to 10.1% at WACC 11.5% — the estimate is meaningfully WACC-sensitive since beta is sourced but the debt/equity mix will move once the Sandals deal closes).

My base case: ~7%/yr — supported by guided capacity growth (2026 +6.6%, 2027 +4%, 2028 +6%, 2029 +7%, averaging ~5.9%), continued modest net-yield/pricing growth, and buyback-driven per-share accretion (~3–4%/yr at the current repurchase pace), partially offset by rising interest expense once the Sandals debt is drawn and a deceleration in fleet growth versus the 2024–2027 "Perfecta" push. This is roughly in line with, not comfortably below, the ~8% implied at the central WACC estimate — hence "in_line," not "below," and the INCLUDE-SMALL (not full INCLUDE) sizing. [Corrected 2026-10-08: method error - net income was used as the cash flow and divided into enterprise value at a WACC; on a free-cash-flow basis (equity value $65.0B, Ke 12.4% = 5.17% + 1.75 x 4.14%, FY26E free cash flow about $2.5-3.0B) implied 10-year growth is about 13-15.5%/yr, well above the 7% base: implied_vs_base = above, not in_line, so the program rule disqualifies INCLUDE-SMALL]

Bear/base/bull (3-year annualized total return, including reinvested dividends/buyback yield in the scenario, WACC/terminal assumptions held constant): - Bear (g = −2%: demand shock, e.g. a recession or a broader geopolitical disruption than Q1 2026's, combined with no capex relief): −28%/yr - Base (g = 7%): +9%/yr - Bull (g = 12%: Perfecta-style double-digit compounding sustained, Sandals JV accretive as promised, buybacks accelerate): +33%/yr [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated on the free-cash-flow basis (FCF0 about $2.75B, Ke 12.4%, 3-year annualised including distributed cash flow): bear about -23%/yr, base about -5%/yr, bull about +6%/yr; sensitivity: at Ke 11% about -20% / -1% / +12%]

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: 1. Booked position and pricing power are real and current, not backward-looking: record forward bookings, 110% load factor, Net Yields still guided up in FY2026 despite the Q1 disruption. 2. Newest, most differentiated fleet in the industry (Icon-class) supports a structural pricing premium over Carnival/NCLH that shows up directly in the 33%+ operating margins in seasonally strong quarters. 3. Aggressive, sustained capital return (>$2bn/yr net of newbuild capex once the current ship-delivery peak passes) directly compounds per-share value.

Bear: 1. Net debt/EBITDA (~3.3x) is already elevated by cruise-industry standards and about to rise further from a $3bn, fully debt-financed acquisition into an adjacent business (land resorts) where RCL has no operating track record. 2. FCF has been negative for four straight quarters; if newbuild capex does not taper as guided (2027 capacity growth of "only" 4% implies a pause, but Icon VI/VII orders show the pipeline is not closed), leverage could stay elevated for longer than the base case assumes. 3. Demand is not immune to shocks: the company itself cut FY2026 guidance in April 2026 citing "prolonged geopolitical activity" affecting Mediterranean and West-Coast-Mexico itineraries — a real, disclosed, quantified (−$0.60/share-ish combined with fuel) demand/cost event within the trailing four quarters. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the April cut (midpoint 17.90 to 17.30, -$0.60) equals the $0.62 per share fuel increase, so the release attributes no net guidance reduction to demand; the geopolitical softness is real but was offset elsewhere and is not a quantified -$0.60 demand event]

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Net debt/EBITDA exceeds 4.0x at any quarter-end after the Sandals deal closes (vs. ~3.26x now).
  2. FCF (OCF − capex) remains negative for two consecutive fiscal years (i.e., still negative at FY2027 year-end) — would indicate the newbuild cycle is not tapering as guided.
  3. FY Adjusted EPS guidance is cut in two consecutive quarterly releases (it has been cut once, in Q1 2026, and then raised back — a second consecutive cut would signal a demand trend, not a one-off).
  4. Net Yield growth (as-reported) turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
  5. The Sandals/Beaches JV fails to close as expected in early 2027, or closes with materially different financing terms (e.g., higher-than-disclosed interest cost) than announced 2026-09-23.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, 2026-10-27 (confirmed via company investor-relations announcement).
  • Sandals/Beaches JV expected to close "early 2027" — a real near-term catalyst/risk event to monitor for financing-cost disclosure.
  • Icon VI and Icon VII delivery dates (ordered April 2026, committed financing in place) not yet disclosed in the sources reviewed.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, material weakness, restatement, or going-concern language found in the FY2025 10-K or Q2 2026 10-Q sections reviewed. No SEC/DOJ investigation disclosed in the filings checked. The 2026-09-23 Sandals/Beaches transaction is the one item that changes the risk profile materially and was not yet reflected in any quant score or prior triage (it postdates the Q2 2026 10-Q). Insider Form 4 pattern was not exhaustively reviewed this pass (time-boxed per the addendum's priority order) — no unusual pattern was surfaced in the sources checked; this is a disclosed limitation, not a clean bill of health.

dossiers.RDDT:
RDDT — Reddit, Inc. — F20 diligence dossier

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months. Statistically one of the cheapest names in the wave-1 batch on a trailing free-cash-flow basis for its growth rate, but the reservation is specific and real: Reddit's revenue quality depends on a Google relationship (referral traffic and a $60m/yr AI data-licensing deal) that is unresolved, litigated, and could move against Reddit in either direction (Google could reduce referral traffic via AI Overviews, or Reddit could itself walk away from the licensing renewal). Combined with only ~2.5 years of public reporting history and a recent cluster of large insider sales, size the position for that uncertainty rather than at full conviction.

2. Business in plain English

Reddit is a network of topic communities ("subreddits") where users post and discuss content; it monetizes primarily through advertising (feed and search ads, increasingly self-serve/automated via "Reddit Max") and a smaller, faster-growing "Other revenue" line from licensing its user-generated content and search data to AI companies (Google, OpenAI). Its moat is a 20-year archive of authentic human discussion that is scarce and valuable as AI-training/grounding data, plus a large, logged-in-adjacent audience (130.3m daily actives, +18% YoY) that advertisers are only now starting to buy at scale. Competitive position: a distinct, defensible niche (community + search-indexed long-tail content) rather than a direct Meta/TikTok feed competitor.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

This name reached full diligence through the quality-growth-lane / triage route, not the top-70 quant gate. The growth is real and getting more durable each quarter (8 straight quarters of accelerating-then-decelerating-but-still-60%+ revenue growth, GAAP operating profitability achieved in Q4-2024 and expanding every quarter since), not a one-off — but the "Other revenue" (AI licensing) piece the market is most excited about is growing slower (+24% per Q2-26 call commentary) than the core ad business, which is the opposite of the popular narrative.

8. Bull case

  1. Ad-tooling ramp (Reddit Max, automated bidding) is early; Active Advertisers +70% YoY and Max revenue +150% sequentially in Q2-26 suggest a long runway of monetization-per-user catch-up versus Meta/Google/Pinterest.
  2. Reddit's decade-plus corpus of authentic human discussion is a scarce, differentiated training/grounding asset for AI systems seeking non-synthetic data — multiple licensing counterparties beyond Google (reportedly OpenAI) diversify this revenue stream over time.
  3. Near-zero capex intensity (TTM capex 0.3% of revenue) means incremental revenue drops through to FCF at a very high rate — operating leverage is structurally favorable versus most social-media peers who must fund large infrastructure.

  1. Reddit's own June-2025 securities class action (N.D.   3. CEO Steve Huffman (~$3.56m) and COO Jennifer Wong (~$7.75m) both sold stock on the same day (15-Jul-2026), shortly before the Google-deal uncertainty hit the stock; combined with a public-trading history too short (2.5 years) to have been tested through a full economic cycle, this argues for a smaller position size regardless of the valuation cushion.

  1. Core advertising revenue growth (ex "Other"/data-licensing) falls below 25% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Daily active users (DAU) growth falls below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
  3. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracts YoY (not just sequentially) for two consecutive quarters.
  4. The Google AI-training/data-licensing relationship terminates (non-renewal or Reddit-initiated cutoff) without a replacement licensing deal of comparable (~$60m+/yr) size within two quarters.
  5. The N.D. Cal. securities class action results in a certified class and/or a settlement or judgment exceeding $150m.
