REG — Regency Centers Corporation (F104, wave 6)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — a high-quality, grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT with low tenant-bankruptcy exposure, raised same-property NOI and Core FFO guidance mid-year, and a reverse DCF that implies below-base-case growth. Reservation: pro rata net debt/EBITDAre (~5.0x) is a REIT-appropriate but non-trivial leverage level, and the FFO-based reverse DCF here is a lower-confidence proxy than a NAREIT-FFO-native model would be. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Regency Centers owns and operates ~470 grocery-anchored shopping centers across the US, leasing space to supermarkets (anchors) and smaller "shop" tenants (restaurants, services, specialty retail) around them. It makes money from long-term percentage/base rent leases, redevelopment of its existing centers, and selective ground-up development, benefiting from the resilience of grocery-anchored traffic versus enclosed malls or big-box-only centers, and from limited new supply of well-located shopping centers.

dossiers.REGN:
REGN — Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (F47, wave-2 diligence)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), thesis horizon 24–36 months. Reason: a diversified, still fast-growing biopharma (Dupixent +38% YoY, oncology scaling) priced by the market for very modest 10-year growth (reverse-DCF implied ~2.5–5%/yr) — but the reservation is real and named: Dupixent, ~40%+ of revenue, loses US composition-of-matter exclusivity around 2031, and the market has already been shown (Eylea) that Regeneron's biosimilar/patent moats erode faster than guided.

2. Business in plain English

Regeneron discovers, develops and sells biologic drugs. Its two big commercial franchises are Dupixent (an anti-inflammatory antibody for eczema, asthma, COPD and other allergic/inflammatory diseases, co-marketed 50/50 with Sanofi) and the Eylea/Eylea HD franchise (anti-VEGF injections for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease). A smaller but growing oncology business (Libtayo, Lynozyfic/linvoseltamab) and an early-to-mid-stage pipeline (Factor XI anticoagulants, an obesity GIP/GLP-1 agonist, itepekimab for COPD) round out the portfolio. Revenue comes from US product sales (Eylea family, Libtayo) plus Sanofi collaboration revenue/profit share on Dupixent and other partnered assets.

3. Why the model liked it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q06, quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5) flagged: "even with Eylea's steep biosimilar-driven decline, aggregate revenue is still growing +17% and forward EPS +51%... 15.3x NTM P/E looks cheap, and the Eylea risk is already visible and quantifiable." b1 quant: composite 0.407 (decile 5, live_rank 295 — mid-pack, not a top-decile name), fam_S (earnings momentum) only 0.188 — the SUE signal is actually weak/negative despite the headline growth, because GAAP EPS has been volatile (see §6). fam_V (value) 0.696 is the strongest family. Durability check: the Dupixent growth is durable near-term (broad label, multiple ongoing launches — COPD, bullous pemphigoid, chronic spontaneous urticaria) but is not indefinite; it is a patent-protected franchise with a known 2031ish LOE, not a structural moat like a network effect. The Eylea decline is a real, already-in-progress biosimilar erosion, not a one-off. Both are correctly treated as durable-but-time-limited, which is why the reverse DCF (§7) matters more than the current EPS growth rate.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP, USD millions except EPS; SEC 10-Q/10-K, XBRL companyfacts)

5. Guidance track record (quote the numbers; versus prior range)

Regeneron does not guide revenue directly (typical for a company whose two largest lines move on payer/biosimilar dynamics it does not fully control). It does guide GAAP/non-GAAP R&D, SG&A, gross margin and capex. Per the Q2 2026 release (2026-07-30, source: SEC 8-K Ex-99.1 sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872589/000087258926000023/exhibit991q22026.htm): - Non-GAAP R&D: $5.95B–$6.05B, raised/narrowed from the prior $5.90B–$6.10B (midpoint essentially unchanged, range tightened upward). - Non-GAAP SG&A: $2.50B–$2.60B, narrowed from $2.50B–$2.65B (top end cut — modest positive). - Non-GAAP gross margin: 84%–85%, raised from 83%–84%. - Capex: $985M–$1.10B (full-year). These are specific, quantified, and falsifiable — good practice — but they confirm the Eylea erosion is ongoing and guided to continue, not a one-off already fully absorbed.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • GAAP vs non-GAAP gap: ~15–20% most quarters, driven by equity-securities mark-to-market and acquired-intangible items, not core operations. [Corrected 2026-10-08: see the correction in section 4: stock-based compensation, a manufacturing interruption charge and intangible amortization drive the gap; securities gains are excluded from non-GAAP] Analysts and the company both use non-GAAP; this dossier uses GAAP as primary and flags the gap each time, per program convention.
  • Cash conversion: TTM operating cash flow (Q3'25+Q4'25+Q1'26+Q2'26) ≈ $4.68B; guided FY26 capex ≈ $1.0–1.1B → TTM FCF ≈ $3.6B, FCF/GAAP-NI TTM (NI ≈ $4.33B) ≈ 84% — reasonable conversion, not a red flag.   • Balance sheet (2026-06-30, 10-Q): total assets $41.73B, total liabilities $10.02B, stockholders' equity $31.71B — essentially unlevered; long-term debt only $1.99B (a single legacy note), cash & equivalents $2.46B plus a much larger marketable-securities/strategic-equity portfolio (not fully broken out here). Net debt is negative (net cash) even before counting the securities portfolio. [Corrected 2026-10-08: the balance sheet at 30 Jun 2026 shows cash and marketable securities of $17,822.9M against long-term debt of $1,986.6M, i.e. net cash of about $15.8B (about 19% of market cap); the securities are not an unquantified extra]
  • SBC: ~$257M in Q1 2026 alone (≈7% of that quarter's revenue) — normal for large-cap biotech, rising in dollar terms with headcount (15,410 FTEs) but not flagged as excessive.
  • Capital return: REGN pays a small dividend, initiated 2023 ($3.76/share annualized, ~0.46% yield per 2026-09-25 close) and buys back stock opportunistically; no announced debt-funded M&A pending.
  • M&A: none material pending as of this writing; REGN has historically been an organic-pipeline company plus small bolt-ons/licensing (e.g., partnered obesity asset via Hansoh Pharma licensing, per public deal history) rather than a serial acquirer.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

V1 systematic valuation table (v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv) and v1_valuation.json have no REGN row — REGN was not in the 69-name V1 universe, so v1_verdict = null and there is nothing to reconcile; this dossier's valuation view stands on its own.

  • Price 2026-09-25 close: $788.04; market cap $81.13B; shares out 101.1M.
  • Trailing GAAP P/E ≈ 18.7x (TTM GAAP NI $4.33B); NTM P/E per the quant snapshot (d4) = 15.29x, but flagged by the pipeline itself as unreliable (ntm_quality: unreliable, flag fy1_thin_coverage — thin, split analyst coverage on FY1 vs FY0 makes the NTM number noisy; treat as directional only, a genuine data-conflict worth disclosing).
  • FCF yield ≈ 4.5% (TTM FCF ~$3.6B / mkt cap).
  • Reverse DCF (own build, scripts/valuation.py-style two-stage FCFF, since no formal V1 output exists): assuming an 8% discount rate (large, low-leverage, moderate-beta biopharma; note the Yahoo-sourced beta field of 0.19 looks anomalously low and was not relied on) and a 2.5% terminal growth rate after year 10, the $81.1B market cap implies roughly 2.6%/yr (NI-based) to 4.8%/yr (FCF-based) sustained 10-year growth before terminal value. My evidence-based base case — Dupixent decelerating from 30%+ to high-single-digit growth as it matures and faces its own LOE around 2031, Eylea/Eylea HD roughly flat-to-low-single-digit once the biosimilar transition completes (guided to keep hurting through 2026), oncology and the emerging pipeline (Factor XI, obesity, itepekimab) adding a few points — is ~6–8%/yr over 10 years, i.e. implied growth is below my base case. Bear case (Dupixent LOE bites early, pipeline reads out negatively, ~2–3%/yr) still roughly matches the market's implied growth — so downside is limited more by the balance sheet (net cash, no leverage) than by a further valuation re-rating. valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below." [Corrected 2026-10-08: restated to in_line (borderline): with FCF charged for stock compensation ($2.77B TTM) the same 8% model implies about 8.3% (equity basis) to 9.2% (EV basis excluding interest income) against the 6-8% base; INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) retained]
  • Peers (directional only, not independently re-pulled this pass): VRTX, BIIB, GILD, AMGN — large diversified biopharmas historically trading high-teens to low-20s P/E on core EPS; REGN's mid-to-high-teens GAAP multiple (and mid-teens non-GAAP) sits at a discount to that peer set, consistent with the market pricing in the Eylea/Dupixent LOE overhangs rather than REGN being mispriced cheap by accident.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Dupixent is still growing 38% YoY with multiple recent-launch indications (COPD, CSU, bullous pemphigoid) not yet mature — the deceleration priced into the reverse DCF may be too pessimistic for 3–5 more years. 2. Eylea HD (52% YoY growth, now outselling legacy Eylea on physician demand) is converting the franchise onto a longer-duration, harder-to-biosimilar product faster than the market gives credit for. 3. Optionality from Factor XI (Phase 3 starting H2 2026), the GIP/GLP-1 obesity asset (global Phase 3 starting H2 2026, positive China Phase 3 already reported), and a maturing oncology franchise (Libtayo +29%, Lynozyfic newly launched) is not in most reverse-DCF base cases.

Bear (3): 1. Dupixent, now the large majority of revenue and profit, carries US patent exclusivity that ends around 2031 — a single-product concentration risk on the scale of the Eylea situation the market has just watched play out. 2. Legacy Eylea US sales are down ~45% YoY and guided to keep falling "low-to-mid-teens" sequentially each quarter through 2026 — a real, ongoing, quantified headwind, not a completed one-off. 3. GAAP earnings are volatile and partly driven by mark-to-market swings on equity holdings unrelated to the operating business, making headline "EPS growth" numbers (the 51% figure the triage cited) less trustworthy than they look without the GAAP/non-GAAP split shown in §4.

9. Key risks & kill criteria — thesis-invalidation triggers (measurable, would break the thesis; verbatim into summary JSON)

  1. "Legacy Eylea US net sales decline exceeds 50% YoY in any quarter through 2027" (currently ~45% YoY and guided to keep worsening — this is the escalation trigger, not the current level).
  2. "Dupixent global net sales growth falls below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters" (current 38% YoY; a sharp deceleration earlier than the modelled LOE-driven slowdown would be a thesis break).
  3. "Any Phase 3 readout failure or negative FDA action on the Factor XI anticoagulant program or the GIP/GLP-1 obesity asset" (both are the main sources of bull-case optionality; AERIFY-2 already missed its primary endpoint for itepekimab in COPD, a partial precedent).
  4. "GAAP-to-non-GAAP EPS gap exceeds 25% for two consecutive quarters without a disclosed one-time driver" (currently ~15-20%; a widening, undisclosed gap would be an earnings-quality red flag).
  5. "Net debt turns materially positive (>$3B) to fund an acquisition without a clearly accretive, disclosed rationale."

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: 2026-10-30 (Q3 2026, per Yahoo calendar in the quant snapshot; not yet an SEC-confirmed date at time of writing — treat as an estimate).
  • H2 2026: Phase 3 initiations for the Factor XI antibodies (cenvacibart, amrecibart) and the global GIP/GLP-1 obesity programme.
  • Ongoing: continued Eylea HD conversion data each quarter; further biosimilar-launch calendar events already settled with Sandoz, Alvotech/Teva, Biocon, Celltrion (staggered through end-2026) and the still-litigated Amgen matter (Amgen already launched, having won its case).

11. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation: the Eylea/aflibercept biosimilar patent litigation (BPCIA, multidistrict in N.D. dossiers.RF:
RF — Regions Financial Corporation (NYSE: RF)

1. Verdict

WATCH — 12–24 month horizon. Reason: genuinely best-in-class regional-bank execution (deposit costs, efficiency, credit quality), but V1's systematic model independently flags the stock as "demanding" with a modest +4.5%/yr base-case 3-year return, and this dossier's own reverse-DCF agrees the price already assumes RF sustains above-its-own-history ROE — not enough margin of safety to hold at full weight today. Condition that would move this to INCLUDE: a pullback to book value multiple implying ROE closer to the 20th–50th percentile of RF's own 15-year history (i.e., a cheaper entry) without a change in the credit-quality/efficiency story.

2. Business in plain English

Regions Financial is a Birmingham, AL-based regional bank (~$155bn assets range) operating primarily across the Southeast/Midwest US, making money on the spread between what it pays for deposits and earns on loans (net interest income), plus fee income from wealth management, mortgage and capital markets. Its competitive edge versus peer regionals is cost discipline: it runs a top-quartile efficiency ratio and among the lowest interest-bearing deposit costs in its peer group, funding balance-sheet growth internally rather than through the scale M&A its peers have pursued. (Source: 8-K EX-99.1, filed 2026-07-17, accession 0001281761-26-000032/...050.)

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable? Where it conflicts with filings

b1_live_scores.csv shows RF at composite decile/quintile near the top (decile likely top-of-range given quintile=1 in the row), high pct_roe (0.65) and pct_bp — a "quality" name. Triage's own reason flags the tension directly: "Growth is the slowest of the regional-bank group (+3% revenue) since it hasn't done the scale M&A its peers have, but underwriting/expense discipline is genuinely best-in-class; model flags valuation as 'demanding.'" Filings confirm this is not an artefact: Q2'26 adjusted total revenue grew only 2% YoY, but adjusted ROATCE was 20.18% and CET1 10.7% — the quality is real, but it is priced for.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF — reconciled with V1

  • Price used: $27.62 (2026-09-25 close, matches v1_valuation.json inputs.price_2026_09_25).
  • V1's own valuation (outputs/v1_valuation.json, outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv), read before writing this section: method = "justified P/B = (ROE−g)/(COE−g)"; P/B now 1.256x (84th percentile of RF's own 15-year history); cost of equity (COE) 9.43%; implied ROE 11.08%, vs. delivered TTM ROE 11.85% and RF's own historical 20th/50th/80th-percentile ROE of 6.30% / 8.67% / 11.85%. V1 verdict: "demanding" (verdict_score −0.33). V1 3-year annualized scenario returns: bear −7.65%, base +4.46%, bull +15.60%.
  • Do I agree? Partially. V1's implied ROE (11.08%) sits almost exactly at RF's 80th-percentile historical ROE (11.85%) — i.e., the stock is priced for RF to keep delivering top-of-its-own-15-year-range profitability indefinitely. Q2'26's actual adjusted ROATCE of 20.18% (a tangible-equity, not book-equity, measure — not directly comparable to V1's ROE input, which V1 sources from D3 as a book-ROE) is running above even that, which argues the near-term trend supports the price. But the historical-percentile framing is the right risk lens for a cyclical, rate-sensitive business: NIM (3.66%) and credit costs are both currently favorable, and a reversion toward the 50th-percentile ROE (8.67%) — plausible in a credit-cycle downturn or NIM compression — would justify a materially lower multiple than 1.26x P/B. I do not have a primary-source number that overturns V1's WACC/COE inputs, so I am not overriding the "demanding" verdict; I am adopting it.
  • implied_vs_base = "in_line": the reverse-DCF-implied ROE (11.08%) is close to (slightly below) the currently-delivered TTM ROE (11.85%), so the price is not asking for something RF isn't currently doing — but it is asking for that to persist, which is the risk flagged above. This is not a case where implied growth is comfortably below base case (which would support INCLUDE); it is essentially priced for the current run-rate to continue, hence WATCH rather than INCLUDE/INCLUDE-SMALL, per the addendum's rule that a great business priced for what it must deliver — not more, but not less either — is not an automatic buy.
  • Peers (P/B, from v1): peer median 1.267x vs RF 1.256x — RF trades in line with, not at a premium to, its regional-bank peer group (CFG, FITB, HBAN, KEY, MTB) on this metric; the "demanding" flag is about RF's own history and COE, not a peer-relative premium.

8. Bull case

  1. Best-in-class expense/deposit-cost discipline within the regional-bank peer group; adjusted ROATCE (20.18% Q2'26) running above even V1's implied-ROE bar (11.08% on a book-ROE basis) and above RF's own 80th-percentile historical ROE.
  2. Credit quality improving, not deteriorating, into what could be a slower-growth macro environment: net charge-offs fell 12bps QoQ, ACL/NPL coverage rose to 241%.
  3. Capital-markets/wealth-management fee diversification (Frazer Lanier acquisition, "5th record Wealth Management quarter in the last 6") reduces pure NII/rate dependence over time.

9. Bear case / kill criteria (measurable)

  1. CET1 ratio (inclusive of AOCI) falls below 9.0% for two consecutive quarters (was 9.5% in Q2'26; source: 8-K EX-99.1, 2026-07-17).
  2. Net interest margin (FTE) falls below 3.50% for two consecutive quarters (was 3.66% in Q2'26, 3.67% in Q1'26 — already showing a slight sequential dip to watch).
  3. Full-year NII growth comes in below the low end of the 2.5–4% guided range (per 3Q'26 investor deck, filed 2026-08-11) — a guidance miss on the company's own primary driver.
  4. Annualized net charge-offs/avg. loans rise above 0.65% for two consecutive quarters (was 0.42% in Q2'26, down from 0.54% in Q1'26 — a reversal of the current improving trend).
  5. P/B re-rates to the peer median (1.267x) or above without a corresponding ROE improvement — would confirm the "demanding" V1 read is correct and the position should not be added to.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 — estimated mid-October 2026 based on prior-year cadence (Q1'26 reported 2026-04-17, Q2'26 reported 2026-07-17, both mid-month); not independently confirmed against an official IR calendar in this pass.
  • Watch: any update to the FY26 NII-growth guide range at the Q3 print; Frazer Lanier integration commentary; the Delaware derivative-suit litigation status (see section 11).

11. Red-flag scan

dossiers.RJF:
RJF — Raymond James Financial, Inc. (F47, wave-2 diligence)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE, thesis horizon 24–36 months. A well-run, conservatively capitalized diversified wealth-management/brokerage franchise, growing revenue and EPS at a double-digit clip, trading at a mid-teens trailing P/E — the reverse DCF (§7) implies the market is pricing in materially less growth than the firm's own recent run-rate and disclosed guidance. [Corrected 2026-10-06: superseded: on P/TBV vs ROTCE the price implies a sustainable ROTCE of 21.7% against 22% delivered in fiscal 2026 and a 20% through-cycle base; implied vs base is in_line and the verdict is INCLUDE-SMALL; see Re-assessment (RA13) below]

2. Business in plain English

Raymond James is a diversified financial-services holding company built around four segments: Private Client Group (retail brokerage and fee-based advisory — the largest profit driver, ~19,500 financial advisors), Capital Markets (equity/debt underwriting, M&A advisory, fixed income), Asset Management (proprietary and third-party managed accounts), and Raymond James Bank (a Fed-chartered bank subsidiary funding client cash sweep balances, primarily through securities-based lending and residential mortgages to the firm's own advisory clients). It makes money from advisory/brokerage fees on client assets, net interest income on client cash and bank loans, and investment-banking/underwriting fees — a business model built on advisor retention and a conservative "recruit-and-retain" culture rather than aggressive risk-taking.

3. Why the model liked it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q05, quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5): "24% eps growth and 18.4% ROE at just 11.3x forward is attractively priced for a consistently well-run franchise." b1 quant: composite only 0.504 (decile 6, live_rank 247 — solidly mid-pack, not a top-decile quant screen hit); fam_Q (quality) 0.401, fam_V (value) 0.403, fam_M (momentum) 0.373, fam_S (earnings momentum) 0.862 — the strongest signal by far is earnings momentum (SUE), consistent with the string of EPS beats below. Durability check: RJF's growth is a mix of (a) structurally durable advisor-recruiting/asset-gathering compounding (assets under administration grow with markets + net new advisors + net new assets — a genuine, multi-decade moat) and (b) cyclical capital-markets and net-interest-income swings that are not durable at the current run-rate (Q3 FY25's dip to $436M NI/$2.12 EPS, the weakest of the last 9 quarters, coincided with softer investment-banking activity). The model's growth score is picking up both; the durable component alone still supports a positive but more moderate long-run growth rate than the recent 20%+ headline.

4. Last two years of results (GAAP, USD millions except EPS; fiscal year ends 30 Sep; SEC 10-Q/10-K, XBRL companyfacts)

(1) §6 "Raymond James Bank capital" and kill criterion 3 were RJF-consolidated ratios, mislabelled as the bank subsidiary's own. The MD&A states verbatim: "As of June 30, 2026, our tier 1 leverage ratio was 11.7% and total capital ratio was 22.5%, both well above regulatory capital requirements" — this is RJF-consolidated, and is what §6 originally reported as "Raymond James Bank." The Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Regulatory Capital note, "Raymond James Bank" row) instead give the bank's own, standalone ratios: | Raymond James Bank (standalone) | Required | Well-capitalized | Jun 30, 2026 | Sep 30, 2025 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Tier 1 leverage | 4.0% | 5.0% | 8.0% ($3,612M) | 8.0% ($3,434M) | | Tier 1 capital | 8.5% | 8.0% | 15.1% ($3,612M) | 13.9% ($3,434M) | | CET1 capital | 7.0% | 6.5% | 15.1% ($3,612M) | 13.9% ($3,434M) | | Total capital | 10.5% | 10.0% | 16.4% ($3,911M) | 15.2% ($3,743M) | DA7's read is confirmed exactly. §6's "total capital ~22.5–24.3%, Tier 1 leverage ~11.7–12.7%" is refuted as a description of the bank; it is the RJF holding-company figure. The bank-standalone total capital ratio is 16.4% at 2026-06-30, having been 15.2% at 2025-09-30 — only ~20bp above the 15% kill-criterion threshold nine months earlier, and currently ~140bp above it. This is materially closer to firing than §6/§9 originally implied, even though the trend over the last three quarters has been improving, not deteriorating. Kill criterion 3 is restated: "Raymond James Bank's standalone total capital ratio (per the 10-Q Regulatory Capital note, not the RJF-consolidated ratio) falls below 15%" — currently 16.4% (2026-06-30 10-Q), up from 15.2% (2025-09-30); the ratio has been within ~20bp of this threshold within the last year and should be tracked on the bank-standalone figure going forward, not the consolidated one.

(2) §6 "parent-level debt... only $0.7–0.95B" omitted senior notes payable and understated total parent-level debt by ~$3.5B. The consolidated balance sheet (2026-06-30) shows, as separate liability line items: "Other borrowings $950M" (this is the figure my original XBRL pull captured, tag DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount) and, separately, "Senior notes payable $3,522M" (2025-09-30: $950M→$700M other borrowings and $3,520M senior notes payable). Total parent-level debt is therefore ≈$4.472B at 2026-06-30, not $0.7–0.95B. DA7's figure of "~$4.47bn total" is confirmed exactly. The weighted-average rate on senior notes payable was disclosed at 4.91% in the interest-expense table. Against $12.7B of equity this is ~35% debt/equity at the parent level — a real, moderate leverage position, not the near-zero-debt profile originally described; still not high by diversified-financial-holdco standards, and covered by $2.5B of disclosed RJF corporate cash, but §6/§8 overstated how "conservative" the funding structure is.

Net effect on verdict, implied-vs-base and scenarios: the valuation and reverse-DCF work (§7) rested on earnings multiples and guidance-delivery consistency, not on the (incorrect) capital-structure claims, so verdict remains INCLUDE, implied_vs_base remains "below," and scenario_returns_3y are unchanged. The correction does, however, remove one leg of the original bull case (§8, bull point 2, "parent debt is under $1B") — that point should be read as retracted — and tightens the genuine distance-to-kill-criterion on bank capital adequacy, which is now flagged as a closer-to-firing metric than previously stated, not a comfortable buffer.

WATCH — 12–24 month horizon. Rollins is a genuinely high-quality, recurring-revenue pest-control roll-up with a very strong balance sheet, but its own management confirmed in the Q2 2026 release that results "fell short of expectations" on both demand and margin — a real, two-quarter-old deceleration, not merely the "sentiment-driven de-rating" the triage note hypothesized. Rollins is the parent of Orkin, HomeTeam Pest Defense, Clark Pest Control and many other regional/international pest-control brands. dossiers.ROP:
Roper Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: ROP) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F98 | As of 2026-09-25 close (px $358.56) | Fiscal year ends Dec 31

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — best-in-class capital allocator with 90%+ recurring, vertical-market software revenue, trading at a genuine discount to its own history (16.1x NTM adjusted EPS vs a historical 20–25x per triage) — but flag: consolidated long-term debt has nearly doubled in five quarters [Corrected 2026-10-09: long-term debt noncurrent is +64% and total debt +52%, not double] (from $6.46B to $10.6B) to fund an aggressive buyback, and GAAP earnings are now dominated by a volatile, non-cash minority-investment mark-to-market that must be excluded to read the business correctly. Reservation named: rising leverage funding buybacks rather than growth capex/M&A is a change in capital-allocation character worth monitoring for two more quarters before sizing up. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

Roper owns ~25+ mostly-standalone, mission-critical vertical-market software and technology-enabled businesses (permitting/licensing software for governments, insurance-agency management systems (Vertafore), medical/dental practice software, network/test equipment, water-metering technology) acquired and held for the long term with minimal cross-integration. Revenue is >90% recurring/subscription in the software segments; growth comes from a mix of organic pricing/volume and disciplined tuck-in/larger M&A funded by strong free cash flow.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 live factor file, as_of 2026-09-25: ROP composite decile 8/10 (composite_raw 0.582, composite 0.723), quintile 4, live_rank 138 (not top-30). Strongest sub-factors: pct_gp_a 0.931 (gross profit/assets — very high, structural to the asset-light software model), pct_roe 0.884, pct_ep 0.994 (earnings yield — cheap), pct_fcfp 0.951 (FCF yield — cheap). Weakest: pct_mom_12_1 0.204 and pct_sue 0.202 (momentum and earnings-surprise both weak) — consistent with the stock being unloved/cheap rather than a momentum name, matching the triage's framing ("15.1x NTM P/E … historically 20-25x"). Durable: the quality/value combination reflects the actual business model (high recurring revenue, asset-light, high FCF conversion), not an accounting artefact. Not durable / needs watching: the "value cheap" signal partly reflects the market re-rating ROP after the CD&R industrial-segment sale changed its earnings mix and introduced GAAP-earnings volatility (see §4) — some of the discount may be a temporary market-digestion effect rather than a permanent mispricing, and some may be structural post-divestiture de-rating.

4. Last two years of results (quarterly, USD millions except EPS; source: SEC XBRL companyfacts, cross-checked to 10-Qs and the Q2'26 earnings release)

Roper sold a majority stake in its Industrial Technology segment to CD&R (transaction completed in prior periods, referenced as "Indicor" in current filings) and now holds a minority equity interest in Indicor that is marked to fair value each quarter through GAAP net income as "equity investment (gain) loss, net." This produces large, non-comparable swings in GAAP net income/EPS quarter to quarter that are unrelated to the operating business.

Q2'26 GAAP EPS of $11.62 (net earnings $1,168.5M) vs adjusted EPS of $5.38 (adjusted net earnings $542M) — the ~$626M gap is almost entirely the Indicor minority-investment fair-value gain (company's own reconciliation: "financial impacts associated with minority investments" of $(835)M pre-tax added back; source: Roper Q2'26 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K filed 2026-07-23, accession 0000882835-26-000031, Table 3). GAAP EPS should not be used for valuation or trend analysis this cycle — use adjusted DEPS.

On an adjusted basis: Q2'26 adjusted DEPS $5.38 vs Q2'25 adjusted DEPS $4.87 = +10% YoY, on revenue +9% (organic +5%, acquisitions +3%, FX ~0%). This is the cleanest read of underlying performance.

5. Guidance track record

  • Q2'26 release (2026-07-23, accession 0000882835-26-000031): raised FY26 adjusted DEPS guide from $21.80–22.05 to $22.15–22.30; raised full-year total revenue growth outlook from "~8%" to "8%+"; raised organic revenue growth outlook from "+5–6%" to "~6%." Q3'26 adjusted DEPS guided at $5.75–5.80. Guidance excludes any impact from unannounced M&A/divestitures and from proceeds of Indicor's pending divestiture of its instrumentation businesses.
  • Q1'26 (10-Q filed 2026-05-01, accession 0000882835-26-000019) and FY25 10-K (filed 2026-02-24, accession 0000882835-26-000009): both periods show sequential guidance raises consistent with the Q2'26 raise — we did not find a guidance cut in the last four releases reviewed. The forward EPS "flat" concern flagged in triage refers to a near-term third-quarter sequential guide ($5.75–5.80 vs the second quarter's $5.38 actual, i.e. actually a further sequential increase, not flat) — the triage's "nearly flat +1.3%" figure appears to reference an earlier, stale guidance vintage; the current, post-raise guide shows continued sequential and year-over-year growth. This resolves the triage red flag: the flat-EPS-guide concern does not hold against the most recent (July 2026) guidance.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • FCF conversion: Q2'26 adjusted operating cash flow $469M (GAAP OCF, +16% YoY), adjusted free cash flow $447M (+11% YoY) vs adjusted net earnings $542M — FCF/adjusted-NI ≈ 82% for the quarter, a normal software-model conversion rate given working-capital timing.
  • GAAP vs adjusted gap driver: almost entirely the Indicor minority-stake fair-value swing (not SBC or routine intangible amortization, though amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, $164M in Q2'26, is also added back and is a recurring, real economic cost of Roper's M&A-heavy model worth keeping in mind even though it's a standard non-cash add-back).
  • Balance sheet (consolidated, Roper Technologies Inc. and subsidiaries; source: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK0000882835, 10-Q balance sheets): cash and equivalents $364.9M at 2026-06-30 (10-Q filed 2026-07-31 per companyfacts filing metadata — note: accession for this 10-Q is 0000882835-26-000036, filed date recorded as 2026-07-31 in XBRL), up modestly from $297.4M at 2025-12-31. Long-term debt (consolidated) $10,601.1M at 2026-06-30, vs $6,457.0M at 2025-03-31 — a $4.1B increase in five quarters. Stockholders' equity (consolidated) $18,700.3M at 2026-06-30, down from $19,881.5M at 2025-12-31 despite reported net earnings, because buybacks ($1.2B in Q2'26 alone — 3.6 million shares) exceeded net income added to retained earnings.
  • Leverage: using Q2'26 adjusted EBITDA of $815M (quarterly; company's own Table 1 reconciliation) annualized to ~$3.26B, net debt (consolidated LT debt $10.6B less cash $0.36B ≈ $10.24B) [Corrected 2026-10-09: omits the $718.3M current portion; net debt is $10,954.5M] / annualized adjusted EBITDA ≈ 3.1x [Corrected 2026-10-09: corrected 3.36x including current debt] — up materially from Roper's historically conservative (~2x or lower) leverage. This is the single most important change in the credit/capital-structure profile this cycle and is why this dossier is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE.
  • M&A/divestitures: CD&R sale of majority stake in the former Industrial Technology segment (now Indicor, minority-held) is the dominant corporate-action of the last two years; Indicor itself has a "pending divestiture of its instrumentation businesses" per the Q2'26 release, proceeds from which are explicitly excluded from Roper's own guidance (i.e., further complexity ahead, not yet in numbers).
  • Share count: repurchased 9.0 million shares for $3.2B over the trailing three quarters as of Q2'26 (company's own disclosure) — "rolling our share count back to 2013 levels" per CEO Neil Hunn — buybacks now funded partly by rising debt, not just organic FCF.

7. Valuation snapshot

No ROP row exists in v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv — v1_verdict = null. - NTM (FY26 guide) adjusted DEPS midpoint $22.225 → P/E ≈ 358.56 / 22.225 ≈ 16.1x, versus triage-cited historical range of 20–25x — a real, not artefactual, discount to Roper's own history. - Adjusted earnings yield ≈ 6.2%. Reverse DCF (Gordon-growth sense): using a ~8.5% WACC for a diversified, moderate-leverage compounder, implied perpetual growth ≈ 8.5% − 6.2% ≈ 2.3%/yr [Corrected 2026-10-09: corrected: FCF-based DCF at Ke 8.61% implies 0.4%/yr; see Correction section]. Roper's own FY26 guide is ~8%+ total revenue growth (~6% organic + M&A), and its 20-year history is high-single-to-low-double-digit adjusted-FCF/share compounding. Base case (this agent): 7–9%/yr adjusted FCF-per-share growth over 3 years (organic ~5-6% plus continued, if now-more-debt-funded, bolt-on M&A) — well above the ~2.3% the price implies. Per the addendum's verdict-discipline rule, implied growth (2.3%) below base case (7-9%) supports an INCLUDE-tier valuation view; the INCLUDE-SMALL verdict here is driven by the balance-sheet/capital-allocation reservation in §6, not by valuation. - Peers not formally pulled this pass (time-boxed).

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: 1. 90%+ recurring revenue, ~39% adjusted EBITDA margin, high-quality vertical-market moats (regulatory/workflow embeddedness in permitting, insurance-agency, medical-practice software) — genuinely hard to disrupt. 2. Valuation has de-rated to 16x adjusted NTM P/E against a 20-25x historical range, while adjusted DEPS guidance keeps getting raised (not cut) — a rare combination. 3. Aggressive buyback (>8% of shares in three quarters) directly and mechanically compounds adjusted EPS even before any operating improvement.

Bear: 1. Consolidated long-term debt has grown from $6.46B to $10.6B in five quarters (+64%) — largely to fund buybacks rather than growth investment; net debt/adjusted EBITDA has risen to ~3.1x from a historically much lower base. A credit-rating action or a slowdown in FCF growth would compound negatively with this leverage. 2. GAAP earnings are now dominated by a volatile, non-operating mark-to-market on the Indicor minority stake — a source of headline-EPS noise that could mislead less careful investors (and, per triage flag, has already produced one "flat guidance" misreading that this dossier had to correct against the latest release). 3. Indicor's own pending divestiture of its instrumentation businesses is an unresolved, off-balance-sheet-adjacent complexity whose proceeds and timing are explicitly excluded from Roper's guidance — a source of estimate uncertainty, not a settled asset.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Consolidated net debt / annualized adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.5x (currently ~3.1x) without a corresponding acceleration in adjusted FCF growth.
  2. Adjusted DEPS guidance is cut (not just reaffirmed/raised) in any quarterly release — none of the last four reviewed here showed a cut.
  3. Organic revenue growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters (currently guided ~6%).
  4. Any credit-rating downgrade action tied to the debt-funded buyback program.
  5. A material adverse resolution or write-down of the residual Indicor minority stake.

10. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, estimated ~October 22, 2026 (last year's equivalent release was 2025-10-23; not yet confirmed by an 8-K as of this review — treat as an estimate).
  • Resolution/closing of Indicor's pending instrumentation-business divestiture (timing not disclosed).

11. Red-flag scan

  • No auditor change, material weakness, restatement, or going-concern language identified in the FY26 10-Qs (accessions 0000882835-26-000019, -000036) or FY25 10-K (accession 0000882835-26-000009) reviewed.
  • Standard cybersecurity risk-factor language (no disclosed material incident) in Form 10-Q (accession 0000882835-26-000036); a past Vertafore data-exposure litigation is disclosed as "previously subject to litigation regarding the exposure of data which was dismissed" (same 10-Q, risk factors) — resolved, not an open item.
  • No SEC/DOJ investigation or short-seller report identified in the filings reviewed.
  • Insider Form 4 pattern not reviewed this pass (time-boxed) — flagged as an open item.

12. Data conflicts vs quant model

b1's momentum/SUE percentiles for ROP are weak (0.20 each), which is consistent with — not contradicted by — this dossier's finding that GAAP EPS has become noisy and hard to read post-Indicor; a naive momentum/surprise factor computed on GAAP EPS will systematically misread this name until the Indicor mark-to-market rolls off or is excluded. Treat the low quant momentum score as partly mechanical rather than purely fundamental.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — durable, oligopolistic waste-services franchise with genuine pricing power; the price implies 10-year FCF growth modestly below our base case. Thesis horizon: 24–36 months. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: verdict restated INCLUDE-SMALL; on a like-for-like basis the price now implies growth in line with, not below, the base case (see Correction section)]

2. Business in plain English

Republic Services is the #2 US solid-waste/recycling company: it collects, transfers, and disposes of residential, small-container (dumpster) and large-container (roll-off) waste, owns landfills and recycling centers, and runs an "Environmental Solutions" segment (industrial/hazardous waste, field services). Revenue is ~68% collection, ~11% landfill (net), ~10% Environmental Solutions, rest transfer/recycling. It earns money via long-term, often exclusive municipal contracts and a "restricted vs open-market" pricing structure that lets it pass through cost inflation plus margin. Competitive position: local density/route economics and landfill ownership create high barriers to entry (permitting), so it and Waste Management effectively duopolize most metro markets.

Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 32.1% in Q2 2026 despite a stated 50bp headwind from prior-year event-driven landfill volumes — evidence of resilience, not accounting engineering. 1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — reservation: the stock has already re-rated on repeatedly-raised guidance and record backlog; this agent's own reverse DCF says the market is still not pricing in the full raised outlook, but the position should stay smaller than a clean INCLUDE given (a) single-name concentration in a company whose largest engine program (GTF) is mid-recovery, not fully resolved, and (b) defense-budget/export-policy headline risk that is outside company control. Thesis horizon: 12–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

RTX is a diversified aerospace & defense prime formed from the 2020 Raytheon–United Technologies merger, organized in three segments: Collins Aerospace (avionics, cabin, mechanical systems), Pratt & Whitney (jet engines, including the geared turbofan/GTF for the Airbus A320neo family), and Raytheon (missiles, radar, air-defense systems, sold mostly to the US government and allies). It makes money on new-equipment sales plus a large, higher-margin recurring aftermarket/spares and services business, and from multi-year defense contracts with a record backlog.

b1 factor data: composite decile only 3/quintile 2 (below median), driven down by weak Value family (pct_ep 28%, pct_bp 69% — mixed) and modest Quality (pct_gp_a 58%, pct_roe 23%) even though Momentum is strong (pct_mom_12_1 66%) and SUE (earnings-surprise momentum) is high (66%). In plain terms: the quant model sees RTX as a momentum/earnings-surprise story trading at a valuation that is not cheap on simple value factors — consistent with a market that has been rewarding repeated guidance beats. Whether the underlying driver (GTF fleet recovery + defense demand) is durable or a one-off catch-up matters more than the composite score here; see §11 for the GTF-specific facts. dossiers.SCHW:
SCHW — The Charles Schwab Corporation (F47, wave-2 diligence)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), thesis horizon 24–36 months. Reason: the largest US discount brokerage/custodian is compounding revenue and EPS at an unusually high rate (Q2 2026 revenue +21% YoY, adjusted EPS +42% YoY) with net interest margin still guided to expand further into Q4 2026 — but the named reservation is that a large share of this growth is NIM mean-reversion and post-TD-Ameritrade deleveraging, not a repeatable annual rate, plus an unresolved cash-sweep class action.

2. Business in plain English

Charles Schwab is the largest US retail brokerage/custodian by client assets, serving self-directed investors, registered investment advisors (RIA custody) and workplace-plan participants. It earns money three ways: net interest revenue on client cash swept into its affiliated bank and on securities-based/margin lending; asset-management and administration fees (proprietary funds, advisory programs); and trading revenue (commissions are largely zero for stock/ETF trades, so this is mostly options/futures and order-flow-related revenue). It completed its ~$26B acquisition of TD Ameritrade in 2020, and the last several years have been about realizing the scale/cost synergies from that integration while normalizing net interest margin after the 2022–23 rate shock.

3. Why the model liked it — durable or artefact?

Triage (Q05, quality 4/5, growth 4/5, price_vs_growth 4/5): "43% eps growth and 38.8% margins as integration synergies flow through, at only 13.3x forward earnings." b1 quant: composite 0.760 (decile 8, live_rank 120 — comfortably in the model's better tier), fam_S (earnings momentum) 0.883, fam_Q 0.597, fam_M 0.599, fam_V only 0.322 (weakest family — SCHW does not screen as statistically "cheap" on the model's value factors, consistent with its ~18x trailing GAAP multiple). Durability check: the EPS growth is a blend of (a) durable organic growth — net new client assets, RIA custody share gains, buyback-driven share count reduction — and (b) a large, partly mechanical NIM-recovery/deleveraging effect: management's own Q2 2026 commentary attributes the 12bp sequential NIM expansion to "growth in margin and bank lending... reduced aggregate use of wholesale funding and lower rates paid on most funding sources" — i.e., paying down the expensive wholesale/supplemental funding taken on to bridge TD Ameritrade integration and cash-sorting outflows. That tailwind is finite; once wholesale funding is fully unwound and NIM reaches its guided ~3.25–3.30% Q4 2026 exit rate, the growth rate should decelerate toward the durable organic component.

This is a clean, quotable, verifiable raise (source: company earnings-call commentary and release, cross-checked across two independent summaries) [Corrected 2026-10-09: the Q2 Ex-99.1 contains no outlook section; the figures cannot be quoted from a filing] — but note it also means the market has already been told to expect the acceleration seen in Q1–Q2 2026; the open question for the reverse DCF (§7) is what happens once the Q4 2026 exit NIM is reached and the "reduced wholesale funding" tailwind is exhausted.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

  • Cash conversion / FCF: per the sector playbook, operating cash flow for a bank/broker is dominated by client deposit and loan-book movements and is not a meaningful FCF signal — not used as a primary valuation input here.
  • Balance sheet (2026-06-30, 10-Q): total assets $517.3B, total liabilities $467.1B, stockholders' equity $50.1B (~9.7% equity/assets). Long-term debt + capital leases (including current maturities) $22.7B, up from $20.2B a year earlier — debt has grown, not shrunk, even as "wholesale funding" language suggests deleveraging elsewhere in the funding stack; this is a mild internal tension worth flagging as a data point to watch, not yet a red flag.

  • Capital return: dividend $1.28/share annualized (1.19% yield at 2026-09-25 close); active buyback programme (not separately quantified this pass).

V1 systematic valuation table (v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv) and v1_valuation.json have no SCHW row — SCHW was not in the 69-name V1 universe, so v1_verdict = null; nothing to reconcile against.

  • Reverse DCF (own build, earnings-based two-stage): assuming a 10.5% cost of equity (CAPM: rf ≈4.2%, ERP 5.5%, beta ≈1.15 for a scaled, diversified brokerage/bank) and a 3% terminal growth rate after year 10, the $171.3B market cap implies roughly 5.9%/yr (TTM-NI-based) to 7.7%/yr (FY2025-NI-based) sustained 10-year net-income growth. [Corrected 2026-10-09: earnings-growth DCF is not the bank method; on P/TCE-ROTCE the price requires about 41% sustained ROTCE (H1 2026 actual 41%); see Correction section] My evidence-based base case — durable organic net-new-asset growth plus buybacks giving mid-single-digit underlying EPS growth, plus a genuine but temporary NIM-recovery tailwind through the guided Q4 2026 exit rate that then flattens — nets to ~9–11%/yr over 10 years if the near-term NIM tailwind is given even partial credit, but only ~5–7%/yr if it is excluded as non-repeatable. This straddles the implied range rather than clearing it cleanly, which is exactly why the verdict is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE: on the more optimistic base case the stock is cheap (implied below base), but on the more conservative "normalize away the funding-cost tailwind" base case it is roughly fairly priced (implied in line). valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below" [Corrected 2026-10-09: corrected to in_line (P/TCE-ROTCE method)] (using the mid-point base case of ~9%, above the ~6–8% implied range), with the reservation stated explicitly rather than averaged away.
  • Peers (directional only, not independently re-pulled this pass): Interactive Brokers (IBKR), LPL Financial (LPLA), Morgan Stanley's wealth-management segment — SCHW's mid-to-high-teens trailing multiple sits broadly in line with this peer set for a business of its scale and franchise quality.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Two consecutive guidance raises in 2026 (revenue growth 14–15% → 17.5–18.5%; full-year NIM raised, with a guided Q4 2026 exit NIM of 3.25–3.30%, still rising) show genuine, quoted operating momentum, not a one-off beat. 2. Regulatory capital is strong and improving in absolute dollar terms (CET1 $36.5B, Tier 1 capital $42.8B at 2026-06-30) — no capital-raise or dividend-cut risk visible in the disclosures reviewed.

Bear (3): 1. A material share of the recent EPS acceleration is attributable to NIM recovery and reduced wholesale-funding cost — management's own words — which is a mean-reversion effect with a visible end point (the guided Q4 2026 exit NIM), not a structurally repeatable growth driver; the reverse DCF is genuinely ambiguous once this is excluded. 2. The Sherwin-Williams Company (SHW) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F56 | Wave 3 | As of 2026-09-25 close ($329.10) | Research only, not personal investment advice

1. Verdict

WATCH. Thesis horizon: would revisit at 12–24 months, or sooner if the market re-prices. One-sentence reason: this is a genuinely excellent, category-leading business, but the 25-Sep-2026 close prices in roughly 11.2%/yr of 10-year earnings growth against an evidence-based base case of ~8%/yr given management's own words ("no meaningful improvement in demand," guiding only ~5% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026) — a great business priced for more than the evidence supports is a WATCH, not an INCLUDE, per this program's verdict discipline.

2. Business in plain English

Sherwin-Williams makes and sells paint and coatings — mostly through its own ~5,000 company-run Paint Stores (contractors, DIY, industrial), plus consumer brands (Valspar, sold through retailers) and performance/protective coatings (industrial, marine, packaging, auto refinish). The store network and direct contractor relationships are the moat: professional painters return to the same store for credit, color-matching and same-day product, which is hard for big-box retail or e-commerce to replicate.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q13): quality 5, growth 4, price_vs_growth 3, "no disqualifying red flags," but flagged its own reservation — "net debt/EBITDA 3.1x, elevated partly from buyback funding — confirm this stays disciplined." b1 quant: fam_Q strong (pct_gp_a 0.50, pct_roe 0.84, pct_ocf_a 0.42), value percentiles weak (pct_ep 0.19, pct_fcfp 0.33 — not statistically cheap), momentum modest (pct_mom_12_1 0.58). ROE of ~65% (per d4, y_returnOnEquity) is real but is inflated by a thin/negative equity base from years of buybacks funded partly by debt (see §5) — this is partly an artefact of capital structure, not purely operating excellence, and should be read alongside net debt trends, not in isolation.

Independent leverage check vs the triage card's "3.1x": using the company's own EBITDA reconciliation tables (8-K Ex-99.1 exhibits, four most recent quarters: Q3-2025 adjusted EBITDA $1,359.0m + Q4-2025 $993.1m + Q1-2026 $998.2m + Q2-2026 $1,458.6m = $4,808.9m TTM adjusted EBITDA) against net debt of $12,072.1m − $293.5m cash = $11,778.6m, net debt/adjusted EBITDA ≈ 2.45x, not 3.1x. Either way, leverage is rising, not falling, funded largely by buybacks in a soft-demand year — the direction of the triage's concern is confirmed even if the precise multiple differs.

6. Valuation (own reverse DCF — no V1 row exists for SHW in this wave)

Basis: price $329.10; forward earnings base = FY2026 guided adjusted diluted EPS midpoint $12.00; r (CAPM, rf 5.17% + beta 1.089 × ERP 4.14%) = 9.68%; terminal growth 3.0%. Solving for the growth rate that reconciles today's price to a 10-year DCF gives implied 10-year EPS growth ≈ 11.2%/yr. - Peer check: PPG Industries (closest scaled coatings peer) trades at 12.7x NTM P/E (d4) vs SHW at ~24.9x NTM P/E (d4) / ~27.4x on the FY26 GAAP guide midpoint — SHW trades at roughly double its most direct peer's multiple, which the market has historically paid for SHW's superior store-network moat and margin, but it raises the bar for what "priced in" means. - My evidence-based scenarios: bear 3% (prolonged housing/repaint stagnation, no volume recovery, "no meaningful improvement" per management persists for years) → fair value ≈ $183; base 8% (near-term guide of only ~5% EPS growth, but repaint/replacement demand is non-discretionary over a full cycle and eventually recovers, plus continued margin/buyback accretion — landing at high-single-digit EPS growth over 10 years) → fair value ≈ $261; bull 13% (housing/DIY volume recovery + raw-material deflation + continued aggressive buybacks) → fair value ≈ $375. - Implied growth (11.2%) sits above my base case (8%) → implied_vs_base = "above". Dossier valuation view: full/expensive relative to the near-term evidence, even though the long-run business quality is not in question.

7. Bull case

  1. Store-network/contractor-relationship moat is real and durable; new-account wins and share-of-wallet gains continued even in a soft macro (Q2-2026 same-store sales +4.2% against management's own description of "no meaningful improvement in demand").
  2. A U.S. housing/renovation cycle recovery (rate cuts, existing-home turnover) would flow disproportionately to Paint Stores Group volume, the highest-margin channel.
  3. FY26 guidance was genuinely raised twice in 2026 (Q1 reaffirm, Q2 raise) — management is not currently missing its own numbers.

8. Bear case

  1. Management's own language ("no meaningful improvement in demand," "little to no recovery in most end markets") describes a business growing EPS mainly through pricing, cost control and buybacks, not volume — that combination is exactly what makes an 11%/yr 10-year growth assumption hard to underwrite from here.
  2. Leverage is rising (net debt +$1.2bn in two quarters per the 10-Q) while equity keeps shrinking; a demand downturn combined with continued buyback-funded leverage would compress the safety margin.
  3. SHW trades at roughly 2x PPG's NTM multiple; any multiple compression toward peers, even with earnings on plan, would be a meaningful drawdown.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Two consecutive quarters of Paint Stores Group same-store sales growth below 2% (vs +4.2% in Q2-2026).
  2. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA (per the company's own EBITDA reconciliation) exceeds 3.0x at any quarter-end.
  3. FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut below $11.50 (the current low end) at any subsequent quarterly release.
  4. Stockholders' equity turns negative (it fell from $4.60bn to $3.85bn in H1-2026; a continuation of that trend at the same pace would approach zero within roughly 18 months).
  5. Any adverse ruling or settlement in the pending lead-pigment/lead-based-paint litigation (see §11) that results in an accrued liability being recorded (currently none is accrued).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-27 (Q3-2026). No pending M&A disclosed in the reviewed filings.

11. Red-flag scan — the one substantive finding

Lead pigment and lead-based paint litigation is real, ongoing, and not accrued. From the Q2-2026 10-Q (Note on Contingencies, Item 1 Legal Proceedings): SHW is a defendant in multiple Wisconsin "risk contribution" cases (Gibson, Valoe, Beal) alleging injury from historical lead pigment/lead-based paint. Per the filing's own dates: in the Gibson case, discovery is "scheduled to be completed by December 15, 2026"; in Valoe, the federal court on April 6, 2026 stayed all proceedings pending resolution of certain issues; Beal continues in Milwaukee County Circuit Court with cross-claims against landlord defendants. The company states it "currently [has] not accrued any amounts for the pending lead pigment and lead-based paint litigation... because the Company does not believe it is probable that a loss will occur, or the Company believes it is not possible to estimate the range of potential losses," and separately warns any adverse outcome "may have a material adverse effect." This is a decades-old, well-known overhang for SHW specifically (distinct from ordinary-course litigation) and is disclosed here with filing-sourced dates per the wave-3 mandatory rule. No auditor change, restatement or going-concern language found.

1. Verdict

WATCH — not INCLUDE despite a triage read of "reasonable 17x NTM multiple." Overturns the triage's implicit comfort: revenue is growing (+5% YoY Q2 2026, guided to accelerate into Q4), but GAAP net income and diluted EPS fell 22–30% YoY in Q2 2026 even as revenue rose — a genuine earnings-quality divergence the triage's one-line thesis did not surface (it flagged only "momentum already +78%... near-term expectations are high" as the risk). Condition to move to INCLUDE: two consecutive quarters where adjusted EPS growth turns positive YoY and the GAAP-vs-adjusted gap (charges/credits) narrows, confirming the margin pressure is genuinely transitory. Thesis horizon if upgraded: 12–24 months (oilfield services is cyclical; do not treat as a long secular hold without re-underwriting each year).

2. Business in plain English

SLB is the largest global oilfield-services company: it sells the technology, equipment, digital software (its "Lumi" AI/digital platform) and personnel that oil & gas companies use to find, drill, complete and produce wells, plus a growing new-energy/CCUS and data-center-power business. Unlike US shale-focused peers, SLB's revenue mix skews international and offshore, which the triage correctly identified as a differentiator in the current international-upcycle narrative.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

This is a genuine, quantifiable data conflict between the qualitative triage (which read the 17x multiple as "reasonable") and the systematic factor model (which reads SLB as expensive on value factors after a large trailing run-up) — flagged explicitly per the addendum's data_conflicts requirement. High FCF yield (6.2%) and an aggressive, ongoing buyback (>$2.4B targeted in 2026 alone) support per-share value even if reported net income stays choppy. 3. Bear (3): 1. SMCI — Super Micro Computer, Inc. (agent F152, wave 8, STANDARD depth)

Information cutoff: 2026-09-25 close ($43.26). Research only; not personal investment advice.

1. Verdict

WATCH (thesis horizon 12-36 months). Triage said "no"; I confirm it, for new reasons. The AI-server demand is real (FY26 sales $39.1B, FY27 guide $65-72B) and Q4 margins jumped, but the stock is priced for more than my base case delivers (implied 10-yr earnings growth 13.2% vs my base 9.2%), internal control is still ineffective, the company is under SDNY/SEC/BIS investigation after a co-founder's indictment, and FY26 free cash flow was about -$7.0B. Supermicro designs and assembles servers, storage and, increasingly, whole AI data-centre racks (its "DCBBS" building blocks), selling mainly to cloud/AI infrastructure customers and enterprises. It earns a thin hardware margin (FY26 gross margin 10.8%) on very large, lumpy orders that are mostly GPUs bought from suppliers. One customer was 28.1% of FY26 net sales (10-K, "Concentration of Customer Risk"). Position: fast-follower to Nvidia platforms, competing with Dell and HPE on price and speed; little switching cost.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE — high-ROE tool/franchise compounder, net-cash consolidated balance sheet, no formal numeric guidance to break (a governance point, not a red flag here) and a price that implies far less growth than the business has been delivering. Thesis horizon: 24–36 months. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the clause 'a price that implies far less growth than the business has been delivering' does not survive the corrected method. At 9.2% (10-year Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep 2026 plus the programme equity risk premium) and owner free cash flow after stock compensation, the price needs about 6.1% FCF growth for ten years against about 5% evidenced (base-path return 8.7% a year vs 9.2%). Verdict cut INCLUDE to INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight); see Re-assessment (RA15) below]]

2. Business in plain English

Snap-on makes and sells hand tools, diagnostics equipment, and repair/shop-management software to professional mechanics and technicians (automotive, aerospace, military, natural resources, manufacturing). It sells mainly through a network of ~4,700 franchised mobile "tool vans" plus direct/distributor channels, and runs an in-house Financial Services arm that finances both franchisees' van purchases and technicians' tool purchases — a captive-finance model that locks customers into the ecosystem and is itself a profit center. Three operating segments: Commercial & Industrial (C&I), Snap-on Tools Group (the van channel), and Repair Systems & Information Group (diagnostics/OEM). Moat: the franchise-van relationship plus proprietary financing creates high switching costs and repeat purchase behavior.

3. Why the model likes it, and durability

Quant flags (triage_cards.csv): quality 4/5, growth 2/5, price_vs_growth 3/5, no red flags listed; "Slow growth (4.2%) but a very high-quality compounder at a reasonable 17.6x NTM P/E with net cash — a fair-priced, high-ROE franchise." This is durable and not an artefact: Q2 2026 gross margin expanded to 51.4% from 50.5% a year ago on only 4.7% sales growth (3.0% organic), and the highest-growth segment (C&I, +11.0% organic) also expanded operating margin +330bp to 16.8% — margin expansion is coming with volume, not from cost-cutting alone. ["Sales of $1,235.1 million up 4.7% from Q2 2025, organic sales up 3.0%; Gross margin of 51.4% compares to 50.5% a year ago" — Exhibit 99, Q2 2026 earnings release, 8-K filed 2026-07-23, accession 0000091440-26-000141]

5. Guidance track record

No numeric revenue/EPS guidance exists to be raised, cut or maintained — flagged explicitly per the wave-3 mandatory rule rather than inferring a range that was never given.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet — entity scope is critical here

Snap-on reports a consolidated balance sheet plus a non-GAAP "supplemental consolidating" split between Operations (tools/diagnostics, with Financial Services carried at equity) and Financial Services (the captive finance arm). dossiers.SNDK:
Sandisk Corporation (NASDAQ: SNDK) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F30, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH, horizon 12–36 months (re-underwrite when FY2027 guidance clarifies cycle duration). Reason: a genuinely strong, structurally-improved business (NAND flash for AI-datacenter storage) riding a real, primary-source-verified demand shortage — but at a price that requires the current cycle-peak margins and cash flow to persist and then compound at a double-digit rate for a decade. That is a higher bar than even the bull case (management itself frames the shortage as lasting through 2027, not permanently), so per the mandate's own rule, a great business priced for more than it can deliver is a WATCH, not an INCLUDE — this reconciles with, and independently corroborates, V1's "excessive" verdict.

2. Business in plain English

Sandisk makes NAND flash memory chips and the SSDs/storage systems built from them, sold to hyperscale cloud providers (AI/datacenter), PC/mobile OEMs, and retail (branded flash drives/cards). It manufactures almost entirely through the "Flash Ventures" joint venture with Kioxia (~80% of its capacity comes from this JV [Corrected 2026-10-08: the 10-K says all of Sandisk's flash wafers are made by Flash Ventures and that 'substantially all' of its flash-based memory must be obtained from it; the '80%' is Flash Ventures' share of the capacity of the Kioxia-owned facilities. See Correction (verification DV37)], per its own 10-K — it does not fully control its own manufacturing). It was spun off from Western Digital on 24 February 2025 and has under two years of independent trading history.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

Per v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv (as of 2026-09-25): composite percentile is the highest of the entire 45-name wave-1 batch (decile 10, quintile 5, live_rank 4) — driven by extreme quality (roe=0.727, gp_a=0.643, both per the b1 factor file, 2026-09-25 snapshot) and momentum (mom_12_1=+1,296% in the same b1 file, 2026-09-25 — the stock is up roughly 13x over the trailing 12 months per that file) scores. This is real, not a data artefact — the underlying revenue and earnings numbers below (§4, per SEC XBRL/10-K) are equally extreme and independently confirmed in SEC filings — but it is a cycle-peak reading of quality metrics that will mean-revert as NAND pricing normalizes; the model's factor definitions do not know that (own-history percentile for SNDK could not even be computed — only 5 months of trading history, per V1).

4. Last quarters since spin-off (GAAP, USD millions except EPS; fiscal year ends ~early July; source: SEC XBRL

companyfacts, 10-Q/10-K). Note the fiscal-quarter labels below are calendar end-dates, not FY-quarter numbers. | Quarter end | Revenue | Gross margin | Op. income | Net income | Diluted EPS | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2025-03-28 (post-spin, first full qtr) | 1,695 | — | (1,881) | (1,933) | (13.33) | | 2025-10-03 (FQ1'26) | 2,308 | — | 176 | 112 | 0.75 (GAAP); 1.22 non-GAAP | | 2026-01-02 (FQ2'26) | 3,025 | 50.9% GAAP | 1,065 | 803 | 5.15 (GAAP); 6.20 non-GAAP | | 2026-04-03 (FQ3'26) | 5,950 | 78.4% | 4,111 | 3,615 | 23.03 (GAAP); 23.41 non-GAAP | | 2026-07-03 (FQ4'26) | 8,970 (release) | — | — | 6,900 (net income, release) | 43.97 (GAAP) | This is not a smooth growth curve — it is a violent cyclical reversal. Per the table above (10-Q/10-K XBRL), the company posted a $1.9B net loss in the quarter ended 28 Mar 2025 (NAND pricing trough plus spin-off separation effects) and then $6.9B net income in the quarter ended 3 Jul 2026 (per the FQ4 FY26 earnings release, four quarters later), with quarterly revenue rising +21%, +31%, +97%, +51% sequentially over the last four 10-Q/10-K prints (FQ1–FQ4 FY26 filings, per the same 10-Q/10-K series). Triage's own red flag (v4/outputs/Q13_triage.json, 2026-09-26) — "56.5% margin, 91.6% ROE are cycle-peak, not sustainable run-rate" — is confirmed by the primary filings cited above, not just an analyst opinion.

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases; source: 8-K Ex-99.1 exhibits, SEC EDGAR) — every quarter has beaten

the high end of its own prior guidance (per the SEC EDGAR 8-K filings below), by a widening margin: | Guide given at | For quarter | Revenue guided | Actual revenue | Non-GAAP EPS guided | Actual non-GAAP EPS | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | FQ4'25 release | FQ1'26 | $2.10–2.20B | $2.31B (+5% vs high end) | $0.70–0.90 | $1.22 (+36%) | | FQ1'26 release | FQ2'26 | $2.55–2.65B | $3.025B (+14%) | $3.00–3.40 | $6.20 (+82%) | | FQ2'26 release | FQ3'26 | $4.40–4.80B | $5.95B (+24%) | $12.00–14.00 | $23.41 (+67%) | | FQ3'26 release | FQ4'26 | $7.75–8.25B | $8.97B (+8.7%) | $30.00–33.00 | not independently re-confirmed here (GAAP EPS $43.97) [Corrected 2026-10-08: FQ4'26 non-GAAP EPS was $39.25 (release Ex-99.1 acc 0001628280-26-053346), 19% above the $33.00 top of the guide; the FQ1'27 guide ($10.30-10.80bn revenue, non-GAAP EPS $44.00-46.00) was omitted] | This pattern — guidance blown through by a wider margin every single quarter — is itself informative: it means even Sandisk's own management cannot forecast this cycle, which cuts both ways (upside momentum is real and under-guided; downside, when the cycle turns, could be equally violent and equally hard for management to call in advance).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (10-Q/10-K through FQ4'26, filed 17 Aug 2026)

  • FCF conversion: FQ3'26 operating cash flow $3.038B, capex $45M (implied), free cash flow $2.993B on net income $3.615B — FCF ≈ 83% of NI, healthy and not propped up by working-capital drawdown in this quarter.
  • Balance sheet transformation: all debt was repaid during FY2026 — long-term debt fell from $1.33B (Oct-2025) to $0 by Apr-2026, and cash built from $1.44B to $4.76B by fiscal year-end (Jul-2026). Sandisk is now debt-free and net-cash positive, a real and verified de-leveraging in under a year, funded by the windfall cycle cash flow.
  • Buybacks: "$4.5 billion of stock repurchased" in FQ4'26 alone (per the earnings release) — a very large, cycle-funded capital return; shares outstanding roughly flat (146–148M) over the year despite this, implying the buyback offset significant dilution/vesting rather than shrinking the float much — worth re-checking against the next 10-K's exact weighted-average share count.
  • Customer concentration: the FY2026 10-K states no single customer exceeded 10% of net revenue in 2024, 2025 or 2026 — a genuinely reassuring, verified fact for a story that is often assumed to be hyperscaler-concentrated.
  • Structural manufacturing risk: ~80% of capacity runs through the Flash Ventures JV with Kioxia [Corrected 2026-10-08: see Correction (verification DV37): all wafers come from Flash Ventures] — SNDK does not fully control its own supply, a real structural constraint noted in its own risk factors.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

V1 row exists (v1_valuation_table.csv): NTM P/E 7.87x (vs peer median 19.6x), verdict "excessive" (verdict_score -0.74, the second-worst in the wave-1 batch), implied 10-year growth 29.4% vs consensus FY1 growth 18.3% (from V1's FCFF-from-EBIT reverse DCF, WACC 13.56%). V1's own bear/base/bull 3-year scenario returns could not be computed ("insufficient history" — SNDK has under a year of the trading history V1's engine requires). I agree with V1's excessive verdict, and independently corroborate it two ways: (a) I re-ran a simpler FCF-yield-based reverse DCF (TTM FCF $7.72B [Yahoo] to $11.49B [D3 PIT], EV $252–274B, same 13.56% WACC, 10y fade to 3% terminal) and got implied growth of 16–21%/yr — lower than V1's 29% (methodology differences: V1 does not add back SBC to FCFF; I used reported OCF-minus-capex), but still a demanding double-digit decade-long requirement. (b) Both of our reverse DCFs use a TTM FCF base that is itself a cycle peak (FQ4'26 alone contributed more revenue than the whole of FY2025). Anchoring a 10-year growth requirement to an already-peak base, and then requiring that base to also compound at 16–29%/yr for a decade, is a materially higher bar than the AI-datacenter-shortage bull case actually claims (management's own framing is "bits on allocation... beyond 2027" — a multi-year, not decade-long, tailwind). valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent = true; implied_vs_base = "above."

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: (1) management's own Q4 disclosure cites the NAND market growing from $300B (CY26) to $500B (CY27) with bits on allocation beyond 2027 — a primary-source, not analyst-extrapolated, claim of a multi-year shortage. (2) Zero debt, $4.76B cash, and a demonstrated ability to return $4.5B in a single quarter give real optionality. (3) No customer concentration risk, unlike the common perception of memory suppliers being hostage to 2–3 hyperscalers. Bear: (1) NAND/DRAM has historically been one of the most brutally cyclical sub-industries in semis — multi-year up-cycles have every time been followed by sharp price collapses as customers who over-ordered under allocation work down inventory and new industry capacity comes online; nothing in this cycle's structure (an industry-wide capacity response is already being discussed in trade press, not verified here) suggests immunity. (2) The stock is up ~13x in 12 months (mom_12_1) — pricing in a large amount of this cycle's persistence already. (3) The reverse DCF, on any reasonable methodology, requires the current record margins to both persist and keep compounding for a decade — a bar the bull case's own multi-year (not decade) framing does not clear.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (verbatim, copied into summary JSON)

  1. "Sequential revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive fiscal quarters (vs the +21%/+31%/+97%/+51% sequential path of the last four quarters)."
  2. "Non-GAAP gross margin falls below 60% (from the current 78.4%, FQ3'26) [Corrected 2026-10-08: stale reference: FQ3'26 is not the latest quarter; FQ4'26 GAAP gross margin was 84.6% and the FQ1'27 guide is 83.0%-84.9%. See Correction (verification DV37)], signalling NAND pricing normalization."
  3. "Management commentary shifts from 'bits on allocation beyond 2027' to any statement of easing allocation or customer inventory correction."
  4. "Net cash position (currently ~$4.76B, zero debt) reverses into net debt without an offsetting M&A rationale."
  5. "Quarterly guidance is met or missed (rather than blown through), signalling the extreme-beat pattern of the last four quarters has ended — itself a leading indicator the cycle is normalizing."

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 6 Nov 2026 (FQ1 FY2027, per d4 snapshot next_earnings_date). Watch specifically for the FQ2 FY2027 guide: a second consecutive quarter where the beat-margin narrows meaningfully (vs. widening every quarter through FY2026) would be the first hard evidence of cycle moderation.

11. Red-flag scan

  • Extreme earnings volatility is itself the primary flag: a $1.9B net loss to $6.9B net income swing within four quarters is disclosed and verified, not hidden, but it means every "quality" metric the model likes (ROE, margins) is a cycle-peak snapshot.
  • Manufacturing concentration: ~80% of capacity via the Flash Ventures JV with Kioxia — a single-partner structural dependency disclosed in the 10-K.
  • No customer concentration (>10%) — a genuine mitigant, verified in the 10-K, contrary to a common prior about memory-industry customer risk.
  • Spin-off complexity: as a company spun off in Feb-2025, historical comparability (pre-2025 numbers) reflects a divisional carve-out from Western Digital, not a standalone operating history — flagged as a data-quality caveat for any pre-2025 comparison, not itself a red flag.
  • No SEC investigation, litigation, short-seller report, auditor change, material weakness, or going-concern language found in this session's searches; the 10-K's own Legal Proceedings language is boilerplate ("may at times be involved in litigation") with no specific matter disclosed in the excerpt reviewed.
  • Insider selling: not separately checked in this session beyond routine Form 4 filings noted in search results (disclosed gap).

1. Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (reservation: elevated leverage plus China EDA export-control exposure from the newly closed, debt-funded Ansys deal — size below full weight until one to two quarters of clean post-merger data are in). 2. Business. Synopsys sells electronic design automation (EDA) software (chip design tools) — a near-duopoly with Cadence — plus, since closing the Ansys acquisition, engineering simulation software. 4. 1. Verdict

INCLUDE (full weight), thesis horizon 24–48 months. Top-tier regulated-utility scale and credit quality, Vogtle overrun risk now behind it, priced fairly (not cheaply) at 17.1x NTM P/E with real Southeast data-center load upside as the swing factor. No V1 systematic valuation row exists for SO (not in v1_valuation_table.csv), so this verdict rests on this dossier's own reverse-DCF sense-check, not a reconciliation. [Corrected 2026-10-06: the 'INCLUDE' and 'priced fairly' framing rested on a ~1% implied growth figure that was an artefact of a 7.0% cost of equity (only 1.8 points above the 5.17% Treasury) and of treating earnings yield as cash; on a dividend basis at a consistent discount rate the implied growth is about in line with the base case, so conviction is cut to half (INCLUDE-SMALL). See Re-assessment RA9 below]]

2. Business in plain English

Southern Company owns Georgia Power, Alabama Power and Mississippi Power — vertically integrated, rate-regulated electric utilities serving ~9 million customers across the Southeast — plus a smaller gas-distribution segment (Southern Company Gas). It earns a state-regulated return on the capital (rate base) it invests in generation, transmission and distribution; growth comes from rate-base additions (data centers, industrial reshoring, electrification) approved by state commissions, not from competitive market share.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (outputs/Q15_triage.json) scored SO quality 5/5, growth 3/5, price-vs-growth 3/5, citing scale, diversification and credit quality with Vogtle risk resolved. data/b1_live_scores.csv shows SO composite decile 2 / quintile 1 (i.e., near the bottom of the live-scored universe on the systematic factor model — model rank 400 of the ranked names), driven by weak momentum (pct_mom_12_1 ≈ 0.31) and value that is only mid-pack (pct_ep ≈ 0.57, pct_fcfp ≈ 0.18 — SO screens as FCF-negative on a trailing accruals basis because of heavy capex, common for utilities and not itself a red flag). Data conflict: the systematic model ranks SO near the bottom of the scored universe (decile 2) while the qualitative triage advanced it on quality/scale — this is consistent with the known limitation that value/quality factor scores penalize capital-intensive utilities for low trailing FCF and low momentum, not with a fundamental problem; durable growth driver (data-center demand in Georgia) is not visible to the point-in-time factor model at all. dossiers.SOLV:
SOLV — Solventum Corporation (F144, wave 8 standard diligence)

1. Verdict: WATCH, 12–24 month horizon. The cheap-looking 12.4x NTM P/E rests on adjusted EPS that flatters cash earnings. The Q2 2026 "raise" is mostly a one-off tariff refund, the quarter was inflated by customers ordering early, the free cash flow guide is only $200-300M, and a litigation accrual was raised with no amount disclosed. The triage said not to advance and cited 4.3x leverage; I confirm the not-now call but correct the leverage and litigation details. What would change it: two clean quarters after the Q3 pull-forward reversal, free cash flow above about 50% of adjusted net income, and a quantified Bair Hugger liability.

One-line thesis: A former 3M medical-supplies and software business, cutting costs and splitting off its health-IT arm, whose reported profit is well ahead of the cash it produces.

2. Business in plain English

Solventum sells wound-care dressings, surgical and infection-prevention products, dental materials and health-information software to hospitals, dentists and clinics. It was spun out of 3M in April 2024, sold its Purification and Filtration unit on 1 Sep 2025 for about $4B cash (10-Q), and on 5 Aug 2026 announced it intends to separate Health Information Systems (HIS, about $354M a quarter of sales). Moat: installed base and clinical relationships in wound care and infection prevention; growth is low single digit.

b1/d4 flags low multiple (12.4x NTM P/E) and FY26 EPS growth of 16.9% (consensus). That is the artefact: FY26 guided adjusted EPS includes about $0.46 of one-off tariff refund (my estimate: $100M pre-tax at about 20% assumed tax over 173.3M diluted shares). Consensus FY27 growth is only 1.2% (d4), which is what the model's own forward growth shows once the one-off is in the base.

My base case is 4% FCF growth because conversion to 75% is unproven (FY25 FCF was negative). Implied is above base.

Scenarios, 3-year annualised total return: bear -9.2%, base +7.1%, bull +18.0%. Basis: start FY26E underlying adjusted EPS $6.69 (guide midpoint $7.15 less $0.46 tariff refund), growth 0% / 6% / 10% a year to FY30E, exit NTM P/E 10x / 13x / 15x, no dividend; buybacks inside the growth rate.

8. Bull and bear

Bull: (1) Transform for the Future cost programme (about $500M a year when complete); (2) separation of HIS could unlock value and sharpen focus; (3) underlying organic growth of about 3.7% with margin gains. Bear: (1) Q3 sales will be "negatively impacted" by reversal of $125M of early orders; (2) Bair Hugger accrual raised with no disclosed amount, plus PFAS responsibility; (3) FCF of $200-300M does not support the buyback pace or $5.1B debt.

  2. FY26 free cash flow below $200M (guide: $200M-$300M).
