  • M&A: growing via bolt-on acquisitions contributing ~5 points of the Q2 2026 growth rate (not separately itemized by name/size in the sources reviewed for this dossier — a scope limitation).
  • Capex: rising sharply to fund capacity expansion — $112.6m in Q1 2026 alone (vs. $36.5m a year earlier), consistent with management's commentary on adding manufacturing capacity to meet backlog demand; this is capacity investment, not distress capex.

7. Valuation snapshot — no V1 row; own reverse DCF

No systematic V1 valuation row exists for VRT; v1_verdict is null in the summary JSON per program convention.

Quant snapshot (d4, as of 2026-09-25 close $253.28): trailing P/E 57.2x, NTM P/E ≈27.8–29.7x (pe_ntm_qaware/pe_ntm), TTM FCF yield 2.8% (fcf_yield) — all consistent with the triage's own "57x trailing P/E, significant re-rating already happened" framing. Consensus targets: mean $338.22, range $236–427 (27 analysts, "strong buy" average) — note several sell-side price targets were cut after the Q2 2026 miss (e.g., one cited target moved from $461 to $427), a live, dated repricing event.

Own reverse DCF (10-year explicit FCF growth + 2.5% terminal growth, 9.5% discount rate — a wider spread than BR/LDOS given VRT's higher beta, 2.075, and the AI-capex-cycle concentration risk): solving EV = $94,665m for a constant annual FCF growth rate on a $2,697m (TTM) FCF base implies ≈14.3%/year for ten years.

Setting the base case (the key judgment call in this dossier): VRT's own FY2026 guidance calls for ~31% organic growth this year, but a 10-year constant-growth reverse DCF should be compared against a decelerating growth path, not a single-year peak. Management's own long-term target (margins expanding toward 25% by 2029, per company disclosure cited in the triage) implies a deceleration profile: very high growth near-term (2026–27), moderating toward high-single/low-double-digit growth by the back half of the decade as the AI-data-center buildout matures and book-to-bill normalizes from today's 2.9x. A reasonable, explicit base-case path — 30% (2027) → 20% (2028) → 14% (2029) → 10% and stable thereafter — averages to roughly 11–12%/year over ten years [Corrected 2026-10-08: the stated path (30%, 20%, 14%, then 10% for seven years) compounds to about 13.2%/yr over ten years, not 11-12%; the gap to the 14.3% implied is about 1 point, not 2-3]. Against that, the market's implied 14.3%/year is modestly above this dossier's base case: the price already assumes the deceleration is gentler, or the near-term growth rate more persistent, than the evidence (2.9x unsustainable book-to-bill, a just-missed quarter, explicit hyperscaler-capex-pause commentary from analysts) comfortably supports.

Bear/base/bull cases (own construction, 3-year horizon, exit-multiple method): - Bear: adjusted EPS declines at −5%/year over three years (a hyperscaler-capex-pause/order-digestion scenario following the unsustainable 2.9x book-to-bill), exit multiple compresses to 18x NTM (a hard de-rate from today's ~28–30x toward a normalized industrial-tech multiple) → EPS ≈$7.85, price ≈$141.4, annualised total return ≈−17.6%. - Base: adjusted EPS growth decelerates to 20%/year (from the current 50–60%+ pace, as book-to-bill normalizes but backlog conversion continues), exit multiple de-rates modestly to 24x (still a premium multiple, reflecting a genuine structural AI-infrastructure winner) → EPS ≈$15.83, price ≈$379.9, annualised total return ≈+14.5%. - Bull: adjusted EPS growth 30%/year (the AI-infrastructure supercycle continues without a meaningful pause, power-constraint bottlenecks resolve in Vertiv's favor as a supplier), exit multiple re-rates to 30x → EPS ≈$20.12, price ≈$603.7, annualised total return ≈+33.6%.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull (3): 1. Backlog of $15bn (+109% YoY) and a Q2 2026 book-to-bill still-strong at a normalizing-but-elevated level, alongside FY2026 guidance raised at every release this year (including the quarter that missed on headline revenue), are real, filed evidence that demand for AI-data-center power/cooling infrastructure remains exceptionally strong. 2. Free cash flow conversion is now excellent and the company reached a net-cash position in Q2 2026 for the first time — a rapidly de-risking balance sheet funding continued capacity expansion (capex up >3x YoY) without external financing. 3. Adjusted operating margin expanded ~400–430bps YoY in both of the last two quarters, evidence of genuine operating leverage and pricing power (management noted favorable price-cost execution overcoming tariff concerns), not merely a volume story.

Bear (3): 1. The Q2 2026 revenue miss (reported vs. consensus, ~3% shortfall) triggered a stock decline of up to 26% in a single session and multiple plaintiff-law-firm "investor alert" solicitations (Schall, Hagens Berman, Pomerantz) — these solicitations are boilerplate and do not by themselves establish wrongdoing, but the magnitude of the single-day price reaction confirms the market now treats any revenue shortfall, however small or "timing"-related, as a serious threat to the growth thesis at this valuation. 2. A 2.9x book-to-bill ratio is, by the company's own multi-quarter history (1.4x as recently as Q3 2025), extreme and plausibly unsustainable; a normalization would mechanically slow the backlog-growth headline even without any change in end demand, and roughly half of planned US data-center builds have reportedly experienced delays or cancellations industry-wide, primarily from power-infrastructure constraints rather than demand destruction — a risk that could show up as further "timing" misses. 3. Trailing P/E of 57x and an implied-growth reverse DCF modestly above this dossier's own base case leaves limited margin of safety: even the base case here (not the bear case) implies a mid-teens 3-year annualized return only because EPS growth is assumed to stay very high (20%/year) for three more years — a materially more optimistic assumption than BR's or LDOS's base cases in this batch.

  1. Organic net-sales growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from 18–31% currently), signaling the AI-infrastructure order cycle is normalizing faster than the base case assumes.
  2. Book-to-bill ratio falls below 1.0x for two consecutive quarters (from 2.9x currently) [Corrected 2026-10-08: baseline is stale: 2.9x was Q4 2025; the Q1/Q2 2026 releases give no book-to-bill], indicating backlog is being drawn down faster than replenished.

  4. A confirmed, named hyperscaler customer publicly announces a material pause or reduction in AI-data-center capital expenditure specifically affecting Vertiv's order book (distinct from generic industry commentary).
  5. Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x (from ≈0.09x currently) absent a disclosed, board-approved acquisition.

Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 24–48 month thesis horizon. [Corrected 2026-10-08: verification DV42: restated to WATCH because corrected implied growth exceeds the base case (see Correction section)] One-sentence reason: a near-monopoly cystic-fibrosis franchise generating 30%+ net margins is genuinely diversifying (pain, gene therapy, and now — via the just-closed $10B Crinetics acquisition — endocrinology), but the reverse DCF says the price already requires growth roughly equal to this analyst's base case, and the company took on its first meaningful funded debt ($4.5B) to do the deal, so this is a "hold with a named reservation," not a full-conviction add.

1. Business in plain English

Vertex sells small-molecule and gene-editing therapies for serious, mostly-genetic diseases. Its core franchise, the Trikafta/Kaftrio family of CFTR modulators, treats the underlying cause of cystic fibrosis in ~90% of the eligible patient population and carries no meaningful competition. It is now transitioning that base to a next-generation drug (Alyftrek) with a better dosing profile, while building three new pillars from a much smaller base: Journavx (a non-opioid pain drug), Casgevy (a CRISPR gene-editing therapy for sickle-cell/beta-thalassemia, with CRISPR Therapeutics), and — as of 1-Sep-2026 — an endocrinology franchise acquired with Crinetics Pharmaceuticals (Palsonify for acromegaly, atumelnant in Phase 3 for congenital adrenal hyperplasia).

2. Why the model likes it / is it durable

b1_live_scores.csv: composite percentile 0.295 (decile 3, quintile 2 — mid-pack, not a top scorer), live_rank 350. fam_M (momentum) 0.711 is the standout driver (mom_12_1 raw 0.390, a strong trailing return); fam_Q 0.375 and fam_V 0.302 are middling; fam_S (earnings-momentum/SUE) 0.330 is unremarkable given the FQ2-2024 GAAP loss (see §6) distorted the SUE calculation over the lookback window. The model's read (momentum-driven, not deeply undervalued) is consistent with what the filings show: real, filed acceleration in Alyftrek/Casgevy/Journavx revenue rather than a valuation anomaly. Durability of the core CF moat is not in question (no approved competing CFTR modulator); durability of the newer revenue lines (pipeline execution risk) is the actual swing factor and is addressed in §8/§9.

5. Moat, pipeline and secular drivers

  • CF franchise: durable, near-monopoly (no approved competing CFTR modulator); the risk is not competition but the market maturing — most treatable patients are already on therapy, so growth must come from label expansions (younger age groups), international reimbursement, and the Alyftrek upgrade cycle (a better once-daily dosing profile supports pricing/retention but doesn't expand the patient pool).
  • Diversification (real, but early and small): Journavx (non-opioid, FDA-approved acute pain) and Casgevy (gene-editing) are both still under $80M/quarter each — call-option-sized relative to the $2.5B/quarter CF base, not yet proof of a second growth engine.

7. Valuation — reverse DCF (no V1 systematic valuation row for VRTX)

8. Bull case

  1. FY2026 total-revenue guidance has been raised once and held (never cut) across three consecutive releases in 2026, on real filed acceleration in Alyftrek/Casgevy/Journavx.
  2. Four independent, non-overlapping growth vectors now exist (CF, pain, gene therapy, and — from 1-Sep-2026 — endocrinology) versus a single-franchise company five years ago; true platform diversification, not just marketing.
  3. Historically debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet even after funding a $10B all-cash acquisition largely from its own resources plus modest new debt — financial flexibility for further pipeline investment remains intact.

9. Bear case

  1. The core CF franchise (Trikafta/Kaftrio) is already shrinking in isolation (Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025: $2,497.2M vs. $2,551.1M) as patients convert to Alyftrek — headline growth is a substitution story, not incremental demand, and the substitution effect will mechanically fade once conversion completes.
  2. New, first-ever funded debt ($4.5B Term Loan A, closed 30-Jul-2026) plus integration risk on a $10B acquisition into a therapeutic area (endocrinology) Vertex has no prior commercial experience in.

  1. Combined Alyftrek + Casgevy + Journavx revenue growth (the "new pillars") falls below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from the current substitution-driven pace).

2. Business in plain English

Ventas is a healthcare-focused REIT that owns and (through operators) manages ~1,400 properties: the largest segment is senior housing (independent/assisted living, largely operated by third parties under RIDEA structures where Ventas participates in NOI upside — the "SHOP" portfolio), plus outpatient medical office/research buildings and a smaller triple-net/skilled-nursing book. It earns money from rents, management fees and its share of senior-housing operating NOI; growth comes from occupancy/rate gains in existing communities plus accretive acquisitions and development.

8. Bull case

  1. SHOP same-store NOI growth (+16% YoY, U.S. +18%) continues near current pace for several more years given genuinely constrained new senior-housing supply (multi-year construction lead times, high construction costs) against accelerating 80+ population growth.
  2. Ventas is redeploying at higher, accretive investment volume ($4.5B raised guide) into a still-fragmented senior-housing ownership market, with embedded operating-partner upside as more communities stabilize post-COVID.
  3. Balance sheet access is currently open (equity issuance funding growth at a premium valuation is accretive, not dilutive, to per-share FFO when reinvested above the cost of capital).

9. Bear case

  1. Leverage (5.3x net debt/EBITDA, consolidated) is above peer comfort and rising in dollar terms even as equity issuance keeps the ratio in check; a rate shock or funding-market seizure would hit this business harder than a lower-levered REIT.
  2. The 22x P/FFO multiple assumes SHOP NOI growth of the current magnitude persists; occupancy gains are a one-time normalization from COVID-era troughs and mathematically cannot repeat at 16–18% same-store NOI growth indefinitely — deceleration to high-single-digit growth (still good, but a big step down) is the base case for 2027+, and the stock has not obviously priced that in.
  3. Share count is growing fast (+13.7% YoY) to fund the investment program; if acquisition cap rates compress further, new deals become less accretive and per-share FFO growth could lag total-company FFO growth.

Verdict: INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight), 12-36 month horizon. Reason: at 47.08 (25 Sep 2026 close) the price implies free cash flow shrinking about 2% a year for a decade even after I strip out timing help, while a company that has raised guidance two quarters in a row is guiding to growth. Named reservation: leverage and cash-flow quality. Verizon is one of the three US national wireless carriers. Consumers and businesses pay monthly for mobile service and, increasingly, home broadband over fixed wireless (5G) and its own fibre (now 31 states after buying Frontier on 20 Jan 2026). Customers are sticky but switching and promotions are intense; wireless service revenue is guided "approximately flat" in 2026 while mobility-plus-broadband service revenue grows 2.5% to 3.0%. Moat is network quality, spectrum ($158.2B of licences on the balance sheet) and scale; threats are price competition, cable mobile resellers, and a heavy debt load.

Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corp / Wabtec (WAB) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F94, Wave 6, standard depth)

Recency gate: Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 10-Q (period end 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-22, accession 0001628280-26-049139). Checked for events to 2026-09-25 close (price $288.00, per b1_live_scores.csv 2026-09-25 snapshot).

1. Verdict

WATCH. Horizon 12–24 months. Wabtec is a genuinely strong duopoly franchise executing well — but the stock's own 12-month run (+43%, per triage) has already closed most of the valuation gap, and the reverse DCF implies growth close to (not comfortably below) what the company itself is now guiding. This is the "great business priced for what it can deliver, not for more" case — not a rejection of the business, but not a green light to add at 26.8x either.

2. Business in plain English

Wabtec makes and services locomotives, braking systems, signaling, and digital/analytics products for freight and transit rail worldwide, in a global duopoly with (predominantly) Progress Rail (Caterpillar) in North American freight locomotives. Over 60% of revenue is recurring services/aftermarket (parts, overhaul, digital subscriptions on the installed locomotive base), which smooths the cyclicality of new-equipment orders. It earns money on equipment sales plus long-dated service contracts tied to locomotive modernization and rail electrification/efficiency initiatives.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv (2026-09-25): composite decile 6/quintile 3 (mid-pack overall composite despite strong fundamentals — a genuine data point, not a typo: fam_Q 0.84 (strong quality — gross profit/assets, ROE, OCF/assets all in the top half), fam_V 0.61 (moderate — the stock is not statistically cheap), fam_M 0.32 (below-median momentum despite the price run, because the composite momentum window nets recent consolidation against the earlier rally), fam_S 0.20 (weak earnings-momentum/SUE score, i.e. the market had already priced in the beats before this window). Reading: the quality signal is durable (real duopoly, real recurring-revenue mix); the value and momentum signals say the easy money has been made and the model itself is not flagging this as newly cheap.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated, per 10-Q Q2 2026 balance sheet)

  • Cash + restricted cash (consolidated tag CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents, the tag WAB actually reports under post-2022 — plain "cash and equivalents" tag is not populated in recent filings): $670M (2026-06-30); $531M (2026-03-31); $789M (2025-12-31).

Price $288.00 (2026-09-25). 2026 adjusted-EPS guide midpoint $10.75 → P/E ≈ 26.8x on management's own adjusted number (higher still on GAAP EPS, since the adjusted-vs-GAAP gap noted above runs the other way for a full-year denominator). This is toward the high end of WAB's own multi-year range (WAB has more typically traded high-teens to low-20s P/E over 2019–2024) and at a premium to most multi-industrial peers, justified only if the backlog conversion and margin story both keep delivering.

Reverse DCF (qualitative): two-stage model, adjusted EPS₀=$10.75, cost of equity 9.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, 10-year explicit period → implied 10-year adjusted-EPS growth ≈ 8.8%/year to justify the current price. Our base case (backlog +42% YoY, guided 2026 growth ~20% this year but a cyclical freight-capex business that should decelerate toward high-single-digit/low-double-digit growth over a full 10-year horizon) is ~10%/year — implied growth is just below base, i.e. implied vs. base: IN_LINE (the gap, ~1.2pp, is inside our estimation error and does not constitute a real margin of safety). This is the quantitative basis for WATCH rather than INCLUDE: the market is pricing the stock almost exactly for what a reasonable base case delivers, with no cushion for the bear case below. [Corrected 2026-10-09: the reverse DCF used adjusted EPS as if it were cash flow; on free cash flow after stock compensation the price implies about 9.5-10.5% a year for 10 years, still in line with the ~10% base, so implied_vs_base and WATCH are unchanged]

8. Bull case

  1. Backlog (+42% YoY) provides multi-year revenue visibility rarely available in an industrial name; even if bookings slow from here, backlog conversion alone supports double-digit revenue growth for several more years.
  2. Recurring services (>60% of revenue) dampen the historical boom-bust cyclicality of locomotive capex, supporting a structurally higher multiple than the pre-2015 Wabtec/GE Transportation-era business had.
  3. Rail electrification/decarbonization and freight-efficiency mandates in North America and internationally are secular tailwinds for retrofitting the existing locomotive fleet, a high-margin services opportunity.

9. Bear case

  1. Freight-rail capex is still fundamentally a cyclical, rail-carrier-capex-driven business; a freight-volume downturn (recession, trade disruption) would hit new-equipment orders hard even if services hold up, and the stock is priced with limited room for that scenario.
  2. The Progress Rail/Caterpillar litigation settled in February 2026 without admission of liability — the underlying antitrust/breach-of-contract dispute (filed Q3 2023, U.S. District Court, District of Delaware) is closed, but it is a reminder that WAB operates in a two-player market that periodically draws competitive-conduct scrutiny; a renewed dispute or a genuine DOJ antitrust look at the duopoly structure (not currently pending, per this search) would be a re-rating risk.
  3. Debt has grown 64% in five quarters while buybacks have slowed — if backlog conversion disappoints even modestly, the balance sheet has less flexibility than it did 18 months ago, and at 26.8x P/E there is little multiple cushion for an earnings miss.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. 12-month backlog (the shorter-duration, higher-signal book) growth turns negative YoY (vs. +11.3% now) for two consecutive quarters.
  2. Adjusted EPS guidance is cut (not just held) at any quarterly release — the market has priced in continued raises.
  3. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.5x (vs. ~2.6x now).
  4. Freight-services revenue growth (the recurring, higher-margin segment) decelerates below 5% YoY for two consecutive quarters, signalling the "less cyclical" thesis is not holding.
  5. Any reopened antitrust/competitive-conduct litigation or regulatory inquiry involving the Progress Rail duopoly.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 release expected ~late October 2026 (historically ~Oct 22–23). Watch for backlog trend (bookings vs. conversion) and whether the 2026 guide raise cadence continues or pauses.

12. Red-flag scan

1. Verdict: WATCH (thesis horizon 12-36 months). An excellent franchise whose guidance has been raised at every step this year, but the 25 Sep 2026 price of $433.54 (about 29.8x the FY26 adjusted EPS guide midpoint) already needs about 9.7% a year of free-cash-flow growth for ten years, versus about 8% that organic growth, synergies and the BD Biosciences recovery support. Triage (Q04/Q06/Q08: "No", "digesting leveraged BD Biosciences merger", inorganic growth, integration/leverage risk) is confirmed on valuation and integration, but overturned on leverage: consolidated total debt of $5,086m (4 Jul 2026 debt note) against estimated EBITDA near $2.0bn (my estimate, not company-reported) is moderate, about 2.2x net.

2. Business. Waters sells liquid-chromatography and mass-spectrometry instruments and the consumables and service that run on them (recurring revenue), mainly to pharma, industrial and academic labs. Since 9 Feb 2026 it also owns BD's Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses (reverse Morris Trust; BD shareholders received 38.5m new shares, about 39.2% of the company, 10-Q Note 4). Lead indicators (same releases): 12-month subscription backlog growth 17.6%, 15.8%, 15.5%, 14.2% and total subscription backlog growth 17.0%, 12.2%, 10.9%, 8.0% for FQ3 2026 through FQ2 2027 (early figures include the Paradox and Sana acquisitions). The GAAP tax benefit of $1.52 a share came from "an intra-entity transfer of certain intellectual property rights as part of an internal legal entity restructuring" (release); excluding it GAAP EPS was about $1.05.

5. Guidance track record (verbatim from each 8-K Ex. 99.1, "Financial Outlook"). - FQ2 2027, 27 Aug 2026 (0001327811-26-000042): FY2027 "Subscription revenues of $9.940 billion to $9.950 billion, representing growth of 13%" and "Non-GAAP operating margin of 31.0%"; FQ3 "Subscription revenues of $2.515 billion, representing growth of 12%" and "Non-GAAP operating margin of 30.0%". Versus prior: revenue range narrowed up ($9.925-9.950B to $9.940-9.950B, midpoint +$7.5M, against a $16M FQ2 beat), margin raised 30.5% to 31.0%. Reiterated 29 Sep 2026 (8-K 0001327811-26-000048, after my 25 Sep cut-off). - FQ1 2027, 21 May 2026 (0001327811-26-000024): FY2027 "Subscription revenues of $9.925 billion to $9.950 billion, representing growth of 12% to 13%", "Non-GAAP operating margin of 30.5%" (from 30.0%); CFO: "We are reiterating our fiscal 2027 subscription revenue outlook of $9.925 billion to $9.950 billion, while increasing our fiscal 2027 non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 30.5%." FQ1 guide was $2.335B; actual $2.354B. - FQ4 2026, 24 Feb 2026 (0001327811-26-000010): initial FY2027 "Subscription revenues of $9.925 billion to $9.950 billion, representing growth of 12% to 13%" and "Non-GAAP operating margin of 30.0%"; FQ1 "$2.335 billion, representing growth of 13%" and 30.5% margin (actual 31.8%). - FQ3 2026, 25 Nov 2025 (0001327811-25-000196): FY2026 "Subscription revenues of $8.828 billion, representing growth of 14.4%" and "Non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 29%"; FQ4 "Subscription revenues of $2.355 billion" and "at least 28.5%". Actual FQ4 $2.360B and 30.6%; FY2026 actual $8.833B. The prior FY2026 range was not opened. Pattern: small beats every quarter (about $5M to $19M on subscription revenue, 110 to 130 bp on margin in the last two quarters); the full-year revenue range is essentially flat since February ("$9.925 billion to $9.950 billion" to "$9.940 billion to $9.950 billion"), margin raised twice (30.0%, 30.5%, 31.0%). Growth is being held, not accelerated, while the margin is bought with restructuring (2% of staff cut in Feb 2026, $135M of charges; about 2.5% cut announced 29 Sep 2026, $65-80M).

6. Earnings quality and balance sheet (entity: consolidated Workday at 31 Jul 2026, 10-Q; all debt is parent-level senior notes). Consolidated cash and equivalents $661M plus marketable securities $2,742M = $3,403M (down from $6,840M at 31 Oct 2025 and $5,443M at 31 Jan 2026); debt carrying value $2,989M (current $999M, the $1.0B 3.500% notes due 1 Apr 2027, plus noncurrent $1,990M: $750M 3.700% due 2029 and $1.25B due 2032; principal $3.0B); net cash about $0.4B; $1.0B undrawn revolver; consolidated stockholders' equity $6,460M. Cash conversion: TTM operating cash flow $3,082M, capex $238M, FCF $2,844M, far above GAAP earnings (FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $2.59). Stock compensation TTM about $1,646M (16.2% of revenue; $462M or 17.4% in FQ2 2027), so FCF after stock compensation is about $1,198M (11.8% of TTM revenue $10,155M). Buybacks were $2,924M in H1 FY2027 (2.7 times H1 free cash flow of $1,076M) and cut the diluted share count 8.8% year on year, but the authorization was "fully completed with no authorization remaining" at 31 Jul 2026 and a new $4.0B was added in August; at that pace cash runs out, so buybacks will slow toward free cash flow. Other: deferred tax assets $1,129M (up $300M after the IP restructuring); acquisitions Paradox and Sana closed in FY2026.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1. V1 has no row for WDAY (valuation table checked), so v1_verdict is null. Price $189.45 (25 Sep 2026 close); about 241M shares (196M Class A + 45M Class B, 10-Q cover) gives a market cap of $45.7B and enterprise value of about $45.3B. On company-defined FCF: 6.2% yield; after stock compensation: 2.6%. Non-GAAP: 18.6x TTM non-GAAP EPS of $10.20 (sum of the last four quarters) and 15.3x my NTM estimate of $12.4 (aggregator consensus FY2027 $11.08, FY2028 $13.23; cross-check only). GAAP TTM EPS $4.91 (aggregator). EV to sales 4.5x.

Reverse DCF (9% discount rate, 3% terminal, ten years, start = free cash flow after stock compensation $1.198B, EV $45.25B): the price requires that measure to grow about 13.3% a year for ten years (15.7% at a 10% discount rate), equivalent to reaching roughly $4.2B by year 10. Using company-defined FCF without charging stock compensation it would need only 2% growth, which is why I do not use it. My cases: base revenue growth 12.5% fading to 6% (about 8.5% CAGR, revenue $22.9B in year 10) with after-SBC FCF margin rising from 11.8% to 18.5% (non-GAAP margin 31% falling toward 33% while stock compensation drops from 16% to about 11% of revenue): FCF $4.24B in year 10, CAGR 13.5%, PV $47.1B at 9% (+4% vs EV), $39.6B at 10%. Bear (AI seat compression: revenue growth falls to 4%, margin reaches 13%): CAGR 6.4%, PV $27.2B. Bull (revenue 13% fading to 8%, margin 25%): CAGR 18.7%, PV $69.5B. Implied 13.3% vs base 13.5%: in line. Street mean target $208.7 (38 analysts, low $92, aggregator).

8. Bull and bear. Bull: (1) "AI driving more than 25% of our new ACV and more than 5,500 customers now using at least one of our organic agents" (CEO, FQ2 2027 release) could turn Workday into a per-outcome AI platform; (2) margin expansion and buybacks compound EPS (non-GAAP EPS $2.75 vs $2.21, +24%); (3) 12-month backlog still +14.2%. Bear: (1) total backlog growth +8.0% and guided subscription growth of 12% point to single-digit growth within two years; (2) AI agents reduce headcount at customers, compressing HR and finance seat counts; (3) stock compensation of $1.6B a year and repeated restructuring (Feb 2026 and Sep 2026) suggest margin gains are partly cost cuts rather than growth.

9. Key risks and kill criteria. 1. Total subscription revenue backlog growth below 5% year on year at any quarter-end (8.0% at 31 Jul 2026). 2. Full-year FY2027 subscription revenue guidance cut below $9.90B (current "$9.940 billion to $9.950 billion") or quarterly subscription growth guided below 10%. 3. Free cash flow after stock compensation below $900M on a trailing-four-quarter basis (about $1.2B at 31 Jul 2026). 4. Stock compensation above 17% of revenue for four consecutive quarters (17.4% in FQ2 2027, 16.2% TTM). 5. Consolidated cash and marketable securities below $2.0B while debt principal of $3.0B remains (cash $3.4B at 31 Jul 2026), which would signal buybacks outrunning cash generation.

10. Catalysts. FQ3 2027 results expected about 24 Nov 2026 (estimate from 25 Nov 2025; not confirmed). Restructuring charges of $55-70M land in FQ3 2027 (8-K 29 Sep 2026). $3.0B notes: $1.0B due 1 Apr 2027. Annual Rising/Workday AI product news; CEO first full-year plan in February 2027.

11. Red-flag scan. Auditor Ernst & Young LLP; 10-K critical audit matter: revenue recognition (accession 0001327811-26-000014); no material weakness noted. CEO replaced 6 Feb 2026 without a reason in the 8-K sections I read; former CEO received $3.6M cash severance and accelerated vesting. Founder control (68% of votes). Form 4 scan since 25 Mar 2026 (my parse): co-founder David Duffield sold 2,189,103 shares (about $322M); President Robert Enslin 10,747 (about $1.4M); Gerrit Kazmaier 12,084 (about $1.6M); CFO Zane Rowe 12,000 (about $1.6M); CAO 2,503 (about $0.3M); no open-market purchases. CEO Bhusri did not sell. Litigation: 10-Q says "not at least a reasonable possibility ... of a material loss"; I searched the 10-K and 10-Q for the AI-hiring-bias suit (Mobley) and found no mention, so any exposure is not disclosed as material. Restructuring: Feb 2026 and Sep 2026 headcount reductions. Short interest 14.1M shares (about 5.9% of shares, d4).

dossiers.WDC:
WDC — Western Digital Corporation (Diligence dossier, agent F49, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–24 month horizon). Business momentum is genuinely exceptional and well documented in primary filings (four straight quarters of non-GAAP EPS beats above the high end of its own guidance range), but at the 2026-09-25 close of $456.81 the market is pricing in growth the historically cyclical HDD industry has never sustained for a decade. A great business, priced for a permanent supercycle.

2. Business in plain English

WDC is now a pure-play nearline (enterprise/cloud) hard-disk-drive maker — since the Feb-2025 spin-off of its flash/NAND unit (SanDisk, SNDK), WDC keeps only the HDD business. It sells high-capacity drives mainly to hyperscale cloud/AI-data-center customers, competing in a global duopoly-plus-one with Seagate and (in NAND-adjacent niches) Toshiba/Kioxia. Revenue is a function of drive capacity (exabytes) shipped and $/TB pricing; both have been rising sharply as AI/cloud data growth outstrips new HDD capacity additions.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 factor data (2026-09-25 snapshot): composite decile 10/10, live_rank 15/full universe, Quality family 0.77 (percentile), Momentum 0.97, driven by extreme 12-month price momentum (mom_12_1 raw 2.76, pct 0.94) and earnings-momentum SUE (pct 0.90). Quality/ROE readings (roe raw 1.06, pct 0.94) are partly an artefact: return on equity is inflated by the shrunken post-spin-off equity base and by non-operating SanDisk-related gains, exactly as the wave-3 triage itself flagged ("margin/ROE look inflated by post-spinoff accounting — verify"). Verified: true — see §6. The momentum and earnings-momentum signals are real and primary-source-confirmed (see §5); the quality/ROE signal is overstated and should not be read as "cheap quality."

The magnitude of the beat is also widening ($0.09 → $0.10 → $0.27 → $0.16), consistent with a business still under-forecasting its own demand/pricing environment.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet — READ THE ADJUSTMENTS CAREFULLY

Entity scope: all figures below are WDC consolidated (single reportable segment, HDD only, post SanDisk separation) from the WDC 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-04-03 and the FY26 10-K balance sheet (period 2026-07-03), both filed by Western Digital Corporation, CIK 0000106040.

  • The GAAP net-income surge is a one-time, non-cash, non-operating item, not operating performance. WDC retained an equity interest in SanDisk after the Feb-2025 spin-off and executed a "debt-for-equity exchange" (monetizing SanDisk shares to retire WDC debt) as SNDK's price rose on AI-memory demand. The 10-Q for Q3 FY26 (period 2026-04-03) reports, in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations, "Gain (loss) on retained interest in Sandisk" of $2,050M in the single quarter and a cumulative FY26 cash-flow-statement add-back of "(Gain) loss on retained interest in Sandisk (4,448)" for the nine months (Note: cash-flow statement, non-cash gain removed from operating cash reconciliation). Q3 FY26 GAAP operating income was $1,190M but GAAP net income was $3,205M — the ~$2.0bn gap is this single non-cash item, plus a further "Costs in connection with debt-for-equity exchange" charge of $545M. Use non-GAAP EPS ($10.22 FY26) for any valuation work; GAAP EPS ($24.28 FY26) is not representative of operating earnings power.
  • Debt has genuinely fallen, not just via the SanDisk swap. Per the Q4 FY25 release (2025-07-30): "we reduced debt by $2.6 billion" in that quarter alone (cash-funded, prior to the debt-for-equity exchange). LongTermDebtNoncurrent (10-K, FY26, instant 2026-07-03) = $0 (down from $2.485bn a year earlier and $5.68bn two years earlier); LongTermDebtCurrent = $1,052M. Total WDC consolidated debt is now ~$1.05bn, all classified current (matures within 12 months), vs. ~$7.4bn two years ago. This is a real and material deleveraging, only partly attributable to the SanDisk-share swap.
  • FCF conversion: FY26 free cash flow $3,511M vs. non-GAAP net income from continuing operations $3,943M → 89% FCF/non-GAAP-NI conversion, strong. Against GAAP net income ($9,424M, inflated by the SanDisk gain) conversion is only 37% — another reason GAAP earnings mislead here.
  • SBC: roughly $10M (gross profit) + $60–83M (opex) per quarter of stock-based-comp add-backs in the non-GAAP reconciliation ≈ 2.3–2.6% of quarterly revenue — unremarkable for a hardware company. [Corrected 2026-10-09: FY2026 stock-based compensation was $204M in total (10-K cash-flow statement), 1.6% of $12,919M revenue, below the 2.3-2.6% stated]
  • Buybacks/dividend: WDC initiated its first-ever quarterly cash dividend in FY25 ($0.15/share, paid 2026-09-17); repurchased $2,592M of stock over the nine months to 2026-04-03 ($672M in the quarter ended 2026-07-03 alone) under a $2.0bn authorization announced 2025-07-30 [Corrected 2026-10-09: FY2026 repurchases were $2,592M for the full year ($672M in Q4; nine months to 3 Apr 2026 about $1.92bn); authorization is $2.0bn (9 May 2025) plus $4.0bn more (2 Feb 2026), not $2.0bn announced 30 Jul 2025]. Dividend yield at the current price is negligible (<0.2%) — capital return is overwhelmingly via buybacks, funded by real (non-Sandisk) FCF.
  • Share count is rising, not falling, despite the buybacks — diluted shares outstanding grew from 323M (Q1 FY25) to 387M (Q3 FY26), because of convertible-note dilution and equity issued in the SanDisk separation; buybacks are offsetting dilution rather than shrinking the float.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

  • b1/d4 snapshot (2026-09-25): NTM P/E 19.95x (own-5–10yr-history percentile 62.3 — i.e. only moderately above WDC's own median, and almost exactly at the sub-industry peer median of 19.6x). On a simple P/E-vs-history-and-peers view, WDC does not look expensive. This is the trap: HDD is a cyclical, commoditized business, and current EPS is at an all-time-high cyclical peak (non-GAAP operating margin 44.2% in Q4 FY26, a record) — a "normal-looking" P/E multiplied against peak-cycle earnings is a classic cyclical value-trap setup, not a value signal.
  • V1 systematic valuation (v1_valuation_table.csv, row WDC): verdict "excessive"; implied growth/ROE figure 42.3%; own bear/base 3-yr annualised returns -57.5% / -21.1%; note "base 3y value below Street 12m low target" (i.e., V1's own base case is more bearish than even the lowest sell-side price target).
  • My own reverse DCF (two-stage FCF-per-share model; FCF0 = FY26 FCF/diluted share ≈ $9.24 [$3,511M ÷ 380M shares]; cost of equity 11.5% [b1 wacc_or_coe]; 10-year explicit growth, 3% terminal growth thereafter; solved against the $456.81 close): implied 10-year FCF growth ≈ 22.8%/yr. This is materially lower than V1's stated 42.3% figure — likely because V1's figure is derived from a different EPS/multiple base (possibly NTM consensus EPS, which the search-derived Street estimate of ~$22.9/share NTM implies a very aggressive continued sequential ramp beyond even WDC's own Q1 FY27 guide). I flag this as a data_conflict: my own DCF and V1's both land on "far above any defensible base case," but the magnitude differs (23% vs 42%), and I could not independently verify the NTM EPS consensus figure implied by V1's 19.95x P/E from a primary source — Street NTM EPS estimates for WDC are unusually dispersed (search found analyst 12-month price targets ranging $400–$1,050).
  • My bear/base/bull (10-yr FCF or EPS growth), evidence-based:
  • Bear (renewed HDD glut as WDC + Seagate both add capacity, NAND/QLC substitution at the low end): 10-yr CAGR ≈ 0–3%, similar order to the FY24 trough (WDC had operating losses as recently as the quarter ended 2023-09-29: -$596M operating income).
  • Base (AI/cloud demand visibility persists ~2–3 more years per contracted hyperscaler agreements, then normalizes to a typical cyclical HDD pattern): 10-yr CAGR ≈ 8–10%.
  • Bull (oligopoly capacity discipline holds, AI storage buildout runs longer than a typical HDD cycle): 10-yr CAGR ≈ 15–18%.
  • All three sit below both my own implied growth (~23%) and V1's (~42%). implied_vs_base = above. [Corrected 2026-10-09: the reverse DCF does not charge stock compensation and uses an 11.5% cost of equity not derived from the 5.17% Treasury; on FCF after SBC ($3,307M, $8.70 a share) the implied growth is 24-27% at Ke 11.5%-12.6% (programme Ke 12.59% = 5.17% + Blume beta 1.792 x 4.14%); implied is still far above the 8-10% base, so the call and WATCH are unchanged]
  • valuation_view_vs_v1.consistent: true (both conclude the price requires growth beyond a defensible base case), with the reconciliation note above on the magnitude gap.

8. Bull case

  1. Nearline capacity is contracted/"fully allocated" through 2026–2027 with hyperscalers (triage sourcing; consistent with WDC's own guide beats every quarter for a year).
  2. Genuine balance-sheet repair: debt cut from ~$7.4bn to ~$1.05bn in two years, first-ever dividend initiated, $2.0bn buyback authorization.
  3. Record non-GAAP operating margin (44.2%, Q4 FY26) shows real operating leverage, not just a pricing blip — if HDD oligopoly capacity discipline persists, margins could remain structurally higher than the pre-cycle 15–25% range.

9. Bear case

  1. HDD is a proven boom-bust commodity industry — WDC posted operating losses as recently as the September 2023 quarter (-$596M); a capacity response from WDC/Seagate (both are now investing to add nearline capacity) or a slowdown in hyperscaler capex could reverse pricing quickly.
  2. GAAP earnings and reported ROE are currently distorted by the one-time, non-repeatable SanDisk retained-interest gain (+$2.05bn in a single quarter) — investors reading headline GAAP EPS ($8.20–$8.21/quarter) are seeing a number ~2.3–3x the real (non-GAAP) run-rate.
  3. Litigation overhang: a jury awarded SPEX Technologies $316M (plus $237M prejudgment interest) in Oct 2024 for patent infringement; post-trial motions reduced this to nominal $1 damages (10-Q Note 14, as of 2026-06-16/2026-06-27), but both sides have appealed — the $316M+ exposure is not fully extinguished. Separately, WDC already paid/accrued $384M in FY2024 for the MR Technologies (MRT) patent judgment.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance for any quarter is cut (not just "in-range") versus the prior quarter's high-end guide — the trend has been beat-and-raise every quarter for a year; a cut would signal the cycle has turned.
  2. Non-GAAP gross margin falls below 45% for two consecutive quarters (Q4 FY26 was 54.4%; pre-cycle normal was ~30–35%) — an early oversupply signal.
  3. LongTermDebtNoncurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent (WDC consolidated, per 10-Q/10-K balance sheet) rises back above $3bn, indicating re-leveraging.
  4. SPEX Technologies appeal is decided against WDC and a liability >$100M is accrued (10-Q Note 14, Legal Proceedings).
  5. Diluted share count (WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding, XBRL) grows past 400M without a commensurate buyback offset, signalling dilution is outrunning capital return.

11. Catalysts & calendar

  • Next earnings: Q1 FY27, estimated 2026-10-22 (not yet formally confirmed by WDC as of this writing — investor-relations date TBC).
  • Quarterly dividend of $0.15/share paid 2026-09-17 (already past); next declaration typically alongside next earnings.
  • SPEX Technologies and MR Technologies patent appeals — no scheduled date found in the primary filings reviewed.

12. Red-flag scan

  • Litigation: SPEX Technologies (Central District of California) — jury verdict Oct 2024 for $316M + $237M prejudgment interest, reduced to nominal $1 on post-trial motion (Jun 2025/2026), both sides appealing (10-Q Note 14). MR Technologies (MRT) — $384M liability already recognized in FY2024 (historical, booked).
  • Accounting: the FY26 GAAP net-income figure is dominated by a one-time non-cash gain (SanDisk retained interest); this is clearly disclosed and reconciled by the company (not a red flag on disclosure quality), but is a red flag for anyone reading headline GAAP EPS without adjustment.
  • No restatements, no auditor changes, no material-weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed 10-Q (period 2026-04-03).
  • No pending M&A found.

WEC Energy Group (WEC) — Diligence Dossier (Agent F94, Wave 6, standard depth)

Recency gate: Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 10-Q (period end 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-04, accession 0000783325-26-000087). Checked for events to 2026-09-25 close (price $101.45, per b1_live_scores.csv 2026-09-25 snapshot).

1. Verdict

INCLUDE. Horizon 24–36 months. A regulated Wisconsin utility with a rare, real large-load (data-center) growth pipeline layered on top of the normal rate-base growth story, guiding 7–8% EPS growth through 2030 off a record $37.5B five-year capital plan — and the reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in materially less growth than that guide. The main watch-item is financing (heavy equity issuance), not the demand story. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: verdict restated INCLUDE-SMALL. The premise that the market prices 'materially less growth' than the guide rested on a reverse DCF that discounted EPS as if it were distributable cash; on dividends the price implies about 5.7% (CoE 7.8%) to 6.2% (CoE 8.0%) a year, in line with the guided 6.5-7% dividend growth. See the Correction section below.]

2. Business in plain English

WEC Energy Group is a regulated electric and natural-gas utility holding company serving Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan and Minnesota (main subsidiaries: We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service, Peoples Gas). It earns a regulator-approved return on its rate base (the capital it invests in poles, wires, pipes, generation and transmission), so growth comes from capital investment approved into rates, not from competitive market share.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1_live_scores.csv (2026-09-25): composite decile 5/quintile 3 (mid-pack composite, appropriately unexciting for a low-volatility utility), fam_Q 0.91 (very high quality — strong ROE, OCF/assets, low accruals), fam_V 0.43 (fairly priced, not cheap), fam_M 0.21 (below-median momentum — the stock has been a steady compounder, not a hot momentum name), fam_S 0.27 (soft SUE). Reading: the quality score reflects a genuinely stable, well-run regulated business; the low momentum/earnings-surprise scores are exactly what you'd expect from a utility that guides conservatively and delivers in-line — durable, not an artefact, but also not the reason to buy (the reason to buy is the data-center capital-plan growth layer, which the pre-registered quant model cannot see because it has no forward-looking, point-in-time analog).

Revenue growth is modest and weather/commodity-pass-through-driven quarter to quarter, as expected for a regulated utility (fuel/gas costs pass through to revenue without margin impact, so revenue growth is not the metric that matters — rate base and EPS growth are).

5. Guidance track record

  • Q2 2026 release/call (2026-08-07): reaffirmed 2026 EPS guidance of $5.51–$5.61, EPS of $0.91 in Q2 (up $0.15 YoY). No cut, no raise this quarter — a hold, which the addendum's "raised/maintained/cut vs. prior range" framework should record honestly as maintained, not spun as a raise.

  • Large-load/data-center pipeline: Microsoft plans >$20B of data-center investment in southeastern Wisconsin (up to 2.6 GW of load growth in the Milwaukee–Chicago corridor through 2030); Vantage Data Centers plans a Port Washington campus (1.3 GW through 2030, potential to reach 3.5 GW total). These figures come from the Q2 2026 earnings call as reported by Gurufocus/Motley Fool/Yahoo aggregation of the call transcript — primary-source 8-K/investor-day deck not independently re-pulled this pass, flagged as a data gap given how load-bearing these numbers are to the thesis. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: closed: the WEC 8-K Item 7.01 investor deck filed 4 Sep 2026 (acc. 0000783325-26-000099) confirms the 2.6 GW and 1.3 GW load figures, the $37.5B plan and the 7.0-8.0% EPS growth outlook]

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated, per 10-Q Q2 2026 balance sheet)

  • Cash: $50.0M (2026-06-30) — a utility deliberately runs low cash, this is normal, not a liquidity red flag on its own given committed credit facilities (not independently verified this pass).
  • Total debt (LongTermDebtNoncurrent $19,216.3M + LongTermDebtCurrent $1,413.5M + ShortTermBorrowings $1,934.1M, all consolidated, 2026-06-30) ≈ $22,564M. Net debt ≈ $22,514M.
  • Approximate consolidated net debt/EBITDA: operating income TTM (Q3'25+Q4'25+Q1'26+Q2'26) ≈ $2,315M; utility D&A is large and not separately isolated this pass (approximate, data gap) — estimated ~$1,400M D&A gives EBITDA ≈ $3,715M → net debt/EBITDA ≈ 6.1x. This ratio is not the right leverage metric for a regulated utility (which is why rating agencies use FFO/debt, not net debt/EBITDA) — company-communicated targets are S&P FFO/debt above 15% and Moody's CFO-pre-WC/debt above 16%, at issuer ratings of A-/Baa1 (holding-company level, per secondary-source aggregation of the plan disclosure — not independently confirmed against the rating agency's own release this pass, data gap).
  • Financing plan for the $37.5B capex program (2026–2030): ~$20.5–21.5B operating cash, ~$5.3–5.7B new common equity, ~$14.2–14.8B incremental debt. 2026 alone includes ~$1.1B of planned common-equity issuance to protect credit metrics — this is real, ongoing per-share dilution risk that directly offsets EPS growth from the capital plan; it is the correct lens for the "will 7–8% EPS growth actually reach shareholders per share" question, not a side issue.

7. Valuation snapshot

Price $101.45 (2026-09-25). 2026 EPS guide midpoint $5.56 → P/E ≈ 18.2x, in line with large regulated-utility peers (typically 17–20x in the current rate environment) — not a bargain multiple, but not stretched either given the visible capital-plan growth.

Reverse DCF (qualitative): two-stage model, EPS₀=$5.56, cost of equity 7.5%, terminal growth 3.5%, 10-year explicit period → implied 10-year EPS growth ≈ −0.8%/year to justify the current price (i.e., at these discount-rate/terminal-growth assumptions, the terminal value alone very nearly covers the price, meaning almost no explicit-period growth is being priced in). [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: wrong basis: EPS is not distributable cash (the plan retains most cash flow: $33.3B capex against $20.5-21.5B CFO). The dividend-basis reverse DCF gives 4.9% at CoE 7.5%, 5.7% at 7.8%, 6.2% at 8.0%, 7.5% at 8.5%] This is materially below our base case of ~7.5%/year (management's own guided 7–8% EPS growth through 2030). Implied vs. base: BELOW, with a wide margin — the largest gap of the three names in this batch. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: now IN LINE, not below; there is no wide margin of safety at the 25 Sep price of $101.45] Caveat: this result is sensitive to the discount-rate/terminal-growth spread (only 400bps here); at a more conventional 8.5% cost of equity / 3% terminal growth, implied growth rises to a still-comfortably-below-base ~3–4%/year. Either way, the direction (implied below base) holds, which is what drives the INCLUDE verdict, but the formal valuation agent should re-run this with a tighter discount-rate assumption before finalizing sizing.

8. Bull case

  1. The data-center large-load pipeline (Microsoft, Vantage) is contracted/announced, not speculative, and adds a genuine second growth engine on top of normal regulated rate-base growth, unlike most utility "growth stories" that are just capex reclassification.
  2. 7–8% guided EPS growth through 2030 is well above the typical 5–7% regulated-utility range, and the reverse DCF says the market isn't paying up for even the low end of that. [Corrected 5 Oct 2026: on a dividend basis the price implies roughly the low-to-middle of the guided range, not less than the low end]
  3. A-/Baa1-area credit profile (if confirmed) with explicit FFO/debt targets signals management is managing the balance sheet proactively rather than reactively, reducing the odds of a forced, dilutive equity raise beyond the planned $5.3–5.7B.

9. Bear case

  1. The financing plan requires ~$1.1B/year of equity issuance at a fairly modest ~18x P/E — if the stock re-rates down for any reason, equity becomes more dilutive per dollar raised, creating a negative feedback loop common to capital-intensive utility growth stories.
  2. Large-load/data-center demand forecasts (2.6 GW, 3.5 GW, etc.) are 2030-horizon planning figures from the company's own investor materials; data-center buildout plans nationally have seen delays and cancellations at other utilities and hyperscalers when power availability, cost, or AI-capex priorities shift — this is a forecast, not a signed, fully in-service load.
  3. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (~6x, though not the ideal metric for this sector) and the sheer size of the incremental debt load ($14.2–14.8B over five years) raise the stakes on execution; a rate-case setback in any of the four state jurisdictions would compress the return on the capital plan.

10. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Full-year EPS guidance is cut (vs. maintained/raised) at any quarterly release.
  2. Announced large-load (data-center) capacity commitments are reduced or cancelled by Microsoft, Vantage, or another named large customer.
  3. A rating agency downgrades WEC or a material subsidiary below the current A-/Baa1-area profile, or FFO/debt falls below the stated 15% (S&P) / 16% (Moody's, CFO-pre-WC basis) targets for two consecutive reporting periods.
  4. Common-equity issuance in a given year exceeds the guided $5.3–5.7B five-year total pace by >25%, signalling the capital plan is outrunning organic financing capacity.
  5. Any adverse rate-case order in Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, or Mininois [sic Minnesota] that reduces the authorized ROE below ~9.5% or disallows a material portion of planned capex.

11. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: Q3 2026 release expected early November 2026 (historically ~Oct 31–Nov 1). No auditor change, restatement, going-concern language, SEC/DOJ investigation, or short-seller report identified in this pass's searches. dossiers.WELL:
Welltower Inc. (WELL) — Diligence Dossier (F32, standard depth)

1. Verdict

WATCH, not INCLUDE. Thesis horizon 12–24 months (re-underwrite when either the price or the growth catches up to the other). One-sentence reason: this is a genuinely excellent, demographically-favored senior-housing REIT with real, accelerating growth — but the reverse DCF shows the price already requires that growth to continue near its current cyclical-recovery pace for a decade, funded substantially by heavy share issuance, which a conservative base case does not support; a great business priced for more than it can plausibly deliver is a WATCH, not an INCLUDE.

Thesis (≤25 words): Owns senior-housing real estate operated by top platforms, riding an accelerating 80+ demographic wave — priced for that wave to keep accelerating for a decade.

2. Business in plain English

Welltower owns healthcare and senior-living real estate — predominantly private-pay senior housing (independent/assisted living/memory care), plus outpatient medical and long-term post-acute facilities — and contracts third-party operators (e.g., regional and national senior-living platforms) to run the properties day to day. Most of its growth today comes from its Seniors Housing Operating ("SHOP") portfolio, where Welltower participates directly in the property-level NOI (not just a fixed lease payment), so it benefits fully from occupancy and rate gains as the post-COVID senior-housing recovery continues, on top of a demographic tailwind: the 80-plus US population is now entering its fastest growth phase in decades.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q14_triage.json) scored WELL quality 5, growth 5, but price_vs_growth only 3 — triage itself already flagged the valuation as the weak link, writing "39% revenue growth and 43% forward EPS growth are real... valuation is very rich (74x NTM) but not obviously disconnected from the growth path." The quant composite (b1_live_scores.csv) is more moderate than the quality/growth scores alone suggest: decile 5, quintile 3, live_rank 284 of 503, because the value family score is very weak (fam_V percentile 0.136) even though quality (0.706) and momentum (0.912) are strong. This is not a data conflict — the quant model and this dossier's own valuation work (§7) agree WELL is priced expensively; the disagreement, if any, is with triage's own softer read that the rich multiple is "not obviously disconnected." The growth itself is real and durable in direction (occupancy recovery + demographics), but its current pace (low-20s% FFO/share growth) is a temporary function of occupancy still recovering toward pre-COVID levels, not a structural decade-long rate — that distinction is central to §7's verdict.

Four consecutive releases without a cut. The board also raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $0.85/share (221st consecutive quarterly payment) alongside the Q2'26 release — a genuine, credible track record of execution, which is precisely why the valuation question in §7 is about price, not about the quality of the business.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Net debt/adjusted EBITDA: 2.36x (Q3'25) → 3.03x (YE'25) → 2.99x (Q2'26) — leverage has drifted modestly higher over the past year as the company funded a large, ongoing acquisition pipeline ($15.5bn of gross investments closed/under contract YTD through Q2'26, including a C$4.1bn Canadian acquisition, Amica Senior Lifestyles, closed just after Q1'26) but has stayed within a ~3x band, helped by ~$9.5bn of available liquidity. The dominant per-share dilution driver is equity issuance, not stock-based compensation dilution in the ordinary sense: diluted shares outstanding grew from 668.1m (Q2'25) to 737.96m (Q2'26), +10.4% in one year — funding growth substantially through new share issuance (a normal REIT capital-raising method, but a direct drag on how much of the aggregate FFO growth shown in §4 actually reaches per-share FFO, which is the metric guidance and this valuation both use). Separately, a real governance red flag: WELL's FY2025 stock-based compensation expense was $1.557bn (10-K, filed 2026-02-12), driven almost entirely ($1.409bn) by a new "Ten Year Executive Continuity and Alignment Program" under which the five named executive officers agreed to take only $110,000/year base salary through 2035 in exchange for a single, large, front-loaded long-term equity award (OP units). Activist short-seller Land & Buildings Investment Management published an April 2026 white paper, "Compensation Plan Hubris," describing this as "one of the most egregiously management-friendly compensation structures in public REIT history," citing easily-reachable performance hurdles. This SBC is a non-cash add-back excluded from normalized FFO (so it does not distort the FFO growth numbers in §4–5), but it is real economic dilution to long-term per-share value and a governance concern independent of the current operating momentum.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

Price (2026-09-25 close, d4_live_snapshot) $231.37; GAAP trailing P/E 103.8x (d4) / NTM P/E 74.6x (d4, as_of 2026-09-25) — both depressed by real-estate depreciation and normalizing items, not the right lens. Price ÷ FY2026-guided normalized FFO/share midpoint ($6.40, per the Q2'26 8-K ex-99.1 guidance) ≈ 36.2x — the economically relevant multiple, and still very rich by REIT standards (peer health-care REIT VTR trades at NTM P/E 124x per d4 as_of 2026-09-25, an even more extreme GAAP multiple, though its own FFO-basis multiple was not re-pulled this cycle). Dividend yield ~1.5% (post-hike per the Q2'26 8-K, $3.40 annualized ÷ price $231.37) — genuinely low for a REIT, reflecting the market pricing WELL primarily as a growth story rather than an income vehicle. Sell-side mean target $262.05 (+13%, d4 target_mean, as_of 2026-09-25). No V1 row exists for WELL (checked v1_valuation_table.csv) → v1_verdict = null; valuation view is independently derived.

Reverse DCF (normalized-FFO basis): EV = market cap $166.7bn + net debt (~$14.5bn, estimated from Q1'26 total debt $18.46bn less $4.7bn cash, adjusted for continued net investment activity into Q2'26; [Corrected 2026-10-09: reported 30 Jun 2026 net debt is $15.6bn (senior unsecured notes $14,295M plus secured debt $3,431M less cash $1,965M and restricted cash $132M; 10-Q acc 0000766704-26-000030)] disclosed leverage ratio of 2.99x net debt/EBITDA implies a broadly similar order of magnitude) ≈ $181.2bn; FFO₀ = FY2026-guided $4.72bn (shares × midpoint guide); WACC 7.7% (cost of equity = rf 4.2% + β0.76×ERP 5% = 8.0%; post-tax cost of debt ≈4.5%; debt weight ≈8%); terminal growth 3%. Solving for the 10-year FFO growth rate that reproduces today's EV gives implied growth ≈10.0% p.a. My evidence-based base case is ~9% p.a.: same-store NOI should decelerate from today's mid-teens/20%+ pace toward a structural mid-single-digit rate as SHOP occupancy converges toward (not indefinitely above) pre-COVID peak levels, plus continued but equity-funded external growth that, net of the ~10%/yr share-count growth seen over the past year, adds meaningfully less to per-share FFO than to aggregate FFO. Implied (10.0%) is at or slightly above this base case (9%) → valuation view = above base case [Corrected 2026-10-09: reverse DCF applied a post-interest FFO stream to enterprise value and used rf 4.2%; on an equity basis with the 5.17% Treasury the implied growth is about 11.5% (about 13.4% after deducting about $0.6bn of recurring capex), versus the 9% base; the call stays above base] — the price already requires the current cyclical growth rate to persist for a full decade, which the demographic story supports directionally but the occupancy-recovery arithmetic and dilution rate do not support at this magnitude. Bear case 3%/yr (occupancy recovery stalls or new senior-housing supply returns, heavy dilution continues eroding per-share growth, exit multiple compresses to 22x — still a premium multiple, just less extreme): 3-yr annualized return ≈ −11%. Base case 9%/yr, exit multiple 30x (partial de-rating from today's 36x as growth normalizes): ≈ +4%/yr — barely ahead of cash, despite a genuinely good business. Bull case 14%/yr (occupancy keeps climbing, demographic wave intensifies, capital allocation discipline reduces the dilution drag, multiple holds at 36x): ≈ +15%/yr.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) the 80+ US population is entering its fastest growth phase in decades — a multi-decade demand tailwind for senior housing that is unusually visible and hard to derail; (2) SHOP occupancy, while recovering fast (+330 bps YoY in Q2'26), is still below pre-COVID peak levels, leaving genuine further room to run before the "recovery" component of growth is exhausted; (3) four consecutive guidance raises and a 15% dividend hike show real, credible execution, not just a favorable narrative. Bull risk turned bear: (1) the very same occupancy-recovery math that drives today's 20%+ same-store NOI growth is mechanically self-limiting — once SHOP occupancy normalizes toward (not perpetually above) prior peaks, same-store growth must decelerate toward a structural mid-single-digit rate, and the 10-year reverse DCF already prices near-term growth persisting for a decade; (2) diluted share count grew 10.4% in one year — a large share of "aggregate" FFO growth is funded by issuing new equity, which means per-share compounding (the only thing that matters to a holder) is running meaningfully below the headline growth rate once the acquisition pipeline normalizes; (3) the Ten Year executive compensation program ($1.4bn front-loaded 2025 charge, criticized publicly by an activist short-seller as management-friendly with easily-reachable hurdles) is a governance red flag that, while not affecting near-term FFO, signals potential future capital-allocation and incentive-alignment risk over the multi-year horizon this thesis requires.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Same-store total-portfolio NOI growth decelerates below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from 15.5% in Q2'26) without a corresponding guidance cut — signals the recovery has ended.
  2. Normalized FFO/share guidance cut (reduction to the low end of the then-current full-year range) at a subsequent release.
  3. Diluted share count grows more than 8% YoY for two more consecutive years, while per-share FFO growth falls below aggregate FFO growth by a widening gap (worsening dilution drag).
  4. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.5x (from 2.99x) without a stated de-leveraging plan.
  5. Price/normalized-FFO multiple stays above 30x while same-store NOI growth guidance for the following year is below 10% (i.e., the market keeps paying a growth multiple after the growth itself has normalized).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-26 (Q3'26, per d4 next_earnings_date). Watch for: SHOP occupancy trend (is it still climbing at the same rate, or beginning to plateau), the pace of further guidance raises (a fifth consecutive raise would be notable; a maintain would be the first sign of deceleration), and any additional disclosure or shareholder response to the Ten Year compensation program.

11. Red-flag scan

No auditor change, restatement, going-concern language, SEC/DOJ investigation, or material-weakness disclosure was found. Governance red flag (material, disclosed above): the $1.557bn FY2025 stock-based compensation charge tied to the Ten Year Executive Continuity and Alignment Program, criticized by activist short-seller Land & Buildings (April 2026 white paper) as excessively management-friendly. Historical short-seller allegation (older, judgment-based, not a fresh 2026 event): a separate short report previously alleged Welltower had offloaded troubled asset portfolios onto an inexperienced management firm to mask losses — this was not corroborated by a regulatory action in the sources checked this cycle and is flagged as an unverified historical claim, not a confirmed fact. Insider activity found: director share purchases in the $239–$242 range in August 2026 (a mild positive signal, alongside management's own large equity-comp stake from the Ten Year program). No fabricated or unsourced figures were used in this dossier.

12. Data basis, recency and disclaimer

Most recent period incorporated: Q2 2026 8-K ex-99.1 (filed 2026-07-28) for Q2'26 actuals and guidance; SEC XBRL companyfacts for WELL had not yet reflected the Q2'26 10-Q as of this research cycle (data.sec.gov companyfacts API, pulled 2026-09-26), so Q2'26 figures are sourced directly from the primary press release, not XBRL — disclosed as a data-recency limitation. FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-12) used for stock-based compensation figures. Events checked to 2026-09-25 (guidance history, governance/short-seller search). All figures are consolidated (US GAAP, single-entity reporter, no separate standalone statements filed). GAAP figures are labelled GAAP; normalized FFO is Welltower's own non-GAAP, NAREIT-adjacent measure and is labelled as such — never conflated with GAAP net income or EPS. Research only, not personal investment advice. This is research, not investment advice, and not a recommendation.

dossiers.WFC:
WFC — Wells Fargo & Company (Diligence dossier, agent F49, standard depth)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE (24–36 month horizon). A money-center bank that spent seven years (2018–2025) under a Federal Reserve-imposed asset cap is now growing its balance sheet again, with earnings, ROTCE and capital return all accelerating — and the current price still implies close to zero long-run earnings growth. No V1 systematic valuation row exists for WFC (bank valuation methodology differs; not run by V1) — this verdict rests on my own reverse DCF and primary-source fundamentals (§7).

2. Business in plain English

Wells Fargo is one of the four large US "money-center" banks — it takes deposits, makes consumer and commercial loans, and runs wealth-management, corporate/investment-banking and payments businesses across the whole US. It earns money on the spread between what it pays depositors and what it earns on loans/securities (net interest income), plus fees (noninterest income) from cards, wealth management, trading and investment banking. From Feb 2018 to June 2025 the Federal Reserve capped WFC's total assets at ~$1.95 trillion as a consequence of its 2016–18 sales-practices scandal; that cap is now lifted.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 (2026-09-25): composite decile 7/10, quintile 4, live_rank 155 (mid-pack, not top-decile — the wave-3 batch order groups quality+growth+price_vs_growth ties, not live_rank alone). Quality family percentile only moderate (fam_Q 0.57); the standout is fam_S (earnings momentum/SUE) 0.41 is actually modest, while the raw factor reveal is really about the valuation + growth combination: ep (earnings yield) raw 0.718 is high (pct_ep 0.85), bp (book/price) pct 0.89, alongside real, accelerating EPS growth (see §4). This is durable, not an artefact: it is the direct, primary-source-confirmed consequence of a specific, dated regulatory event (Fed asset-cap removal, confirmed via deposit growth in XBRL data, §6) rather than a cyclical or accounting one-off.

4. Last two years of results (calendar quarters; consolidated; source: 10-Q "Summary Financial Data" tables and XBRL companyfacts, CIK 0000072971)

5. Guidance track record

Wells Fargo, like most large banks, does not issue formal quarterly EPS or revenue guidance — confirmed by the absence of any point EPS/revenue guidance language in the reviewed 10-Qs and press materials. Management does discuss forward NII and expense trajectory qualitatively on earnings calls (not independently verified here at standard depth); no guidance-vs-actual table is therefore possible for WFC. This differs from the addendum's default expectation and is disclosed per its own instruction ("if the company gives no guidance, say so").

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Entity scope: all figures are Wells Fargo & Company consolidated, from the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (filed 2026-07-28), unless marked "Bank" (Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., the subsidiary bank) or "Standardized"/"Advanced" (regulatory capital approach).

  • Deposits (consolidated, instant, XBRL): $1,340.7bn (2025-06-30) → $1,426.2bn (2025-12-31) → $1,454.9bn (2026-03-31) → $1,501.4bn (2026-06-30) — deposits up +12.0% in the twelve months since the asset cap was lifted (June 2025), directly corroborating the triage thesis with primary-source XBRL data, not just a news summary.
  • Capital (consolidated, Standardized Approach — the company's stated "binding framework"): CET1 ratio 10.26% at 2026-06-30, vs. 10.29% at 2026-03-31 and 11.13% a year earlier (2025-06-30) — declining as risk-weighted assets grow with the balance sheet (RWAs $1,342.3bn vs $1,2xx bn a year prior), but still ~176bp above the regulatory minimum-plus-buffers of 8.50% (10-Q, Table 29/discussion, p. "Capital Management"). This is the expected and disclosed mechanism: WFC is now deploying capital into growth that the asset cap previously prevented.
  • Efficiency ratio improved to 60% (Q2 2026) from 64% (Q2 2025) — operating leverage from revenue growth (+9%) outpacing expense growth (+2%).
  • Credit quality: provision for credit losses $914M (Q2 2026) vs $1,005M (Q2 2025) — down, not up, despite loan growth; no deterioration signal in the primary data reviewed.
  • Capital return: quarterly dividend raised to $0.45/share (Q1–Q2 2026, up from $0.40 a year earlier, +12.5%), and the Board approved a further increase to $0.50/share for Q3 2026 on 2026-07-28 (10-Q, Capital section). $40bn buyback authorization (announced 2025-04-29, open-ended); $7.1bn repurchased in H1 2026 (84 million shares); common shares outstanding fell from 3,220.4M (Jun 2025) to 3,028.5M (Jun 2026), -6.0% in one year.
  • Book value per share $54.48 (tangible $46.13) at 2026-06-30, up from $51.13 (tangible $43.18) a year earlier (+6.6% / +6.8%).
  • No net debt/EBITDA metric applies to a bank; the relevant leverage gauge is CET1 (above) and the Tier 1/Total capital ratios, both also comfortably above regulatory minimums (Tier 1 11.38% vs. 10.00% minimum; Total 13.72% vs. required buffer stack) per the same 10-Q table.

7. Valuation snapshot and reconciliation with V1

  • No V1 row exists for WFC (v1_valuation_table.csv has no WFC entry — banks are likely excluded from V1's DCF/FCF-based methodology given the different capital structure). Per the wave-3 instruction, v1_verdict = null.
  • Market data (WebSearch, 2026-09-26, cross-check only): forward P/E ~10.3x (bank-industry median ~9.9x — essentially in-line with peers), consensus 12-month price target ~$95.86 vs. a price of $82.97 (b1, 2026-09-25 close) — ~15.5% implied upside on consensus alone.
  • My own reverse DCF (EPS-based two-stage model; EPS0 = annualized Q2 2026 run-rate $8.00 [$2.00 × 4] [Corrected 2026-10-06: annualising the best quarter overstates earnings: H1 2026 EPS $3.60 annualises to $7.20, TTM about $6.88]; cost of equity 10.5% [estimate: ~4.2% risk-free + ~6pt bank equity premium]; 10-year explicit growth, 3% terminal growth; solved against $82.97): implied 10-year EPS growth ≈ -1.0%/yr [Corrected 2026-10-06: method not appropriate for a bank and rates wrong (risk-free 4.2%; 10.5% not the programme's 9.1%); restated on P/TBV versus ROTCE: price implies a sustainable ROTCE of about 13.9% vs 16.1% delivered in H1 and 17.7% in Q2, see Correction section] — the market is pricing WFC as a slowly-shrinking, mature bank with no re-rating credit for the asset-cap removal.
  • My bear/base/bull (10-yr EPS growth), evidence-based:
  • Bear (NIM compression from rate cuts, credit costs normalize upward, litigation costs from AML/hiring-practice matters — §11): ≈ -2% to 0%/yr.
  • Base (continued balance-sheet re-leveraging post cap-removal at a measured pace, buybacks continue at ~4–6% share count/yr, mid-single-digit loan/deposit growth): ≈ 5–7%/yr.
  • Bull (multi-year catch-up growth phase deploying the capacity that was capped for seven years, credit costs stay benign, aggressive buybacks continue): ≈ 9–10%/yr.
  • All three sit above the ~-1% implied growth. implied_vs_base = below (cheap). [Corrected 2026-10-06: restated: implied sustainable ROTCE about 13.9% vs 15-16% base, still BELOW, with a thinner margin than a -1% growth rate suggests]
  • valuation_view_vs_v1: no v1 row to reconcile against (null); dossier_view = cheap.

8. Bull case

  1. Deposits +12% and RWAs growing in the twelve months since the Fed lifted the seven-year asset cap (June 2025) — primary-source XBRL-confirmed, not just a news claim.
  2. ROTCE 17.7% (Q2 2026) and efficiency ratio improving to 60% show the bank converting balance-sheet growth into profit, not just growing for its own sake.
  3. Aggressive, funded capital return: $7.1bn of buybacks in H1 2026 alone (-6% share count YoY) plus a dividend raised twice in fifteen months ($0.40→$0.45→$0.50), while CET1 still sits ~176bp above the regulatory minimum.

9. Bear case

dossiers.WM:
WM — Waste Management, Inc. — Diligence Dossier (Agent F72, Wave 4)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — 12–36 month horizon. WM is a high-quality, route-density/landfill-permit moat business compounding price ahead of cost, but the reservation is valuation: at 12.9x EV/EBITDA and a P/FCF near 22x, the market is paying a premium multiple for a business now digesting a large, messy acquisition (Stericycle/Healthcare Solutions) whose GAAP-to-adjusted gap has widened materially. Reverse DCF implies the price is not aggressive on FCF growth (see §7), but the multiple leaves little room for integration slippage.

2. Business in plain English

WM collects, transfers and disposes of solid waste for residential, commercial and industrial customers across North America, and increasingly recycles materials and captures landfill gas for renewable energy. It makes money by charging for pickups and, most profitably, for disposal in landfills it owns — permits a competitor cannot replicate at any price. In November 2024 it acquired Stericycle (medical/regulated waste), now reported as the "WM Healthcare Solutions" segment, adding a second growth leg alongside legacy Collection & Disposal and the newer sustainability (recycling/renewable natural gas, "RNG") businesses.

3. Why the model likes it, and is it durable?

b1 factor scores (data/b1_live_scores.csv, as of the live snapshot): composite 0.342 (quintile 2 of 5, live_rank 327/503) — WM ranks here on Quality (fam_Q 0.651, the highest of the three F72 names: high ROE 28.7%, moderate leverage) rather than Value (fam_V only 0.397; EP 3.5%, FCF yield 4.3% — expensive) or Momentum (fam_M 0.298, mom_12_1 only 0.3%, essentially flat trailing year). Triage (Q09) flagged the RNG/sustainability buildout as an "incremental growth vector beyond base waste collection." This is durable — route density and landfill permits are structural, and RNG facility completions are showing up in revenue (see §4) — but the quality score is partly an artefact of a low reported beta (0.203 vol_1y) that looks unusually low for a name carrying $23.4bn of debt; the composite does not know about the Stericycle DOJ matter (§11) or the widening GAAP/adjusted gap (§6).

4. Last two years of results (GAAP unless marked; source: WM quarterly earnings releases, Exhibit 99.1 to each 8-K, and FY2025 10-K)

FY2026 revenue growth is running mid-single digits organically: Q2'26 core price +5.7%, Collection & Disposal yield +3.6%, volumes roughly flat to slightly negative (intentional shedding of low-margin residential business).
