Earnings-quality flag: the GAAP-to-adjusted gap widened sharply in Q3'25 ($989m vs $1,241m operating income, a 25% adjustment) and stays elevated through Q1–Q2'26, driven by Stericycle integration/restructuring costs. This is disclosed and reconciled by the company, but a reader relying only on "adjusted" figures would understate how much of FY2025–26 earnings growth is integration-cost-driven optics rather than underlying operating improvement.

5. Guidance track record (last 4 releases; source: same Ex-99.1 releases)

  • Q3'25 (Oct 2025): affirmed FY2025 guide — adjusted operating EBITDA $7.475–7.625bn, FCF $2.8–2.9bn.
  • Q4'25 / initial FY2026 guide (Jan 2026): revenue $26,425–26,625m (+5.2% at midpoint); adjusted EBITDA $8,150–8,250m; FCF $3,750–3,850m (+29.4% at midpoint, mostly a step-up from lapping heavy 2025 Stericycle integration spend and completing sustainability capex).
  • Q1'26 (Apr 2026): reaffirmed the full FY2026 outlook as given at Q4'25.
  • Q2'26 (Jul 2026): CUT revenue guidance to $26,275–26,475m (a ~0.6% reduction from the January range) on lower volume expectations, partly offset by higher energy surcharges; adjusted EBITDA dollar range held at $8.15–8.25bn but margin guide raised 20bp (30.8–31.0% → 31.0–31.2%); FCF guide unchanged at $3.75–3.85bn. Net: a real, if modest, top-line guidance cut absorbed by cost control — not a "beat and raise" quarter.

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet (consolidated, GAAP; source: 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, filed 2026-07-29, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets and Note 2)

  • Debt: current portion of long-term debt $1,075m + long-term debt (non-current) $22,281m = $23,356m total debt; cash $557m → net debt $22,799m. Against FY2026-guided adjusted EBITDA midpoint $8.2bn, reported net debt/EBITDA ≈ 2.8x.
  • Sector-adjusted leverage (waste-environmental playbook): WM's own balance sheet carries landfill + environmental remediation liabilities of $3,569m ($244m current + $3,325m long-term, 10-Q Note 2, June 30 2026) — these are contractually mandated closure/post-closure obligations that standard net-debt screens exclude. Adding them lifts adjusted net debt to ~$26.4bn and adjusted net debt/EBITDA to ~3.2x. This is a normal feature of the sector, not a red flag on its own, but it means the "2.8x" headline understates true leverage by roughly half a turn.
  • Cash conversion: H1 2026 operating cash flow $3,227m vs H1 2026 net income $1,508m — OCF/NI ≈ 2.1x, strong, typical for a high-D&A capital-intensive business. Q2'26 FCF (WM's own definition, after both "capital to support the business" and sustainability growth capex) was $1,104m vs $818m in Q2'25 (+34.5%).
  • Capital returns: Q2'26 returned $1.04bn to shareholders ($659m buybacks + $379m dividends); H1'26 dividends paid $764m, buybacks $1,003m — capital return is roughly in line with or slightly ahead of H1 FCF ($2,024m through Q2'26), i.e. no unfunded distribution.
  • Share count: diluted shares roughly flat (403.2m → 402.4m over the trailing eight quarters) — buybacks are offsetting dilution, not meaningfully shrinking the share count.

7. Valuation snapshot and reverse DCF

  • Price (2026-09-25 close): $206.83; market cap ≈ $83.1bn; EV ≈ $105.9bn (market cap + total debt + minority − cash).
  • Trailing multiples (own calc, valuation.py): EV/EBITDA 12.9x (on FY2026-guided adjusted EBITDA midpoint), P/FCF 21.9x, FCF yield 4.6%, dividend yield 1.8%.
  • No V1 systematic valuation row exists for WM in outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv — v1_verdict = null, per the wave-4 instructions.
  • Reverse DCF (own model, scripts/valuation.py; WACC 7.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, base FCF = FY2026-guided midpoint $3.8bn — an assumption, stated as such): the current EV implies ~4.0%/year FCF growth for 10 years [Corrected 2026-10-09: this pairs a levered, after-interest FCF with enterprise value at a 7.0% WACC; on equity value ($82.7bn) against FCF after stock compensation ($3,625M) at the programme Ke of 7.73%, the price implies about 3.6% a year (5.5% at 8.5%), so the call 'below' the 6-7% base stands], fading to 3.0% terminal. This is a modest bar: WM's own multi-year algorithm (mid-single-digit core price, RNG/recycling ramp, Stericycle synergies, buybacks) plausibly supports a base case nearer 6–7%/year FCF growth over a decade. Implied growth is below my base case → "below." The EV/EBITDA multiple (12.9x) is not cheap in absolute terms, but the reverse DCF says the market is not pricing in the full extent of WM's own growth algorithm — consistent with triage's "attractive at 23.4x NTM P/E for this quality tier" read, though I'd frame it as fair-to-attractive rather than a screaming bargain.
  • Sensitivity: at WACC 7.5% (a reasonable alternative given WM's low reported beta of 0.203 looks understated for a levered issuer), implied growth rises to roughly 4.8–5%/year — still at or below a 6–7% base case, so the "below" conclusion is not razor-thin but is sensitive to the WACC assumption, which I flag as a genuine judgement call, not a precise number.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) Route density plus owned landfill disposal is a structural, non-replicable moat — no new large MSW landfill permits are being granted in most of WM's markets. (2) RNG and recycling investments are converting from capex to cash: three new RNG facilities completed in Q2'26 alone, adding to the sustainability EBITDA bridge management guides to $235–255m of growth for 2026. (3) Stericycle gives a second, less cyclical revenue stream (medical waste) with disclosed cost synergies still being realized (SG&A down on "synergies achieved from our acquisitions, particularly Stericycle" per the Q2'26 10-Q).

Bear: (1) The stock is not cheap on any absolute multiple (12.9x EV/EBITDA, 21.9x P/FCF) for a business now guiding down its own revenue outlook one quarter after reaffirming it. (2) The Stericycle integration is not clean: a related DOJ deferred-prosecution settlement (§11) and a persistently wide (20–25%) GAAP/adjusted gap suggest integration costs could run longer than modeled. (3) Sector-adjusted leverage (net debt + closure/remediation liabilities) is closer to 3.2x than the headline 2.8x, and WM's own volume trend is negative (Collection & Disposal volume -1.8% in Q2'26), meaning growth is entirely a price/mix story — vulnerable if commercial or industrial customers push back on 5%+ price increases in a softer economy.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (each, if it occurs, would invalidate the INCLUDE-SMALL thesis)

  1. Core price minus WM's own cash-cost inflation turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the sector's central "is the moat still working" test; not yet observed — Q2'26 core price +5.7% still comfortably ahead of cost).
  2. Sector-adjusted net debt/EBITDA (reported net debt + landfill/remediation liabilities, divided by adjusted EBITDA) exceeds 3.5x for two consecutive quarters (currently ≈3.2x).
  3. FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance (currently $8.15–8.25bn) is cut in dollar terms (not just margin-adjusted) at the Q3'26 (Oct 27, 2026) or later release.
  4. A material adverse development in the Stericycle DOJ deferred-prosecution matter (beyond the already-disclosed penalty) or a new SEC/DOJ inquiry tied to Healthcare Solutions.
  5. Collection & Disposal volume decline exceeds 2% for two consecutive quarters excluding the disclosed wildfire-comparison effect (i.e., volume loss broadens beyond the flagged residential shedding).

10. Catalysts & calendar

Next earnings: 2026-10-27 (Q3 2026, confirmed cadence from the last four releases; not a Yahoo estimate). No investor day disclosed in the reviewed filings. Watch for the FY2026 Q4 outlook-setting release (typically late January) for the first FY2027 guide.

  • DOJ/litigation (real, disclosed): Stericycle (now wholly owned) received a 2020 DEA subpoena and DOJ/California DTSC search warrants tied to its now-divested "ESOL Retail Controlled Substances Business" (2015–2020 conduct, predating WM's ownership). In May 2026, Stericycle entered a one-year deferred prosecution agreement with DOJ, paid the agreed penalty and settlement amounts, and remains subject to ongoing compliance/reporting obligations during the DPA term (WM 10-Q for Q2 2026, Note on Litigation). WM states it does not expect a material adverse effect, but this is a live, ongoing compliance obligation, not a closed matter, and it sits inside the same segment driving the earnings-quality gap noted in §6.
  • No auditor changes, no material-weakness or going-concern language found in the reviewed 10-Q/10-K.
  • No PFAS-specific disclosure found in the Q2'26 10-Q text (a sector-wide watch item per the waste-environmental playbook; absence of disclosure is not the same as absence of exposure — worth a follow-up read of the FY2025 10-K's full risk-factor section, which was not re-read line-by-line in this pass).
  • Financial assurance for closure/post-closure obligations is supported by letters of credit, surety bonds, insurance and a wholly-owned captive insurer per the 10-Q (Note 6) — a normal, disclosed structure, not itself a flag.

WRB — W. R. Berkley Corporation

Agent: F116 (wave 7 standard diligence). As of: 2026-09-25 close (WRB $66.82, mkt cap ~$26.0bn — stockanalysis.com, live retrieval 2026-09-27).

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL — best-in-class specialty P&C underwriter compounding book value at a low-teens rate through the cycle, but the market is now pricing in materially less growth than the franchise has delivered, and specialty/E&S pricing is softening, which caps position size. Horizon: 24–36 months.

2. Business in plain English

W. R. Berkley is a Greenwich, CT-based commercial property-casualty insurance holding company operating through two segments — Insurance (specialty/E&S commercial lines sold via independent agents/brokers) and Reinsurance & Monoline Excess. It makes money two ways: underwriting profit (premiums minus claims and expenses) and investment income on the "float" (premiums held before claims are paid). Its edge is decentralized underwriting through ~60 small, specialized operating units that price niche risks (excess/surplus casualty, professional lines, workers' comp, marine, surety) better than generalist carriers.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q06) flagged quality=4 but growth=2, noting "revenue growth has stalled to +1% and EPS is flat" as of the triage snapshot. That triage read is now stale: FY2025 net premiums written actually grew to $12.71bn (+6.2% vs FY2024's $11.97bn), and TTM diluted EPS growth is +10.9% (see §4). The durable quality driver is disciplined cycle underwriting (management has never chased top-line growth into a soft market) plus a growing, high-quality fixed-income book benefiting from higher reinvestment yields. This is a genuine, structural quality signal, not an artefact — the deceleration the triage saw was likely a single-quarter reading during a period when premium growth normally moderates late in a hardening-to-softening pricing cycle.

Reverse DCF (Gordon-growth on distributable earnings, since P&C insurers can return ~all of ROE-generated earnings via dividends/buybacks over time): using TTM operating EPS $4.80, price $66.82, and a cost-of-equity estimate of 10% (beta ~0.85–0.9 for a specialty insurer, risk-free ~4.2%, ERP ~7%): P/E₀ = (1+g)/(r−g) → 13.9 = (1+g)/(0.10−g) → implied perpetual growth g ≈ 2.6%. The market is pricing WRB for growth well below both its 2026 delivered rate and its long-run track record — implied growth is below our base case (base case: mid-single-digit to high-single-digit EPS/BVPS CAGR over the next decade, reflecting a moderating-but-still-hard specialty pricing cycle plus reinvestment-yield tailwind). This is a "cheap for the quality" signal, tempered by the rate-of-increase deceleration in §5.

8. Bull case / bear case

Bull: 1. Reinvestment yields on the $2.6bn+ cash pile and the broader ~$30bn+ investment portfolio continue to exceed the portfolio's ~book yield (stated explicitly in the Q2'26 release), meaning net investment income keeps growing mechanically even if underwriting flattens. 2. Combined ratio has stayed in the high-80s/89–91% range for eight straight quarters despite a softening rate environment — underwriting discipline is holding, unlike weaker specialty peers. 3. At 2.5x book and ~14x operating EPS for an insurer compounding book value in the high teens ROE, the reverse DCF shows the market pricing conservative (~2.6%) growth — upside optionality if the specialty cycle re-hardens (e.g., a large cat year across the industry).

Bear: 1. Quoted average rate increases (ex-workers' comp) decelerated from ~7.6% (Q3'25) to ~7.1–7.2% (Q4'25, Q1'26) — a genuine, sourced sign the E&S/specialty hard market is turning, which historically pressures forward combined ratios with a lag. 2. TTM net income growth is being flattered partly by record net investment income ($418.7m in Q2'26, +10.4% YoY) rather than underwriting alone; if rates fall, that tailwind fades. 3. A large catastrophe year (the Q3'25 release already disclosed $78.5m of current-accident-year cat losses in that quarter alone) could push the combined ratio above 95% and compress ROE sharply, as WRB carries meaningful cat exposure in Insurance and Reinsurance & Monoline Excess.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. Quoted average rate increase (ex-workers' comp) turns negative for two consecutive quarterly releases (currently +7.1–7.2%, down from +7.6%).
  2. Reported combined ratio exceeds 95% for any single quarter (currently 89.0–90.9% range over the last 8 quarters).
  3. Consolidated debt/equity rises above 0.40x (currently ~0.29x) without a stated strategic rationale (e.g., large M&A).
  4. TTM net investment income growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (currently +10–12% YoY).
  5. Quarterly net premiums written growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (currently positive every quarter shown above).

Next earnings: Q3 2026 results, expected ~mid-to-late October 2026 (Q3 2025 was reported 2025-10-20; no confirmed date found for Q3 2026 — treat as an estimate, not a quoted date). No investor day or index event identified in the filings reviewed.

1. Verdict

WATCH — thesis horizon 12–36 months. A genuinely high-quality, fast-growing supplier to injectable drugs: sales grew 13.8% in Q2 2026 (12.7% organic), 2026 guidance ("$8.85 to $9.05" adjusted EPS) has been raised at each release, the company is net cash and buying back stock. But at $370.44 the market price demands about 17% a year of free-cash-flow growth for ten years, against my evidence-based base case of 11% and a bull of 14%. Even the bull case sits under the implied rate, and my base three-year return is about 3% a year. It becomes INCLUDE-SMALL at roughly $310 or lower (base return of 9% a year), or if FCF compounds faster than base. Triage (Q07) said not to advance on price; the primary-source work confirms that, and adds a CEO handover (effective 31 Aug 2026), a May 2026 cyberattack and a mislabelled cash-flow figure in the Q2 release.

West makes the rubber stoppers, plungers, seals, syringe components and self-injection devices that sit inside vials and prefilled syringes for injectable medicines, and sells them to drug makers (biologics, GLP-1 and generics). It earns money per component or device, with premium "high-value" products (HVP) carrying better prices and margins; 49% of Q2 2026 sales were HVP Components and 15% HVP Delivery Devices. The moat is regulatory qualification: once a drug is approved with West components, switching is slow and costly. Bull: (1) Lumber and OSB leverage is large and the stock is a cheap call on it: each $10/MBF lumber = about $50M EBITDA, and Q2 lumber realizations rose 15% q/q; (2) timberland base, Climate Solutions (conservation easement $94M in Q1), the Monticello facility (start-up goal 2027) and the stated $1.5B EBITDA add by 2030 against a 2024 baseline are real optionality; (3) investment-grade balance sheet (BBB per S&P, 85% fixed rate, no maturity cliff, revolver undrawn). Bear: (1) FCF of $22M TTM (consolidated) does not cover a $606M dividend; the dividend is being funded by asset sales ($306M timberland proceeds H1'26) and debt; (2) leverage rose from 1.0x (2022) to 5.0x as EBITDA fell; Q3 Wood Products outlook was cut on Sep 24 and lumber has given back about $30/MBF from the Q3 QTD level; (3) 2025 EBITDA about $1.0B vs $1.3B, with Canadian softwood duties and mortgage-rate uncertainty outside management's control.

9. Key risks and kill criteria

  1. Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA (LTM, consolidated, company table "NET DEBT TO ADJUSTED EBITDA RECONCILIATION") above 5.5x at any quarter-end (Jun 30 2026: 5.0x).
  2. Base dividend cut below $0.21 per share per quarter, or Adjusted FAD below base dividends in four consecutive quarters (Q1'26 FAD -$58M, Q2'26 +$323M).

  4. LTM consolidated Adjusted EBITDA below $850M at two consecutive quarter-ends (about $0.98B now).
  5. Monticello engineered wood facility start-up slips beyond 2027 or 2026 capex exceeds the $400-450M range plus $300M Monticello stated in the Q2 10-Q.

Q3 2026 results about 2026-10-29 (estimate: d4 timestamp, flagged as estimate; no date confirmed in an 8-K); supplemental dividend normally declared in Q1; Canadian lumber duty reviews; Fed/mortgage-rate path; Monticello progress; Gallatin, TN distribution center start late 2026.

KPMG LLP is the auditor; the 10-K reports internal control over financial reporting as effective (one "material weakness" string in the 10-K is the generic definition in risk text; no weakness disclosed). 10-Q Note 10: "We are not currently a party to any legal proceeding that management believes could have a material adverse effect" (CERCLA/Superfund accruals disclosed). Reservation: leverage is elevated (net debt/EBITDAR ~4x on a pre-rent basis, higher on a post-rent EBITDA basis) and the September 2026 refinancing raises the marginal cost of debt (5.250% notes replaced by 6.875% notes), just as ~$1bn+ more is still to be spent on the unlevered UAE project. Xcel Energy Inc. (XEL) — Diligence Dossier

Agent: F50 · Wave 3 · Standard depth · As of: 2026-09-25 close ($69.80/share; mkt cap ≈$43.6bn per v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv)

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight). Thesis horizon 24–48 months. [Corrected 2026-10-08: verdict is WATCH after verification DV44: the reverse dividend model used the wrong dividend and growth objective; corrected, implied dividend growth is above the guided 4-6% (see Correction section)] High-quality, fully regulated multi-utility with a credibly funded $60bn five-year (2026–2030) rate-base growth plan and a clean four-release guidance record — but a previously under-disclosed Texas wildfire liability (Smokehouse Creek Fire Complex, still open, insurance headroom nearly exhausted) and leverage already near the top of the healthy band for its sub-sector are real, named reservations that the triage did not fully weigh.

2. Business in plain English

Xcel Energy is a holding company for four fully rate-regulated electric/gas utilities — PSCo (Colorado), NSP-Minnesota, NSP-Wisconsin and SPS (Texas/New Mexico Panhandle) — serving ~3.8m electric and ~2.2m gas customers across eight states. It earns a regulator-set return on its invested capital (rate base); growth comes from building transmission, distribution, generation and grid infrastructure that regulators allow into rates, not from selling more units. Competitive position is that of a monopoly franchise utility with no direct competitor for its wires and pipes.

3. Why the model likes it / is it durable

Q15 triage (v4/outputs/Q15_triage.json) scored quality 4, growth 4, price_vs_growth 4, citing "24% forward EPS growth at 15.8x NTM P/E." b1 factor data (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as_of 2026-09-25) shows XEL in decile 6 (mid-pack) with pct_sue=0.37 (moderate positive earnings-surprise momentum) and pct_ep=0.30/pct_bp=0.55 (unremarkable value scores, as expected for a fairly-valued regulated utility). The growth driver — rate-base expansion funded by a filed, board-approved five-year capital plan and reinforced by signed large-load (data-center) contracts — is durable and structural (secular return of load growth to a utility that had none for two decades), not an accounting artefact. The "24% forward EPS growth" figure in the triage note is not confirmed by the company's own guidance (see §5); management guides 6–8% long-term EPS CAGR off a $3.80 (FY2025 ongoing) base, which is the correct, durable read.

XOM — ExxonMobil Corporation — F59 diligence (2026-09-26)

1. Verdict

WATCH (12–36 month thesis horizon). ExxonMobil is the highest-quality, lowest-leverage integrated major with genuine multi-year production growth (Permian, Guyana), but roughly half of the last two quarters' earnings strength is a war-driven oil-price spike (2026 Iran war / Strait of Hormuz disruption) rather than the durable Permian/Guyana ramp the market is also paying for. On a normalized (pre-spike) FCF base the current close prices in ~4.4%/yr perpetual FCF growth (below XOM's own production plan) — cheap on that basis — but the trailing multiple (20.7x) and NTM multiple (14.2x) sit on top of an earnings run-rate that is not sustainable at post-war oil prices, and the analyst's normalized base case is closer to "fair" than "cheap" once the war premium is stripped out. This differs from the triage call (ADVANCE, quality 5/growth 4/price_vs_growth 3, "cheapest-in-class 14.2x") by adding the earnings-normalization adjustment triage could not do from a data card alone.

2. Business in plain English

ExxonMobil explores for, produces, refines and markets oil, natural gas and petrochemicals globally. It sells crude oil and refined products (gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, chemicals) to industrial customers, retailers and consumers. It makes money on the spread between what it costs to find/produce/refine a barrel and what the market pays for the refined product; its economics are exposed to global crude and refining-margin cycles but partly insulated by owning the lowest-cost production per barrel among its integrated-major peers (Permian shale, Guyana deepwater) and by vertically integrating upstream-to-chemicals.

3. Why the model likes it — durable or artefact?

b1 quant context (data/b1_live_scores.csv, live_rank 99/503, composite decile 9): earnings-yield percentile 0.28 and FCF-yield percentile 0.26 are unremarkable; the real driver is momentum (mom_12_1 = +47.9%, pct_mom_12_1 = 0.98, i.e. top-2% 12-month price momentum) and SUE (+6.6, near-maximum earnings-surprise percentile). Both of those inputs are largely an artefact of the same war-driven oil-price spike, not a durable re-rating — Q2 2026 EPS beat consensus mainly because Brent/WTI moved with the Iran-war shock (Brent low-$60s in late June 2026 → back over $100 by late July/August; EIA/OilPrice.com, CNBC 2026-07-31/2026-04-21). Quality-family inputs (leverage percentile 0.69, low net debt) are durable and real. Data conflict: b1_live_scores.csv's cik field for XOM is 2115436; the correct SEC CIK is 0000034088 (confirmed via SEC EDGAR company search) — flagged as a vendor-data error, not used for any filing lookup below.

5. Guidance track record

ExxonMobil does not give quarterly EPS/revenue guidance in the way tech/semis do; it guides capex and the buyback pace and updates its multi-year corporate plan. - FY2026 capex: guided $27–29bn, maintained unchanged through 2026 (Hudson Labs Q2 2026 preview; ExxonMobil Q1 2026 8-K, investor.exxonmobil.com). - Buyback pace: $20bn/yr in 2025, maintained at that pace through 2026 "assuming reasonable market conditions" (ExxonMobil IR). - 2030 corporate plan: raised Dec 2025 — cumulative 2030 earnings/cash-flow potential lifted by ~$5bn without raising capital spending; upstream production target confirmed at 5.5 mmboe/d by 2030, with "advantaged assets" (Permian/Guyana/LNG) rising to 65% of volumes (corporate.exxonmobil.com, 2025-12-09). This is a genuine guidance raise, not an artefact of the oil-price spike (published before the Iran-war price move fed through to results).

6. Earnings quality & balance sheet

Entity scope: all figures below are consolidated ExxonMobil Corporation (condensed consolidated balance sheet/cash-flow statement, Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-03, tables R5/R7 of the filing's financial-statement viewer). - Balance sheet (30 Jun 2026 vs 31 Dec 2025): Cash $10,588M (Dec-25: $10,681M). Total assets $464,482M. Net debt/annualized-Q2-EBITDA is near 0.3–0.4x and net debt/TTM-normalized-FCF (using FY2025 FCF, see §7) is ~1.3x — both consistent with triage's cited "0.5x net debt/EBITDA," among the lowest leverage of any energy major. - Cash flow (H1 2026 vs H1 2025, consolidated statement of cash flows): OCF $32,260M (H1'25: $24,503M); capex (additions to PP&E) $12,997M (H1'25: $12,181M) → H1 2026 FCF ≈ $19,263M. Buybacks (common stock acquired) $10,007M; dividends to XOM shareholders $8,633M — shareholder distributions ($18,640M) below OCF, self-funded. - FY2025 (full year, less distorted by the single-quarter war spike): OCF $51,970M, capex $28,358M → FY2025 FCF = $23,612M (10-K FY2025, filed 2026-02-18). This is the base used for the reverse DCF below because H1 2026 annualized (~$38.5bn) is inflated by the Q2 spike. - Share count: diluted shares outstanding fell from ~4.31bn (Mar-25) to ~4.14bn (Mar-26), a ~4%/yr reduction pace from buybacks — a real, durable per-share tailwind independent of the oil-price cycle. - SBC: immaterial for an energy major; no material GAAP-vs-adjusted gap outside the always-disclosed "special items" (asset impairments/identified items), which XOM breaks out by segment in its earnings release.

7. Valuation snapshot (vs V1: no V1 row exists for XOM — v1_verdict = null; d4 live snapshot as of 2026-09-25 close, calendarised)

Price $160.59 (2026-09-25 close), market cap $660.3bn, EV (filing-based net debt) ≈$692.1bn (d4's Yahoo-sourced EV of $705.2bn uses a slightly higher net-debt figure — a minor, disclosed data conflict, not decision-relevant). Analyst target mean $172.55 / median $174.50 (22 analysts) — 7–9% above spot. Beat-streak: 8 of last 8 quarters beat consensus EPS, average surprise +6.1% (d4 beats_last8/avg_surprise_pct_last8).

Reverse DCF (own construction; single-stage Gordon growth on normalized FY2025 FCF, WACC 8% for a low-beta, investment-grade integrated major, consolidated basis): EV ($692.1bn) = FCF₀×(1+g) / (WACC − g), FCF₀ = $23.612bn → implied perpetual FCF growth g ≈ 4.4%/yr. That is below XOM's own stated 2030 production-growth plan (5.5 mmboe/d by 2030 from a ~4.7–4.8 mmboe/d base, i.e. mid-single-digit volume CAGR) plus ~4%/yr buyback-driven per-share accretion — so on a normalized earnings base the market is not paying for more than XOM's own plan delivers. [Corrected 2026-10-08: wrong: 5.5 mmboe/d from about 4.7-4.8 mmboe/d is a 2.8-3.2% CAGR, not mid-single digit; buyback accretion is per share and cannot be added to total-firm FCF growth; the model also divides EV by levered FCF and assumes 4.4% growth forever. On the programme method (10 years then 3% terminal, equity $660.3bn) implied FCF growth is 6.9% at 8%, 8.2% at 8.5%, 9.4% at 9%: implied_vs_base is above; verdict WATCH unchanged] However, if the reverse DCF is instead run off the elevated H1 2026 run-rate (annualized FCF ≈$38.5bn), the implied growth rate falls to roughly flat-to-negative — i.e. the stock is only "cheap" if you believe the current war-elevated oil price is durable. My view: fair, not cheap — the 14.2x NTM multiple already embeds a meaningful chunk of the current elevated strip price; a return to the pre-war ~$65–70 Brent base case would compress both earnings and, likely, the multiple simultaneously.

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull (3 points): 1. Genuine, funded multi-year production growth — Permian output on a confirmed 9% CAGR path, Guyana ramping, 2030 plan raised in Dec 2025 without extra capex. 2. Lowest leverage among integrated majors (net debt ≈$31.8bn on $266bn equity) gives capacity to sustain the $20bn/yr buyback through a commodity downturn that would force peers to cut. 3. If Iran-war disruption to Strait of Hormuz flows persists or recurs, XOM's refining and upstream mix captures disproportionate upside (Q2 2026 showed the operating leverage: refining alone swung $6.8bn quarter-over-quarter).

Bear (3 points): 1. Reverse DCF off the actual H1 2026 run-rate implies close to zero further growth is priced for — i.e. much of the "cheap 14.2x" read is an artefact of using a spike-quarter EPS in the denominator; a real reverse DCF off FY2025 normalized FCF is closer to fair value. 2. Oil-price mean reversion risk is unusually high right now: Brent swung $61→$118→$70→$109 within 2026 alone (OilPrice.com; CNBC timeline, 2026-04-21) on a live geopolitical conflict — a ceasefire or de-escalation could reverse Q2's refining/upstream tailwind quickly. 3. California's SB253/261 climate-disclosure litigation (XOM is the plaintiff, suing to strike the laws down, E.D. Cal., filed ~Oct 2025) and the broader California AG climate-deception suit represent ongoing legal/regulatory tail risk and disclosure-compliance cost, even though XOM's own suit is offensive, not defensive.

9. Key risks & measurable kill criteria

  1. Brent crude average below $65/bbl for two consecutive quarters (a return toward XOM's own long-run planning price) without a corresponding capex cut — would invalidate the "cheap on normalized FCF" thesis.
  2. Quarterly refining segment posts a loss for two consecutive quarters (as it did in Q1 2026) — signals margin normalization is structural, not one-quarter noise.
  3. Net debt rises above $60bn (roughly 2x the current level) — would break the "lowest-leverage major" thesis that justifies holding through a commodity downturn.
  4. Buyback pace cut below $15bn/yr run-rate — a direct signal management no longer sees the stock, or FCF, supporting the current $20bn/yr distribution plan.
  5. FTC Pioneer consent order breach or reopening (five-year board-composition restriction on Pioneer-affiliated directors, through ~2029) — would reintroduce integration/antitrust overhang; currently compliant (FTC denied Sheffield's petition to reopen, 2025-07, ftc.gov).

1. Verdict

WATCH — the franchise economics (KFC/Taco Bell unit and margin growth, 60%+ digital mix) are genuinely strong and the Pizza Hut divestiture is a credible focusing catalyst, but (a) the balance sheet carries negative shareholders' equity and rising near-term debt, (b) a live, unresolved Taco Bell food-safety event (July 2026 Cyclospora outbreak) sits in the current quarter with no reported sales impact yet disclosed, and (c) the current price already implies growth close to the company's own long-run algorithm — this is not a bargain on the numbers in front of us, even though the business quality is real. Revisit after Q3 2026 results show whether the outbreak dented Taco Bell same-store sales and after the Pizza Hut sale closes (expected Q3 2026). [Corrected 2026-10-09: stale: the Pizza Hut sale had closed before the 25 Sep as-of date (China 7 Aug 2026, ex-China 1 Sep 2026); see the Correction section] Horizon: 12–24 months.

2. Business in plain English

Yum! Brands is the worldwide franchisor of KFC, Taco Bell and (until its pending sale closes) [Corrected 2026-10-09: stale: sale completed 7 Aug and 1 Sep 2026] Pizza Hut. It makes money almost entirely from franchise royalties and fees on system-wide sales generated by independently owned restaurants, plus a smaller company-owned restaurant base — a capital-light model that generates high margins and heavy free cash flow relative to its own invested capital, which the company has historically returned to shareholders via debt-funded buybacks (hence negative book equity; see §6). Its competitive position rests on brand scale (34,747 KFC units, 9,046 Taco Bell units globally per the Q2 2026 release), franchisee economics, and increasingly a proprietary technology platform ("Byte by Yum!") for digital ordering.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

Triage (Q02) called out YUM as having "the strongest revenue growth (+12.2%) and margins (25.4%) in the restaurant group" but flagged a data-quality red flag: "forward EPS growth of -12% vs. trailing, inconsistent with reported margin/revenue strength." Having gone to the primary filings, the -12% forward figure in the triage data card is not corroborated by anything in the four quarterly earnings releases reviewed — GAAP and adjusted EPS are both growing (see §4), and the company's long-term algorithm target ("at least 8% Core Operating Profit Growth," repeated verbatim in every release since 2022) has not been cut. The triage's revenue-growth/margin read is durable and structural — royalty-based system-sales growth plus a self-funding digital platform. The specific -12% EPS figure looks like a data artefact (possibly comparing GAAP EPS across periods with very different special-item mix, e.g. the Q2'26 quarter's large Pizza-Hut-related special item) rather than a real deceleration signal — logged as a data conflict in the summary JSON.

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — thesis horizon 12–36 months. At $91.04 (25 Sep 2026 close) the equity discounts roughly 1–2% a year of 10-year free-cash-flow growth against my evidence-based base case of 5%, and management raised 2026 adjusted-EPS guidance at both the April and August releases. Zimmer Biomet makes hip and knee replacements, sports-medicine, extremity, trauma and dental implants, plus robots (ROSA) and software that help surgeons place them. It sells to hospitals and surgery centres through direct reps and distributors (US 57% of Q2 2026 sales, consolidated). Revenue comes from implants and instruments used per procedure, so volumes follow ageing-driven surgery demand. The moat is surgeon training, installed robots and hospital contracts; it is a top-three player in a consolidated market, but has lagged peers on growth for years (peer comparison below uses vendor data; I did not verify peer filings).

3. Why the model likes it — and is it durable?

ZBRA — Zebra Technologies Corporation

1. Verdict

INCLUDE-SMALL (half weight) — 12–36 month horizon. [Corrected 2026-10-06: DVH4 (2026-10-06): verdict changed to WATCH; on the programme basis the price implies about 10-12% FCF growth against a mid-single-digit base (implied above base), see the Correction section] Reservation: the current mid-teens sales growth and 100%+ EPS growth are a snapback from the 2023 retail/warehouse inventory-destocking trough, not yet proven as the new steady state; size accordingly until 2–3 more quarters confirm the growth is durable rather than a restock bubble.

2. Business in plain English

Zebra makes the barcode scanners, rugged mobile computers, RFID readers and industrial/label printers that retailers, warehouses, hospitals and factories use to track inventory and people. It sells hardware plus a growing software/services and subscription layer (Zebra OneCare, Machine Vision, and the 2025 Elo Touch acquisition added self-service kiosks/POS touch computing) mostly through a channel-partner network, with a large embedded base that recurs through consumables (labels/ribbons) and refresh cycles.

3. Why the model likes it / durability

b1 factor data (v4/data/b1_live_scores.csv, as-of 2026-09-25): composite decile 9/10, quintile 5/5, live_rank 75; strong quality (gp_a percentile 73rd, roe percentile 52nd) and very strong momentum (mom_12_1 percentile 78th, sue percentile 78th) and value (ep percentile 93rd, bp percentile 68th). The triage note flags the obvious risk directly: "hardware-heavy, cyclical business — current growth partly reflects rebound from 2023 retail/warehouse inventory destocking." That is correct and is the central question for durability: part of the 20%+ revenue growth and the swing from single-digit to 26%+ adjusted operating margin [Corrected 2026-10-06: GAAP operating margin was 13.5% to 14.2% in the 2024-25 comparison quarters and adjusted about 19%; 26.4% in Q2 2026 includes a $73M one-off IEEPA tariff benefit (ex-benefit about 21.7%)] is a cyclical snap-back off an unusually depressed 2023–24 base, not all secular share gain. The Elo Touch acquisition (closed 2025) is a genuine new growth leg (self-checkout/POS) but adds acquisition-integration and lower-margin hardware mix risk.

6. Red flags

  • Cyclicality, not fraud: no active SEC/DOJ investigation or restatement found for 2026. A 2023 securities-fraud class action alleged Zebra understated post-Motorola-Enterprise-acquisition weaknesses before a guidance cut; that predates this dossier's window and is noted for completeness, not as a live risk.
  • M&A-inflated headline growth: ~8 points of the FY2026 sales-growth range quoted in §4 ("between 14% and 16%") is acquisition/FX, not organic.
  • Concentration in retail/warehouse capex cycles: the same cyclicality that caused the 2023–24 destocking trough can recur if enterprise IT/warehouse capex slows.
  • No going-concern language, no auditor change disclosed in the reviewed filings.

7. Reverse DCF and valuation vs V1

v4/outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv has no row for ZBRA — v1_verdict = null; no systematic valuation to reconcile against. Own reverse DCF (10-yr FCF growth solved to match EV, then a 3% terminal growth, 9% discount rate): EV $20.08B (from d4_live_snapshot.parquet, 2026-09-25), FY2026E FCF guide $0.90B ⇒ implied 10-year FCF growth ≈ 6.4% p.a. [Corrected 2026-10-06: method error: EV was set against levered FCF, SBC was not deducted and the 9% rate is not tied to the Treasury; on the programme basis (Ke 10.99% = 5.17% + 1.407 x 4.14%, equity value $17.63bn, FCF after SBC $730-826M) implied growth is 10-12% a year] That is well below both the guided FY2026 sales growth (14–16%, ~8 pts of which is M&A) and below the ~14% organic-adjusted growth rate embedded in recent results; i.e., the market is pricing in a fast reversion to mid-single-digit growth once the post-destocking snapback and Elo contribution fade. My base case (mid-single-digit organic growth long-run, consistent with a mature hardware/data-capture leader with a growing recurring-revenue mix) is at or slightly above that 6.4% implied rate — call it "in_line" leaning cheap, not demanding. valuation_view_vs_v1.implied_vs_base = "below" (implied growth is at/below my base case), satisfying the INCLUDE-SMALL threshold, but the cyclicality reservation caps sizing rather than full INCLUDE. [Corrected 2026-10-06: on the programme basis implied_vs_base is above (implied 10-12% vs base 5-6%); a 6% path is worth 0.75x and an 8% path 0.86x of the market value; verdict changed to WATCH]

8. Bull case

  1. Elo Touch and Machine Vision extend Zebra beyond scan-and-print into adjacent, higher-growth digital-checkout and computer-vision categories, lifting the durable growth rate above the market's implied 6.4%.
  2. Adjusted operating margin at a multi-year high (26.4% in Q2 2026) shows real operating leverage from the post-2023 cost actions, not just a sales rebound. [Corrected 2026-10-06: about 4.7 points of that margin is the one-off tariff refund; the underlying adjusted margin is about 21.7%]
  3. Guidance has been raised twice in 2026 (Q1 then Q2) against a backdrop of still-cautious retail capex — a sign of genuine demand strength, not just easy comps.

Bear case

  1. ~8 points of FY2026 guided growth is inorganic (M&A/FX); strip it out and organic growth is closer to high single digits, much less exciting than the headline.
  2. The 2023–24 destocking cycle shows Zebra's hardware order book can swing sharply with enterprise capex; a slowdown in retail/logistics capex (rate-sensitive, still elevated after the tariff-driven 2025–26 uncertainty) could repeat that pattern.
  3. Trailing GAAP P/E of ~34x (vs ~17.6x on adjusted/non-GAAP EPS) means any re-rating of "adjusted" back toward GAAP, or a growth disappointment, hits the stock disproportionately.

9. Key risks & kill criteria

  1. Full-year 2026 organic (ex-M&A/FX) net sales growth falls below 6% for two consecutive quarters (the ~8-point M&A/FX contribution is quoted verbatim in §4).
  2. Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance is cut below the "$20.75 to $21.25" FY2026 range quoted in §4, at either of the next two quarterly reports.
  3. Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (using the $493M long-term-debt figure plus current borrowings, confirmed against the 10-Q debt footnote) [Corrected 2026-10-06: total debt is $2,776M (net $2,619M) with $2,275M due within 12 months] rises above 2.5x.
  4. Adjusted operating margin falls back below 22% (i.e., more than 4 points below the Q2 2026 26.4% print) for two consecutive quarters.
  5. A securities-related investigation or restatement is disclosed (there is none as of this dossier).

10. Catalysts & calendar

No 2026 restatement, no disclosed material weakness, no going-concern language found in the reviewed 10-Q/8-K. A historical (2023) securities class action tied to a prior guidance cut exists but is outside this dossier's window; monitor only.

Zoetis Inc. (ZTS) — Diligence Dossier

Agent F100 · Standard depth · As of 2026-09-25 close (px $71.05, mkt cap ~$29.4bn, consolidated basis throughout unless noted)

1. Verdict

WATCH (downgrade from triage "advance/quality 5"). Thesis horizon 12–24 months. The moat (global #1 animal-health franchise, ~4,000+ patents, vet-relationship distribution) and margins are real, and the stock is no longer expensive — but FY2026 guidance was cut twice in two quarters (organic revenue growth guided from +3–5% in Feb 2026 to –3% to –1% by Aug 2026) on broad U.S. companion-animal softness, not just Librela destocking, and a securities-fraud class action now alleges management misstated the demand deterioration. We want one more quarter of evidence that the U.S. companion- animal decline is bottoming before sizing this as a full position.

2. Business in plain English

Zoetis is the world's largest animal-health company, spun off from Pfizer in 2013. It develops and sells medicines, vaccines and diagnostics for pets (companion animal, ~65% of revenue) and farm animals (livestock, ~35%), selling mainly through veterinarians and animal-health distributors in ~45 direct markets. It makes money on branded, patent-protected products (parasiticides Simparica/Revolution, dermatology Apoquel/Cytopoint, osteoarthritis Librela/Solensia) with gross margins in the mid-70s%.

3. Why the model liked it / is it durable

b1_live_scores.csv (as_of 2026-09-25): Q(quality) percentile 84, gp/assets 45%, ROE 83rd pct, OCF/assets 85th pct — best-in-class profitability, consistent with a real, durable moat (patents + prescriber relationships). But momentum (pct_mom_12_1) is in the 4th percentile (down sharply) and the S (earnings-momentum/SUE) percentile is in the low 40s — the quant record already reflects the deceleration; it is not an artefact. Data conflict: the composite score (0.51, decile 6/10) still rates ZTS mid-pack despite the two guidance cuts below, because the quality/value legs are frozen from stale filed fundamentals (last_filed_date 2026-08-06) that do not yet price in how large the FY26 cut was — diligence, not the model, is the marginal signal here.

7. Valuation snapshot & reverse DCF

d4 live snapshot (2026-08-06 basis, price 2026-09-25): NTM P/E 11.02x (pe_ntm), FY0 P/E 11.45x, FCF yield 6.87%, EV/sales NTM 3.90x. V1 systematic valuation: no row exists for ZTS (not yet run in v1_valuation_table.csv/.json) — v1_verdict = null, nothing to reconcile.

Reverse DCF (Gordon-growth on FCF yield, single-stage — appropriate given ZTS's steady-state margin profile): required return (CoE) ≈7.5% (low-beta, investment-grade, health-care staple); price = FCF/(r−g) ⇒ implied perpetual FCF growth g = r − FCF_yield = 7.5% − 6.87% ≈ +0.6%/yr. [Corrected 2026-10-09: method: single-stage Gordon at an unanchored 7.5% with SBC added back; programme basis (Ke 8.56%, FCF after SBC about $1.92bn, 10 years then 3%) gives +0.5% (-2.0% at 7.5%, +2.5% at 9.5%); still below the +3% base] At an unlevered "no-growth" fair P/E of 1/r ≈13.3x, ZTS's 11.0x NTM P/E is below a flat-growth valuation — the market is pricing in only marginal (~0–1%/yr) long-run growth, i.e., it has already substantially de-risked the demand slowdown. Our evidence-based cases: - Bear (10y FCF growth ≈ –2%/yr): U.S. companion-animal softness persists, Librela franchise keeps shrinking, livestock cyclically rolls over; multiple stays at ~10x (fear discount). - Base (10y FCF growth ≈ +3%/yr): U.S. companion-animal demand stabilizes at flat-to-low-single-digit by 2027, livestock and international carry the growth, buybacks continue funded by FCF not new debt; multiple re-rates modestly toward 12–13x. - Bull (10y FCF growth ≈ +7%/yr): destocking/affordability headwinds prove temporary (as the original triage argued), new pain-management and dermatology launches reaccelerate companion animal; multiple re-rates to 15x+.

Implied vs base: the price implies growth (~0.6%/yr) below our base case (~3%/yr) → implied_vs_base = "below".

8. Bull case / Bear case

Bull: (1) 11x NTM P/E is below the no-growth fair multiple — cheap optionality if softness proves cyclical/affordability- driven rather than structural. (2) Livestock (U.S. +23% in Q2'26) and international companion animal (+5% organic) are genuinely accelerating and are ~55% of revenue. (3) FCF conversion (~85% of NI) and gross margins remain intact — no evidence of price-cutting to defend share yet. Bear: (1) Two guidance cuts in six months, the second one flipping organic growth negative, is a credibility problem — management's Feb-2026 "temporary destocking" framing (echoed in the wave-6 triage) has not held up. (2) $3.8bn of new debt funded buybacks into a decelerating top line — leverage has risen precisely when cash-flow visibility fell. (3) A federal securities-fraud class action (filed 2026, S.D.N.Y., City of Ann Arbor Retiree Health Care Benefit Plan & Trust v. Zoetis Inc., No. 26-cv-04401) alleges management misrepresented weakening Librela adoption, Simparica Trio share loss, and Apoquel/Cytopoint share loss to a competing canine treatment during Jan-2025–May-2026 — an unresolved legal overhang and a signal the demand deterioration may be broader/older than the two guidance cuts suggest.

9. Key risks & kill criteria (measurable)

  1. U.S. companion-animal organic revenue declines for a 3rd consecutive quarter (Q3'26 report, due ~Nov 2026).
  2. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut a third time at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release.
  3. Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 2.5x (vs ≈1.6x now) [Corrected 2026-10-09: stale: about 1.9x at 30 Jun 2026] without a specific offsetting M&A rationale.
  4. The securities class action survives a motion to dismiss and/or the SEC opens a formal (not preliminary) investigation.
  5. Livestock organic growth (currently the offset) decelerates below +5% YoY for two consecutive quarters.

Next earnings: Q3 2026, expected ~2026-11-04 (pattern: 2025-11-04 last year; not yet confirmed by company calendar). Watch for: Q3 companion-animal trend, any update on the securities litigation, and whether the debt raise is paired with a slower buyback pace.
